Content analytics for your LinkedIn Page

Content analytics provide LinkedIn Page admins the opportunity to gauge trends in engagement among their followers by providing meaningful metrics for various components of their Page.

Important to know

Content analytics for boosted posts might be different from what is shown in Campaign Manager. Pages content analytics only includes boosted posts that appear in feed, while Campaign Manager also includes data from other ads and offsite views.

The following analytics are available:

  • Highlights - Shows the number of total likes, comments, and reposts for up to 365 days. It also indicates the percent of change from the previous time period, up to 365 days

  • Metrics - Shows key metrics for your organic and sponsored posts over time and can be filtered by time ranges. These metrics can be viewed in aggregate or non-aggregate form. It might take 48 hours for metrics to be reflected, except for reactions and comments which reflect in real time. #### Important to know

    Keep in mind, demographic data will be displayed as a percentage of the total number of unique visitors who view a Page article or video post.

    The following metrics are available:

    • Impressions - The number of times your post was shown on LinkedIn. This number is an estimate and may not be precise.
    • Members reached - The number of distinct members and Pages that saw your post. This number is an estimate and does not include repeat displays.
    • Clicks - Shows the number of clicks on your content, company name, or logo by a signed in member. This doesn’t include interactions, such as reposts, reactions, and comments. If a member clicks on a document multiple times it will count as one click.
    • Reactions, Comments, and Reposts - Shows the number of reactions, comments, and times your content was shared by members, including Direct Sponsored Content and video posts.
    • Engagement rate - Shows the ratio of interactions per impressions on your post. Interactions include clicks, reactions, comments, and shares.

  • Content engagement - Shows engagement details by individual post and can be filtered by time ranges. The following metrics are available:

    • Post title - Shows the first few words of your post if it included text. If only an image was posted, you’ll see the image’s alt text or file type. All titles are hyperlinked to the post.
    • Audience - Shows whether the post was sent to all followers or a targeted audience, as well as if employees were notified.
    • Boost available - Shows eligible posts that you can boost. You’ll see Boost unavailable next to posts that are ineligible.
    • Posted by - Shows the name of the Page admin who posted the content.
    • Created - Shows the date each post was posted.
    • Impressions - The number of times your post was shown on LinkedIn. This number is an estimate and might not be precise.

    Video performance:

    • Video views - The total number of times your video was watched for more than 2 seconds, including sponsored and organic views.
    • Time viewed - The cumulative length of time your video was viewed, including sponsored and organic views.
    • Audience tab - Gives Page admins access to insights about where their viewers work, what titles they occupy, and their geographical location in the Video Analytics window.
    • Clicks - Shows the number of clicks on your content, company name, or logo by a signed in member. This doesn’t include interactions, such as reposts, reactions, and comments. If a member clicks on a document multiple times it will count as one click.
    • CTR - Shows the number of clicks your post received divided by the number of impressions your post received.
    • Reactions - The number of reactions (for example, likes) your post received.
    • Comments - The number of times people commented on your post.
    • Reposts - The number of times people shared your post to their feed.
    • Boosted leads
      • Leads – Shows the number of people who have shown interest in your campaign and filled out a lead gen form. This number will vary based on your target audience, schedule, budget, and more.
      • Cost per lead – Shows the estimated amount you’ll spend per lead for your campaign. This number will vary based on your target audience, schedule, budget, and more.
      • Contact form completion rate - The rate at which members of your targeted audience have clicked into and submitted your lead gen form.
    • Follows - Shows the number of follow clicks on your Sponsored Content.
    • Engagement rate - Shows the ratio of interactions per impressions on your post. Interactions include clicks, reactions, comments, and shares.
    • Engagements - The total number of interactions on your posts, which includes clicks, reactions, comments, and reposts.
    • Cost per sponsored engagement - The average cost per sponsored engagement. This metric is only available for certain posts and might not be available to you at this time.
    • eCPM (effective cost per mille) - The average cost per 1,000 impressions. This metric is only available for certain posts and might not be available to you at this time.

While post analytics are available on desktop, content analytics for the last 30 days are available on mobile.

Important to know

Keep in mind, demographic data will be displayed as a percentage of the total number of unique visitors who view a Page article or video post.

The following analytics are available for your Page posts:

  • Content highlights - Shows impressions and the engagement rate for organic and Sponsored Content.

    • Impressions - Shows the number of views your content receives when it’s at least 50 percent on the screen for 300 milliseconds or more, or when it’s clicked.
    • Engagement rate - Shows the ratio of interactions per impressions on your post. Interactions include clicks, reactions, comments, and shares.

  • Content metrics over time - Shows aggregated metrics for your organic and Sponsored Content over the last 30 days. You can filter the metrics by:

    • Impressions - Shows the number of views your content receives when it’s at least 50 percent on the screen for 300 milliseconds or more, or when it’s clicked.
    • Engagement rate - Shows the ratio of interactions per impressions on your post. Interactions include clicks, reactions, comments, and shares.

  • All posts - Shows engagement metrics for individual posts in real-time according to:

    • Impressions - Shows the number of views your content receives when it’s at least 50 percent on the screen for 300 milliseconds or more, or when it’s clicked.
    • Engagement rate - Shows the ratio of interactions per impressions on your post. Interactions include clicks, reactions, comments, and shares.
    • Organic stats - Shows engagement rate metrics individually.

Follower analytics for your LinkedIn Page

As a LinkedIn Page admin, you can access analytics that provide an insightful look into the followers that have taken interest in your Page. Use your Follower analytics to tailor your engagement strategy with current and prospective followers.

The following analytics are available for your Page followers:

  • Follower highlights shows the number of members who have followed your Page since it was created and the number of new followers in the last 365 days. Any adjustments to the date range will not change the total follower count displayed. The total number of followers is updated once a day. If you subscribe to Premium Company Page, you can also see how many followers came from Premium features.

  • Follower metrics shows how your number of followers has changed over time and can be filtered by time ranges. These metrics can be viewed in aggregate or non-aggregate form.  If you turn on auto-invites (only available with a Premium Company Page subscription), you’ll see how many followers came from automatically inviting people who engaged with your content.

  • Follower demographics shows a total breakdown of who’s currently following your Page, using Location, Seniority, Job function, Industry, and Company size data. The top results for each attribute are split out individually, and the remaining results are combined into an Others category. The demographics won’t change based on the reporting dates. The total number of followers is approximately rounded, which means it may appear greater or less than the exact number of followers.

    Follower demographics will be displayed as a percentage of the total number of unique visitors who view a Page post. Follower analytics will update when a minimum number of unique visitors view a post.

  • All followers shows your current Page followers along with their current place of employment and when they followed your Page. All followers are approximately rounded, which means it may appear greater or less than the exact number of followers. Followers are listed in order of recency. Select People to see members who follow your Page, or select Pages to see other Page followers. If a subscriber came from auto-invites (only available with a Premium Company Page subscription), you’ll see Auto-invited with Premium below the specific follower.

To better support admins with more reliable insights about reach and engagement, inactive accounts, including restricted and hibernated accounts, aren’t included in the total number of followers.

Here’s a tip

To gain more followers on your Page, you can use the Invite to follow feature to invite your connections to follow the Page.

Hirer responsiveness insights FAQ

LinkedIn showcases hirers’ responsiveness on job posts to enhance their employer brand and demonstrate their commitment to candidates by making their job posts more transparent. For companies actively engaging with candidates, these insights will highlight their active review status or applicant review times.

Important to know

We’re gradually making this feature available, and you might not have access to it at this time.

Where do responsiveness insights appear?

Responsiveness insights are displayed on job search results and job description pages. Example insights you may see on jobs include:

  • Actively reviewing applicants
  • Review time is typically 1 week
  • Responses managed off LinkedIn

Why are responsiveness insights beneficial?

  • Enhance your employer brand: Increase transparency and responsiveness, which builds trust and boosts your employer brand reputation among job seekers.
  • Stand out and attract more talent: Set your company apart from others who don’t respond to candidates as quickly or frequently and attract more confident and qualified applicants.

How is the “Actively Reviewing Applicants” insight calculated?

  • “Actively Reviewing Applicants” is displayed on a job post when the recruiter has reviewed one or more applications in the past two weeks and is updated daily.
  • The following interactions count as a ‘Review’: InMail, rejection (auto, bulk, or manual), move candidate to any stage past ‘uncontacted’ in LinkedIn Recruiter, application view, profile view, and resume download.

How is applicant review time calculated?

  • Applicant review time is calculated based on the average response/review time for at least 35% of on-site and Apply Connect applications to a company over the last 30 days. If the average response/review time is over 21 days, this badge is not shown.
  • The following interactions count as a ‘Review’: InMail, rejection (auto, bulk, or manual), move candidate to any stage past ‘uncontacted’ in LinkedIn Recruiter, application view, profile view, and resume download.

What does the “No response insights available yet” insight mean?

This insight is shown for jobs posted via LinkedIn Jobs, external ATS integrated with Apply Connect, and LinkedIn Recruiter* (select jobs only) where a recruiter hasn’t:

  • Reviewed at least 1 application in the past 2 weeks
  • Reviewed at least 35% of applications

This insight can also change if a recruiter ends up reviewing one application OR the company ends up reviewing at least 35% of applications. It’s not a permanent status; it can change based on recruiter and company activity.

*LinkedIn Recruiter jobs eligible for insights include:

  • Manually posted jobs where customers choose to receive applicants on LinkedIn and be notified by email. Jobs that direct applicants to an external site to apply are not eligible.
  • Job wrapping jobs that are posted from an external ATS integrated with Apply Connect.

What does the “Responses managed off LinkedIn” insight mean?

This insight is shown for jobs posted through an external ATS. Since the application process is separate, LinkedIn does not have responsiveness data for these posted jobs. This insight makes it clear to job seekers that they shouldn’t view these jobs any differently and to set the expectation that the process lives off LinkedIn.

How can hirers improve their response time?

By making sure you’re active and reviewing at least 1 application for a specific role every 2 weeks and/or also reviewing at least 35% of the applications you receive. Enabling automated rejection messages to applicants who don’t meet your must-have qualifications is an efficient way to improve your response or review time without having to manually respond more. Just add screening questions to your job posts on LinkedIn, and auto-rejections will be enabled by default.

Important to know

If you are not interested in having responsiveness insights on your job posts, please reach out to your LinkedIn Sales partner or our support team to opt-out.

  • Apply Connect in Recruiter
  • LinkedIn Jobs ATS Integrations: Candidate application

LinkedIn Page analytics

Gain insight into the performance of your LinkedIn Page with rich analytics that gauge trends across metrics and time periods. Analytics are available for all Page admin roles.

Page analytics include the following:

  • Analytic type: Content; Definition: Effectiveness of your updates, including posted videos; Purpose: Evaluate the quality and topics of content shared with your Page followers and visitors.
  • Analytic type: Followers; Definition: Demographics and sources of followers; Purpose: Understand who’s following your Page and how to best engage with them.
  • Analytic type: Visitors; Definition: Demographics and sources of visitors; Purpose: Understand who’s visiting your Page and how to convert them into a follower.
  • Analytic type: Search appearances; Definition: Demographics and sources of searches; Purpose: Understand who’s searching for your Page, the keywords used to search for your Page, and how to increase visibility of your Page.
  • Analytic type: Competitors; Definition: Compare Page followership and content engagement with competitors; Purpose: Understand how your Page’s followership and content compare to your competitors’.
  • Analytic type: Employer brand; Definition: Engagement with your Career Pages; Purpose: Understand how to improve engagement with your Career Pages audience.
  • Analytic type: Newsletter; Definition: Track newsletter performance and understand audience; Purpose: Review trends, article totals and subscriber demographics to optimize content quality.

Newsletter analytics

LinkedIn members and Pages who are Newsletter authors can access newsletter analytics to better understand their newsletter performance and their audience.

Newsletter analytics page

At the top of your newsletter analytics page, you can select the date range you want to view for your data, from the past seven days up to the past 365 days. The date range you select here applies to the Trends and Article totals sections only. The Subscriber demographics and New subscribers sections are not limited by this date range.

Trends

This shows trends over the date range selected above. Use the drop down menu to select whether to display Article views or New subscribers.

  • Article views - The number of times a member clicked on one of your newsletter editions to view it either on the article page or within a newsletter email within the selected date range. Article views from organizations are not included.
  • New subscribers - The number of members who subscribed to your newsletter(s) in the selected date range.

Here’s a tip

Email sends for each article in your newsletter are available on the article analytics page.

The percentage under these numbers represents the change rate, or the number of article views or new subscribers over the selected date range expressed as a percentage of that number for the period previous to this. For example, if you received 15 article views for the past seven days, and 10 article views for the seven days before that, you will see a 50% increase over the past seven days.

Here’s a tip

The percentage change will not appear if you did not receive any article views in the date range previous to this, as we cannot divide by zero.

Article totals

This shows the total impressions, engagements and article views that your newsletter editions gained over the date range selected above. Analytics are available for newsletter editions posted within two years.

  • Impressions - The number of times your newsletter editions were displayed on screen within the date range selected above.
  • Engagements - The number of engagements received within the selected date range on the posts containing your newsletter editions, including reactions, comments, and shares.
  • Article Views - The number of times a member clicked on one of your newsletter editions to view it either on the article page or within a newsletter email within the selected date range. Article views from organizations are not included.

Subscriber demographics

This shows demographic information about all the members who subscribed to your newsletter(s). Use the drop down menu to select the demographics category to display: Job titles, Company, Company size, Seniority, or Locations.

New subscribers

This shows your newest subscribers with the most recent at the top. You can click on the button next to each subscriber to engage with them by following, connecting, or messaging.

To access newsletter analytics:

  1. Click the  Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click View Profile.
  3. Scroll down to the Activity section.
  4. Click on Newsletter to see a list of your newsletters.
  5. Click on the newsletter you want to view analytics for.
  6. Click on View analytics at the top of your newsletter page.

To access newsletter analytics:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.
  3. Scroll down to the Activity section.
  4. Tap on Newsletter to see a list of your newsletters.
  5. Tap on the newsletter you want to view analytics for.
  6. Tap on View analytics at the top of your newsletter page.

Post analytics for your content

As a LinkedIn member, you can access post analytics for individual posts including text posts, images, videos, events, polls, and articles. You can use analytics to see how far your post reaches, spot trends after every post, and explore audience demographics. These analytics are specific to the post itself and do not apply to poll results or events attendee metrics.

The following analytics are available for LinkedIn members on individual posts. Please note that the numbers in your post analytics are estimates and may not be precise:

Discovery

  • Impressions - Number of times your post was shown on LinkedIn.
  • In network - Percentage of impressions from members who follow or are connected to you.
  • Out of network - Percentage of impressions from members who don’t follow or aren’t connected to you.
  • Members reached - Number of distinct members and Pages that saw your post. This number is an estimate and does not include repeat views.

Profile activity:

  • Profile viewers from this post - The total number of distinct members and Page admins who viewed your profile from your post.
  • Followers gained from this post - The total number of members who followed you from your post.

Social engagement

  • Reactions - The number of times members or Pages reacted (i.e. liked) your post.
  • Comments - The number of times members and Pages commented on your post.
  • Reposts - The number of times members and Pages shared your post to their feed.
  • Saves - The number of times members saved your post.
  • Sends on LinkedIn - The number of times members sent your post to others on LinkedIn.

Link engagement:

  • Premium custom button interactions - The total number of times members and Page admins clicked on a Premium custom button in your post, including repeat clicks.

  • Visits to links in this post - The total number of times members and Page admins clicked on an external link in your post, including repeat clicks.

    • Data is not available for links that are detected as spam, malicious, or that violate LinkedIn’s professional community policies.
    • Data is also not available for links that point to content within the LinkedIn platform, such as your own posts or LinkedIn Pages.

Post viewers demographics

Demographic information may include the job title, location, company, company size, industry, and seniority of your post viewers. Guest views are excluded to provide a more accurate representation of your audience.

Depending on the type of content, you may also see additional performance metrics, such as:

  • Article views - The total number of times your article was seen on LinkedIn or via email. This number is an estimate and may not be precise.

    If your article is part of a newsletter, you’ll also see:

    • Email sends - The number of subscribers that have received an email for this article.
    • Email open rate - The percentage of subscribers that have opened the email sent for this article. This number is an estimate and may not be precise.

  • Video views: The total number of times your video was watched for two or more continuous seconds, including replays.

  • Watch time: The cumulative length of time your video was viewed.

  • Average watch time: The average amount of time that your video was watched. This is calculated by the time watched divided by the number of views.

If you’re a Premium member, you may see a Who viewed your profile after this post section at the bottom of your post analytics page. This section displays members who viewed your profile within the first month after your post was published (starting the day after it was shared).

You can click Show allto expand the list and view up to 100 recent profile viewers, depending on their privacy settings. Viewers are listed in reverse chronological order, with the most recent appearing at the bottom.

If you’re not a Premium member, you’ll need to upgrade your membership to access this information.

The Who’s viewed your profile since this post section will not appear if:

  • Your post is older than 90 days, or

  • You did not receive any profile viewers within the first month after publishing the post.

  • Your post analytics are private to you.

  • Your own views, social engagements, link engagements, saves, and sends are counted towards the analytics of your content.

  • Demographic data won’t be available for any content you share with only your connections or in LinkedIn Groups.

  • We’re always working on maintaining member anonymity. For example, demographic data is only shown when there are enough unique viewers to help protect individual privacy.

  • Video performance analytics and video viewer demographics are available for 365 days.

  • Article performance, article viewer demographics, and newsletter specific analytics are available for two years.

  • For all other content types, discovery and social engagement counts are available for 1,000 days. Members reached data is available for 400 days. Demographic breakdowns are available for 180 days.

If you’ve boosted a post, you may see ad-only breakdowns for certain analytics, such as discovery, social engagement, and ad performance.

Recent changes to viewers demographics

At LinkedIn, we’re always working to provide valuable analytics to our creators, and have been building more tools for creators. We’re also always working to maintain member anonymity while viewing posts, and recently made changes to our demographics analytics.

In addition to expanding creator analytics, we have made changes to help safeguard anonymity for viewing posts (including articles and videos) on LinkedIn. Recent changes include:

  1. We introduced a small amount of noise to the number of members reached in each demographic to help prevent visibility into exact viewer behavior. The demographic percentages that you see in your demographics will be representative of your audience but may not be precise.

  2. We changed the threshold for displaying results in the viewers demographics section. The threshold is now based on members reached, not impressions.

    Note: Impressions represent the number of times your post was displayed on screen. Members reached represent the number of members your post was displayed to at least once.

  3. We changed the results for each category to be shown as a percentage of members reached rather than as a count.

  4. We redesigned the demographics analytics to highlight the top insights based on your members reached (currently available only on the LinkedIn mobile app). Up to three will be shown. Tap on Show all to see the detailed breakdown.

We are always evaluating, and in some cases adjusting, how we show analytics, including privacy protections, such as differential privacy designed to prevent visibility into exact viewer behavior. Because of these protections, numbers may not be precise.

As a result of these changes, your viewers demographicsmay take longer to populate or your detailed breakdown may show information for some demographics categories while others remain blank until your post gets more views. In addition, you will see your results shown as a percentage of members reached rather than as a count.

Search Appearances analytics for your LinkedIn Page

As a LinkedIn Page admin, you can gain a better understanding of your Page’s visibility and determine the right way to increase its discoverability using the Search Appearances analytics information.

Search Appearances refers to the number of instances where your Page name appears in search results. This information is displayed in the Search Appearances tab which is available from the Analytics menu.

The Search Appearances tab provides you with the following information:

  • Total number of search appearances - Number of times your Page appeared in search results in a given period of time. This number is refreshed daily.

  • Number of searches in which your Page appeared in the last seven days. This number does not include Page visitors.

  • Top keywords that were used to find your Page #### Here’s a tip

    You can start a post using these same keywords to improve the visibility of your Page.

  • Demographic details about the people who searched for your Page such as companies that they are from, their industry, and job titles

How is Search Appearances analytics different from Page Visitor analytics?

Visitor analytics for a Page gives you information on who is visiting your Page. You can view details on visitor traffic such as the total number of visitors to your Page, number of unique visitors, and demographic details of the visitors for a specific period of time.

Search Appearances analytics on the other hand provides you information on the number of times your Page has appeared in member search results, and the keywords that were used in search to find your Page. Using this information, you can take actions to improve the discoverability of your Page. For example, you can create posts on your Page with keywords that have been used by members to find your Page.

Video performance:

Visitor analytics for your LinkedIn Page

Track your LinkedIn Page’s visitor traffic and demographic trends to understand audience engagement.

As a LinkedIn Page admin, you can gain a better understanding of your Page’s performance through visitor analytics which includes visitor traffic and demographic trends across different time periods.

Visitor analytics information for your LinkedIn Page is available to you from:

  • Notifications tab in your LinkedIn Profile
  • Activity tab on your LinkedIn Page – This tab tracks and displays all activity around your Page. You can click the Analytics tab to access detailed Visitor analytics.
  • Visitors tab within the Analytics menu on your LinkedIn Page

If you have enabled notifications for Page-related insights, then you will see analytics information for your Page from the Notifications tab on your profile. If you are an admin for multiple LinkedIn Pages, then the Notifications tab displays analytics information for the recent Page that you had signed in to.

Visitor analytics information in the Notifications tab from your profile displays the following:

  • Number of new page visitors in the last 7 days
  • Percentage change in the number of weekly visitors for the Page

To view detailed analytics for your LinkedIn page, click the notification displayed in the Notifications tab from your profile, and it will take you to the Activity tab on your LinkedIn Page which tracks all activity related to your Page. From here, you can click Visitor analytics to view detailed information on visitors to your Page.  

Visitor analytics in your LinkedIn Page displays the following information:

  • Visitor highlights - Number of total Page views, Unique visitors, and Custom button clicks in the last 30 days. It also indicates the percentage change from the previous 30 days.
  • Visitor metrics - Key metrics based on traffic to your Page and can be filtered by time ranges, Page sections, how many times your Page was viewed, and how many unique visitors (non-duplicate) visited your Page. These metrics can be viewed in aggregate or non-aggregate form.
  • Who’s visited your Page - List of recent visitors to your Page. As an admin, you can see up to one new visitor’s details each day when eligible members visit your Page. This is only available with a Premium Company Page subscription.
  • Visitor demographics - A breakdown of who has visited your Page and can be filtered by time ranges, Job function, Location, Seniority, Industry, and Company size. Visitor demographics will be displayed as a percentage of the total number of unique visitors who view a Page post.
  • Life page traffic - Total number of visits and unique visitors to your Life Pages and can be filtered by time ranges, Published Pages, Unpublished Pages, or All Pages.

We’ve made changes to how we display visitor analytics on Pages to enhance privacy protection. As a result, visitor demographics below Visitor metrics and Visitor highlights may not update as often as the algorithm requires a minimum number of unique visitors to display results.

  • To download the larger data archive, go to Download my data page. This will include the CSV file of all of their receipts.

Add your tax registration or VAT number to your billing information

If you have purchased your subscription online, you can enter your tax registration, value added tax (VAT), goods and services tax (GST), or other similar transaction number either from the payments page or the Tax information page in LinkedIn Admin Center.

  • If you need to update your information for an Ads account, you’ll use Campaign Manager.
  • If you purchased your services through our sales team, contact our Billing Support team to update the information.
  • If you used PayPal to purchase your services, contact us to update the information.

To add your VAT number in the payment page:

  1. Select the checkbox next to I’m purchasing as a business.

    Note: This checkbox appears only for VAT eligible countries.

  2. Enter your value added tax number in the VAT textbox that appears and click Add.

    • After the VAT number is verified, the tax ID is added to your order, and the Order summary section is updated with the total amount to be paid.

  3. Click Place order. An email is sent with the attached receipt, which has the VAT number printed on it.

Notes:

  • To remove the VAT number before placing your order, click or the VAT number itself and the Order summary will again get updated.
  • To remove, use, or add a different Tax ID after completing your purchase, go to the LinkedIn Admin Center to manage the tax registration information.

To add your VAT number in LinkedIn Admin Center after you have placed an order:

  1. Sign in to the LinkedIn Admin Center.

  2. Click Tax information on the left pane.

  3. In the Tax information page, click Add tax ID.

  4. In the Add tax ID pop-up window, select a country or region in the Country/Region textbox.

    Note: An error message appears if you select a country that already has a tax ID.

  5. Select a country from the suggestions that appear in the dropdown, and click Next.

    • Only LinkedIn supported tax jurisdiction countries will appear in the dropdown.
    • The type-ahead feature predicts related search terms as you type your keywords into the search bar.

  6. Enter your value added tax number in the Tax number textbox provided, and click Add.

    • After the VAT number is verified, it is successfully added in the Tax information page.

Notes:

  • You can also add the VAT number from the Purchases page. After selecting an active subscription, you can click Manage all tax IDs under the Billing Information section and follow the same steps mentioned above.
  • To remove the VAT number, click the More icon in the Tax information page, and click Remove tax ID. In the Remove tax ID pop-up window, click Remove.

Available payment methods and currencies for sales rep-assisted purchase

As the primary contact on your LinkedIn contract purchased through a sales representative, you’ll work with your designated LinkedIn representative to select a payment method before signing the contract.

LinkedIn accepts the following payment methods for contracts:

  • Credit or debit cards
  • ACH and wire transfers
  • Check (only available in the US and Canada)

You may be able to update your payment method after your contract start date provided the contract meets the requirements for change. Please contact us by clicking Start chat displayed at the bottom of this help center article if you need to change your payment method.

If you choose to pay by credit or debit card, you’ll use LinkedIn Admin Center to enter and save your payment details.

The following credit and debit cards are accepted:

  • American Express
  • Discover
  • Mastercard
  • Visa
  • RuPay
  • Japan Credit Bureau (JCB)
  • Diners Club

Keep in mind:

  • We don’t accept other forms of payment like PayPal, Bill Me Later, or ACH.
  • If the contract payment method is listed as check, wire, or ACH and you want to pay by credit card, it’ll require a payment method change.
  • We don’t accept credit card information over phone, fax, or email.
  • You’ll be required to use a United States (US) credit card for contracts with a US ship-to address. Contracts with an international ship-to address can use a US or non-US credit card.
  • Billing admins can access LinkedIn Admin Center using the sign in information from their personal LinkedIn account. Their sign in details are only used as entry point. Their profile and account information won’t otherwise be linked to their LinkedIn contract.

Payment information for ACH and wire transfers are found on the bottom portion of your invoice.

You can pay by check if you reside in the US and Canada. Instructions for check payments are located on the Payment Instructions section of your invoice.

Your LinkedIn representative will help you select an available currency during the order completion process. We accept the following currencies:

  • Australian Dollars (AUD)
  • British Pound (GBP)
  • Canadian Dollars (CAD)
  • Danish Krone (DKK)
  • Euro (EUR)
  • Hong Kong Dollar (HKD)
  • Indian Rupee (INR)
  • Japanese Yen (JPY)
  • Singapore Dollar (SGD)
  • Swedish Krona (SEK)
  • Swiss Franc (CHF)
  • United States Dollar (USD)

Notes:

  • Some currencies aren’t available within select regions.

  • You’ll be billed in the currency selected in your sales contract.

Available payment methods for online purchase

LinkedIn offers a Basic (free) account and various Premium accounts (i.e., Business, Recruiter Lite, or Jobseeker). You can also purchase items like the PMP® Certification Exam Preparation course, job postings, and LinkedIn Ads.

Important to know

This article is only applicable for subscriptions purchased online. It doesn’t apply to payments for contracts purchased through our sales team or for ads payments.

We accept credit, debit, and prepaid cards issued by the following networks:

  • American Express
  • Discover
  • MasterCard
  • Visa
  • RuPay: While LinkedIn accepts RuPay for payments, it’s important to note that not every RuPay card issuer is compatible with the RBI’s e-mandate requirements.
  • UPI: If you’re in India, you can now use Unified Payment Interface (UPI), an available payment method, for your purchases on LinkedIn.
  • JCB
  • Diners Club (USD currency only)
  • SEPA direct debit: This is only available to certain countries using the EUR currency. The payment option is available for Premium Business, Premium Career, Sales Navigator, and Recruiter. It is unavailable for job postings or ads.
  • iDEAL: This is only available members residing in the Netherlands. Only one iDeal account may be used per LinkedIn account. This payment option is unavailable for Learning subscriptions, job postings, or ads.
  • Sofort: This is only available for members residing in Germany using the EUR currency. The payment option is unavailable for Learning subscriptions, job postings, or ads.

PayPal and iOS: We accept PayPal as a payment method for Premium accounts and Job Postings on desktop. Only one PayPal account may be used per LinkedIn account. When you select PayPal, you’ll be redirected to PayPal.com to log in and complete your purchase. PayPal is not supported for advertising products. If you’re using the LinkedIn iOS app, purchases can only be managed through your Apple account. For more details, visit the Apple website. You cannot use Paypal with your current payment information. Paypal can be added as a new payment method and once added, the payment option can be modified.

Apple Pay: We accept Apple Pay as a payment method for all new and recurring online purchases of Premium subscriptions and posts you boost. You might see an Apple service fee while checking out when you boost a post. This fee is separate from your ad credits and accounts for Apple’s transaction fee.

Google Pay: We accept Google Pay as a payment method for all new and recurring online purchases of Premium subscriptions.

Note: You can’t switch an existing payment method to Apple Pay or Google Pay, as these options won’t appear in your list of available payment methods. Currently, Apple Pay and Google Pay are only supported on desktop and mobile web.

We don’t accept the following payment methods:

  • Bill Me Later
  • ACH payments

Important:

  • Some pre-paid cards may not allow monthly recurring billing. We recommend checking with the pre-paid card company or bank to confirm whether recurring billing is possible.

  • If you don’t see PayPal as an option on the secure checkout page, it isn’t available in your region at this time.

  • If any other payment method is not shown during checkout or when adding a payment method, it’s unavailable in your area or for the product being purchased.

  • We are gradually accepting SEPA, Ideal, and Sofort as a payment method for purchases. Some EU customers may not have access to these payment methods at this time. Please select an available payment method to complete your purchase.

  • If your preferred payment method fails during a recurring charge, LinkedIn can automatically try another eligible payment method saved to your account. This helps keep your subscription active without any interruption or action needed on your part.

Backup payment for online purchase

If your preferred payment method fails during a recurring charge, LinkedIn can automatically try another eligible payment method saved to your account. This helps keep your subscription active without any interruption or action needed on your part.

Backup payments are turned on by default for eligible accounts. When enabled, LinkedIn will:

  • Always charge your preferred payment method first.
  • Automatically attempt up to 2 other eligible payment methods from your wallet if your preferred method is declined.
  • Never change your preferred payment method, only you can do that.

Important to know

This feature applies to all recurring LinkedIn subscriptions purchased online, including Premium, Learning, and Recruiter. It does not apply to one-time purchases.

Here’s a tip

Only credit and debit cards can be used as backup payment methods. Other payment methods such as PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, RuPay, SEPA, iDeal, and Sofort are not eligible as backups. Your backup payment method must also be registered in the same country as your preferred payment method.

Backup payment methods are available in most regions, including North America, Latin America, and parts of Asia Pacific and EMEA. This feature is not currently available in Europe (EEA), the United Kingdom, or India due to local payment authentication requirements.

Backup payment for online purchase FAQ

If your preferred payment method fails during a recurring charge, LinkedIn can automatically try another eligible payment method saved to your account. This helps keep your subscription active without any interruption or action needed on your part.

Check out some of these frequently asked questions about backup payments.

Backup payment methods allow LinkedIn to automatically charge another eligible payment method saved to your account if your preferred payment method fails during a recurring subscription charge. This helps prevent service interruptions.

Yes. Backup payments are enabled by default for eligible accounts. You can turn them off at any time from the Payment methods page in your LinkedIn Admin Center.

No. Your preferred payment method will not change. LinkedIn will always attempt to charge your preferred method first. If it fails, a backup may be used for that charge only. Only you can change your preferred payment method.

Only credit and debit cards are eligible as backup payment methods. PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, RuPay, SEPA Direct Debit, iDeal, and Sofort cannot be used as backups because they require you to approve or authenticate each transaction.

Yes. Your backup payment method must be registered in the same country as your preferred payment method.

Yes. If your preferred payment method fails, you’ll receive an email letting you know that LinkedIn will attempt other eligible payment methods on your account. Your receipt and transaction history in the Admin Center will also show which payment method was charged.

Yes. Your receipt, invoice, and transaction history in the Admin Center will reflect the actual payment method that was used, including the last 4 digits of the card.

If you’re eligible for a refund, it will be returned to the same payment method that was charged — including if a backup payment method was used.

No. LinkedIn has safeguards in place to prevent duplicate charges. If a duplicate charge is ever detected, it will be automatically canceled or refunded.

No. Backup payment methods apply only to recurring subscription renewals, not to one-time purchases.

Yes. Your backup payment setting applies to all subscriptions associated with your LinkedIn account. You cannot enable or disable it for individual subscriptions.

Go to the Payment methods page in your LinkedIn Admin Center, click Manage backup payments, and toggle the setting off.

If your preferred payment method fails, LinkedIn will not attempt any other payment methods. This may result in an interruption to your subscription.

Backup payment methods are not available in all regions. If you’re located in Europe (EEA), the United Kingdom, or India, this feature is not currently available due to local payment authentication regulations. You also need at least one additional payment method saved to your account.

Billing for promoted job posts FAQ

Important to know

These FAQs apply to jobs posted with a personal LinkedIn member account and not a Recruiter or Recruiter Lite account.

After posting a promoted job on LinkedIn, you’ll be charged based on several defined conditions. Your charge amount depends on the budget you’ve set for your job posts and the number of views your post receives.

After posting a promoted job on LinkedIn, your default payment method on file will be charged when one of the following conditions is met:

  • You’ll be charged every 30 days from the date of your first job post, and your billing cycle will begin on this date. Any accrued balance for subsequent job posts will be applied to your billing cycle for as long as the job remains open.
  • You’ll be charged within 24 hours if your total account balance across all jobs is greater than or equal to $500. For new customers, this threshold may be lower for the first few invoices. After successful payments are established, your account will move to the standard threshold.
  • You’ll be charged within 24 hours if all jobs are closed. If there is at least one job still open, you won’t be charged immediately.

Important to know

The date of your billing cycle will reset after all jobs are closed or suspended. If you post a new job, a new billing cycle will begin on this date.

Your charge amount depends on your job posts’ budget and the number of views from candidates. Daily charge calculations are based on UTC time and resets each day at 12AM UTC.

For jobs located within the European Economic Area (EEA), you won’t be charged for clicks that come from outside the EEA. For all other jobs, you won’t be charged for clicks outside your country. You only pay for job views by candidates and aren’t billed for views from LinkedIn employees or the job poster. As a result, you might see a discrepancy in the number of views and the amount charged.

We’ll always charge the current default payment method on file. If you change your default payment method at any time before the end of your billing cycle, your new card on file will be charged.

Note that the total spend of the job posting may appear on your jobs management page on a slightly different timeline than the number of views or applicants you receive.

Important to know

The total spend of the job posting doesn’t include promotions or discounts as those are applied once the member is charged and the payment is processed.

The higher your budget, the more your job post is marketed into newsfeeds and emails of members that match the information listed in your job description.

At the end of your billing cycle, you’ll receive your bill via email. You can also view and print receipts from your billing history page.

The number depends on job title, industry, location, and other factors. As some of these factors are not constant across all job posts is calculated based on the performance of similar job posts on LinkedIn.

We’ll share your job across LinkedIn and through email to professionals whose skills and location match the job. Anyone on LinkedIn can find your post through search, and if you have a LinkedIn Page, it will appear there too. You can also share your job via social media.

For jobs located within the European Economic Area (EEA), you won’t be charged for clicks that come from outside the EEA. For all other jobs, you won’t be charged for clicks outside your country.

When you post a job, you can select how you want to receive applicant information. You can collect it on LinkedIn and get email updates with new applicants. Alternatively you can route applicants to an external website to apply, such as your career site or ATS.

The cost per click (CPC) for each job fluctuates per day based on the overall marketplace and activity. This includes the job location, job title, and additional factors such as other job posters looking for similar candidates in the area. Because some of these factors are not a constant, the CPC cannot be determined until the job is posted and generates some activity.

Once the posting is live, you’ll have access to the Manage tab for your posting where you can see views, applies, and more.

We’ll never charge you more than your budget (excluding any applicable taxes).

For any day that you edit your average daily budget, you’ll be charged based on the highest budget that you set for that day.

To make your job post as competitive as possible and to maximize your allotted daily spend, unused daily budget will be rolled over into the next day.

Important to know

If a job promotion payment fails, all affected promotions immediately stop. You need to repost the job to continue.

Sometimes your daily budget will go unused for a number of reasons. When this happens, it will be rolled over into the next day to maximize your allotted spend and make your job post as competitive as possible.

Your job will be posted until:

  • your total budget is reached (for total budget jobs only)
  • you close the job, which you can do at any time
  • after six months when the job automatically closes

To stop spending, you must close the job. You’ll only be charged for views received on the days your job was open.

Currently, there isn’t a feature to pause a job post on demand. The available options are to close the job at any time, or to set a total budget for a promoted job, which will cause the job post to pause automatically once the budget limit is reached. You can then decide to add more budget or close the job entirely.

If you repost a free job within 7 days, you’ll be required to promote it. Job posts with the same title and company as a previous job post are ineligible to be posted within 7 days for free.

Once a job post has been promoted, it cannot go back to a free job. You will have to close the job post and post a new free job.

The minimum and maximum budget for promotion depends on the role being promoted, applicant forecasting, and whether you’ve already promoted a job.

If the charges for existing job postings cannot be processed, current jobs will close.

When you have credits available in your account, these credits are used first for any accrued charges. You will only be charged if the credits are insufficient to cover the total cost.

When you have credits available in your account, these credits are used first for any accrued charges. You will only be charged if the credits are insufficient to cover the total cost.

Yes, you can choose a budget below the recommended budget suggested. However, you may lose access to AI-assisted features.

Yes. Recruiter Lite now allows admins to promote jobs using a payment method that differs from the one tied to their subscription. This update applies to both desktop and mobile platforms, including purchases made through the Play Store and App Store. Non-admin users can only promote jobs if an admin has already set up a valid payment method. Only purchasing admins can use separate payment methods for Recruiter Lite and Recruiter Lite jobs. The change improves flexibility, simplifies job promotion, and expands access across devices.

Change your billing cycle

You can choose between a monthly or annual billing cycle for your Premium Account.

Your membership will be renewed at the end of each billing cycle. Billing due date information is available on the Manage Premium account page. You can save up to 50% if you pay annually compared to paying monthly. All billing, cancellation, or renewal dates are shown in local US time zones for US-based English-speaking members only. For all other countries or languages, this is in UTC.

To change your billing cycle:

  1. Click the  Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Premium features from the dropdown menu.
  3. Click Manage your subscription on the left pane. You’ll be redirected to the LinkedIn Admin Center, where the subscription page appears by default.
  4. In the Billing information section, under Billing frequency, click ** Edit**.
  5. In the Edit billing cycle pop-up, choose either Monthly or Annual.
  6. Click Update to confirm your changes.

Notes:

  • Your billing cycle will be updated at the end of the current billing period. The price you pay will be based on the new billing cycle, not the original one.

  • You can upgrade to annual from the switcher page, which will take effect immediately, however, this option isn’t available for subscriptions purchased through Google Play or iOS App Store.

  • If you’re a paying member on a monthly subscription and decide to upgrade to an annual plan in the middle of the month, the cost for the remaining days of your monthly cycle will be adjusted in your new annual billing, which begins right away.

  • If you’re on a free trial and choose to upgrade to an annual subscription, you’ll be charged immediately, and your annual plan will start right away, meaning you’ll forfeit any remaining days of the free trial.

India payment regulations

Reserve Bank of India has imposed regulations to increase payment transparency for consumers in India. Beginning October 1, 2021, all LinkedIn customers from India with recurring payments must re-verify their payment method via two-factor authentication with their banks. This includes:

  • Premium subscriptions - Learning, Career, Business, Sales Navigator, and Recruiter Lite
  • Job posts (does not include job slots)
  • Ads
  • InMails
  • Enterprise contracts with credit or debit card payment method. Contracts include Talent Solutions, Sales Navigator, and Learning

New users will be required to submit a one-time password code to ensure you have an e-mandate created. Existing users will need to re-verify your payment method to have an e-mandate created.

When you add or update a payment method, you may see a higher amount on the E‑mandate authorization alert than your actual charge. Because the final amount isn’t known yet, banks may display the maximum permitted amount, up to INR 199,999. This is only an authorization request, not the amount you’ll be charged.

For each recurring payment, you’ll be notified by your bank at least 24 hours prior to being charged, with the option to cancel or continue subscribing to the product. If the charge is less than 15,000 INR, then no additional action is required.

For charges greater than 15,000 INR, you’ll be required to give consent to banks before LinkedIn can charge your payment method.

Banks won’t process transactions without consent from customers and can result in a disruption of services. Consult your bank for details on how to give consent to charge your payment method as this process is not handled via LinkedIn.

Important to know

It may take at least 48 hours from the time you receive the notification for your payment to process. During these 48 hours, do not attempt to edit your payment method or add a new payment method as this will cause the current payment to fail.

A limited number of cards issued by banks support the new RBI e-mandate payment process. For those cards issued by banks that don’t support the process, recurring payments may be declined.

While LinkedIn accepts RuPay for payments, it’s important to note that not all issuers of RuPay cards support the RBI’s e-mandate. You can use RuPay to only purchase subscriptions online and not through a LinkedIn sales representative.

If you’re in India, you can now use Unified Payment Interface (UPI), an available payment method, for your purchases on LinkedIn. You can use UPI to only purchase subscriptions online and not through a LinkedIn sales representative.

Note: If you’re using a credit card issued in India or making transactions in a non-INR currency, you may experience higher approval failures. To avoid this, we recommend making your purchase in INR with payment methods issued in India.

Below is a chart of banks and cards supporting transactions through the new RBI e-mandate process. If your payment has been declined, you can add a new payment method from the list of accepted cards/banks.

We’ll continue updating this list as more issuers begin supporting the e-mandate process.

In accordance with the Reserve Bank of India’s tokenization regulation, LinkedIn cannot store card details (card number, expiry date, etc.) for customers located in India. We’ll now require customer consent to tokenize credit or debit cards to continue processing transactions. 

For cards that are not tokenized, they’ll be removed from your saved payment methods, and you’ll be required to re-enter your payment details for any new transaction. Learn more about RBI’s guidelines here.

This impacts the following products in India:

  • Premium subscriptions - Learning, Career, Business, Sales Navigator, and Recruiter Lite
  • Job posts and Job slots
  • Ads
  • InMail
  • Enterprise contracts with credit or debit card payment methods. Contracts include Talent Solutions, Sales Navigator, and Learning.

Tokenization refers to the replacement of card details with a unique identifier called the “token”.

When you purchase a new product or subscription by selecting Review Order during the checkout process, you indicate that you agree to LinkedIn managing your card details and are providing consent to tokenize your card.

Yes, you can provide consent to tokenize multiple payment methods associated with your account.

We’ll remove any saved debit and credit cards that have not been tokenized by September 30, 2022. If your card is removed, you’ll be required to re-enter your card information to make a payment and have the option to provide consent to tokenize your card during checkout.

Unfortunately, we are no longer able to save card information for new credit/debit cards issued in India due to the recent tokenization regulation. However, during checkout, you can enter your card information or utilize a tokenized credit/debit card to complete your purchase.

If you’ve re-entered your card details and we are still unable to process your transaction successfully, we ask that you try another payment method.

  1. Click Contracts and Orders on the left pane.

  2. Click on the contract you’d like to view or for which you’d like to edit the credit card information.

  3. Scroll down to the Billing information section.

  4. Click Editnext to the credit card you’d like to update.

  5. In the Change Payment Method page, select a different credit card from your wallet or click Add a new payment method.

  6. Select Confirm changes after making all the changes.

    Note:

    • The new credit card information will appear in the Billing information section of the contract.
    • By updating payment method on the contract, you are updating all the payment methods tied to any related orders.

LinkedIn SEPA Direct Debit payment

Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) direct debit is available as a payment method for certain countries using the EUR currency. You’ll see this option when purchasing LinkedIn subscriptions, starting a free trial, or adding a payment method for your existing subscription. SEPA is currently available in these countries:

  • Germany
  • France
  • Netherlands
  • Australia
  • Belgium
  • Cyprus
  • Greece
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Luxembourg
  • Portugal
  • Spain
  • Austria

Important to know

We are gradually accepting SEPA, Ideal, and Sofort as a payment method for purchases. Some EU customers may not have access to these payment methods at this time. Please select an available payment method to complete your purchase.

Notes:

  • If SEPA direct debit is not shown during checkout or when adding a payment method, it is unavailable in your area or for the product being purchased.
  • The payment option is available for Premium Business, Premium Career, Sales Navigator, and Recruiter. It is unavailable for job postings or ads.
  • To use SEPA, you must have a SEPA direct debit bank account using the EUR currency and an IBAN.

LinkedIn does not apply any foreign exchange fees to your purchase. However, your bank or financial institution may impose such fees on purchases or refunds. If the transaction amount on your bank statement exceeds the amount shown on your LinkedIn receipt, please contact your bank directly. LinkedIn is unable to refund any foreign exchange fees charged by your bank.

If you exchange a product purchase and are eligible for a refund, the transaction will be processed immediately, and you should receive your refund within approximately 2-5 days.

If upgrading your subscription requires an additional charge and you are using the SEPA direct debit payment method, the transaction will not be processed immediately. Payment processing for the additional amount typically takes 7 to 10 business days, after which you will receive an email confirmation.

Notes:

  • You cannot upgrade your subscription immediately after a payment transaction has been initiated. It may take up to 7 to 10 business days after your initial billing or renewal date, during which the transaction status will appear as Pending.
  • You can track your transaction status on the Transactions page in LinkedIn Admin Center.
  • Once we receive the payment, the Pending status will be removed, and you’ll be able to upgrade your subscription.

If you made a purchase using SEPA direct debit, you are entitled to request a refund from your bank under the terms of your agreement. A SEPA direct debit refund must be requested within eight weeks from the date your account was charged.

Since your bank needs to verify authorization of the transaction, processing refund requests for SEPA direct debit payments may take up to 7 to 10 business days.

If you request a cancellation or refund through your bank, your LinkedIn subscription will be downgraded. However, LinkedIn will not immediately delete any files when your subscription is downgraded.

Manage backup payment for online purchase

You can turn backup payments on or off from the Payment methods page in LinkedIn Admin Center. This enables LinkedIn to charge an alternative payment method if your preferred one fails for a recurring charge. You must ensure that you’ve added at least one backup payment method for this to work.

To manage backup payment for online purchase:

  1. Navigate to the LinkedIn Admin Center page.

  2. Click Payment methods on the left pane.

  3. In the Payment methods page, click Manage backup payments in the upper right.

  4. In the Manage backup payments dialog box:

    • Turn on the Backup payments toggle to allow LinkedIn to charge a backup payment method if the primary one fails.
    • Turn off the Backup payments toggle to prevent backup payment methods from being charged.

  5. Click Close to save your setting.

Notes

  • Turning off backup payments may cause interruptions to your purchase if your preferred payment method fails.

  • When you add a new payment method, you’ll see a reminder that backup payments are turned off, along with an option to turn them on.

If you have purchased your subscription online, you can add, edit, delete, or change payment information from the Payment methods section of the LinkedIn Admin Center page. After adding a new payment method, you’ll need to apply it to your active subscription to ensure future payments are processed successfully.

Who can use this feature?

This information is for users who purchased Premium Subscriptions, Job Postings, and InMail credits.

Notes:

  • Payment information cannot be updated via the LinkedIn mobile app.
  • When you purchase an InMail, Premium account or a job posting, we automatically store your payment method so you can make additional purchases without re-entering your information. You can also store multiple payment methods and manage them for different products.
  • If your preferred payment method fails during a recurring charge, LinkedIn can automatically try another eligible payment method saved to your account. This helps keep your subscription active without any interruption or action needed on your part.
  • We don’t currently store payment information for LinkedIn Ads or Sponsored Jobs.

Reasons for declined payments

You can continue enjoying your LinkedIn services by ensuring your payment is successfully processed.

Common reasons for declined payments include, but aren’t limited to:

  • Common reasons for declined payments: Insufficient funds; Description: The payment method does not have enough funds to cover the transaction.
  • Common reasons for declined payments: Invalid or expired payment method; Description: The payment method is no longer valid or has expired.
  • Common reasons for declined payments: Blocked charge; Description: The charge was blocked by the bank or card issuer due to approval issues.
  • Common reasons for declined payments: Mismatched billing zip code; Description: The billing zip code on the payment method does not match the zip code listed with the financial institution.
  • Common reasons for declined payments: Recurring transactions not allowed; Description: The payment method does not allow recurring transactions.
  • Common reasons for declined payments: India payment regulations; Description: The bank declined the charge due to India payment regulations (for Online billing members). Note: For customers in India, if you are using an India based credit card and the transaction amount is less than $2000 USD, you will need to re-enter your card information due to RBI regulations. If the transaction amount is higher than $2000 USD, please reach out to our support team.

For details, please contact your financial institutions. Due to confidentiality, LinkedIn does not have access to your financial details.

Notes:

  • To ensure a successful transaction, you may need to re-enter your payment information.

  • Your transaction will be processed again within 48 hours.

  • If you still have questions about a charge status, please contact us by clicking Start chat displayed at the bottom of this help center article.

Value Added Tax (VAT) or Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Tax rates

This article summarizes the expected VAT treatment of LinkedIn services, by country. B2B customers refer to customers operating as a business. B2C customers refer to private consumers or non-VAT registered customers.

If you do not have a valid VAT ID but believe that you should not be charged VAT, please provide LinkedIn with valid proof of the VAT exemption issued by the local Government Authorities.

For European Customers

European Union (EU) tax regulations require LinkedIn to charge value added tax (VAT) to all customers located in Ireland and to private customers within the EU.

A VAT charge is applied to all services for both private (B2C) and business (B2B) customers in Ireland, with some small exceptions.

LinkedIn is not required to apply VAT on services for EU members outside of Ireland who have provided a valid VAT number. Customers may add their VAT number to their billing information. If customers do not provide a valid VAT number, VAT will be charged at the rate of the specific EU Member State.

LinkedIn Admin Center

View and download receipts for online purchases in LinkedIn Admin Center.

View receipts

You can view and download your receipts for Premium subscriptions from LinkedIn Admin Center.

Important to know

You can now download your receipt directly in chat.

Here’s a tip

If you purchased your subscription online, you’ll have access to receipts. If you purchased through a LinkedIn sales representative, you’ll have access to invoices instead.

Option 1: To download your receipt in chat, click Start chat at the bottom of this help center article, type ‘Download my receipt’, and follow the instructions.

Option 2: Follow the steps below to download your receipt manually.

To view and print your receipts for Premium subscriptions:

  1. Click the  Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Premium features from the dropdown.

  3. Click Manage your subscription on the left pane.

    • You’ll be redirected to the LinkedIn Admin Center.

  4. Select Transactions on the left pane.

    • You will see a list of receipts tied to the subscriptions you have purchased.

  5. Click the More icon next to each transaction to perform the following functions:

    • Download receipt: Click Download receipt to download the receipt tied to the subscription. After the receipt is downloaded in PDF format, you can access it from your browser’s download folder. You can click the PDF to open the receipt in a new tab for printing.
    • Edit receipt: Click Edit receipt details to edit the receipt tied to the subscription. In the pop-up window, add the information you’d like to appear on the receipt, and click Save. You may need to manually refresh the page after about a minute. Please note that these changes will not apply to future receipts.

Here’s a tip

To add details like a business address or purchase order number to future receipts, go to the Purchases page, select the relevant purchase, and scroll down to the Transactions section. Click Customize receipt details in the upper-right corner. Enter the updated details in the Receipt details pop-up window that appears, and click Save. Changes will apply to all future receipts.

Notes:

  • We don’t provide email receipts.

  • Your purchase history only displays receipts for charges associated with your account.

  • The purchase history on another member’s account can only be accessed by that member.

  • LinkedIn can’t provide purchase history for your subscriptions through Google. You can check your purchase history via Google order history page.

  • We currently don’t provide invoices for Premium subscriptions.

  • Receipts for purchases made via the Apple Store or from the LinkedIn iOS app are not available on LinkedIn.com. You can view your receipts from your Apple iTunes account. Visit Apple’s Support site for additional information.

Add an address to in-person events

When creating an in-person LinkedIn event, it is mandatory to include an address.

To add an address to in-person events:

  1. Click into the Address field and start typing the street, city, or other parts of your address.
  2. A dropdown menu will display.
  3. Select the address of your in-person event from the dropdown menu.

If you have issues selecting the correct address, try these troubleshooting steps:

  • Do not copy and paste the address into the Address field, but start typing to display the dropdown menu.
  • The addresses in the dropdown menu are based on Bing Maps. Check which address is available on Bing Maps.
  • If the exact address is not available, choose the closest address and use the optional Venue field to give your attendees more information.

Note: The event type and format cannot be changed after the event is created. If you initially created an online event, it cannot be changed to an in-person event later.

Create a LinkedIn Event

LinkedIn Events help you organize online and offline events. As a LinkedIn member or Page admin, you can create an event, add details regarding the theme and itinerary, and invite members to join.

If you don’t see the option to use LinkedIn Live in the event creation form, you may not be eligible. Check the LinkedIn Live access criteria.

Important to know

Once the event is posted, you can’t change the Organizer, Event type (Online or In person), or Event format (LinkedIn Live or External event link).

Avoid creating test or temporary Pages to try out events. Instead, use the built‑in test event option during event creation to safely validate your setup. Learn how to create a LinkedIn Live Test event from your LinkedIn Page.

To create an event:

  1. Click the Home icon at the top of the page.
  2. Click Events in the left pane.
  3. In the events page, click Create an Event.
  4. Follow the instructions below for each field in the Create an event pop-up window:
  • Field: Upload cover image; Instructions: You can use different banner sizes including 480x270 or 1280x720 pixels. The minimum width is 480 pixels, and the aspect ratio must be 16:9. Note:You can upload an image from your device, but uploading images stored in the cloud is not supported.
  • Field: Add alternative text (Alt text) to the cover image; Instructions: After uploading the cover image, click Alt text to add a description for screen readers. Alt text isn’t visible to members who are not using screen readers.
  • Field: Organizer; Instructions: Select your profile or Page to show who’s hosting the event.
  • Field: Event type; Instructions: Select Online for online events Select In person for offline events. You’ll need to add venue and location.
  • Field: Event format; Instructions: Select LinkedIn Live to stream your video event on LinkedIn using a third-party tool (available only if you have access to LinkedIn Live). Select External event link, if you plan to stream or host your event off LinkedIn but only want to promote your event on LinkedIn. Add the link to your external broadcast location so attendees can join your event easily. We recommend selecting LinkedIn Live where possible to prevent attendees from dropping off as they switch to other platforms.
  • Field: Event name; Instructions: Type a unique name that reflects the event’s theme.
  • Field: Timezone; Instructions: Select the applicable time zone from the dropdown.
  • Field: Start date/Start time; Instructions: Select the date and time of the event.
  • Field: Add end date and time; Instructions: Select this checkbox if you want your event to end at a specific date and time. You’ll have to select the date and time of the event.
  • Field: Use a LinkedIn registration form (available for Pages only); Instructions: Select this checkbox to allow members to register for the event. You’ll have to provide your privacy policy link explaining how attendee information will be used.
  • Field: Description; Instructions: Type a brief description that highlights the theme and purpose of the event.
  • Field: Speakers; Instructions: Type the speaker’s name and select them from the suggestions. They’ll be auto-invited to the event. The speaker’s name only appears if they are your LinkedIn connection.
  1. Click Next.
  2. Write a short post in Share your thoughts… field of the Share box to promote your event.
  3. Click the dropdown next to your Profile or Page name to select who you want to share the post with.
  4. Click Post to create the event. The event won’t be created until you complete this step.

To create an event:

  1. Tap  My Network in the navigation bar.

  2. Tap Manage my network.

  3. Tap Events.

  4. Tap Create in the upper-right corner.

  5. In Organizer dropdown, select your profile or Page to show who’s hosting the event.

  6. Under Event type, you can select:

    • Onlinefor online events
    • In person for offline events. You’ll need to add venue and location.

  7. In Event format dropdown, you can select:

    • LinkedIn Live to stream your video event on LinkedIn using a third-party tool (available only if you have access to LinkedIn Live).
    • External event link, if you plan to stream or host your event off LinkedIn but only want to promote your event on LinkedIn. Add the link to your external broadcast location so attendees can join your event easily. We recommend selecting LinkedIn Live where possible to prevent attendees from dropping off as they switch to other platforms.

  8. Select Use a LinkedIn registration form checkbox to allow members to register for the event. You’ll have to provide your privacy policy link explaining how attendee information will be used.

    Note: This option is only available when creating an event on behalf of a page.

  9. Tap the  Edit icon on the upper-right corner to upload a cover image.

    • You can use different banner sizes including 480x270 or 1280x720 pixels.
    • The minimum width is 480 pixels, and the aspect ratio must be 16:9.

  10. After uploading the cover image, tap ALT to add a description for screen readers. Alt text isn’t visible to members who are not using screen readers.

  11. Tap Next.

  12. Write a short post in Share your thoughts… field of the Share box to promote your event.

  13. Tap the dropdown next to your profile or Page name to select who you want to share the post with.

  14. Tap Post to create the event. The event won’t be created until you complete this step.
