LinkedIn Events overview

LinkedIn Events allow individuals or organizations to create, promote, and host professional gatherings on LinkedIn. Events can be online, in person, or hybrid. LinkedIn members can join events to grow their business, network with others, and learn new information.

Each event has an Event Page, the dedicated hub with all the details of an event, such as the event’s title, date, time, description, speakers, and agenda.

The following types of roles are available for events:

  • Organizer – The host of the event is the organizer. They create the event, decide the details, invite attendees, and can add one or more speakers. Organizers can share updates, and post content before, during, and after the event. The organizer can either be an individual profile or a LinkedIn Page (if the organizer is a Page admin).
  • Attendee – A member who accepted an event invitation or joined an event.

Important to know

  • The event organizer can’t be changed once the event has been created.
  • To ensure attendees receive notifications, we recommend creating events within 1 year of the scheduled date. Events created more than 1 year in advance may not generate notifications for attendees.

There are two types of events. The type and format can’t be changed once the event has been created.

  • In person events take place offline in a physical venue and are promoted on LinkedIn. The session is not streamed to audiences online.

  • Online events can have two different formats:

    • LinkedIn Live events are streamed on LinkedIn, with real-time conversations in the comments and a recording on your Page or profile. To create a live event, the organizer must have access to LinkedIn Live and to a third-party streaming tool. LinkedIn Live events can be either spontaneous or scheduled, but we recommend scheduling the event in advance to maximize attendance. Attendees can network during the event by minimizing the event window without exiting the event.
    • External events are still online, and while they are not streamed on LinkedIn, they are still promoted on LinkedIn. The organizer must provide a link to an external broadcast location that attendees can use to join the event. We recommend using LinkedIn Live as it prevents attendees from dropping off as they switch platforms.

After creating an event, the organizer can manage the details at any time, and the attendees will be notified about the important changes. Both organizers and attendees can invite connections to attend an event, but only the organizer can withdraw an invitation or remove an attendee at any time.

After accepting an event invitation, attendees can access a list of LinkedIn members attending the event. This is a great place to start interacting with other attendees, by inviting them to connect.

Organizers of LinkedIn Events

As an organizer, you’re responsible for setting the agenda for the LinkedIn Event, deciding logistics, and inviting attendees.

You can organize Events based on your audience or the Event’s theme. For example, you could schedule:

  • A workshop or training
  • A fireside or panel to discuss a topic
  • A happy hour to connect with your college alumni
  • A meetup to interact with fellow entrepreneurs
  • An Event to discuss best practices in design
  • An announcement or product demo

Note: The organizer can either create an Event from an individual profile or as a LinkedIn Page (if the organizer is a Page admin). The organizer can’t be changed once the Event has been created. Check out these FAQs about how to organize an Event as a Page.

As an organizer, you can use the LinkedIn Events feature to create or mange an Event for professionals who share common interests with you. For your convenience, you can control this feature from either the desktop or mobile LinkedIn experience.

All events on LinkedIn are public, making them discoverable to members who aren’t directly connected to you.

While creating an Event on behalf of a Page, the Event organizer (Page admin) can enable a registration form to collect the first name, last name, and email addresses of the attendees.

  • Create a LinkedIn Event
  • Cancel or delete a LinkedIn Event
  • Registration forms used for Events organized by Pages
  • Create a LinkedIn Live Test event from your LinkedIn Page

Once you’ve created an Event on LinkedIn, you can invite your connections to attend it. You should consider inviting connections who share a common interest in your Event’s purpose or theme. This will ensure that the attendees can leverage each other and share relevant knowledge and ideas.

As all events on LinkedIn are public, your attendees can also invite their connections to your Event.

A great way to promote your Event to individuals who may be interested in attending is to share the Event with your network. Sharing your Event increases its visibility and it gives people who aren’t in your network (not one of your 1st-degree connections) the opportunity to read more about your Event and decide whether they’d like to attend.

You can also share the URL link directly with others.

To increase the reach and visibility of your event outside of your network, you can launch Event Ads or Thought Leader Event Ads promoting your event to a target audience.

Here are some tips to run a successful Event on LinkedIn:

  • Choose a name that’s short and clear in order to help attendees understand what to expect.
  • Share and promote your Event from your individual profile or Page to reach your network and followers. If you’re hosting an Event as a Page, you can also try targeted promotion for the Event URL.
  • Customize your Event content to suit your attendees’ needs. You can do this by reviewing profiles of the attendees and understanding their professional backgrounds.

While creating an Event, you now have two options:

  • LinkedIn Live - If you’re eligible to use LinkedIn Live to stream to your event, you can choose LinkedIn Live from the Event Format dropdown. To make the most of events on LinkedIn, especially if you have access to LinkedIn Live, we recommend promoting and hosting the event on LinkedIn itself, as it prevents attendees from dropping off as they switch platforms. Using LinkedIn Live for your event helps you get viral reach and engagement as we notify attendees and a subset of your Page or Profile followers when you go Live. Learn more about how to get Live access.
  • External - If you’re not eligible to use LinkedIn Live to stream to your event, you can choose the ‘External’ option in the dropdown. We recommend using this option when you plan to stream or host your event off LinkedIn and only wish to promote your event on LinkedIn. In this case, we ask you to provide a link to your external broadcast location so that attendees can easily join your event off LinkedIn.

Note: You can’t edit the event format once the event is created.

Check out our FAQs for:

  • Events organized by individual profiles.
  • Events organized by Pages.

For further assistance with your Event, please contact us.

Here’s a tip

Video thumbnails are displayed in the emails sent to subscribers. Clicking on a thumbnail will redirect subscribers to the article page. 3. Click Next to add the cover video.

To add rich media to your article:

  1. From the tool bar next to your name at the top of the article, you can:

    • Add Links: Click the Link icon to paste the rich media content’s URL (For example, Tweets or Instagram images) into the Link field.
    • Embed content: Click the Embed icon to embed content within the article. From here, you can copy paste respective link into the widget to embed a embed a LinkedIn post, member profile, or a LinkedIn Page.
    • Add Image: Click the  Media icon to upload an image from your computer or drag an image into the box.

Important to know

Captions for other supported languages may not always be available.

Video upload file requirements (same as Sharebox)

  • Parameter: Minimum file size; Requirement: 75 KB
  • Parameter: Maximum file size; Requirement: 5 GB
  • Parameter: Minimum duration; Requirement: 3 seconds
  • Parameter: Maximum duration; Requirement: 15 minutes (desktop)/ 10 minutes (mobile app)
  • Parameter: Resolution range; Requirement: 256 x 144 to 4096 x 2304
  • Parameter: Aspect ratio; Requirement: 1:2.4 to 2.4:1
  • Parameter: Frame rate; Requirement: 10 fps to 60 fps
  • Parameter: Bit rate; Requirement: 192 kbps to 30 Mbps

Notes:

  • GIFs can no longer be used for the cover photos.
  • The supported file types for cover images are JPEG, JPG, PNG, and WEBP.
  • The optimal image size for the cover image is 1920 (w) x 1080 (h) pixels. Cover images are cropped to a 16:9 aspect ratio.
  • We support video sharing platforms like YouTube, SlideShare, TED, Getty, Vimeo, Vine, Lifestream, and more.
  • Make sure that you’re including the URL (…) and not the embed code (< blockquote class=“instagram-media”…). The URL can be found in the navigation bar at the top of your browser.
  • To embed an Instagram photo, open the individual photo and copy the URL in the navigation bar.
  • Images that aren’t your own should include a reference to the source of the image. The requirements for using a Creative Commons image vary depending on the image owner. Members must ensure that they follow the specified conditions.
  • The supported file types for in-article images are GIF, JPEG, JPG, PNG, and WEBP.
  • GIFs must be smaller than 400 frames.

Add the LinkedIn site-wide Insight Tag to Google Tag Manager

To use Google Tag Manager as your tag management system, you’ll need to add the LinkedIn Insight Tag 2.0.

To add the LinkedIn Insight Tag 2.0 to Google Tag Manager:

  1. Go to tagmanager.google.com and sign in.

  2. Select your account and your container.

  3. In the New Tag box, click Add a new tag.

  4. Click Tag Configuration, then select Discover more tag types in the Community Template Gallery.

    • Click Add to workspace if you haven’t added the tag template.
    • Click Choose template if you’ve already added the template.

  6. Add the partner ID from your Insight tag into the Partner ID field.

Here’s a tip

If you’re using the previous version of the LinkedIn Insight Tag, we recommend you move over to the new LinkedIn Insight Tag 2.0.

To move to the new LinkedIn Insight Tag 2.0 from the previous LinkedIn Insight Tag:

  1. Add the LinkedIn 2.0 Insight Tag to Google Tag Manager.
  2. Confirm that the new tag is working as expected.
  3. Pause the original LinkedIn Insight Tag.
  4. Publish the LinkedIn Insight Tag 2.0.

AI-powered tool for LinkedIn Page posts

With LinkedIn’s AI-powered writing tool, you can generate a first draft of a post for your Page using your ideas on a topic. The tool quickly transforms your ideas into a draft that you can edit before posting. You have ultimate control and ownership over the final post, so you should review and revise the generated content before sharing your post. As always, we recommend that you create content on topics you have expertise or personal knowledge about.

Here are some ideas to keep in mind when using the tool:

  • Use the tool as a place to jot down your notes and ideas. The tool will transform them into your draft.
  • Be specific and detailed with your ideas, rather than giving high-level talking points.
  • The more details you provide the tool, the better your draft will be.
  • Don’t ask the tool to come up with ideas for you or help you brainstorm.
  • Don’t use the tool to do anything other than write a LinkedIn post.
  • Review our best practices for creating content with the help of AI and follow our Professional Community Policies.

Who can use this feature?

Our AI-powered writing tool is only available with a Premium Company Page subscription. Your LinkedIn profile language must be set to English, and you must have created at least one Page post in the last 90 days.

Best practices to customize what you see on your LinkedIn feed

Your LinkedIn feed contains updates such as posts, shares, comments and reactions from your network, companies, and interests that you follow, along with recommended content and sponsored content. Your social activity on LinkedIn impacts the type of content seen in your feed.

Here are some best practices to customize posts and other updates that appear on your feed, through the control menu:

  • Unfollow or mute people or companies - You can unfollow or mute people or companies if you no longer want to see their posts.
  • Tell us what you dislike - If you see content in your feed that you don’t believe to be high-quality or relevant to you, you can choose I don’t want to see this post. You can let us know why you aren’t interested in seeing the content anymore.
  • Flag inappropriate content - We encourage you to report inappropriate or offensive content to help us keep LinkedIn constructive.
  • Add new perspectives to your feed - If you want to get updates from a member or company on your feed, you can choose to follow them. You can navigate directly to the Follow fresh perspectives page, which displays recommended sources to follow.
  • Sort updates - You can control if your feed shows recent updates or top updates at the top of your LinkedIn homepage. This feature is only available on the desktop experience.

Some of your feed updates may be delivered as push notifications and/or emails. You can control these by customizing your email settings and push notification settings.

Boost a post from your company’s LinkedIn Page

Boost your LinkedIn Page posts to extend their reach through an advertising campaign. You’ll select an objective for boosting your post, define the audience (who will see your post), and set a budget and schedule to limit how long the post is boosted.

Who can use this feature?

You’ll need super admin or content admin access on your LinkedIn Page to boost a post. If you’re a Sponsored Content poster, you can sponsor Page posts in Campaign Manager.

Boosting a post from your LinkedIn Page provides a lighter campaign and ad set creation experience, but also limits the options available for objectives, audience criteria, and bid and budget. For full options, create campaigns and ad sets in Campaign Manager.

Important to know

• At this time, you can only boost a post from your desktop. Also, only posts with text, single images, events, videos, documents, or LinkedIn articles or newsletter articles can be boosted. Boosted posts are billed through your ad accounts in Campaign Manager, not the LinkedIn Page. • Previously boosted posts can’t be boosted again. If you boost a post that’s edited, it’ll need to go through the ad review process again. Once it’s approved, the ad status will change from paused to active.

To boost a post from a LinkedIn Page:

  1. Access your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Click Page posts in the left menu and scroll down to find the eligible post you’d like to boost in your Page feed.

  3. Click the Boost button in the upper-right corner of the post.

  4. Select a goal for your boosted post.

    • Note: The More leads goal isn’t available for document posts.

  5. From the Audience section, choose how you’d like to build your audience.

    • Suggested audience (default) - Uses AI-driven targeting that adapts to your goal and content, ensuring optimal audience reach.
    • Create audience: Click the Create audience button in the upper-right corner of the Audience section to choose attributes to define your audience (for example, location or language).
      • You can also use LinkedIn Audience templates or your saved targeting templates when available.
      • For more advanced audience options, continue in Campaign Manager. Your current selections will carry over, and you won’t be able to return to this page.

Important to know

Beginning on May 15, 2024, Member Groups will no longer be available as a targeting attribute for the European Economic Area (EEA) or Switzerland. For more information, please review our best practices for LinkedIn Ads audience targeting. 6. Use the available fields to Set a start and end date and Total budget. 7. If you select Get more leads as a campaign goal:

  • Select a lead gen form template using either a personal or work email and fill out the required fields.
  • Enter in a privacy policy URL.

Important to know

For article or document posts, you can select a different call-to-action button for your form. For video posts, you’ll need to add a headline which will appear on both the organic and boosted version of the post. 8. Select an ad account to bill.

  • This step is only available if you have campaign manager access or higher on multiple ad accounts associated with the LinkedIn Page.
  • If you don’t have an active ad account with campaign manager access or higher, a new ad account will be created.
  1. Click the Boostbutton.

Results

Once you’ve boosted a post, an ad set will be created in your ad account with the selected settings and ad. The name of the ad set will include Boost Post, the selected goal, and the date the post was boosted.

You can also review and filter boosted posts from your Page or Campaign Manager by clicking Page posts in the left menu of your Page admin view. Keep in mind, you won’t be able to filter posts that are eligible for boosting.

You can view ad performance or edit ad set settings from your ad account in Campaign Manager. You can also edit the boosted post and ad set settings from your LinkedIn Page.

Boost your own LinkedIn post FAQ

As a LinkedIn member, you can boost your posts on the LinkedIn feed to increase your visibility, grow your followers, and get more website clicks. You can select your budget and target audience to boost key posts, increasing visibility to target audiences by selecting from facets including location, language, job title, job function, company industries, and job seniorities.

Important to know

  • Boosting a post will turn the post into an ad. See the LinkedIn Ads Agreement for more information.
  • Boosting is gradually being released. You might not have access to it at this time, and some functionality might change over time.
  • Boost credits included with Premium All-in-One can only be used to boost posts from your personal profile. You can’t use these credits to boost posts from a LinkedIn Page.

Here are some frequently asked questions about the feature.

If you have access to this feature, you can boost your posts from your Activity tab on both desktop and mobile. Click Boost on the upper-right corner of eligible posts.

After you boost your post as an ad, it will be reviewed before it can be displayed to member accounts in your target audience. We strive to review ads as soon as possible and usually within 24 hours.

All languages are available to be boosted.

Both old and new posts can be boosted.

Boosting is only available for text, single- or multi-image, article, video, and newsletter posts. Job posts, events, documents, polls, group posts, and connections-only posts cannot be boosted currently.

To see if you have any ad credits to use for boosting your post:

  1. Click Boost on the upper right of an eligible post from your LinkedIn profile.
  2. Scroll to the Payment details section.
  3. If you have ad credits, you’ll see them to the right of Remaining ad credits.
  4. Finalize your post, then click Boost to promote it.

To apply a coupon code to a post you want to boost:

  1. Click Boost on the upper right of an eligible post from your LinkedIn profile.
  2. Scroll to the Payment details section.
  3. Click Add coupon code and enter your coupon number.
  4. Finalize your post, then click Boost to promote it.

Each boosted post will have its own analytics view where you can see both the organic performance and the paid boosted performance of your posts throughout the five-day boost period. You can find the analytics view by clicking on the post and selecting View analytics.

The duration of a boosted post is dependent on the budget and end date selected when you set up your boost campaign.

We’ll use the content of your post to target the most relevant audiences and amplify your post beyond your network.

Yes, posts can be boosted to all geographical areas.

All languages can be targeted. When setting up targeting, you can select your preferred language.

Yes, you can boost from a mobile device by tapping Boost on the upper-right corner of eligible posts.

Important to know

Mobile boosting is currently in testing and is gradually being released. You might not have access to it at this time, and some functionality might change over time.

You’ll need to use prepaid ad credits to boost on mobile. Learn more about prepaid ad credits.

To boost a post on mobile, you’ll need prepaid ad credits. On iOS, credits are purchased through the Apple in‑app purchase flow. On Android, you’ll complete the purchase via LinkedIn Secure Checkout in a mobile web view. Credits are tied to your ad account and are used first when you boost. If you don’t have enough, you’ll see an Add credits prompt during checkout to purchase the amount needed. Learn more about prepaid ad credits.

Important to know

Mobile boosting is currently in testing and is gradually being released. You might not have access to it at this time, and some functionality might change over time.

Thought Leader Ads allow company pages to sponsor posts from members they’re affiliated with, while boosting allows individual members to boost their own posts.

Yes, you can edit and delete your boosted post. When you edit a boosted post, you can:

  • Edit the post itself. Keep in mind, your new post will need to be reviewed and approved before it can be shown to your target audience.
  • Change your audience.
  • Change the credit card used as the payment method.

Important to know

You can’t change the budget of a boosted post. If you need to change the budget, you must delete the post and boost it again with a new budget.

You can update your credit card payment details when you edit a boosted post. If there is an issue with the credit card, your boosted post will be paused until the credit card details are updated.

All boosted posts are reviewed and must adhere to the LinkedIn ads policy. If your ad violates the ads policy, you will receive a notification. You can boost a new variation that aligns with our policies. You will also receive a link to submit an appeal if you believe your ad already aligns with our advertising policies.

You can view your receipts by going to the Ads Module section of the Single Post Analytics page and select the Receipt option.

Your campaign ends when your budget is spent or the end date is reached, whichever comes first. We do our best to pace the delivery of your ad over your chosen duration, but if the budget runs out early due to high engagement, the campaign may end sooner.

In certain instances, campaigns with both a very large target audience and a small budget may spend the budget faster than expected. We are constantly working to improve how our system handles these cases. This can be more common when using Suggested Audience with no text in the post (e.g. just a video or image). Our AI relies on text to better understand your content and pick the best audience — so when there’s no text, it may struggle.  To improve performance, we recommend:

  • Including some text in your post if using Suggested Audience
  • Try creating a custom audience and keeping the audience between 50,000 and 500,000 for best results

When you boost a post directly from your profile, you won’t have access to an ad account in Campaign Manager. You’ll manage the boosted post, including viewing performance metrics and managing payment, from the post on your profile.

Collaborative articles

At LinkedIn, we regularly evaluate our features to ensure we’re investing in the tools that deliver the most value to our members. As part of this ongoing effort, we’ve made the decision to retire some features of collaborative articles.

Collaborative articles are knowledge topics published by LinkedIn with insights and perspectives added by the LinkedIn community. While we are no longer developing new collaborative articles, you can still explore a wide range of existing articles.

What’s changed

  • We’re no longer creating new collaborative articles.
  • You can’t add new contributions or edit existing ones.
  • Notifications about collaborative article recommendations and contributions are stopped.
  • All existing collaborative articles and contributions are now read-only.

What hasn’t changed

  • You can still find and read the collaborative articles and contributions.
  • You can report collaborative articles if you believe it violates our professional community guidelines.
  • Contributors can still delete their past contributions.
Viewing collaborative articles and contributions
  • Browse this list of collaborative articles. Click the categories on the right side of the page to explore collaborative articles of a particular skill.
  • Search for skill-related keywords or specific ‘how-to’ questions in the LinkedIn search bar to find relevant skills page or collaborative articles.
  • Find collaborative articles on all search engine results outside of LinkedIn.
  • Find your contributions under Comments in the Activity section of your profile.
Interacting with collaborative articles
  • You can share, react to, and save collaborative articles like any post on your feed.
  • If you find a contribution helpful, you can like or react to the contribution.
  • At the end of every article, you can rate the overall quality of the article to help LinkedIn improve the content experience.
  • You can also report a contribution or the entire article if you believe it violates our Professional Community Policies.
Tracking your contribution performance

You can monitor the performance of your contributions by checking the total view count under it. This count reflects the total number of times a contribution has been viewed across LinkedIn. This information is only visible to the contributor.

  • Delete your contributions from a collaborative article
  • Give feedback or report a collaborative article
  • Community Top Voices (Gold Badge)

Comment on posts and reply to a comment

Members and LinkedIn Pages can comment on posts and reply to comments from other members and LinkedIn Pages.

Notes:

  • Members and LinkedIn Pages can disable comments on their posts. This will prevent you from commenting.
  • Members can limit commenting on their posts to connections only. This will prevent you from commenting if you aren’t their 1st-degree connection.
  • LinkedIn Pages can allow or restrict comments on their Page posts from all LinkedIn members.
  • Members can block members and LinkedIn Pages from commenting on their posts.
  • When a member or a LinkedIn Page comments on their own post, an Author tag is displayed next to the name.
  • To keep LinkedIn safe and professional, we may limit how many comments a member or a LinkedIn Page can make in a certain time period. Similarly, if we detect excessive comment creation or use of an automation tool, we may limit the visibility of those comments. Verifying your Page, and ensuring that you and the other admins of your Page have added a workplace or identity verification to your member accounts can help you optimize your Page’s content creation and visibility.

To comment on a post:

  1. Click Comment below the post or in the textbox that says Add a comment.
  2. Type your comment.
  3. Optional: Type @** to mention someone in your comment. Click the Emoji** icon to add an emoji, the **** icon to select a GIF, or the ** Image** icon to attach a photo.
  4. Click Comment.

To reply to a comment:

  1. Click Reply below a comment or in the text box that says Add a reply.
  2. Type your reply.
  3. Optional: Type @** to mention someone in your comment. Click the Emoji** icon to add an emoji, the **** icon to select a GIF, or the ** Image** icon to attach a photo.
  4. Click Reply.

To comment on a post:

  1. Tap ** Comment** below the post or in the textbox that says Leave your thoughts here.
  2. Type your comment.
  3. Optional: Tap @** to mention someone in your comment, tap the ** icon to select a Gif, or tap the  Image icon to add a photo.
  4. Tap Reply.

To reply to a comment:

  1. Tap Reply below the comment.
  2. Type your reply.
  3. Optional: Tap @** to mention someone in your comment, tap the icon to select a Gif, or tap the  Image** icon to add a photo.
  4. Tap Reply.

You can sort comments by Most relevant or Most recent comments. Click or tap on the Most relevant dropdown below a comment textbox and select an option. Some comments will only be visible under Most recent view.

Create a LinkedIn Live Test event from your LinkedIn Page

LinkedIn Live Test events are an opportunity to familiarize yourself with LinkedIn events and feel confident on the day of your event. As a LinkedIn Page admin, you can create test events from your admin view on desktop. Test events are available only for LinkedIn Live and not for other event formats. We recommend running an end-to-end test to set up the connection between your stream and a scheduled event and to fine-tune your encoder settings without broadcasting to your audience.

Test live events are visible only to Page admins and to anyone, including non-admins, who are sent a direct link to the test event. Non-admins need to confirm attendance to the test event by clicking Attend or Register. Notifications are only sent to page admins.

To create a test event:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.
  2. Click Create.
  3. Click Create an event.
  4. Select the event type and enter a name for your event.
  5. Select This is a test event checkbox.
  6. Fill out the remaining event details, including the time zone, start and end date, event link, description, and speakers.
  7. Click Next.
  8. Add any introductory text to your event post. By default, the post visibility setting is set to page admins as the target audience.
  9. Click Post.

Notes:

  • Page admins will get notified when the test event goes live, when the live stream ends, and when the recording is available.
  • Non-admins, who are sent a direct link to the test event, can confirm attendance, see comments, and view the stream before, during, and after the event. Non-admins need to confirm attendance to the test event by clicking Attend or Register.
  • Test events will have a Test label next to the event name on the event page.
  • Page admins can delete the test event immediately after creation; no notification will be sent for the event cancellation.
  • The test event post will also be deleted from the admin view once the event is deleted.
  • If you plan to stream via RTMP, set the start time of the test event no more than one hour before the time you want to set up the test stream.

Create a LinkedIn Page newsletter

A LinkedIn Page newsletter is a set of regularly published editions on LinkedIn, typically about a specific topic. You can create up to five newsletters as yourself or as a LinkedIn Page and you can create an unlimited number of editions for each newsletter.

Who can use this feature?

To create a newsletter as a Page, you must be a super or content admin of that Page and meet the newsletter access criteria. If you don’t see the option to create a newsletter within the admin view, your Page might not currently meet the access criteria, but you can take simple actions to meet the criteria.

Important to know

If you create a newsletter for your Showcase Page, the newsletter isn’t linked to the parent Page.

Anyone can discover, read, and share your LinkedIn newsletter. LinkedIn members can also subscribe to it.

To create a newsletter for your Page:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.
  2. Click Create in the left menu.
  3. Click Create a newsletter.
  4. Enter a newsletter title, select how often you’d like to publish your newsletter, and add a description.
  5. Upload an image.
  6. Click Done.

Results

After you create a newsletter, you can publish your first edition. You can publish additional editions and edit or delete editions at any time.

Publishing your first edition automatically creates a newsletter page with an overview of your newsletter, your Page information, and a list of the editions in the newsletter. You can use your newsletter page to provide a preview of your newsletter and share it on or off LinkedIn to increase your reach. You don’t need to be logged in to view the page, but members must log in to subscribe or share it on LinkedIn.

Your Page followers will be invited by notification to subscribe to your newsletter once the first edition of your newsletter is published. Subscribing means they’ll receive a notification and email when you write a new newsletter edition.

Create a LinkedIn Page post with our AI-powered tool

With LinkedIn’s AI-powered writing tool, you can generate a first draft of a post for your Page using your ideas on a topic. The tool quickly transforms your ideas into a draft that you can edit before posting. To create a successful post, review our best practices for creating content with the help of AI and follow our Professional Community Policies.

Who can use this feature?

Our AI-powered writing tool is only available with a Premium Company Page subscription. Your LinkedIn profile language must be set to English, and you must have created at least one Page post in the last 90 days.

To create a post with our AI-powered writing tool:

  1. Go to your Pages super or content admin view.

  2. Click Page posts in the left menu.

  3. Click Start a post.

  4. Write a draft with a minimum of 20 words. Share the main points that you want to highlight in your post, and be detailed and specific to generate a better draft.

  5. Click Rewrite with AI.

  6. Review and edit the content created by the AI-powered writing tool based on your input.

  7. Click Post.

    • Note: If you don’t edit the content, the Add your own thoughts pop-up window will appear reminding you to review and add your own thoughts before posting. We strongly recommend editing and adding your own thoughts to ensure the post reflects your point of view.

  8. Click Keep editing to edit your post, and after you’ve made your final reviews and edits, click Post.

To create a post with our AI-powered writing tool:

  2. Tap the Post icon in the upper-right corner.

  3. Write a draft with a minimum of 20 words. Share the main points that you want to highlight in your post, and be detailed and specific to generate a better draft.

  4. Tap Rewrite with AI.

  5. Review and edit the content created by the AI-powered writing tool based on your input.

  6. Tap Post.

    • Note: If you don’t edit the content, the Add your own thoughts pop-up window will appear reminding you to review and add your own thoughts before posting. We strongly recommend editing and adding your own thoughts to ensure the post reflects your point of view.

  7. Tap Keep editing to edit your post, and after you’ve made your final reviews and edits, tap Post.

Create and host LinkedIn Live: Access criteria

All members can join LinkedIn Lives as viewers. Eligible members and Pages can create and broadcast a LinkedIn Live.

[Embedded video omitted]

There are no applications to request LinkedIn Live access. Eligibility to create and broadcast a LinkedIn Live is based on a set of criteria.

  • If you trigger a review of your profile or Page and fulfill the criteria, you can instantly create LinkedIn Lives.
  • If you do not meet one or more criteria, you will not have access to create or broadcast LinkedIn Lives.

The criteria to create and host LinkedIn Lives are:

  • Audience base Members and Pages with more than 150 followers and/or connections are eligible to be evaluated for LinkedIn Live access.
  • A history of abiding by our Professional Community Policies We want to ensure our members have a safe, trusted, and professional experience on LinkedIn, as defined by our Professional Community Policies. Only members, Pages, and their admins that have a good standing record will be considered for Live Video access.
  • Geography LinkedIn Live is not available at this time for members and Pages based in mainland China.
  • The account or page must have been created at least 30 days ago.

Once you meet all of our criteria, there are two ways to trigger a review of your profile or Page and get access instantly:

  • Create an event on LinkedIn: If your profile or Page is eligible, you will see the option to select LinkedIn Live in the Event format dropdown. If you don’t fulfill the criteria, you will not see LinkedIn Live in the dropdown or the event format dropdown will be missing.

    • To trigger a review of any Pages you admin, change the organizer in the Organizer dropdown menu, or the event format dropdown will be missing.

  • Create an event via a preferred third-party broadcast tool: You’ll be notified immediately, if your profile or Page has access to LinkedIn Live or not.

Important to know

You cannot stream directly from LinkedIn. A streaming tool is needed to broadcast LinkedIn Lives (Video).

If you have any other questions related to LinkedIn Live, please contact us.

Create LinkedIn Polls

You can create a poll from LinkedIn’s homepage. If you’re an Admin of a LinkedIn Page or a LinkedIn Group you can create a poll directly from the Page or group’s homepage.

To create a poll from your homepage:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. In the post pop-up window, click the More icon, and then click the Create a poll icon.

  3. In the Create a poll pop-up window, type your question and fill in the options.

    • There is a minimum of two options and a maximum of four options on a poll.
    • Click +Add option to add another option.

  4. Select the Poll duration from the dropdown.

    • The default duration is one week.

  5. Click Done.

  6. Click the Edit icon to edit the poll.

    • Click the dropdown next to your name to select who you want to share the poll with.
    • You can add more to the post in the What do you want to talk about? field (optional).

  7. Click Post.

To create a poll from your homepage

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar.

  2. Tap the More icon, and then tap Poll.

  3. In the Create a poll page, type your question and fill in the options.

    • There is a minimum of two options and a maximum of four options on a poll.
    • Tap +Add option to add another option.

  4. Select the Poll duration from the dropdown.

    • The default is seven days.

  5. Tap Done on the upper right.

  6. Tap Edit to edit the post.

    • Tap the Anyonedropdown next to your name in the post page and select who you want to share the poll with.
    • You can add more to the post in the What do you want to talk about? field (optional).

  7. Tap Post.

Delete an article or a draft

Important to know

This feature is not available on the LinkedIn mobile app.

You can delete a published article or its draft on our publishing platform.

Once you delete your article or draft, it won’t be available on LinkedIn and we won’t be able to retrieve the content of your article. Additionally, we’ll no longer distribute your article. We can’t delete copies of your content that have been archived or cached by your followers or other external parties, such as Google.

Deleting an article or draft removes it from LinkedIn permanently and we don’t save content from deleted articles. If you wish to republish an article, you will need to either copy and paste the content or rewrite it. Republished articles won’t include views, shares, or comments from the previous version of the article.

To delete a published article:

  1. Click Write article in the share box near the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Manage dropdown menu on the upper right of the publishing tool and select Published to view a list of your published articles.

  3. From the Articles pop-up window, locate the article you’d like to delete.

    • The Published tab is automatically selected.

  4. Click the Delete icon next to the article you want to delete and confirm Delete.

To delete an article draft:

  1. Click Write article in the share box near the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Manage dropdown menu on the upper right of the publishing tool and select Drafts to view a list of your saved drafts.

  3. From the Articles pop-up window, locate the article you’d like to delete.

    • The Drafts tab is automatically selected.

  4. Click the Delete icon next to the article draft you want to delete and confirm Delete.

Difference between posts, articles, reposts, and newsletters

Members have several ways to share content on and off LinkedIn. Here are some definitions of terms you will see:

  • Posts are content shared through the LinkedIn feed. This content may consist of a wide range of information that may be of interest to other professionals on LinkedIn. Posts may contain media (for example, photos or videos) and third-party content (for example, URL).

  • Articles are long form, in-depth content that may be distributed to your LinkedIn connections and beyond. Articles typically consist of professional insights that can help members establish their brands in their areas of expertise.

  • Repost refers to sharing content that has been created by other LinkedIn members.

  • Newsletters on LinkedIn can be used to talk about a professional topic you’re passionate about on a regular basis. LinkedIn members can subscribe to your newsletter to be notified about new articles you publish, allowing you to build and grow a regularly engaged audience.

Important to know

All members and admins (super admins or content admins of a LinkedIn Page) have the ability to publish articles about their expertise and interests. Articles are displayed in the Activity section of your profile. You can edit an article even after it’s published.

Notes:

  • You can also ‘@’ mention a LinkedIn Page or another member while editing an article. The mentioned member/page will be notified of the mention and their profile/page will be displayed when someone moves their cursor over the hyperlink.

Enable collaboration for your LinkedIn Page posts

Members and Pages on LinkedIn can collaborate with other members and Pages on posts that they create. As a super admin of a LinkedIn Page, you can allow members and other Pages to collaborate with your Page on their content that they post on LinkedIn.

As a super admin of a Page, you are notified when your Page is invited to collaborate on a post. You will receive this notification only if you have enabled notifications on collaborations from your personal profile.

Important to know

We are gradually making this notification feature available and not all Page admins might have access to it at this time.

To enable collaboration on your LinkedIn Page:

  1. From your personal profile, click Me on the top of your LinkedIn Homepage.
  2. Click Settings and then Notifications.
  3. Click -> displayed for Collaborations and switch the toggle to On for the type of notification you would to receive.

To enable collaboration on your LinkedIn Page:

  1. From your personal profile, click Me on the top of your LinkedIn Homepage.
  2. Tap Settings and then tap Notifications from the left rail.
  3. Click -> displayed for Collaborations and switch the toggle to On for the type of notification you would to receive.

Important to know

As a super admin of Page, until you accept an invitation for your Page to collaborate, no one can view your Page as a collaborator.

Get access to LinkedIn Live via preferred partners

LinkedIn Live allows eligible members and Pages to broadcast live video content to a LinkedIn profile, Page, or Event. If you’d like to become a LinkedIn Live broadcaster, review the create and host LinkedIn Live: access criteria.

You cannot stream directly from LinkedIn. A streaming tool is needed to broadcast LinkedIn Lives (Video). Depending on your level of expertise with streaming, you can choose to go live using a third-party broadcast tool or a custom stream (RTMP).

The following third-party broadcast tools are our preferred partners and allow you to schedule a Live event on LinkedIn: SocialLive, Streamyard, Switcher Studio, and Restream. If you believe you meet the criteria and are using one of these broadcast tools, you can trigger a review of your profile or Page and get access instantly.

To get access to LinkedIn Live via one of our preferred partners:

  1. Log in to the third-party broadcasting tool.
  2. When prompted, connect your LinkedIn account by entering your LinkedIn credentials.
  3. Review the security authorization and if you’d like to proceed, select Allow.
  4. Follow the prompts to complete the process.
  5. You’ll be notified immediately whether or not you’re approved for LinkedIn Live access.
  6. If approved, follow the steps to set up your live stream.

If you don’t meet one or more of our criteria, we’ll not grant you access. If you’d like to be reconsidered, you can check again when you feel your status has changed.

If you have not yet selected a third-party broadcast tool, you can create an event on LinkedIn to trigger a review of your profile or Page and get access instantly. If your profile or Page is eligible, you will see the option to select LinkedIn Live in the Event format dropdown. If you don’t fulfill the criteria, you will not see LinkedIn Live in the dropdown, or the event format dropdown will be missing.

If you have any other questions related to LinkedIn Live or Events, please contact us.

Get started with boosting posts on LinkedIn

Member boosting, Page boosting, and thought leader ads allow advertisers to promote content on LinkedIn and are designed for different needs and stages of growth:

  • Member boosting - Helps individual members quickly increase visibility for a single post from their own LinkedIn profile.

  • Page boosting - Gives businesses and organizations the ability to increase their LinkedIn Page’s visibility, grow followers, or get more website clicks.

  • Thought leader ads - Helps individual members boost authentic content from real LinkedIn members with their permission.

  • Feature: Where you boost; Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile: Your own LinkedIn profile from either desktop or mobile devices; Page boosting: From a LinkedIn Page; Thought leader ads: Campaign Manager

  • Feature: Requirements to boost; Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile: You can boost your personal LinkedIn posts with a Premium Business Suite subscription. We’re also gradually releasing this feature to members without a Premium Business subscription. If you have access to this feature, you can boost your posts from your Activity tab. Click Boost on the upper-right corner of eligible posts.; Page boosting: To boost a post from your Page, you must have super or content admin permissions. To boost a post from Campaign Manager, you need super admin, content admin, or Sponsored Content poster access.; Thought leader ads: You must have super admin, content admin, or Sponsored Content Poster access on the LinkedIn Page associated with the ad account. You must also request approval from the member whose post you’d like to sponsor.

  • Feature: Content being boosted; Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile: Your own LinkedIn post; Page boosting: A LinkedIn Page post; Thought leader ads: Posts you have been given permission to sponsor from the content creator

  • Feature: Supported post types; Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile: - Single image - Video - Event - Article and newsletter - Text; Page boosting: - Single image - Video - Document - Event - Article and newsletter - Text; Thought leader ads: - Single image - Video - Event - Article and newsletter

  • Feature: Supported objectives; Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile: - Brand awareness - Engagement - Video views - Website visits; Page boosting: - Brand awareness - Engagement - Video views - Website visits - Lead generation; Thought leader ads: - Brand awareness - Engagement - Video views

Member boosting from your LinkedIn profile

Member boosting lets individual LinkedIn members promote one of their own posts to reach a wider audience. Member boosting is a good choice if you:

  • Want to increase reach on a single post quickly
  • Are promoting yourself, your expertise, or a small business
  • Prefer a simple, lightweight boosting experience
  • Don’t need advanced targeting or long-term campaign management

Keep in mind:

  • Member boosting is tied to the individual member, not a LinkedIn Page
  • It’s best for short-term or one-off promotion
  • Reporting and optimization options are more limited than Page boosting

Page boosting from a Company Page

Page boosting allows Page admins to promote posts published by a LinkedIn Page. Page boosting is a good fit if you:

  • Are promoting brand or company content
  • Manage a LinkedIn Page
  • Want more targeting and budget control
  • Plan to promote multiple posts or run ongoing promotions

Keep in mind:

  • Page boosting is managed by Page admins, so you’ll need the right permissions on the Page.
  • Boosted posts represent your brand or organization, not an individual member.
  • You’ll have more control than member boosting, but fewer options than full Campaign Manager campaigns.
  • Page boosting works best when you have clear goals, such as increasing awareness or engagement.
  • As your advertising needs grow, Page boosting makes it easier to transition into Campaign Manager without needing to start from the very beginning.

Thought leader ads

Thought leader ads help individual members boost authentic content from real LinkedIn members with their permission. Thought leader ads are a good fit if:

  • You want to boost authentic content from a real LinkedIn member, such as an employee, executive, or creator.
  • You want to amplify a strong organic post while still using advertiser tools like targeting, budget, and reporting in Campaign Manager.
  • You’re looking for a scalable way to boost member content beyond self‑serve member boosting.

Keep in mind:

  • Member permission is required before you can boost a post as a thought leader ad.
  • Not all organic posts are eligible for thought leader ads and must meet ad requirements.
  • Thought leader ads are managed by advertisers, while member boosting is done by individuals on their own posts.

Give feedback on a LinkedIn Product Page

A LinkedIn Product Page showcases an organization’s available products. Page followers and visitors can provide their feedback on your products through free-form recommendations.

LinkedIn Page admins and members can report inaccurate Product Page information, product recommendations, and highlighted customers, and give feedback on a Product Page.

When giving feedback, keep the following in mind for each Product Page component:

  • Product Page information refers to general details on the Page, such as the product name or description. It excludes product recommendations and highlighted customers.
  • Product recommendations refers to any visible details in a product recommendation left by a member.
  • Highlighted customers refers to any organization that is identified as a user of the product.

To give feedback on one of the listed Product Page components, please contact us.

Important to know

Product Pages are currently only available to Pages in the following types of industries: business-to-business (B2B) software, computer hardware, financial services, insurance, education, healthcare, and pharmaceutical. While creating a Product Page, you will need to specifically mention an industry name within these industry groups.

Guidelines for LinkedIn Live Streaming Content

Approved LinkedIn Live Video broadcasters must keep videos professional, respectful, and safe in accordance with our:

  • LinkedIn User Agreement
  • Professional Community Policies

Please use these guidelines when streaming your live videos:

  • Avoid selling or promotional streams.

  • Do not use pre-recorded content. All streams should be live and happening in real time, or you may confuse members and potentially betray their trust.

  • Live stream for at least 15 min. Shorter streams won’t give enough time to build an audience base and encourage interactions. You can share shorter videos from your homepage.

  • Avoid talking about how to use LinkedIn on LinkedIn. No meta streams.

  • Avoid sponsor logos that dominate the video. If you must use sponsor graphics, keep them small.

  • Don’t keep your audience waiting for more than one or two minutes with long “starting soon” screens.

  • Keep your content professional. All live content is publicly visible and should be appropriate for a LinkedIn audience.

  • LinkedIn Live overview

Hide content in your feed

If you see a post in your Feed that isn’t relevant to you, you can hide it to help personalize what you see. LinkedIn uses your feedback to improve your Feed experience while giving you control over the content you see.

Your Feed is personalized based on the content, people, and topics that matter to you. If you see a post that isn’t relevant or useful, you can hide it and provide feedback to help improve your Feed experience.

Different options may be available on a post depending on the type of content you’re viewing. Some options remove a single post, while others help personalize future recommendations or reduce content from a specific source.

  • If you want to..: Stop seeing a specifc post; Select…: X or Not interested (when available)
  • If you want to..: See fewer similar posts in the future; Select…: Not interested
  • If you want to..: Reduce content from a specific person, Page, or company; Select…: The available author-specific option, such as Unfollow or Hide posts from [author]

Understanding the difference between these options can help you quickly personalize your Feed and avoid seeing content that’s less relevant to you.

To hide a post:

  1. Click the More icon on the upper right of a post.
  2. Click Not interested or Hide a posts by [Name].

To hide a post:

  1. Tap the / More icon to the right of the post.
  2. Tap Not interested or Hide a posts by [Name].

After you select Not interested, the post is removed from your Feed and your feedback may be used to improve future Feed recommendations.

Notes:

  • Members won’t be notified when you hide their post.

  • If you believe the post violates LinkedIn’s Professional Community Policies, you can report it.

  • Hiding a post doesn’t report it to LinkedIn.

How to repost a post on LinkedIn

You can repost existing public posts from other members or LinkedIn Pages and add your own ideas or questions to share with your network.

You can either repost on LinkedIn or send it in a private message to specific individual(s).

You can now repost something that has already been reposted.

To repost on LinkedIn:

  1. Click Repost under the post you want to share. From the dropdown, you can:

    • Select Repost with your thoughts to repost with your comments.

    • Select Repost to repost directly without being prompted to add any comments. A repost successful confirmation message appears on the lower left of the homepage. You can click View post next to the message to view your repost.

  2. If you click Repost with your thoughts, the post pop-up window appears. Enter your comments or use “@” to mention people, companies, or schools.

  3. Click the dropdown next to your name.

  4. In the Post settings pop-up window, select who you want to share the post under Who can see your post?, and click Done.

  5. Click Post on the lower-right corner. A repost successful confirmation message appears on the lower left of the homepage.

Note: To delete the repost, click the  More icon on the upper-right corner of the repost. Select  Delete post from the dropdown. Click Delete in the Delete post? pop-up window.

To repost a repost:

  1. Click Repostunder the post you want to repost. From the dropdown, you can:

    • Select Repost with your thoughtsto repost with your comments.
    • Select Repost to repost directly without being prompted to add any comments. A repost successful confirmation message appears on the lower left of the homepage. You can click Viewnext to the message to view your repost.

  2. If you click Repost with your thoughts, the post pop-up window appears. Enter your comments or use “@” to mention people, companies, or schools.

  3. Click the dropdown next to your name.

  4. In the Post settings pop-up window, select who you want to share the post under Who can see your post?, and click Done.

  5. Click Post on the lower-right corner. A repost successful confirmation message appears on the lower left of the homepage.

    After posting, your commentary will display as the top level on the post. The level displayed below your commentary is the previous repost’s commentary. You can click on this level to see any connected previous reposts with commentary and navigate back to the original post.

Note: To delete the repost, click the  More icon on the upper-right corner of the repost. Select  Delete post from the dropdown. Click Delete in the Delete post? pop-up window.

To share a post in a private message:

  1. Click Send on the lower-right corner of the post that you want to share.
  2. In the Send [Name of author]’s Post pop-up window, type and select the name(s) of the recipient(s) under Suggested.
  3. You can also type a message in the Write a message… field.
  4. Click Send.

Note: You can view the list of people who’ve reposted your post in the [number] reposts pop-up window by clicking on the [number] reposts on the lower-right of a post. You can also click [number] comments to view the comments that have been added to the reposts. This list will not display posts that are shared privately.

Label post as brand partnership

If you share content in an exchange for value (including monetary payment, endorsements, free products or services, or other benefit), you must label the post as a brand partnership and comply with our Advertising Policies and applicable local laws. Your sponsorship or brand partnership should be clear, conspicuous, and transparent.

To label your post as a brand partnership:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage to share a post.

  2. Type the content of your post in the Start typing field.

  3. Select who you want to share the post with.

  4. Switch the toggle next to Brand partnership to On to label your post as brand partnership or Off to not label your post as brand partnership.

    After you publish the post, it will be labeled with Brand Partnership.

To label your post as a brand partnership:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar to share a post.

  2. Type the content of your post in the Start typing field.

  3. Select who you want to share the post with.

  4. Switch the toggle next to Brand partnership to On to label your post as brand partnership or Off to not label your post as brand partnership.

    After you publish the post, it will be labeled with Brand Partnership.

Notes:

  • This label is only available for Public posts. If you change the visibility setting to Connections only or Groups, the toggle will automatically be disabled until you change the visibility to Public.

  • This setting applies only to the current post and will reset to its default Off for your next post.

  • Please make sure to check any applicable laws and guidance in your location around disclosures for posts like this.

  • As part of our commitment to creating a safe and trusted experience, and to comply with the law, posts labeled as brand partnerships will be publicly searchable by members and visitors.

Like, unlike, and react to posts or comments

If you’re on desktop, move your cursor over the Like icon to select your reaction to a post or comment. To react to a post or a comment from a mobile device, tap and hold the Like icon.

Posts and comments that you like or react to will be shared with your network, and they’ll be informed of the reaction you chose. To undo this action, move your cursor over the Like icon or the reaction you chose, and click or tap it again.

The duration for activities that remain in your own Activity feed may change. Your complete history of liked and unliked content may not be accessible to you.

LinkedIn Feed - Overview

LinkedIn focuses on providing a relevant feed that encourages members to engage with people and topics they value. Our goal is to provide each professional with relevant content. In particular, your LinkedIn feed contains insights from your network, companies you follow, sponsored content, and other posts that we believe you may be interested in.

Check out some additional information to help you start managing your feed.

You may see recommended content with labels such as Trending, Recommended for you, or Popular in your feed. This recommended content is determined by LinkedIn’s algorithms and editorial team. We incorporate signals on and off LinkedIn designed to find the right stories, articles, videos, and more to make professionals better at what they do.

You may see content about connections or organizations you follow with labels such as Latest News or Mentioned in the News in your feed. This content is derived from an automated tool that looks for online news articles and matches names in the articles with organizations and LinkedIn members. Learn more about Mentioned in the News.

Unlike an organization’s own updates from its LinkedIn Page, the Latest News articles are not intended to represent the organization or its point of view. In addition to the Mentioned in the News or Latest News label, you can identify such articles by the LinkedIn news icon that appears next to the article.

Sponsored Content allows organizations to raise awareness, build relationships, and drive quality leads through their LinkedIn Page updates. Sponsored Content is shown to LinkedIn members who follow the sponsoring organization on LinkedIn, and may also be shown to members who fit the audience criteria of the advertiser. However, most of your updates will continue to be organic information from your network.

There are multiple ways to customize and manage the content that appears in your feed. You can follow, unfollow, or mute people, companies, and hashtags, hide content in your feed that you don’t want to see, and report inappropriate content. Check out additional information on customizing your feed.

LinkedIn Live broadcaster features

LinkedIn Live video broadcasting is only available to members who meet the access criteria to create and host LinkedIn Lives. Tigger a review of your Page or Profile to check if you fulfill the criteria.

Important to know

Availability of these features vary depending on the tool you’re using to go live. All features are available on Preferred Partners: Restream, Socialive, StreamYard, or Switcher Studio. For all others, check the respective tool.

You can schedule your live video in advance and promote it both on and off LinkedIn.

LinkedIn Live allows eligible members and organizations to broadcast live video content to LinkedIn Page followers, profile connections, or LinkedIn Events attendees. It’s a great way to ensure your attendees can connect with each other and have conversations before, during, and after the event in a dedicated space.

If you’re using one of the third-party streaming tools, sign in to your LinkedIn account. You’ll see the option to stream from your profile, your Page, or into an Event. Select Event to see all the upcoming events you manage. Learn more about organizing a LinkedIn Event.

Note: You can only choose one destination for your stream. You can’t simultaneously stream into an event and into your profile or Page.

Before livestreaming on LinkedIn Live, you can create a test stream to make sure everything is right. Steps to set up a test stream vary depending on the tool you’re using. Refer to the guidance from your tool.

Real-time auto captions are currently supported for livestreams created through LinkedIn’s API partners with audio in English. Enabling auto captions for your video will make it more accessible to a broader audience. Captions enabled for a livestream will continue through post-live playback.

You must enable auto captions on your broadcast tool before going live. You can then enable or disable the captions on the LinkedIn platform while you’re live or after the stream ends by clicking on Edit video on the upper right of your stream. You won’t have the option to enable captioning after going live. Your live video won’t include auto captions in replay mode if you disabled them during the stream.

If auto captions are enabled on a live stream with pass-through closed captioning, the player will only display the auto captions.

Captions are always shown at the bottom of the screen. Do not position any headings, banners or stickers at the bottom of the screen to avoid overlap with the captions.

For Pages admins broadcasting on behalf of a Page, you have the ability to respond to comments within a livestream as the Page, rather than with your profile. To do this, enter into your Admin View and ensure you are in the View as Admin setting (this should be the default setting). Then navigate to your video that is live currently, click into it and go into theater mode (if on mobile). You can then start commenting on behalf of your Page.

As a broadcaster or admin for a broadcasting Page, you can moderate the chat during your live stream by deleting, reporting, or muting specific comments or commenters. If you see an unwanted comment, you can mute the commenter by clicking the More icon and selecting Mute. By muting a commenter, you’re muting their ability to react or comment on that specific live video and any replays of that video. This doesn’t prevent the commenter from reacting or commenting on other live videos.

If you have a ‘starting soon’ screen at the beginning of your stream or if you’ve spent a few minutes testing audio/video prior to getting started, you can choose to trim the beginning or end of your live video once recording is available.

You can trim recordings or scheduled Live Events; however, this feature is not available if you go live spontaneously.

To trim the video:

  1. Go to the Event Details page of your event.

  2. In the Your event recording is available section, click Edit.

    • The Edit your video pop-up window appears.

  3. On the timeline, move the start point and end points to the section you want to keep.

  4. Click Trim.

You’ll see a Trim processing message. The updated recording will be available shortly.

If you want to undo your trim, click ** Revert to original** on the Edit your video pop-up window.

As an event organizer, you can download the event recording from the Event Details page after the event ends.

If you have any questions related to LinkedIn Live Video, please contact us.

LinkedIn Live Overview

Important to know

As of June 22, 2026, the ability to go live spontaneously is no longer available. All events must be scheduled ahead of time. You can still go live on short notice by scheduling your event minutes before going live to preserve the same real-time, in-the-moment experience. Learn more about how to create a LinkedIn Event or Schedule from a third-party broadcast tool.

LinkedIn Live allows eligible members and Pages to broadcast live video content to a LinkedIn profile, LinkedIn Page, or Event. If you’d like to become a LinkedIn Live broadcaster, review the create and host LinkedIn Live: access criteria.

You can’t stream directly from LinkedIn; you’ll need a streaming tool to broadcast LinkedIn Lives (Video). The right tool depends on your level of expertise with streaming:

  • New broadcasters: Use a third-party broadcast tool. Choose one of our five preferred partners (Restream, Socialive, StreamYard, or Switcher Studio) or one of your supported partners.
  • Advanced broadcasters or professional producers: Connect directly to any streaming software or encoder using a custom stream (RTMP Ingest). Go live from your desktop browser by visiting the LinkedIn custom stream page. You can use the tool of your choice (For example OBS, Elemental, Zoom, etc.) or your own production workflow for streaming.

With either option, you can go live spontaneously or schedule your live stream in advance. We recommend scheduling your live stream in advance to promote it on or off LinkedIn.

LinkedIn Live troubleshooting

If you’re an eligible LinkedIn Live Video broadcaster and are having trouble setting up or live streaming, try the following troubleshooting recommendations:

  1. Check Your Permissions: LinkedIn Live Video broadcasting is available only to members who meet the access criteria to create and host LinkedIn Lives. Trigger a review of your Page or Profile to check if you meet the eligibility criteria.

    If you encounter error messages in your broadcast tool, check the following:

    • Access for Pages and personal profiles is separate. Try to authenticate each profile and Page individually.
    • For LinkedIn Pages, only the Page admins can stream on behalf of the Page. Page Admins cannot stream from their personal profile.
    • If you have broadcasted before but not recently, disconnect LinkedIn from your broadcast tool and reconnect. This refreshes your authentication token.

  2. Check for firewalls or server errors: Talk to your network administrator to confirm that the following ports are open:

    • TCP port 1935 + 1936
    • TCP port 2935 + 2936

  3. Check for issues with third-party broadcasting tool: If you use a third-party broadcasting tool, reach out directly to their support teams:

    • Restream.io: Visit Restream’s help center article, or chat with a support representative via Restream support center.
    • Socialive: Visit the Socialive support center, or contact your Socialive representative via email.
    • StreamYard: Open a request ticket through the StreamYard help center.
    • Switcher Studio: Contact support through their website or email, or visit the Switcher user group.
    • All other third-party broadcasting tools: Visit the tool’s help center and reach out to its support team directly

  4. Ensure the broadcast meets the guidelines for encoder settings.

Troubleshooting when going live with RTMP

If you’re going live using RTMP and encounter issues, check the following:

  • The RTMPS ports should be 2935 and 2936.

  • If your stream fails to process, use the Baseline video profile instead of High or Main. Higher profiles can introduce B-frames and timestamp issues that prevent successful ingest.

  • Each region is allocated a certain bandwidth and sometimes regions run out of available bandwidth. If this happens, try selecting the next closest region.

  • You’ll get the RTMP URL and Stream Key one hour before your scheduled start time. We recommend creating them about 15 minutes before you go live. You can go live in preview mode 10 minutes before your scheduled time.

  • All articles about going live with RTMP

If the steps above don’t resolve your issue, submit a LinkedIn Live Video case with LinkedIn help. To expedite the troubleshooting process, include required screenshots and logs when submitting your case.

LinkedIn Live Video encoder settings

For eligible LinkedIn Live Video broadcasters, it’s important to choose a reliable streaming quality based on your Internet connection. We recommend that you run a speed test to ensure that you’re getting at least 10 Mbps upload speed.

Encoder settings for cloud services (Restream, Vimeo Live, Easy Live, and Switchboard)

Use the following recommended settings when ingesting from your encoder:

  • Setting: Aspect Ratio; Recommended value: 16:9
  • Setting: Resolution; Recommended value: 720p Recommended; 1080p Maximum
  • Setting: Frame Rate; Recommended value: 30 fps
  • Setting: Key Frame; Recommended value: Every 2 seconds (60 frames @ 30 fps)
  • Setting: Video Bitrate; Recommended value: 3.5 Mbps Recommended; 6 Mbps Maximum
  • Setting: Audio Bitrate; Recommended value: 128 Kbps
  • Setting: Audio Sample Rate; Recommended value: 48 KHz
  • Setting: Encoding; Recommended value: H.264 video, AAC audio
  • Setting: Protocol; Recommended value: RTMP/RTMPS

Here’s a tip

If your stream fails to process, check your encoder’s video profile. Use the Baseline profile instead of High or Main. Higher profiles can introduce B-frames and timestamp issues that prevent successful ingest.

LinkedIn Newsletter access criteria

A newsletter is a set of regularly published articles on LinkedIn, typically about a specific topic. You can create a newsletter as yourself or as a LinkedIn Page.

Members

All LinkedIn members have access to create a newsletter on LinkedIn.

Pages

Pages must meet the following criteria to create a newsletter:

  • Audience base Pages with more than 150 followers and/or connections are eligible to be evaluated for LinkedIn Newsletters access.
  • Recent shares of original content (any type) We look for Pages who have experience creating original content on LinkedIn (For example, creating posts with text, images, or videos, publishing articles, etc.) to evaluate if they will be able to make the most of LinkedIn Newsletters.
  • A history of abiding by our Professional Community Policies We want to ensure our members have a safe, trusted, and professional experience on LinkedIn, as defined by our Professional Community Policies. Only Pages and their admins that have a good standing record will be considered for Newsletters access.

LinkedIn Newsletters

All LinkedIn members have the ability to create a newsletter about their expertise and interests. Follow the instructions below to create your newsletter.

To create a newsletter:

  1. Click Write article in the share box near the top of your homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right.

    • You can also click the ** Dropdown** next to your name on the upper left to choose if you want to publish an article as yourself (personal profile), Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, or if you want to publish it as an Individual article or to a newsletter (if applicable).

  3. If you have access to newsletters, you’ll see theCreate newsletteroption here.

  4. Fill all the required information in the Create a newsletter pop-up window and click Done.

You can leverage newsletters on LinkedIn to talk about a professional topic you’re passionate about on a regular basis. LinkedIn members can subscribe to your newsletter to be notified about new articles you publish, allowing you to build and grow a regularly engaged audience.

Starting a newsletter on LinkedIn means you’ll engage your audience from the minute you publish. LinkedIn makes it easy to invite all your connections or followers to subscribe when you create a newsletter. Also, after publishing each newsletter edition, push, in-app, and email notifications are sent to all your subscribers to help drive views. You’ll get real-time feedback and comments from your readers, and you can understand how your content is doing with analytics.

When a member starts following another member or a page with newsletter, a notification inviting them to subscribe to the newsletter is automatically sent.

All LinkedIn members can discover, read, and share LinkedIn newsletters. Any LinkedIn member can subscribe to a newsletter. Newsletters you’ve subscribed to will be visible to others and on your profile as well, unless you unsubscribe. The newsletter author can see your name, profile photo, job title, and headline as they appear on your LinkedIn profile, based on your settings. When you subscribe to a newsletter, you also start following the newsletter author.

LinkedIn Page posts FAQ

As a Page super admin or content admin, you can use LinkedIn Page posts to directly engage with viewers and followers of your Page.

Here’s a tip

Pages that post weekly have over five times more followers that grow seven times faster than Pages that post monthly.

Create a Page post

To create a post, you must be a super or content Page admin.

You can post text, images, videos, and documents to engage with your Page’s followers. You can post and repost information like organization news, promotions, relevant industry articles, member posts that mention your organization, videos, and employee recognition. A variety of formats are supported, including text, URLs, images, documents, YouTube videos, and video files.

Yes, you can import posts from your external sources like your organization’s website, blogs, YouTube channels, and other RSS supported sources directly to your Page. Content sharing can help you efficiently post your content from your external web sources to your LinkedIn Page and grow and engage your followers. You’ll need to be a super or content Page admin to set up content sharing.

Super admins and content admins can edit Page posts they’ve sponsored from the post. The associated ad will go through the review process again, and the status will be changed from paused to active. The original version of the ad might be visible to your Page followers while it goes through the review process again.

You must have access to the ad account associated with the Sponsored Content to edit the post.

Pages that are associated with at least one enterprise ad account have Sponsored Content editing capabilities regardless of follower and employee count.

Deleting a post from your LinkedIn Page can have several implications:

  • Not Reversible – When you delete a post from your LinkedIn page, it is permanently removed and won’t be visible to your followers or anyone visiting your Page. This action cannot be undone. But the deleted post might still appear in other places on LinkedIn if a member has the direct URL to the post.
  • Loss of Engagement - Any likes, comments, or shares associated with the post will be lost. This means that any interaction or engagement generated by the post will be removed.
  • Impact on Analytics - Metrics and insights related to the post, such as views, clicks, and engagement rates, will no longer be available. This can affect your overall analytics and understanding of your audience’s preferences.
