Following are some of the reasons why you may not be able to edit a boosted post:

  • You need Super admin, Content admin, or Sponsored Content admin access to the Page to edit a boosted post. If you don’t have the right admin access, ask another admin to update your permissions or to make the edit to the boosted post.
  • Your Page must have an adequate number of employees associated with it or must have an adequate number of followers.
  • Boosted video posts can’t be edited after they’re live. If you need to make changes, you could try duplicating the video and then edit it, and resubmit your ad creative for an ad review.
  • Posts that are rejected or restricted can’t be edited. Learn more about the guidelines for ad reviews and approvals.

LinkedIn Polls

The LinkedIn Polls feature helps you engage with other members by asking them for their perspectives about various topics. Polls help you understand trends and opinions and can be a great conversation starter.

The poll author can select the visibility of the poll. The default visibility option is set to Anyone. Duration of poll can be one day, three days, one week or two weeks. The author of the poll will be able to view who voted and how each person voted. In addition, the author will be able to view aggregate results displayed in a percentage format and the number of votes per option. When a poll is created by a LinkedIn Page, all Admins of that Page will be able to see who voted and how each person voted.

Notes:

  • Poll authors may not ask for political opinions, health status, or other sensitive data.

  • Poll authors must adhere to LinkedIn’s standard terms, including our “Do’s and Don’ts” and Professional Community Policies.

  • You may also see LinkedIn Brand Surveys in your LinkedIn feed, messaging, or other placements. While brand surveys resemble LinkedIn Polls, personal information is not shared with the sponsoring advertiser when answers are submitted.

  • Visibility of shared posts

  • Learn more about the LinkedIn Professional Community Policies

LinkedIn Polls – FAQ

The LinkedIn Polls feature helps you engage with other members by asking them for their perspectives about various topics.

Check out some of the frequently asked questions about the LinkedIn Polls feature.

How you vote is visible to the author of the poll (i.e. the person or organization who posts the poll). With regard to polls created by an organization via a LinkedIn Page, how you vote is visible to admins of that Page. Though polls will be available for Groups, the ability to view who voted will not be available for all admins of a Group. When a poll is created in a LinkedIn Group, only the poll author can view these results. While LinkedIn only shares how you vote with the poll author, we cannot guarantee that a poll author will not disclose your vote to others.

Anyone eligible to see the post can see the total aggregate responses in a percentage format after the poll is closed. Voters will be able to see the total aggregate responses in a percentage format once they vote. Poll authors can see the total aggregate results displayed in a percentage format and the number of votes per option.

No, voting does not show the poll on the Activity section of your profile.

Yes, polls can be created on mobile and desktop. Learn more about creating a LinkedIn Poll.

The number of options depends on the device you’re using:

  • On desktop and Android app, you can add up to four options.
  • On iOS app, you can add up to five options.

A member can submit only one vote on a poll at a time. If a member removes the vote before the poll is closed, they can vote again provided the poll has not closed.

Yes, poll questions are limited to a maximum 140 characters and options are limited to a maximum of 30 characters.

Yes, super admins of LinkedIn Pages can create polls.

No, a poll can’t be edited once it’s created. A poll can be deleted after it is created.

No, a poll can’t be reopened once it’s closed.

Yes, a LinkedIn Page super admin may vote on behalf of a LinkedIn Page.

Yes, the author of the poll can vote and remove their own vote on their own poll.

Poll voters can change or remove their votes up until the close of the poll by clicking/tapping Undo on the poll. After a poll is closed, voters can remove their votes by clicking/tapping Remove vote on the poll. You may find the poll you voted for by going to the poll author’s Activity section of their profile.

Yes, the author will be notified in the app about the first vote and subsequent votes. Vote notifications can be turned off via the Responses to your posts, comments and polls setting.

Your connections will get notified that you created a poll.

Poll authors may not ask for sensitive data (nor ask for data for the purpose of inferring sensitive data). Sensitive data includes, for example, race, ethnic origin, religious, political, or philosophical beliefs, sexual orientation or lifestyle, physical and mental health, trade union membership or membership in a religious or political organization, or precise geolocation and anything else defined as such by law (such as the GDPR).

As always, poll authors need to adhere to LinkedIn’s standard terms, including our “Do’s and Don’ts” and Professional Community Policies.

Yes, learn more about reporting inappropriate or offensive polls.

LinkedIn Polls are created by both members and Page super admins to engage with their LinkedIn communities on various topics.

LinkedIn Brand Surveys are created by companies and organizations to better understand how their brand resonates on LinkedIn. Personal information is not shared with the sponsoring advertiser when answers are submitted to brand surveys. Learn more about brand surveys.

Learn more about creating a LinkedIn Poll.

Manage a newsletter on LinkedIn

As a newsletter author, you get to write about a professional topic you care about on a regular basis. Members can subscribe to your newsletter to receive updates when you publish something new. The most engaging newsletters specifically address a unique topic consistently enough that subscribers look forward to the next article.

Anyone can discover, read, and share your LinkedIn Newsletter. LinkedIn members can also subscribe to it.

You can create a newsletter as yourself or as a LinkedIn Page.

Who can use this feature?

Members who meet the newsletter access criteria will be able to create a newsletter.

To create a newsletter on LinkedIn:

Important to know

Authors can create up to five newsletters at a time. After deleting or creating a newsletter, you must wait two weeks before creating a new one.

  1. Click Write article at the top of the homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right and select Create newsletter.

    • Click the dropdown next to your name on the upper left to choose if you want to publish an article as yourself (personal profile), Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, or if you want to publish it as an Individual article or to a newsletter (if applicable).

  3. Add a Newsletter title, Newsletter description, How often do you want to publish?, and an image or logo (optional) for your newsletter and click Done.

    • Avoid adding emojis into the title of your newsletter

  4. Once you have created a newsletter, you’ll see your Newsletter title near the upper right corner of the page. If you don’t see the newsletter title, click on the Manage dropdown menu and select the newsletter you want to write in.

  5. You can now write the first article for your newsletter.

  6. Once the article is ready to be published, click Next on the upper right.

Important to know

By default, your connections and followers will be invited by notification to subscribe to your newsletter once the first article of your newsletter has been successfully published. Subscribing means they’ll receive a notification or email each time you write a new newsletter edition. 7. Click Publish.

  • A window will pop up for you to add more context. You can comment on what this specific newsletter edition is about, ask questions of your readers, and use ’**@**’ to mention people or LinkedIn Page . When you click Post, your newsletter will also be shared in the feed.
  • Once you publish your first article, a page for your newsletter is automatically created with an overview of your newsletter, your profile information, and a list of the articles in the newsletter. You can use your newsletter page to provide a preview of your newsletter and share it on or off LinkedIn to increase your reach. You do not have to be logged in to view the page but members must log in to subscribe or share it on LinkedIn.
  • Share your newsletter edition on your other social channels to drive more engagement across your entire audience.

To publish a new article in your newsletter:

  1. Click Write article at the top of the homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. You’ll see the title of your newsletter next to your name on the upper left.

    • If you don’t see the newsletter title, click on the dropdown menu next to your name and select the newsletter you want to write in.

  3. Once the article is ready to be published, click Nextnear the upper right.

  4. Click Publish.

To edit or delete a Newsletter:

  1. Click  Write article at the top of the homepage. This takes you to the publishing tool.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click on the Manage dropdown to select the newsletter you want to delete from the Newsletter dropdown list.

  3. From here, you can:

    • Edit Newsletter: Click  Editbelow your name. In the pop-up window that appears, you can edit the Newsletter title, Newsletter description, How often do you want to publish?, and image/logo (if added).
    • Delete Newsletter: Click the More icon on the right of the newsletter’s name, then select Delete newsletter from the dropdown and confirm Delete.

Manage comments on articles

Members can comment on published articles that have enabled comments. Comments are a great way for members to engage with other professionals on topics that matter the most to them. Friendly discussions and respectful debates are encouraged.

Comments on published articles are visible to other members and are associated with your professional identity. They can be viewed by your network and other individuals on the web. Some published articles may have comments disabled. You can choose to enable or disable comments while publishing an article.

To manage comments before publishing an article:

  1. Click Next on the upper right after writing your article.

  2. Click the Dropdown next to your name on the pop-up window.

  3. Click on Comment control, from here you can:

    • Anyone: Select Anyone to allow anyone who may view to comment.
    • Connections only: Select Connections only to allow only connections to comment
    • No one: Select No one to disable comments

You can also disable comments on articles you’ve previously published. Disabling comments will delete all existing comments.

To disable comments on previous articles:

  1. Locate your article from your recent activity or from the publishing tool.
  2. Click the Comments settings icon below your article.
  3. Select No One to disable comments and then click Save Changes.

To re-enable comments, navigate to Comments settings and select Anyone or Connections only and Save Changes. If you had previously disabled comments, re-enabling comments will not bring back any comments that were deleted.

Here’s a tip

The ability to disable comments on an article isn’t available on the LinkedIn mobile app.

To flag and hide abusive or offensive comments made on your own articles:

  1. Click the More icon on the top right of a comment.
  2. Click Report to report the comment.
  3. In the Report this comment pop-up window, select a reason and follow prompts to report the comment.

Manage LinkedIn Trending Employee Content hashtags

Populating LinkedIn Trending Employee Content begins with activating hashtags on your Life or What We Do Page. Members then apply these hashtags to their video and photo posts. The same hashtags can be used across multiple Life or What We Do Pages but must be activated on each Page.

Here’s a tip

Make sure the Trending Employee Content is on to enable set hashtags.

To activate a hashtag:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.

  2. Click Life or What we do in the left menu.

  3. On the correct targeted page, scroll down to the Trending employee content section.

  4. Click Add a hashtag.

  5. Enter the hashtag name in the Search hashtag field. Capitalization doesn’t impact what content is populated. Example: #XYZ is equal to #xyz.

    • You can add up to 3 hashtags.
    • To remove a hashtag, click the next to the hashtag name

  6. Click Save on the top right of the page.

  7. Open the page edited for the hashtag, and scroll to the Trending Employee Content section to see which posts are eligible.

Important to know

As a super admin of the Page who is adding or deleting hashtags, after you click Save or Delete, you must return to the targeted Page after about 6 hours to verify that the changes are live.

Boolean logic can be used to customize your Trending Employee Content hashtags. For example, if you want hashtags customized for your sales Life Page at company XYZ, enter #XYZlife OR #Saleslife.

Manage your LinkedIn feed preferences

Improve your LinkedIn feed by discovering new content and customizing your feed preferences. You can follow, unfollow, or mute people and companies for topics you’re interested in from desktop experience and the LinkedIn mobile app.

Note: All edits to your feed preferences made on the LinkedIn mobile app will be applicable on the desktop experience as well.

To manage your feed preferences:

  1. Click the My Network icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click Following & followers on the left pane under Manage my Network.

    • You will also find a list of recommended sources to follow on this page.

  3. In the [Your Name]’s Network page, you can view the following tabs:

    • Following - This is a list of people or companies you currently follow. Click Following to the right of the person or company to stop seeing content in your feed from that source. In the Unfollow dialog that appears, click Unfollow. The displayed text will change back to Follow.
    • Followers - This is a list of people who currently follow you.

Notes:

  • If you regularly post content that is engaging and professionally relevant, we may recommend you to other members in their feed preferences as someone to follow.

  • If a member chooses to follow you, you won’t be connected but they may see any posts or articles that you share publicly in their feed.

  • Your followers won’t be able to see anything that you share to your connections only. If you want to see who’s following you, check out your list of followers.

Manage, share, or duplicate LinkedIn article drafts

Your article is automatically saved as a draft as soon as you start writing. You can access your saved draft at any time to edit, publish, or delete it.

You can share drafts of your articles with other members to get feedback on the content, before sharing it on LinkedIn. The draft preview is public and can be shared by copying the current URL.

You can also duplicate drafts to quickly create a copy of the existing page, if you’d like to publish an article in the same format.

Important to know

Article formatting may appear differently after publishing. This feature isn’t available on LinkedIn mobile app.

To manage saved drafts of your articles:

  1. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right of the publishing tool and select Drafts.

  2. From the Drafts section in the Articles pop-up window, you can:

    • Click on the article to continue working on it
    • Click on the More icon on the right to ** Edit** or ** Delete** the article.

To share or duplicate a draft of the article you’re currently writing:

  1. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right of the publishing tool and select Preview.

    • Click Duplicate as draft to create a draft copy of the article (opens up in a new page).

  2. Click Share draft near the upper right of the publishing tool and click Copy from the Share draft pop-up

    • Alternatively, you can copy the current URL link to share the draft.

    Note: Members can view the draft only when they’re logged into LinkedIn.

To share or duplicate a previously saved draft:

  1. Click  Write article at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right of the publishing tool and select Drafts.

  3. From the Articles pop-up window, click on the draft article (draft tab selected by default) you’d like to share.

    • The article opens up in the publishing tool.

  4. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right of the publishing tool and select Preview.

    • Click Duplicate as draftto create a draft copy of the article (opens up in a new page).

  5. Click Share draft near the upper right of the publishing tool.

  6. From the Share draft pop-up window, click Copy.

  7. Share the URL with the members you want to receive feedback from.

Mention people in your posts

Mentioning a connection or other members encourages engagement with your posts and comments. Connections or other members mentioned get notified about the post or comment. A post or comment is associated with a connection’s or other member’s profile. Viewers can click on a connection or other member’s name to navigate to their profiles.

Note: LinkedIn members don’t need to be your connection in order to mention you or be mentioned by you.

To mention someone in a post:

  1. From your LinkedIn homepage, click Start a post or click Comment at the bottom of someone else’s post.

  2. Type “@” and then begin typing a name. The type-ahead feature predicts related names as you type your keywords.

    Note: If you are trying to mention someone with a common name, type their company in addition to their name, for example, ‘Jane Doe LinkedIn’.

  3. Click the name of the person or people you want to mention from the list and continue typing your message.

  4. Click Post.

To mention someone in a post:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar.

  2. Tap the At icon from your keyboard. The type-ahead feature predicts related names as you type your keywords.

    Note: If you are trying to mention someone with a common name, type their company in addition to their name, for example, ‘Jane Doe LinkedIn’.

  3. Tap the name of the person or people you want to mention from the list and continue typing your message.

  4. Tap Post.

After you select someone from the list and finish your post, that person will receive email and app notifications of the mention.

Notes:

  • Some members might have their setting turned off for mentions. In this case, you will be notified that the member can’t be mentioned.

  • You can edit your posts and comments to add a mention.

  • In an effort to keep LinkedIn safe and professional, we may limit your ability to mention members you’re not connected with.

Newsletter Page on LinkedIn

A newsletter is a set of regularly published articles on LinkedIn, typically about a specific topic. You can make use of this feature to talk about a professional topic that interests you. Each newsletter on LinkedIn has its own page, a place where members can learn about the newsletter and its author, see past editions, and subscribe to or share the newsletter.

Authors of newsletters can use their newsletter page to provide a preview of their newsletter and share it on or off LinkedIn. You don’t have to be logged in to visit the page, but you must log in to subscribe to the newsletter or share it on LinkedIn.

If you create a newsletter as a LinkedIn Page, your newsletter page is separate from your LinkedIn Page.

There are several ways to get to a newsletter page:

  • Clicking on a newsletter you see in the LinkedIn feed or in a LinkedIn message
  • Clicking on the name of a newsletter on an individual newsletter article
  • Clicking on a newsletter recommendation in the My Network tab
  • Clicking on a newsletter you’re subscribed to in the Manage my network section of the My Network tab.
  • Clicking on a Newsletters from the Interests section of a profile

A newsletter page is automatically created when you create a newsletter. If you have an existing newsletter, your newsletter page already exists.

Post and share updates

You can create a post and share updates using the share box at the top of your LinkedIn homepage. The character limit for a post is 3,000 characters.

If you’re a super or content admin of one or more LinkedIn Pages, you can share an update directly from your LinkedIn homepage.

Note:

  • Use Start a post from the main share box on the LinkedIn desktop experience to view additional sharing options.
  • Post suggestions are displayed below the pop-up window that appears when you click Start a post. Click a suggestion, select an option, and follow the prompts to create a post.

To create a post from your homepage:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click the name dropdown and select your post settings:

    • Who can see your post? Select Anyone, Connections only, or Group.
    • Who can comment on your post? Select Anyone, Connections only, or Off.
    • Brand Partnership – Turn the toggle on to label your post as a brand partnership.

  3. (Optional) On the What do you want to talk about? screen, use these icons to enhance your post:

    • Emoji Face icon to add emojis
    • ** Add media** icon to add a photo or video
    • ** Calendar** icon to create an event
    • ** Celebrate** icon to celebrate an occasion
    • Plus icon to view more options:
    • ** Briefcase** icon to share that you’re hiring
    • ** Poll** icon to create a poll
    • ** Document** icon to add a document
    • ** Person Tag** to find an expert

  4. (Optional) Click the ** Clock** icon to schedule your post to go live at a specific date and time.

  5. Click Post.

To create a post from your homepage:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar to create a post.

  2. Tap the Anyone dropdown beside your profile photo. Select your post settings:

    • Who can see your post? - Select Anyone, Connections only, or Group.
    • Comment control - Select Anyone, Connections only, or Off.
    • Brand Partnership - Turn on the toggle to label your post as a brand partnership.

    Note: If you manage a Page, tap your name and choose whether to post as your profile or the Page.

  3. In the Share your thoughts… screen, type your content.

  4. Tap the ** Media** icon to add a photo or video.

  5. Tap the Plus icon to view more options.

  6. Tap the following:

    • Media to add a photo or video
    • Event to create an event
    • Celebration to celebrate an occasion or milestone
    • Job to share that you’re hiring
    • Poll to create a poll
    • Document to add a document

  7. Tap the  Clock icon to schedule your post to go live at a specific date and time.

  8. Tap Post.

If your post exceeds 3000 characters, you can instead write an article using LinkedIn’s Publishing Platform.

Publish articles or newsletter editions as your LinkedIn Page

As a super or content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you can write and publish an article as the Page or as yourself. The article can be published individually or as an edition of a newsletter.

To publish an article or newsletter edition as your Page:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Click Newsletters in the left menu.

  3. Click the Write article button at the bottom.

  4. Click your name in the upper-left corner and select the correct Page to write an individual article or newsletter to write an edition.

  5. Click the Upload from computer button to upload a cover image. We recommend uploading an image that’s 1920 x 1080 pixels.

    • Click the Remove cover icon to delete the image.

  6. Optional: Once the image is uploaded, click the Add credit and caption field below the image and enter your text. For videos, you can add captions and select a thumbnail image.

  7. Click Title and enter your article title.

  8. Click Write here at the end of the page and enter your article text and use the formatting toolbar at the top to adjust your text.

    • Click the image icon to embed an image, video, slides, links, and snippet. You can also @mention another member or a LinkedIn page,  which links their profile or a Page in the article. The mentioned member or Page will be notified.
    • You can’t embed other LinkedIn articles for privacy reasons.

  9. Optional: Click the Manage button in the upper-right corner to use several drafting options for your article:

    • To create a copy of your draft, select Duplicate as draft.
    • To share a preview of your article, select Preview. Click the Share draft button in the upper-right corner to generate a URL that you can share.
    • Select SEO settings to adjust the title and description of your article.

  10. Click Next.

  11. Optional: To determine who can comment on your post, click your Page name in the upper-left corner and click Comment Control. The default setting is Anyone.

  12. At the top of the preview, enter a description of the post.

    • Optional: Click the  ** Emoji** icon under the image to add emojis to your description.

  13. Optional: Click the  Clock icon to schedule publishing for a later date and time. You can also view other scheduled posts.

  14. Click the Publish button.

After you publish your newsletter, you can click the Share button to share the article or edition with your personal network, generate a shareable subscribe link URL, or generate a subscribe button to embed on a website.

React or comment on posts as your organization’s LinkedIn Page

You can react to or comment on posts in your LinkedIn feed as your organization’s LinkedIn Page.

You must be a super admin or content admin to react to or comment on posts as your organization’s Page. You can only react to or comment on public posts that you find in your feed or via search.

By reacting to or commenting on posts as your organization’s Page, you can improve the visibility of your Page as your reactions and comments are visible to your Page followers. This form of engagement helps your organization build and foster better brand presence on LinkedIn which could influence and improve your Page followers.

As a LinkedIn Page, to optimize your Page’s visibility, and the number of comments your Page can make on a post, we recommend that you verify your Page (if eligible), and that all admins for your Page complete workplace verification using your organization’s official email address.

Important to know

To keep LinkedIn safe and professional, we may limit how many comments a member or a LinkedIn Page can make in a certain time period. Similarly, if we detect excessive comment creation or use of an automation tool, we may limit the visibility of those comments.

To react to a post or comment as your organization’s Page:

  1. Find the correct post, either from your LinkedIn feed or from the search bar at the top of the page.

  2. In the lower-left corner of the post, click the dropdown icon next to your profile picture.

    [Image: React or comment as LinkedIn Page]

  3. Select the correct Page and click Save.

  4. React to the post or leave a comment on the post.

To react to a post or comment as your organization’s Page:

  1. Find the correct post, either from your LinkedIn feed or from the search bar at the top of the page.
  2. In the lower-left corner of the post, tap the dropdown icon next to your profile picture.
  3. Select the correct Page.
  4. React to the post or leave a comment on the post.

Recent Changes to LinkedIn Live and Events

At LinkedIn, we’re always working to elevate our member experience. We constantly evaluate our portfolio to make sure that the solutions we offer meet the needs of our audience. With this in mind, we brought together parts of the LinkedIn Live and Events experiences to enhance your virtual events on LinkedIn.

  1. All new events created on LinkedIn are now fully public: Your event is now discoverable by search, and anyone, attendees and non-attendees, can view your content during and after the Event.

    Important Notes:

    • Events scheduled before this change: If you have a private event already created on LinkedIn, it will be unaffected. However, you may not be able to go Live to this private event, as we are removing the ability to go Live to attendees only. Consider looking into alternative streaming methods for your upcoming private events.

  2. For members and Pages with LinkedIn Live access, you can now choose LinkedIn Live as an Event format. To host your event using LinkedIn Live, you can select LinkedIn Live in the event format dropdown when creating an event. This live event will automatically show up in the streaming tool of your choice (preferred partners only, including Streamyard, Restream, Socialive, and Switcher). Similarly, when you schedule a LinkedIn Live event from one of our preferred partners, it will automatically show up on your LinkedIn Page or feed. This change combines the discovery benefits of LinkedIn Events with the viral reach and engagement of LinkedIn Live.

    Timing: This change is now available to all members with LinkedIn Live access.

  3. For Pages with LinkedIn Live access, you can add a registration form to your Live Event. If you are hosting from your LinkedIn Page, you can easily add a registration form with up to 6 fields to your Live Event while creating it on LinkedIn. This gates your event and collects attendee registrations before, during, and after the event. You can download registration information at any time or sync it with a CRM platform of your choice using Zapier.

    Timing: This change is now available to all Pages with LinkedIn Live access.

  4. Live Event will now behave like any LinkedIn Feed post. We are removing the dedicated Event feed to post event-related content (which was earlier visible to attendees only). When you create an event, an event post is created on the LinkedIn feed. You can leverage the comments section of the event post to communicate with attendees and LinkedIn members before, during, or after the event. Your event post will get the same reach and discovery benefits as any LinkedIn Feed post.

    Important Notes:

    • Timing: This change is now available to all Pages with LinkedIn Live access.
    • Notifications: As Events do not have dedicated feed, organizers can no longer send a notification by recommending posts to their attendees. However, you can always communicate with attendees who are your connections via LinkedIn messages and with attendees who are not your connections via InMail.

  5. Your Live Event content is visible to anyone on the LinkedIn feed and your profile or Page. The Live Event shows as a post on your Page’s feed or in the posts section of your profile. For LinkedIn Pages, it can also be found under the Events and Videos tabs. Anyone can watch the replay of your Live Event, even if there’s a registration form. A member needs to fill the registration form before they can watch the replay. This way, you can continue to collect views, engagement, and leads on the content even after the event has ended.

    Timing: This change is now available to all members with LinkedIn Live access.

If you have any questions related to these changes, please contact us.

Remove a mention or tag of yourself

You can remove a mention or tag of yourself from a post, comment, or photo at any time.

To remove a mention from a post or comment:

  1. Click the More icon in the upper-right corner of the post or comment.
  2. Click ** Remove mention**.
  3. In the confirmation pop-up window, click Remove.

Your name stays in plain text, but the link to your profile is removed.

To remove a tag from a photo:

  1. Click the ** Tag** icon on the photo.
  2. In the Tagged pop-up window, click the ** Trash** icon next to your name.
  3. In the confirmation pop-up window, click Remove.

The member who tagged you won’t be notified.

Your name stays in plain text, but the link to your profile is removed.

To remove a tag from a photo:

  2. In the Tagged pop-up window, tap the ** Trash** icon next to your name.

Save a post as a draft

You can save your post as a draft by clicking the Cancel button at the end of the post and share content process on LinkedIn.

To save your post as a draft:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage to share a post. The post pop-up window appears.
  2. Type the content of your post in the What do you want to talk about? field.
  3. Click the Cancel button in the upper-right corner. The Save this post as a draft? pop-up window appears.
  4. Click Save as draft if you want to save a draft of your post and return later to edit and share it. A message appears stating that the draft is successfully saved.

Notes:

  • The draft of your post will auto-populate for editing and sharing when you open the Create a post pop-up window next time.
  • To delete the post, click Discard.
  • You’ll not be able to edit any photos or videos. You’ll have to delete and re-upload them if you want to make any changes.
  • You’ll have to re-upload your attachment if you want to change the visibility of your post.

To save your post as a draft:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar to share a post. The post page appears.
  2. Type the content of your post in the What do you want to talk about? field.
  3. Tap the Cancel button in the upper-left corner. The Save this post for later?/Save for later? pop-up appears.
  4. Tap Save draft/Save if you want to save a draft of your post and return later to edit and share it. A message appears stating that the draft is successfully saved.

Notes:

  • The draft of your post will auto-populate for editing and sharing when you open the post page next time.

  • To delete the post, tap Delete draft/Discard.

Schedule posts

You can now create posts and schedule them to go live at a later time. You can also view the list of all the posts that you’ve scheduled.

Currently, scheduling posts is not supported for the following types of posts:

  • Events
  • Jobs
  • Services

If you add any of the above types to your post, you will see an error message indicating that scheduling is not supported for that post. Either clear the selected date/time to post immediately or remove the invalid post type.

To schedule a post:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage. The Create a post pop-up window appears.

  2. Type the content of your post in the What do you want to talk about? field.

  3. Click the Clock icon in the lower-right corner to schedule your post.

    • In the Schedule post pop-up window, select a date and time when you want to publish the post. The time selected must be within 10 minutes to 3 months from the current time (rounded to the nearest interval).
    • You can also enter the exact time to schedule a post instead of using the 30-minute increment options from the dropdown.

    Note: Scheduled time will be standardized in UTC based on your device’s time zone settings.

  4. Click Next.

    • You can see the scheduled date and time above the post.

  5. Click Schedule.

    • A post scheduled confirmation pop-up appears on the lower left of the page.

Notes:

  • To change the time of the post before scheduling it, click the Clock icon, update the time, click Next, and then click Schedule to schedule the post.
  • If you don’t want to schedule a post, click Edit next to the time mentioned above the post. In the Schedule post pop-up window, click Clear time. The schedule details are no longer available. Click Post to create a post immediately or click the Close icon on the upper-right corner to discard the post.
  • Once a post is scheduled, you can reschedule the publish time or delete the post.

To view scheduled posts:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click the Clock icon on the lower-left of the Create a post pop-up window.
  3. In the Schedule post pop-up window, click View all scheduled posts in the lower-left corner. You can view a preview of all the posts that you’ve scheduled in the Scheduled posts page.

Notes:

  • To preview a schedule post, click the post, and view the details.
  • To delete a scheduled post, click the Delete icon next to the post. In the Delete scheduled post? pop-up window, click Delete, and confirm your action.
  • To edit or reschedule a scheduled post, view your scheduled posts, click the More icon in the upper right, and then click Modify schedule or Edit post.

To schedule a post:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar. The Share post pop-up window appears.

  2. Type the content of your post in the What do you want to talk about? field.

  3. Tap the Clock icon in the upper-right corner.

    • In the Schedule pop-up window, select a date and time when you want to publish the post. The time selected must be within 10 minutes to 3 months from the current time (rounded to the nearest interval).
    • You can also enter the exact time to schedule a post instead of using the 30-minute increment options from the dropdown.

    Note: Scheduled time will be standardized in UTC relative to your current location.

  4. Tap Next. You can see the scheduled date and time above the post.

  5. Tap Schedule on the upper-right corner. A post scheduled confirmation pop up appears.

Notes:

  • If you don’t want to schedule a post, tap Edit next to the time mentioned above the post. In the Schedule pop-up window, tap Clear. The schedule details are no longer available. Tap Post to create your post immediately or tap the Close icon on the upper-left corner to discard the post.
  • Once a post is scheduled, you can reschedule the publish time or delete the post.

To view scheduled posts:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar. The Share post pop-up window appears.
  2. Tap the Clock icon.
  3. In the Schedule pop-up window, tap View all. You can view a preview of all the posts that you’ve scheduled in the Scheduled posts screen.

Notes:

  • To delete a scheduled post, tap the Delete icon next to the post. In the Delete scheduled post? pop-up window, tap Delete, and confirm your action.

  • To edit or reschedule a scheduled post, view your scheduled posts, tap the More icon in the upper right, and then tap Modify schedule or Edit post.

Schedule your LinkedIn Live event from a third-party broadcast tool

Eligible LinkedIn Live broadcasters can schedule a Live Event for their profile or LinkedIn Page using our preferred third-party broadcast tools:

  • Restream
  • Socialive
  • Streamyard
  • Switcher

Approved LinkedIn Live Video broadcasters can then promote their scheduled Live Event on and off LinkedIn.

Schedule the Live Event

To begin scheduling your Live Event, click on any of the following broadcasting tools to access its instructions to log in and set up: Restream, Socialive, Streamyard, and Switcher. After logging in and adding the details for your broadcast, you’ll see the option to schedule the Live Event.

Note: The option to schedule your live stream is only available on these broadcast tools.

Important to know

Avoid creating test or temporary Pages to try out events. Instead, use the built‑in test event option during event creation to safely validate your setup. Learn how to create a LinkedIn Live Test event from your LinkedIn Page.

LinkedIn Pages cannot use the LinkedIn registration form if the Live Event is created using third-party broadcast tools. This form is only available for events created directly on LinkedIn.

Gather an audience

When you schedule the stream in advance, a public LinkedIn Live Event post will be generated on LinkedIn to announce your upcoming stream. This post will be visible on the feed of your LinkedIn Page or profile. When you start your stream, the post will automatically show your live video.

On the scheduled Live Event post, LinkedIn members can click the Attend button to RSVP. Anyone who clicks Attend (your event “attendees”) will receive reminder notifications three days and 15 minutes before the scheduled Live Event. When you go live into the scheduled event, we will send a notification to all registered attendees. In addition, we will send a notification to a subset of the followers of your profile or LinkedIn Page, targeting the ones most likely to view your video based on a variety of factors.

Here are some additional best practices for gathering an audience:

  • Schedule your Live Event on LinkedIn at least two weeks in advance to allow your post to gather more reach and attendees over time. This will increase the number of viewers for your Live Event.
  • Use the Invite functionality to invite your connections on LinkedIn to attend the Live Event. This helps increase discovery and maximize the reach.
  • You can also sponsor or amplify a Live Event post using Events Ads.

When you’re scheduling your Live Event:

  • You can choose a banner image to show on LinkedIn to give members an idea of what to expect from your stream. The recommended aspect ratio is 16:9.

Once you have scheduled your Live Event:

  • Any event edits or cancellations you make on the Live Event must also be made manually on your broadcast tool.
  • You can add more details by editing the event description. You can also edit the title, date and time of the Live Event from the event page.
  • To delete a scheduled live stream that does not have any attendees yet, you can simply delete the event. To delete one that already has attendees, you will need to first cancel the event on LinkedIn. Then, after your event has been cancelled for seven or more days, you can delete it.
  • Once the event post is shared from your profile or LinkedIn Page, you can share the URL anywhere you’d like, including on other social platforms, in a newsletter, and more.

When you’re ready to go live:

  • You can go live any time from 15 minutes before to two hours after your scheduled start time. If you don’t go live within this time period, the post will show that your stream is cancelled.

  • For LinkedIn Pages, any content admin or super admin can begin the broadcast from a third-party broadcast tool.

  • Any member can access the Live Event content on your LinkedIn Page or profile before, during and after the Live Event, even if they were not an attendee.

Search for member posts

You can use the search bar to find Top Voices and member posts.

To search for a post:

  1. Enter your keyword in the Search bar at the top of your page.

    • The type-ahead feature predicts related search terms as you type your keywords into the search bar.

  2. Click See all results at the bottom of the search.

  3. Click the Posts tab at the top of the page.

  4. Click the Dropdown to the right of a search category tab to further sort and filter your search.

  5. Select a post that interests you from the search results.

To search for a post:

  1. Tap the Search bar at the top of your screen.
  2. Enter your keyword into the Search bar.
  3. Tap See all results at the bottom of the dropdown.
  4. Tap the Posts tab at the top of the page.
  5. Tap the Dropdown to the right of a search category tab to further sort and filter your search.
  6. Select a post that interests you from the search results.

Notes:

  • If you wish to find posts by a specific individual, search by their name and any recent posts or activity by them will be available on their profile.

  • If a member has deleted a post they shared on LinkedIn, you won’t be able to find it in search results or the member’s profile.

  • You can find additional search filters in the All filters section at the end of the categories list which includes Sort by, Date posted, Content type, From member, From company, Posted by, Mentioning member, Mentioning company, Author industry, and Author company.

SEO settings for articles or Newsletters published on LinkedIn

You can customize Search Engine Optimization (SEO) for titles and descriptions of articles or newsletters you publish on LinkedIn, controlling how it shows up on search engines, and making it easier for others to find your content.

From the SEO settings on the LinkedIn publishing platform, you can add:

SEO title: Add SEO title which we’ll use in place of your article title for search engine result pages, such as Google search. If your SEO title is over 60 characters, it will be truncated.

SEO description: Add SEO description in place of the first few lines of your article on search engine result pages. We suggest utilizing keywords, summarizing your writing, and aiming to write between 140-160 characters.

Share articles or links

You can share relevant articles or links with your network using the share box at the top of your LinkedIn homepage. You can share an article on your feed directly from the article page.

To share an article or a link from your homepage:

  1. Click Start a post, try writing with AI at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Paste the link or type the URL in the What do you want to talk about? field.

    • Allow a few seconds for a preview image to display (image frame is a 1.91:1 ratio and 1200 (w) x 627 (h) pixels). If we’re not able to retrieve a preview image, you can still share your update as a link.
    • You may encounter an error message or missing preview information if the URL you’re sharing doesn’t meet certain requirements. Check out our URL troubleshooting guide for tips on successful URL sharing.

    Note: You also have the option of adding text (up to 3000 characters) to your post.

  3. Click the dropdown next to your name in the post pop-up window, select who you want to share the post with in the Post settings pop-up window, and click Done.

  4. Click Post.

To share an article directly from the article page:

  1. Navigate to the article page and click Share above the comments on the right.

  2. From the Share pop-up, you can select:

    • Repost to Feed to share the article post with your thoughts on LinkedIn.
    • Send in a message to privately message one or many of your connections.
    • Copy link to share the article on any other app or platform.
    • Facebook
    • Twitter

  3. Follow the prompts to share the article.

To share an article or a link from your homepage:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar.

  2. Paste the link or type the URL in the Share your thoughts field.

    • Allow a few seconds for a preview image to display. If we’re not able to retrieve a preview image, you can still share your update as a link.
    • You may encounter an error message or missing preview information if the URL you’re sharing doesn’t meet certain requirements. Check out our URL troubleshooting guide for tips on successful URL sharing.

    Note: You also have the option of adding text (up to 3000 characters) to your post.

  3. Tap the Anyone dropdown below your name. Select who you want to share the post with in the Who can see this your post? pop-up.

  4. Tap Post on the upper right.

To share an article directly from the article page:

  1. Navigate to the article page and click Share in the navigation bar.

  2. Select from the following options:

    • ** Share in a post** / Post on feed to share the article post with your thoughts on LinkedIn.
    • / Share via to share the article on any other app or platform.

  3. Follow the prompts to share the article.

  4. Tap Post on the upper right.

To reshare or quote an article:

  2. Tap the selection to see the editing options.

  • Minimum video duration: 3 seconds when uploading from desktop and 2 seconds when uploading from the LinkedIn mobile app.
  • Resolution range: 256x144 to 4096x2304
  • Aspect ratio: 1:2.4 - 2.4:1
  • Frame rates: 10fps - 60 fps
  • Bit rates: 192 Kbps - 30 Mbps

Video safe zones

Keep the edges (top, bottom, and sides) of your video free of key elements, text, and logos to ensure they are within the safe zone and aren’t overlapped by the LinkedIn user interface.

[Image: Video safe zones]

Sharing Public Posts On and Off LinkedIn

When sharing a post, you can control who sees it from the share box. Public posts can be shared on other sites as long as your public profile is also showing. If your profile isn’t public, your post will only be visible to members who are signed in to LinkedIn.

Important: Posts created on other LinkedIn sharing platforms that use the Public setting, such as InShare, will continue to be visible only to those signed in to LinkedIn.

  • Within your privacy settings and under Blocking and Hiding the followers setting should be set to Everyone.

    • Note: If you’ve blocked a member on LinkedIn, they may still be able to see a Public post that appear outside of the LinkedIn network.

  • Public profile visibility - Set to Make my public profile visible to everyone and select Posts & Activities.

To share a public post off LinkedIn:

  1. Click the More icon in the top right corner of the post.
  2. Click Copy link to post.
  3. Paste the URL to another site such as Facebook or Twitter.

To share a public post off LinkedIn:

  1. Tap the More icon in the top right corner of the post.
  2. Tap Share via.
  3. Tap Copy from the option menu that slides up.
  4. Paste the URL to another site such as Facebook or Twitter.

To share a public post off LinkedIn:

  1. Tap the More icon in the top right corner of the post.
  2. Tap Share via.
  3. Tap Copy to clipboard from the option menu that slides up.
  4. Paste the URL to another site such as Facebook or Twitter.

Note:

  • It isn’t possible to change the visibility of posts shared before July 2017.
  • Storyline and multi-photo posts aren’t currently available to users who aren’t signed in to LinkedIn.

Sort your feed by Top or Recent posts

Your LinkedIn feed displays Topposts by default. These posts are personalized based on your activity and interests. You can switch to Recentposts to view updates in reverse chronological order from people you follow, without personalization.

To change your feed view:

  1. Go to your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click the Sort bydropdown above your feed.

  3. Select one of the following:

    • Top – You’ll see posts that are sorted based on your interests and activity.
    • Recent– You’ll see posts in reverse chronological order from people you follow.

  4. Scroll down to view posts based on your selection.

To make your feed view preference permanent:

  1. Click the  Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown. The Account preferences page appears by default.

  3. Click Preferred Feed View under General preferences.

  4. From the Preferred Feed View page, select one of the following as your preferred permanent feed view:

    • Most relevant posts – You’ll see posts that match your interests and activity.
    • Most recent posts– You’ll see the latest posts first, only from people whom you follow. Your interests and activity data will not be used to sort the feed or make recommendations.

    The change is automatically saved.

Notes:

  • If Most relevant posts (Recommended) is set as your preferred permanent feed view: 

    • You’ll see the most recent posts from people you follow. Your interests and activity data won’t be used to sort your feed.
    • You’ll see updates from your network when using an EU IP address.
    • You’ll see relevant updates in reverse chronological order when you are not using an EU IP address.

  • After the feed view preference is made permanent from the Settings page, your feed will always show the selected feed view.

  • Your ad personalization preferences are not affected by changes to the Feed Preferences setting. To control your ad personalization preferences, go to your Advertising preferences setting.

  • If you are located in the European Economic Area and in the Most Recent feed view, you will see all updates from your network in reverse chronological order.

  • If you are located outside of the European Economic Area and in the Most Recent feed view, you will see the updates most relevant to you in reverse chronological order.

Suggested Feeds in your LinkedIn feed

Important to know

This experience is currently a test and is limited to a select group of US members only.  It’ll not impact feed preferences you made in settings.

Suggested Feeds help you discover content aligned to your professional interests, while keeping your main feed as your default experience.

You may see Suggested Feeds displayed as topic tabs at the top of your feed or as a carousel within your feed. These experiences are designed to help you explore topic‑based content more easily, without changing your feed preferences.

Topic tabs

You may see up to five topic tabs at the top of your main feed. Each tab displays topic tailored to your interests.

When you select a topic tab:

  • You’ll see a feed focused on that topic.
  • The topic tabs remain visible as you scroll, making it easy to switch topics.
  • You can return to your main feed at any time.

Feed carousel

You may see a carousel in your feed that displays posts from a suggested topic.

With the carousel:

  • You can scroll horizontally to browse posts.
  • You can like, comment on, or share posts directly from the carousel.
  • Selecting the carousel header takes you to a dedicated feed for that topic.
  • Selecting an individual post opens the feed detail page for that post.

Turn off and limit comments on posts

You can control who can comment on your posts by limiting comments to only your connections or turning comments off completely. You can change this before or after you share a post.

  • When you turn off comments, existing comments aren’t deleted.
  • When you choose a comment setting, that preference is saved as your default for future posts.

To change comment settings before sharing a post:

  1. Click Start a post at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click your profile name dropdown.

  3. Click Comment control.

  4. Choose one of the following options:

    • Anyone to allow comments from everyone
    • Connections only to limit comments to your 1st-degree connections
    • No oneto turn off comments completely

  5. Click Save.

To change comment settings after sharing a post:

  1. Go to the post.

  2. Click the ** More** icon on the upper right of the post.

  3. Click ** Who can comment on your post?**.

  4. Choose one of the following options:

    • Anyone to allow comments from everyone
    • Connections only to limit comments to your 1st-degree connections
    • No oneto turn off comments completely

  5. Click Save.

To change comment settings before sharing a post:

  1. Tap Post in the navigation bar.

  2. Tap the dropdown next to your profile photo.

  3. Tap Comment control.

  4. Choose one of the following options:

    • Anyone to allow comments from everyone
    • Connections only to limit comments to your 1st-degree connections
    • No oneto turn off comments completely

  5. Tap Done.

To change comment settings after sharing a post:

  1. Go to the post.

  2. Tap the More icon on the upper right of the post.

  3. Tap Who can comment on this post?.

  4. Choose one of the following options:

    • Anyone to allow comments from everyone
    • Connections only to limit comments to your 1st-degree connections
    • No oneto turn off comments completely

  5. Tap Save.

Upload and share documents on LinkedIn

You can upload documents to a post on LinkedIn from your homepage, Group, or LinkedIn Page. We recommend that you share documents that include topics such as career advice, culture stories, insights & trends, event content, and knowledge sharing.

Important:

  • The file size cannot exceed 100MB and 300 pages. The following file types are supported: PPT, PPTX, DOC, DOCX, and PDF.
  • You can edit the description of your document or remove the post after it’s uploaded, but you can’t change or edit the document in the post.
  • For accessibility purposes, members who can view your post will be able to download your document as a PDF.

Here are some best practices for preparing your document prior to uploading it:

  • Share high-quality documents that reflect how members already use LinkedIn to find new opportunities and make connections.
  • Convert files to PDFs whenever possible to ensure the highest quality upload.
  • PDFs with multiple layers must be flattened or merged.
  • Videos and other animations in documents aren’t supported and will display as static images instead.
  • Add a title to your document to let members know what your document is about.
  • Review LinkedIn’s Copyright Policy to ensure your document is compliant.
  • Please ensure that the PDFs you upload have secure hyperlinks.
  • PDFs with multiple sized pages must be fit to the same page size.

To upload a document to your homepage:

  1. Click Start a post in the sharebox at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click More in the pop-up window, then click on the Add a document icon.

  3. Click Choose file to select a document from your computer.

    • You can also upload a document from the cloud, using the Dropbox or Google Drive options. You may encounter an alert that requires admin approval if you’re using a corporate cloud account.

  4. Select the file that you want to upload (choose one).

  5. Add a title to your document and click Done.

  6. Add a description to the post.

    • You can use hashtags or **@** to mention someone (Optional).

  7. Click Post.

To upload a document to your homepage:

  1. Tap Post.

  2. Tap More icon, then tap on Document.

  3. Your device will prompt you to choose a file from your device folder or a cloud service.

    • To upload a file from a cloud service, you need to have the app for that cloud service installed on your mobile device. You may encounter an alert that requires admin approval if you’re using a corporate cloud account.

  4. Select the file you want to upload (choose one).

  5. Add a title to your document and tap Next.

  6. Add a description to the post.

    • You can use hashtags or @** mention someone (Optional).**

  7. Tap Post.

Use LinkedIn reactions

LinkedIn reactions are a set of expressions that offer members a way to more easily participate in conversations and communicate with their network.

Important: This feature isn’t currently available for mobile users in China.

To react to a post or a comment, from a mobile device, tap and hold the Like icon. If you’re using a desktop, move your cursor over the Like icon to select your reaction to a post or a comment.

Check out the reactions you can use:

[Image: LinkedIn Reactions]

Celebrate – Expresses that you’re celebrating an announcement, congratulating a personal or professional milestone, or praising an accomplishment. For example:

  • Welcoming a new team member.
  • Securing a speaking opportunity, getting promoted, or landing a new job.
  • Completing a successful project launch on time or fun team offsite to end a strong quarter.

Support – Expresses that you empathize with someone’s experience or support them during a challenging time. For example:

  • Demonstrating you’re there for a connection who was vulnerable about their journey in finding a new job.
  • Encouraging a coworker who is finding work from home difficult to manage.

Love – Expresses that the post is heartwarming, resonates with you, or makes you feel an overall sense of appreciation or happiness. For example:

  • When your child visits you at work and thinks you have the greatest job in the world.
  • Posts about the importance of work-life balance.
  • Witnessing a colleague achieve a goal.
  • Thanking your past mentors who helped you get to where you are today.

Insightful – Expresses that you thought the post made a great point, offered a new idea, or shared helpful insights or advice. For example:

  • When your company encourages you to take a day off each month to work on a project that you’re passionate about.
  • Posts about tips and tricks.

Funny – Expresses that the post made you laugh, felt humorous, or offered light-hearted fun in a professional context.

For example:

  • Laughing along with a coworker who shared a funny virtual meeting mistake while working from home.

  • Sharing an inside joke relevant to your role or industry.

  • Heartwarming humor that shows vulnerability.

  • Like, unlike, and react to posts or comments

Video sharing troubleshooting

You can share a video on LinkedIn from your computer or mobile device. You can’t upload an unsupported file type and you’ll get an error message if you do so. If you’re experiencing any issues uploading your videos, please check the supported file types and video file requirements below.

Important to know

Please check that your video is one of the supported types of video files. For example, if your file type is ProRes, you may be able to upload it, but it will not be able to process.

  • File Type/Codecs: MP4; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: MOV; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: AVI; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: WEBM; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: MKV; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: WMV; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: VC1; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: MPEG, MPEG2, MPEG1VIDEO; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: DVVIDEO; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: QTRLE; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓
  • File Type/Codecs: TSCC2; Desktop: ✓; iOS: ✓; Android: ✓

Video File Requirements:

  • Maximum file size: 5 GB
  • Minimum file size: 75 KB
  • Maximum video duration: 15 minutes
  • Minimum video duration: 3 seconds when uploading from desktop and 2 seconds when uploading from the LinkedIn mobile app.
  • Resolution range: 256x144 to 4096x2304
  • Aspect ratio: 1:2.4 - 2.4:1
  • Frame rates: 10fps - 60 fps
  • Bit rates: 192 Kbps - 30 Mbps

Video safe zones

Keep the edges (top, bottom, and sides) of your video free of key elements, text, and logos to ensure they are within the safe zone and aren’t overlapped by the LinkedIn user interface.

[Image: Video safe zones]

Notes:

  • While uploading a video from an iOS device, you’ll need to remain in the LinkedIn mobile app. You may experience the upload stall if the LinkedIn mobile app is in the background. However, once the video is uploaded and begins processing, you can use other applications. You should receive a notification when your video is ready to view.

  • While uploading a video from an Android device, you’ll still be able to access and use other applications while your video is uploading in the background. You should receive a notification when your video is ready to view.

  • Videos stored on iCloud aren’t supported for upload on the LinkedIn mobile app. To upload the videos stored on your iCloud, you must move the video from your iCloud account to your local phone memory.

View your activity or a member’s activity on LinkedIn

The Activity section shows posts, comments, articles, and profile activity on LinkedIn. It’s a quick way to review what you’ve shared and to see what other members are doing.

Write and publish articles on LinkedIn

Important to know

This feature isn’t available on the LinkedIn mobile app.

All members and admins (super admins or content admins of a LinkedIn Page) have the ability to publish articles about their expertise and insights. Articles are displayed in the Activity section of your profile.

Check out LinkedIn’s official resource for guidance on creating content that is valuable and impactful.

To write an article:

  1. Click Write article in the share box near the top of your homepage.

    • If you’re a Super admin or Content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you’ll see an option to Publish as, select which account you want to publish from, and click Next. This takes you to the publishing tool.

  2. Click the Dropdown next to your name on the upper left to choose if you want to publish an article as yourself (personal profile), or from a Page you manage. You can also choose to publish to an Individual article or as a new edition of your newsletter if you have one.

  3. Click Upload from computer or drag in an image above the Title of the article, to add a cover image.

  4. Click into the Title field to type the title of your article.

    Note: If you’re unable to click into the Title field, you may have a browser extension that is blocking this functionality  (i.e. Lazarus, Grammarly). This can be resolved by disabling these extensions and refreshing the editor.

  5. Click in the Write here field to add the content of your article.

    From the tool bar next to your name at the top of the article, you can:

    • Add Image or Video: Click the  Media icon to upload an image or video from your computer.
    • Add Link : Click******Link** to add hyperlinks throughout your article.
    • Add Code Click  Code to add a highlighted snippet into your article.
    • Embed content: Click the Embed icon to embed content within your article. From here, you can paste in a link to embed a LinkedIn post, member profile, a LinkedIn Page or external content.
    • Style and Formatting: To make your article more visually engaging for your readers, you can change the style, bold or italicize any text, add ordered or unordered lists, add blockquotes, or add a divider.

    To add a cover image:

    • Add cover image: Click Upload from computer above the Title of the article, to add a cover image.

Here’s a tip

You can type ‘@’ to mention another member or a LinkedIn Page in your article. 6. Click the Manage dropdown near the upper right, from here you can:

  • Manage settings: Select Settings to create an Article URL, add an SEO title, and add an SEO description to control how your article shows up on search engines and make it easier for others to find your content
  • Preview: Select Preview to view a preview of your article
  • Share draft: Select Preview and then click Share draft near the upper right of the publishing tool to share your article draft with other members before publishing

Note: Members can view the draft only when they’re logged into LinkedIn. 7. Click Next near the upper right. 8. Click Publish.

  • (Optional) You can add text commentary about your article in the Tell your network what your article is about field.
  • (Optional) Click the ** Clock** icon next to Publish and follow prompts to schedule your article to be published at a later time.

Notes:

  • You can disable the ability to leave comments on your published articles.
  • You can edit or delete your articles at any time.
  • When you mention another member or LinkedIn Page their profile/page will be hyperlinked in the article. The mentioned member/page will be notified of the mention.

Access country specific employment types

You can now select employment types that are specific to the country in which you’ve worked and more accurately represent your professional experience.

Note: You must change the location on your introduction section in order to access a new employment type list that is country specific when you’re adding or editing the experience section.

To edit your location from your profile:

  1. Click the Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click the Edit icon in your introduction section.

  4. From the Edit intro pop-up window that appears, scroll down to Location.

  5. Select your Country/Region from the dropdown. Note: This is a required field.

  6. Depending on the country you select, you’ll be given the option to add your:

    • City/District
    • Postal code

  7. Click Save.

  8. Tap your profile photo, then View Profile.

  9. Tap the Edit icon from your introduction section.

  10. From the Edit intro pop-up scroll down to Country/Region.

  11. Tap and select your country from the list. Note: This is a required field.

  12. Depending on the country you select, you’ll be given the option to add your:

    • City/District
    • Postal code

  13. Tap Save on the upper right.

Note: Country specific employment types will be translated only to the language indicated by the member’s language setting, if an equivalent employment type exists in that language. Employment types for a country that don’t have an equivalent in the member’s interface language will display the original term in its origin language. For example, “Funcionario” is a new Spain employment type. The term “Funcionario” doesn’t conceptually exist in the English language. If the member’s country is Spain but their interface language is English, then the member will see “Funcionario” listed in their employment type dropdown.

Availability of your content off LinkedIn

You can post and share content on LinkedIn and control who is eligible to see it by selecting its audience. If the audience you select is Anyone, that content may be visible to anyone on or off of LinkedIn. For example:

LinkedIn may allow third parties to display your content if the visibility of such content was set to Anyone.

Members can embed content from LinkedIn (desktop only) and distribute it online if the visibility of the content is set to Anyone. Members can embed text posts, first-part or third-party articles, images, videos, live videos, and document posts.

Important to know

We’ve made updates to ensure that when you embed a LinkedIn post in third-party sites, they look more polished and are easier to engage with. These enhancements include a cleaner design, a compact preview option, and clearer recognition that the content comes from LinkedIn — helping you build trust with your audience.

To embed a post from LinkedIn on desktop:

  1. Navigate to the post you want to embed.

  2. Click the More icon in the upper-right corner of the post.

  3. Click Embed this post.

  4. Select one of the following:

    • When embedding a post, you can choose between Embed with less text or Embed full post to better fit the layout of your site. For video posts, you can select Embed video only to highlight the video without any accompanying post text.

  5. In the Embed this post pop-up window, click Copy code.

    • You’ll receive a notification in the lower-left corner of the page stating that the code has been copied to your clipboard.

  6. Close the Embed this post pop-up window.

Notes:

  • We don’t offer the option to embed multi-photo posts or reposts with commentary.
  • Notifications won’t be sent to the author of the post when you embed their content.
  • Only posts that an author has shared as Public can be embedded.
  • If an author deletes the content you’ve embedded, the embeds will also get deleted.

LinkedIn may allow search tools to crawl and display certain content, such as posts and shares set to Anyone, and elements of your public profile (depending on your public profile settings). These search tools (such as Google, Bing, or ChatGPT) may use that content to enhance their search experiences. For example, they might show LinkedIn posts in search results or include them in AI-generated summaries.

  • Adjust your settings to allow your posts to be embedded
