Country specific employment types

You can now select employment types that are specific to the country in which you’ve worked and more accurately represent your professional history. Some country specific employment types are contracts, full-time, part-time, temporary staff etc.

Country specific employment types are available for the following countries:

  • Brazil
  • Canada
  • France
  • Germany
  • India
  • Japan
  • Netherlands
  • Spain
  • UK

All other countries will continue to use the list of definitions for employment types under the Employment types that are currently available section below. As we continue to research employment types that are specific to other countries, we will add them to the platform.

Notes:

  • For Canada and France, the employment types ’contract’, ‘part-time’, and ‘full-time’ have been replaced with more specific definitions.

  • The list under the Country specific employment types section represents either changes in the definition of a previous employment type, or the addition of a new definition for a listed country.

  • Employment Type: Contract; Definition: A temporary employment with a fixed length. Though not specified, it is often as an independent contractor directly through the company. However, it may also refer to a seasonal or otherwise temporary worker, an employee through a third-party agency etc.

  • Employment Type: Self-employed; Definition: Working for oneself, it may refer to sole proprietorships, entrepreneurs, small business owners etc.

  • Employment Type: Part-time; Definition: A general term that members can use to indicate that they don’t dedicate all their professional time to the position.

  • Employment Type: Full-time; Definition: A general term that members can use to indicate that they dedicate all their professional time to the position. It doesn’t explicitly describe their contractual status, such as permanent, contract, etc.

  • Employment Type: Internship; Definition: An employment program that a member goes through in order to gain work experience. This typically doesn’t warrant in certification.

  • Employment Type: Apprenticeship; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program a member goes through in order to gain work experience for a specific job. This usually results in certification.

  • Employment Type: Freelance; Definition: Self-employed service providers who aren’t committed to a single employer for long-term. It may refer to gig workers, freelance photographers etc.

UK

  • Employment Type: Temporary Staff; Definition: Contract employment directly through a client company.

Canada

  • Employment Type: English: Self-Employed French: Travailleur autonome; Definition: Working for oneself, it may refer to sole proprietorships, entrepreneurs, small business owners etc.
  • Employment Type: English: Contract Full-time French: Contrat à temps plein; Definition: A combination of Contract and Full-time.
  • Employment Type: English: Contract Part-Time French: Contrat à temps partiel; Definition: A combination of Contract and Part-time.
  • Employment Type: English: Apprenticeship French: Apprenti; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program a member goes through in order to gain work experience for a specific job. This usually results in certification.
  • Employment Type: English: Freelance French: Pigiste; Definition: Self-employed service providers who aren’t committed to a single employer for long-term. It may refer to gig workers, freelance photographers etc.
  • Employment Type: English: Permanent Full-Time French: Permanent à temps plein; Definition: A combination of Permanent and Full-time.
  • Employment Type: English: Permanent Part-Time French: Permanent à temps partiel; Definition: A combination of Permanent and Part-time.
  • Employment Type: English: Seasonal French: Saisonnier; Definition: A short-term contract which is limited to specific times of the year, such as winter or summer, often in specific industries only such as agriculture.
  • Employment Type: English: Casual / On-call French: Occasionnel / Sur appel; Definition: Direct employment by a company, but with no guaranteed hours.
  • Employment Type: English: Co-op French: Coop; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program where a member attends school but also works in alternating terms (weeks, months or semesters) for credit.

France

  • Employment Type: Fonctionnaire; Definition: A life-time contract to work for the government, often earned by passing an official test.
  • Employment Type: Intermittent du spectacle; Definition: Employment within the entertainment industry that is ongoing, and benefits are awarded when unemployed or between contracts.
  • Employment Type: Service Civique; Definition: Working for a non-profit or public sector entity, arranged through the government.
  • Employment Type: VIE/VIA; Definition: Working for an international company or government department abroad, arranged through the government.
  • Employment Type: Intérimaire; Definition: Contract employment through a third-party, outsourced company, performed for a client company.
  • Employment Type: CDI temps partiel; Definition: Part-time employment on a permanent basis with no fixed term.
  • Employment Type: CDD temps partiel; Definition: Part-time fixed-term employment on a temporary basis.
  • Employment Type: English: Self-Employed French: Indépendant; Definition: Working for oneself, it may refer to sole proprietorships, entrepreneurs, small business owners etc.

Germany

  • Employment Type: Verbeamtet; Definition: A life-time contract to work for the government, often earned by passing an official test.
  • Employment Type: Freiwilliges soziales Jahr; Definition: Working for oneself, it may refer to sole proprietorships, entrepreneurs, small business owners etc.
  • Employment Type: Werkstudium; Definition: Working while in school, with specific regulations and requirements.
  • Employment Type: English: Co-op German: Duales Studium; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program where a member attends school but also works in alternating terms (weeks, months or semesters) for credit.
  • Employment Type: English: Apprenticeship German: Azubi; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program a member goes through in order to gain work experience for a specific job. This usually results in certification.

Netherlands

  • Employment Type: English: Contract Dutch: Tijdelijk contract; Definition: A temporary employment with a fixed length. Though not specified, it is often as an independent contractor directly through the company. However, it may also refer to a seasonal or otherwise temporary worker, an employee through a third-party agency etc.
  • Employment Type: English: Apprenticeship Dutch: Leerwerktraject; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program a member goes through in order to gain work experience for a specific job. This usually results in certification.
  • Employment Type: English: Self-Employed Dutch: Zelfstandig / Eigenaar; Definition: Working for oneself, it may refer to sole proprietorships, entrepreneurs, small business owners etc.
  • Employment Type: English: Internship Dutch: Stage; Definition: An employment program that a member goes through in order to gain work experience. This typically doesn’t warrant in certification.

Japan

  • Employment Type: English: Permanent Japanese: 正社員・職員; Definition: Employment on a permanent basis with no fixed length.
  • Employment Type: English: Apprenticeship Japanese: 研修生・実習生; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program a member goes through in order to gain work experience for a specific job. This usually results in certification.
  • Employment Type: English: Part-Time Japanese: パート・アルバイト; Definition: A general term that members can use to indicate that they don’t dedicate all their professional time to the position.
  • Employment Type: English: Contract Japanese: 契約社員・職員; Definition: A temporary employment with a fixed length. Though not specified, it is often as an independent contractor directly through the company. However, it may also refer to a seasonal or otherwise temporary worker, an employee through a third-party agency etc.
  • Employment Type: English: Indirect Contract Japanese: 派遣社員; Definition: Contract employment through a third-party, outsourced company, performed for a client company.

Brazil

  • Employment Type: English: On-Call Portuguese: Intermitente; Definition: Direct employment by a company, but with no guaranteed hours.
  • Employment Type: Trainee; Definition: A temporary, often rotational employment program for new graduates who trained for top management.
  • Employment Type: Terceirizado; Definition: Contract employment through a third-party, outsourced company, performed for a client company.

Spain

  • Employment Type: Formación Profesional Dual; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program where a member attends school but also works in alternating terms (weeks, months or semesters) for credit.
  • Employment Type: Funcionario; Definition: A life-time contract to work for the government, often earned by passing an official test.
  • Employment Type: Interino; Definition: A substitute contract to work in place of a Lifetime Civil Servant.
  • Employment Type: Contrato por obra o servicio; Definition: Contract employment directly through a client company.

India

  • Employment Type: Trainee; Definition: A formal/structured education and employment program where a member attends school but also works in alternating terms (weeks, months or semesters) for credit.

Learn more about accessing country specific employment types.

Custom cover image

Important to know

Currently, this feature is only available to LinkedIn members in the USA.

You can select a cover image from the LinkedIn custom image photo gallery that captures your interests or personality.

To add a cover image from the Add a custom image gallery:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click View Profile.
  3. Click the ** Camera** icon on the upper-right corner of the introduction section.
  4. Select an image from the Add a custom image gallery.
  5. Click Save.

To change or delete cover image:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click the Edit icon on the upper-right corner of the cover image in the introduction section.

  4. From the cover image pop-up, you can:

    • Change cover image: Click Change photo and select an image from the Add a custom image gallery.
    • Delete cover image: Click Delete photo and confirm your action to delete your cover image.

  5. Click Save (if applicable).

To add a cover image from the Add a custom image gallery:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap View profile or tap your profile photo again.
  3. Tap the ** Camera** icon on the upper-right corner of the introduction section.
  4. Select an image from the Add a custom image gallery.
  5. Tap Save.

To change or delete cover image:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap View profile or tap your profile photo again.

  3. On your profile, tap your custom image in the introduction section.

  4. From the cover image page, you can:

    • Add photo: Tap Add photo to select an image from the custom image gallery.
    • Delete: Tap** Delete** to delete and confirm your action to delete the cover image.

  5. Tap Save (if applicable).

Notes:

  • LinkedIn will periodically update the custom image photo gallery that members can choose their cover images from.
  • You won’t have to reposition the custom cover image you’ve selected.

Professional sources - no longer available

Important to know

This feature is no longer available.

Professional sources previously helped bring your accomplishments from trusted external platforms into your LinkedIn experience. These sources were automatically matched to your account and used to improve recommendations, connections, and profile summaries.

As part of this change, LinkedIn no longer collects or uses professional sources. Any existing professional sources data has been removed, and related settings are no longer applicable.

Recommend someone on LinkedIn

You can write a recommendation only for your 1st-degree connections whose work you’d like to recognize, like a colleague, co-worker, or student. The recommendation recipient can choose to display it on their profile. If a contact requests a recommendation from you, the request will be sent to you via a message which you can access from the Messaging icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  1. Navigate to the profile of the 1st-degree connection you’d like to recommend.
  2. Click the More button in the introduction section.
  3. Select Recommend.
  4. Fill out the Relationship and Position at the time fields of the recommendations pop-up window, and click Next.
  5. Write your recommendation in the message field and click Send.

To respond to a recommendation request you received through your LinkedIn account:

  1. Click the Messaging icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select the Write [member name] a recommendation message from the left side of the Messaging page.

    • Alternatively, you can select the Write [member name] a recommendation message from the LinkedIn Messaging conversation windows and click on the link.

  3. Click the link provided in the message to write the recommendation.

  4. From the Recommendation requests pop-up window, click Write recommendation. You can click Ignore if you don’t want to recommend your connection.

To recommend someone from their profile:

  1. Navigate to the profile of the 1st-degree connection you’d like to recommend.
  2. Tap the More button in the introduction section.
  3. Tap Recommend. This will take you to the How do you know [member name]? page.
  4. Select relationship and Select [member name’s] position at the time from the dropdowns, and tap Next.
  5. Write your recommendation in the message field.
  6. Tap Send.

To respond to a recommendation request received through your LinkedIn account:

  1. Tap the Messaging icon in the upper right corner.
  2. Tap the link provided in the Write [member name] a recommendation message from the Messaging page to write the recommendation.
  3. From the Requests Received screen, tap Recommend. You can tap Delete if you don’t want to recommend your connection.

Notes:

  • You can edit or delete recommendations you’ve sent at any time.

  • When you give a recommendation, the other person can see it by clicking the Received link in the Recommendations section of their profile. You can see the recommendation by clicking the Given link in the Recommendations section of your own profile. Either one of you can choose to hide the recommendation.

  • Recommendations can only be displayed on your LinkedIn profile if they’re requested through LinkedIn and both parties have LinkedIn profiles. You can’t add an email or other type of message as a recommendation.

Unrecognized Charges from LinkedIn

If you received an unrecognized charge from LinkedIn, you can search for and view the charge on your account. Keep in mind that you can only see receipts for purchases made on your own LinkedIn account.

Before contacting us, compare your purchase history with your charges, then confirm if:

  • A current/former employee, family member, or friend used the payment method to make purchases on LinkedIn. We recommend reaching out to them so they can remove the payment information from their account. They can contact us if they can’t remove the information on their account.
  • Your Premium free trial or promotion may have ended.
  • You may have an active Premium subscription, job posting, or advertisement. Your bank may have placed an authorization hold for a recent purchase, free trial, job posting, or ads account.

If you still don’t recognize the charge, please review our refund policy.

What is LinkedIn and how can I use it?

LinkedIn is the world’s largest professional network on the internet. You can use LinkedIn to find the right job or internship, connect and strengthen professional relationships, and learn the skills you need to succeed in your career. You can access LinkedIn from a desktop, LinkedIn mobile app, or mobile web experience.

A complete LinkedIn profile can help you connect with opportunities by showcasing your unique professional story through experience, skills, and education.

You can also use LinkedIn to organize offline events, join groups, write articles, post photos and videos, and more.

LinkedIn is a platform for anyone who is looking to advance their career. This can include people from various professional backgrounds, such as small business owners, students, and job seekers. LinkedIn members can use LinkedIn to tap into a network of professionals, companies, and groups within and beyond their industry.

LinkedIn is an online platform that connects the world’s professionals. Here are a few steps to get started on LinkedIn:

  1. Create your profile: Signing up and creating your profile is the best way to begin using LinkedIn. A complete LinkedIn profile will summarize your professional experience to your connections, current and future employers, and recruiters. Through your profile, you can showcase your professional life, milestones, skills and interests.
  2. Build your network: Your network plays a crucial part in unlocking the power of LinkedIn. It’ll help you understand what is happening in your industry and professional circle. You can begin by adding your family, friends, past or current classmates, and coworkers to your network. You can also follow people, companies, or topics by navigating directly to the Follow fresh perspectives page, which displays recommended sources to follow. You can use the LinkedIn Events feature to create and join professional Events such as online workshops, seminars, sales and marketing Events, networking Events and more.
  3. Find a job: If you’re looking for a new professional opportunity, you can get started on your job search on LinkedIn. You can use LinkedIn to research companies and reach out to the hiring community. You can also apply directly for roles, save job searches, and notify your connections and recruiters that you’re open for job opportunities.
  4. Participate in conversations: You can easily participate in conversations on LinkedIn. Participating in conversations can allow you to share your perspective on relevant issues and topics with others. You can like and comment on posts and articles on LinkedIn. You can create or join LinkedIn Groups to connect and grow with members who share your interests, experiences, or aspirations. You can also use a set of lightweight expressions called LinkedIn reactions, to easily communicate with your network.
  5. Post content: Millions of members come to LinkedIn every day to connect, learn, and share. You can empower and educate your professional circle with the content you post on LinkedIn. You can also share your thoughts and ideas with LinkedIn members using the share box.

LinkedIn offers a free, basic membership to anyone who wants to create and maintain a professional profile online.

If you upgrade to a Premium subscription, you’ll gain further access to LinkedIn’s products and features. Our paid subscriptions include marketing, recruitment, sales, and learning products. You can try LinkedIn Premium for free for a month.

Learn more about free accounts and Premium subscriptions.

Groups

Access your LinkedIn groups

You can access your groups from your LinkedIn homepage. Some of the LinkedIn groups you belong to are visible in the Interests section of your profile.

You can also bookmark Groups (linkedin.com) to quickly and easily open groups in the future.

To access your groups from homepage:

  2. Click View profile.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of your profile to the Interests section.
  4. Click the Groups tab.
  5. Click Show all groups.

To find your groups through search:

  1. In the Search bar at the top of the page, enter the group name.
  2. Click See all results at the bottom of the search.
  3. Click on the correct group name from the results.

To access your groups from homepage:

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Groups on the left pane.
  3. In Your groups tab, all the groups you belong to are displayed. In the Requested tab, all the group names you have requested to join are displayed. In the Discover tab, you can find new groups
  4. Click the group name you’d like to access.

To view your groups from your profile:

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap your profile picture again to access your profile.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of your profile to the Interests section.
  4. Tap the Groups tab.
  5. Tap Show all groups.

Find your groups through search:

  1. Tap the Search bar.

  3. Tap See all results  at the bottom of the dropdown.
  4. Tap on the group name from the results.

Important to know

Private unlisted groups do not appear in search results for non-group members and are not visible to others on your LinkedIn profile. You can access an unlisted group through a direct link, or when invited.

Difference between LinkedIn group owners and managers

LinkedIn group admins consist of group owners and managers. They’re responsible for managing group activities, member requests, and post approvals. However, group owners and managers have different types of accesses and roles in managing groups (refer to the table below).

  • Action: Invite members to join the group; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Add more group owners and managers; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✖

  • Action: Delete a group; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✖

  • Action: Edit group information; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✖

  • Action: Recommend group posts; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Pin or unpin a group post; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Review and approve group posts; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Remove or block group member; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Moderate LinkedIn Group content; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✔

  • Action: Block a group owner; Owners: ✔; Managers: ✖

Find and Join a LinkedIn Group

[Embedded video omitted]

You can find LinkedIn Groups you’re already a part of and discover new groups to join by using the Search bar at the top of your homepage. Note: There may be multiple groups on LinkedIn for each interest, organization, or affiliation.

You can search for groups by name or keyword, or you can browse groups recommended for you by LinkedIn.

To search for groups by name or keyword:

  1. Enter your keyword or group name in the Search bar at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select (group name) Groups from the dropdown.

To browse for groups recommended for you by LinkedIn:

  1. Click the Work icon in the top right of your LinkedIn homepage and select Groups from the menu that appears.

  2. Scroll down to the bottom of the page and click Search. Notes:

    • On the search results page, you can view a list of groups that are relevant to your search. Learn more about searching on LinkedIn.
    • This feature identifies existing groups on LinkedIn that may interest you. We look for similar attributes between you and other members in groups (attributes such as companies, schools, or industries in common) and present suggestions for groups you may want to join. You’re not obligated to join any group.

If no groups are recommended for you, the reason could be:

  • You’ve already joined or requested to join all available recommended groups.
  • All available recommended groups have been removed.
  • There are currently no recommended groups available for you.
  • Your profile may be missing information like current or past companies, schools, or industries, which makes it difficult for LinkedIn to recommend a group.

Click on a group’s name to learn more about it. The information About this group can be found on the group homepage.

You can join a group by:

  • Clicking Request to join on the group’s homepage.
  • Responding to an invitation from a group member or manager.

To search for groups to join:

  1. Tap into the Search bar.
  2. Type keywords or group names into the search bar and tap Search.
  3. In the search results page, filter the results by tapping Groups on top of the page.
  4. Tap the group name you’re interested in to learn more.
  5. Tap Ask to join.

To search for groups to join:

  1. Tap into the Search bar.
  2. Type keywords or group names into the search bar and tap Search.
  3. In the search results page, filter the results by tapping Groups on top of the page.
  4. Tap the group name you’re interested in to learn more.
  5. Tap REQUEST TO JOIN.

Note: You may not be able to join a group if you’ve exceeded certain limits. Learn more about general limits for LinkedIn Groups.

Group managers may review your request to join or ask for additional information to make sure you meet their membership criteria. Membership approval is solely up to the group.

Learn more about limits for groups.

General limits for LinkedIn groups

To make LinkedIn groups relevant and manageable, we have some set limits for membership, content, and other activities within a group.

  • Group Entity: Number of groups a member can create in one day; Limit: Five
  • Group Entity: Number of groups a member can delete in one day; Limit: 30
  • Group Entity: Membership limit for one group; Limit: 3 million
  • Group Entity: Number of owners a group can have; Limit: 10
  • Group Entity: Number of managers a group can have; Limit: 20
  • Group Entity: Number of groups a member can manage; Limit: 30
  • Group Entity: Number of groups a member can be part of; Limit: 100
  • Group Entity: Number of groups with pending request to join; Limit: 20
  • Group Entity: Character limit for group posts; Limit: 3000
  • Group Entity: Number of mentions within one conversation; Limit: 20
  • Group Entity: Character limit for comments; Limit: 1250
  • Group Entity: Number of new message requests group admins can send to members they are not connected to in their group per day; Limit: 50
  • Group Entity: Number of posts a member can make in a single group each week; Limit: 15
  • Group Entity: Number of groups a member can post in each week; Limit: 20
  • Group Entity: Total number of posts a member can make across all groups; Limit: 60

Important: The change in character limit for a post will be gradually rolled out and may not be available to you at this time. If you don’t see this yet, please check back in the coming weeks.

Notes:

  • Currently, we can’t increase the above-mentioned limits.

  • We encourage group members to post content that is relevant and unique to the group. If members post the same content across multiple groups, the post could be automatically flagged as spam and won’t be displayed.

Types of LinkedIn Groups

Understanding how LinkedIn Groups are categorized helps group members and admins manage visibility and access effectively.

There are three types of groups on LinkedIn:

  • Private Groups (Listed and Unlisted) - These groups are only accessible to members. Posts are visible only within the group.

    • Listed groups: Appears in LinkedIn search results and is visible on member profiles under Interests.
    • Unlisted groups: Does not appear in search results and on member profiles. Access is available only via a direct link or invitation.

  • Public Groups - These groups appear in search results and are visible on member profiles. Posts can be viewed by anyone, including people not signed in to LinkedIn.

Important to know

Only group owners can request a change to the group type. Please contact our customer support team to make this request.

Invitations and Connections

Add follow link or button to your profile

LinkedIn members can use the Follow link to easily share a personalized link or button on your web channels, email, or other platforms. This link or button allows anyone to start following you with just a click.

The criteria for access to the Follow link:

  • A history of abiding by our Professional Community Policies and a good standing record on LinkedIn, and
  • Geographic location is outside of mainland China.

Important to know

To add the Follow link or button to your profile, go to your settings page and set Follow as the primary action. Learn how to manage who can follow you settings.

To access the Follow link:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click Contact info in your introduction section.

  4. The Follow link is available at the bottom of this section under Sharing on socials.

    • If you see Learn more under the Follow link, it means you do not meet our criteria at this time. Please review our Professional Community Policies and try again in the future.

  5. Click on +Copy link or + Copy code.

  6. Paste copied content in your desired destination.

To access the Follow link:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap the More icon next to Add section in your introduction section.

  4. Select Contact info.

  5. The Follow link is available at the bottom of this section under Sharing on socials.

    • If you see Learn more under the Follow link, it means you do not meet our criteria at this time. Please review our Professional Community Policies and try again in the future.

  6. Tap on +Copy link or + Copy code.

  7. Paste copied content in your desired destination.

Alternatives to inviting someone to connect

LinkedIn members have conveyed that they don’t like receiving invitations from people they don’t know, and that they will often ignore or mark those invitations as spam.

We have invitation limits in place to protect our overall member experience and to ensure that our members only receive relevant requests. Your LinkedIn account (Basic or Premium) may be temporarily restricted from sending invitations if you’ve reached the invitation limit.

To ensure that LinkedIn remains a safe community, we recommend that you only send invitations to people you know and trust, in accordance with LinkedIn’s User Agreement and Professional Community Policies. By sending fewer and more thoughtful invitations to connect with others, you will improve: the relevance of content shown in your feed, your search results, and your experience in using other LinkedIn features, to help you discover opportunities on LinkedIn.

  • Follow someone to see the updates and new content that they share in your feed, and establish familiarity by interacting with their posts.
  • Find and join a group that’s relevant to you, so you can meet other professionals with similar interests.
  • Send an InMail to introduce yourself and explain why you’d like to connect with someone you haven’t met yet.
  • Use Sales Navigator to help you find the right prospects faster with customized insights, like lead recommendations and company updates.
  • Run a search in Recruiter to find the best candidates and send messages to applicants or send an InMail to contact LinkedIn members who haven’t applied for your job but might be strong candidates.

Build your professional network

Your LinkedIn network is a professional directory made up of people you know and trust professionally. Building your network helps you stay in touch with alumni, colleagues, and recruiters, discover career opportunities, and engage with professionals in your industry.

As your network grows, you may see more relevant updates in your feed, identify professionals with shared interests, and learn about new roles, events, or industry trends.

Note: To ensure an optimal site experience, LinkedIn members can have a maximum of 30,000 1st-degree connections.

Ways to build your professional network

LinkedIn provides several opportunities to connect with people, depending on how you want to interact and build professional relationships.

Connect

Sending a connection invitation creates a 1st-degree connection. Once connected, members can message each other directly and see more information on each other’s profiles.

You may be asked to add a note to your invitation when sending an invitation.

When this is helpful
  • You’ve worked together before or share a professional context.
  • You want to start a direct conversation or collaborate.
  • You’re following up after a meeting or event.
Example
  • You send a connection invitation to a former teammate to stay in touch professionally.
  • You connect with a recruiter you spoke with at a hiring event to continue the conversation.

InMail messages

InMail message is a Premium feature that lets you send a message to a LinkedIn member you’re not connected to. This can help you introduce yourself professionally before sending a connection request.

If you have a Basic (free) account, you can only message members you’re already connected to.

When this is helpful
  • You want to explain your context before connecting.
  • You’re reaching out to someone outside your existing network.
  • You want to introduce yourself clearly before requesting a connection.
Example
  • You send an InMail message to a hiring manager about an open role before sending a connection invitation.
  • You introduce yourself to a potential collaborator before deciding whether to connect.

Follow

Following a member lets you see their posts, articles, and activity in your feed without sending a connection request. Following doesn’t create a 1st‑degree connection or enable direct messaging.

When this is helpful
  • You want to learn from someone’s posts before reaching out.
  • You’re interested in industry insights without starting a direct relationship.
  • You want to stay updated on professional content at your own pace.
Example
  • You follow an industry expert to learn about emerging trends.
  • You follow a company leader to stay updated on announcements and job opportunities.

Engaging with member content

You can interact with posts by reacting, commenting, or sharing them with your network. This helps you stay engaged in professional conversations and build visibility with other members.

Example
  • Comment on a post about a recent industry trend.
  • React to a colleague’s work anniversary update.

Joining LinkedIn Groups

Groups allow members with shared professional interests to participate in discussions, ask questions, and share knowledge with others.

Why this helps
  • Groups make it easier to meet professionals with similar goals.
  • Learn from others in your field.
  • Build connections around common interests without sending connection requests right away.
Example

You might join a group related to digital marketing to exchange ideas with other professionals or participate in conversations about new tools used in your industry.

Attending LinkedIn Events

Events provide opportunities to interact with other attendees before, during, or after the session.

Why this helps
  • Engaging with content helps you take part in professional conversations.
  • Show interest in topics you care about.
  • Become more visible to other members, often making future connections feel more natural and relevant.
Example
  • Comment on a post about a recent industry trend to share your perspective.
  • React to a colleague’s work anniversary update to stay connected.

Importing contacts

You can build your network by importing contacts from your mobile device. This helps LinkedIn suggest relevant connections and show updates from people you may know.

Why this helps
  • Makes it easier to reconnect with people you already trust.
  • Helps grow your network using existing professional relationships.
Example
  • You can import contacts to find former colleagues who are already on LinkedIn.

Alumni tab

The Alumni tab helps you find former classmates or alumni from specific schools or graduation years.

Why this helps
  • Alumni often share context that makes reaching out easier.
  • Helps you identify people with shared educational backgrounds.
Example
  • You explore alumni from your university who work in a field you’re interested in.

Search

Search lets you explore professionals by name, role, company, location, or industry.

Why this helps
  • Helps you find people relevant to your career goals.
  • Supports targeted networking instead of generic requests.
Example
  • You search for marketing managers to learn more about career paths in that role.
  • You search for professionals at a company you’re interested in working for.

Connect with people using a follow button on their profile

You should only invite people you know and trust to connect with you. If you see a Follow button on a member’s profile, you can still send them an invitation to connect if you know them.

Note: For some members with a Follow button, you may be prompted to enter the member’s email address to connect with them.

To connect with someone using a Follow button on their profile from your desktop:

  1. Navigate to the member’s profile page.

  2. Click the More button on their introduction section.

  3. Select Connect from the dropdown.

  4. From here, you might see any of these options:

    • Connect
    • Message
    • Follow
    • Add a note

  5. Follow prompts accordingly to connect.

Note: To help other members stay up to date with their frequent posts, some members on LinkedIn prefer to be followed. When you send an invitation to connect with someone whose primary action is Follow, you will immediately start following that person while you await their response.

To connect with someone using a Follow button on their profile:

  1. Navigate to the member’s profile page.
  2. Tap the More icon in the introduction section.
  3. Tap Connect.

To send a personalized invite:

  1. Navigate to the member’s profile page.
  2. Tap the More icon in the introduction section.
  3. Tap Personalize invite to include a personal message.
  4. Tap Send invitation.

Connections - Overview

On LinkedIn, the basic type of connection is a contact you know personally and who you trust on a professional level. Once you’ve “connected” to them on LinkedIn, you are considered a 1st-degree connection.

You also have an extended network of connections made up of people that your connections know. Your communication options for your extended network vary based on how closely connected you are. Here are some things you can to do with connections:

  • Connect with others by sending them an invitation, or by accepting their invitation to you. Learn more about invitations.

  • Control who sees your Connections List.

  • Interact with and learn more about your connections.

    • Send them messages
    • See their updates on your homepage

Here are some common concerns about connections:

  • Differences in connection counts
  • Missing connections
  • Removing a connection

Note: You can send emails directly from LinkedIn to people you’ve synced into your Contacts, even if they’re not a 1st-degree connection. Learn more about syncing contacts or sending messages.

Sometimes, all it takes is one connection to start your career journey. Read LinkedIn member Rutha Nuguse’s story about how she started her career in technology.

Connections who follow a LinkedIn Page

When you view a Page on LinkedIn, you can see the number of your LinkedIn connections who follow the Page. When you click or tap [Name] and [Number] other connections follow this page, a Connections following [Page] pop-up window displays a list of your connections who follow the Page.

Depending on the settings of your connections, you might see fewer people listed than the total number of connections. This is because members can set their preferences for whether their profile information is displayed in certain content on LinkedIn. As a result, you might see higher total numbers and less specific information listed at the individual profile level.

To control whether your profile information is displayed in the list of connections who follow a Page , you can adjust your settings.

Contact customer support from the LinkedIn Help Center

The LinkedIn Help Center contains resources, troubleshooting tips, and useful information to help you use our products. If you have additional questions, you can reach our customer support team through help assistant, our AI chat experience.

If you see something you believe may violate our policies, whether in profiles, posts, messages, comments, or anywhere else on LinkedIn, please report it to us by clicking the More icon in the upper-right corner of the content.

Important to know

We don’t offer a phone number for customer support. Some websites advertise LinkedIn phone support for a fee. These websites are in no way affiliated with LinkedIn, and we’re proactively working to take action against them. Keep in mind that we don’t charge for customer support, and we’ll never ask you for your password or access to your computer.

To contact our customer support team from the LinkedIn Help Center:

  1. Go to the LinkedIn Help Center.

  2. Sign in to your LinkedIn account. You must be signed in to your LinkedIn account to contact our customer support team.

  3. Scroll to the bottom of a Help Center article or the Help Center homepage and click Contact us, then click Chat with support.

    • Premium members - You can also click Start Chat on the right pane or at the bottom of the page.

  4. Ask your question or describe your issue in the chat window.

  5. After you ask your question, help assistant will:

    • Answer your question by summarizing information from trusted LinkedIn sources.
    • Provide a link for more information about your answer or the topic.
    • Ask follow-up questions to provide more personalized information or help you take action to complete a simple task when applicable.

  6. If you need additional help, you’ll be given options to connect to our support team.

Premium members can also speak to a live consultant from help assistant. Live chat is currently available in English, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, and Italian.

Delete imported contacts from LinkedIn

You can delete the contacts you’ve imported to LinkedIn at any time.

To delete your synced contacts:

  3. Under Syncing options, click Sync contacts.

  7. Tap Settings.

  8. Tap Account preferences.

  10. Tap Remove all next to Contacts.

Your contacts will be deleted immediately. Updates to suggestions may take up to 72 hours.

Follow a LinkedIn Page on behalf of your organization

As a super admin or a content admin of a LinkedIn Page, you can follow another organization’s Page. By increasing the number of Pages that your organization follows on LinkedIn, you will help establish your brand image on LinkedIn and increase your networking and engagement opportunities with industry players and business leaders.

Important to know

As a Page admin, if you follow another organization’s Page, then it implies that your organization is following the other organization on LinkedIn. This action is different from a member following an organization on LinkedIn.

You can view recommendations on Pages your organization could follow to increase your Page visibility. These recommendations are based on the information you provided when creating your Page and on the Pages followed by your Page followers. You can choose to follow Pages that are recommended to you, and you can also search for and follow a specific organization.

When you follow another organization’s Page, you can see and interact with posts from that Page from your Page admin view. These interactions are visible to your own Page followers which results in increased visibility of your Page, and can also influence an increase in your Page followers.

To follow another organization’s Page:

  1. Go to your Page super admin or content admin view.

  2. Click Settings in the left menu.

  3. Click Manage following.

  4. Click either the Following or Recommended tab.

    The Following tab displays all Pages that your Page is currently following. These are Pages that any other super admin or content admin of your Page chose to follow. The Recommended tab displays suggestions of Pages that are currently trending in your industry or Pages that your followers already follow.

  5. Click Add Pages to follow.

  6. Enter the name of the Page and select the correct Page.

  7. Click Done.

To follow another organization’s Page:

  1. Go to your Page super admin or content admin view.

  2. Tap Dashboard from the upper-left corner and select Feed from the dropdown.

  3. Tap Manage following or Find Pages to follow.

    To see suggestions of Pages to follow, click the Recommended tab. See Pages trending in your industry and Pages that your followers already follow.

  4. Tap Search for Page name….

  5. Enter the name of the Page and select the correct Page.

  6. Tap Done in the upper-right corner.

Follow an organization’s Page or a skills Page on LinkedIn

As a member on LinkedIn, you can search for and follow an organization’s LinkedIn Page or a skills Page. A LinkedIn Page is an organization’s brand or online presence on LinkedIn. A skills Page on LinkedIn allows users to follow updates and engage with content related to a specific professional skill such as Machine Learning, or Digital Marketing.

By following an organization’s LinkedIn Page, you get access to:

  • Networking opportunities – View and discover employees at the organization that you can connect with to expand your professional network.
  • Job opportunities – View and discover open roles at the organization and determine your next career move or gain insights into hiring trends at the organization.

By following a skills Page, you get access to:

  • Curated content for skills that you are specifically interested in
  • Networking opportunities with members interested in the same skills as you are
  • Exposure to industry trends for skills that you are interested in

You can follow up to 1,000 Pages and get updates on key information that’s posted. When you follow a Page, you’ll receive all posts shared by the Page in your homepage feed. Also, your public profile information will be visible to all Page admins. Information about Pages that you follow may be used to show you more relevant ads on LinkedIn. You can opt out of this by changing your advertising preferences.

To follow an organization’s Page or a skills Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Page or the skills Page.
  2. Click Follow.

To follow an organization’s Page or a skills Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Page or the skills Page.
  2. Tap Follow.

Follow and connect on LinkedIn

Following and connecting are two ways to build your professional network on LinkedIn. Following lets you learn from someone’s content, while connecting builds a two-way relationship.

Use the guidelines below when sending connection invitations:

  • Only send invitations to people you know and trust, in line with LinkedIn’s User Agreement and Professional Community Policies.
  • You can start by connecting with people you already know—such as colleagues, classmates, mentors, or volunteers.

Connect

Connections are members you know and trust. When you connect with someone, you both become first‑degree connections. This allows you to message each other directly and see each other’s posts and updates in your feeds.

Following

Following someone lets you see their public posts and articles in your feed without sending a connection invitation. When you follow someone, their content appears in your feed, but you don’t become part of their network and they won’t automatically see your posts. You can unfollow them at any time.

When to Connect vs Follow

  • If you: Know the person from work, school, or your community; Best action: Connect; Why: You already have a relationship and may want to message each other.
  • If you: Don’t know the person but enjoy their posts or insights; Best action: Follow; Why: You can stay informed without sending a connection invitation.
  • If you: Recently met someone at an event and want to stay in touch; Best action: Connect with a note; Why: A personalized note reminds them how you met and establishes context.
  • If you: Are exploring a new field and want to learn from others first; Best action: Follow; Why: Helps you identify thought leaders before reaching out.

If you see Follow instead of Connect on a profile

Some members have Follow set as their main profile action. If you choose to connect instead using the overflow menu, you’ll automatically follow them while your invitation is pending. If they decline your invitation, you’ll continue following them unless you manually unfollow.

Follow or Unfollow Member Articles

When a LinkedIn member becomes one of your connections (a 1st-degree connection), you automatically start following them and their activity.

Following a member lets you see their public posts, including articles they publish and other shared content such as videos and pictures, even if they’re not a connection. Their activity will appear on your LinkedIn homepage.

Note: Not all posts that you see on your LinkedIn feed are from members that you follow. You will see posts from other members that you are not following if one of your connections comments or shares their post.

To follow a member who’s publishing articles:

  1. Click on the article written by the member.

  2. Click Follow next to the member’s name.

    • This will change to Following.

If you’re unable to locate the article, you can visit the member’s profile and follow them for future articles.

To unfollow a member’s articles whom you’re not connected with, move your cursor over Following next to the member’s name and click Unfollow.

To follow a member who’s publishing articles:

  1. Navigate to the member’s article.
  2. Tap Follow next to the member’s name.

To unfollow the member’s articles whom you’re not connected with, tap the Following button in the member’s profile and then tap Unfollow.

To follow a member who’s publishing articles:

To unfollow the member’s articles whom you’re not connected with, tap FOLLOWING in the member’s profile and it changes to FOLLOW.

If you’re connected to a person and choose to unfollow them, you’ll remain connected but won’t see their updates in your feed. They won’t be notified you’ve unfollowed them.

Follow or unfollow people

When you follow someone, new content posted or shared by the person will be displayed in your feed. If you no longer wish to see the content of someone in your feed, you can always unfollow this person.

You can find people to follow from your feed, the Notifications tab, My Network page, or from the Search bar at the top of the page.

Unfollowing a person will hide all updates from them on your LinkedIn feed. If you’re connected to a person and choose to unfollow them, you’ll remain connected, but won’t see their updates. They won’t be notified that you’ve unfollowed them. LinkedIn members will receive a notification if you begin following them again.

Note: You can also follow people, companies, or topics by navigating directly to My Network page, which displays recommended sources to follow.

To follow a person, click Follow on their profile page. If you don’t see a Follow button:

  1. Click More or the More button in the introduction section of the person’s profile.

  2. Select Follow from the dropdown.

    • Select Unfollow from the dropdown to unfollow.

Note:

  • Members can follow up to 5,000 people who aren’t connections.

To unfollow a person from your feed:

  1. Click the More icon on the upper right of the post.
  2. Click Unfollow [name] from the list.

To follow or unfollow a person from the People I Follow page:

  1. Click the My Network icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click People I Follow, under Manage my network, on the left pane.

  3. Click Follow under the person’s name to follow the person.

    Note: This will change to Following indicating that you now follow the person.

  4. Click Following under the person’s name to unfollow the person.

    Note: This will change to Follow indicating that you no longer follow the person.

To follow a person after previously unfollowing:

  1. Click the  Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Under the Account preferences > Site preferences section, click People you unfollowed.
  4. Click Follow next to the person’s name to follow the person.

To follow a person, tap Follow on their profile page. If you don’t see a Follow button:

  1. Tap More or the ** More** button in the introduction section of the person’s profile.

  2. Select Follow from the dropdown.

    • Select Unfollow from the dropdown to unfollow.

To unfollow a person from your feed:

  1. Tap the / More icon on the upper right of the post.
  2. Tap Unfollow [name] from the list.

To unfollow a person from the People I Follow page:

  1. Tap the My Network icon below the LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Tap Manage my network > People I follow.
  3. Tap the / More icon next to the person’s name.
  4. Tap Unfollow [name].

To follow a person after previously unfollowing:

  1. Tap your profile photo > Settings.
  2. Tap Account preferences.
  3. Under the Site preferences section, tap People you unfollowed.
  4. Tap Follow next to the person’s name to follow the person.

Invitation limits for your LinkedIn Page

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can grow your followers by inviting members to follow your Page. You can invite your 1st-degree connections or, with a Premium Company Page subscription, you can invite followers of similar Pages or people who interacted with your Page’s content.

Pages are granted monthly invitation credits which are shared across all admins of the Page. The invitation credit limit renews on the first day of every month.

Important to know

We are changing the available invitation credits for free Pages and Premium Company Pages. This change is gradually being made available and you might not have access to it right now.

You can view your available invitation credits by clicking Invite connections in the upper-right corner of your admin view. Your balance appears at the top of the window. As your Page and network grow, you might see the number of available invitations increase. If you notice that credits in your usual balance are missing, it might be that the recipient declined or ignored the invitation. Since credits are shared with all other admins, it’s also possible that another admin on your Page used the credits.

How invitation credits are used and earned:

  • Sending an invitation uses one credit.
  • When an invitation is accepted, the credit is earned back and applied back to the Page’s balance. It can take up to 72 hours for the credit to reflect in the Page’s balance.
  • When an invitation is rejected or withdrawn, the credit is removed from Page’s balance.
  • Automatic invitations to people who engage with your content don’t use invitation credits (only available with a Premium Company Page subscription).
  • If you’ve exhausted your invitation credits for the month, you won’t be able to invite members to follow your Page. In this situation, you can either wait for the credit limit to be renewed next month, or you can upgrade to Premium Company Page, if eligible, to access a higher number of monthly invitation credits.

Invitations to follow a LinkedIn Page

You can grow the followers of a Page by inviting your 1st-degree connections to follow the Page. With a Premium Company Page subscription, you can also invite non-connections, including followers of similar Pages and people who engaged with your content. We recommend that Pages have at least 150 followers to help optimize growth, and invitations can help you reach your follower goals.

The person who receives the invitation can see the name of the person who sent the invite, except for auto-invites to people who engaged with your content.

[Image: invite to follow]

Members can opt out of receiving invitations to follow Pages from their Data Privacy settings. Members can also turn off invitation notifications from their notification settings.

Pages you manage

To invite connections to follow a Page that you manage, you must be a super or content admin. There are three ways to invite people to follow your Page:

  • 1st-degree connections – We recommend only inviting connections who are likely to be interested in the Page.
  • Followers of similar Pages (Premium Company Page only) – Invite members who follow Pages like yours, including Pages in your industry, near your location, and with a similar number of employees. We’re gradually making this feature available, and you might not have access to it at this time.
  • Content engagers (Premium Company Page only) – Automatically invite members who engage with your content, including members who publicly reacted, commented on, or shared your Page’s posts in the past 30 days.

Pages are granted monthly invitation credits which are shared across all admins of the Page. Auto-invites to content engagers don’t use any credits.

Important to know

We are changing the available invitation credits for free Pages and Premium Company Pages. This change is gradually being made available and you might not have access to it right now.

Your employer’s Page

If you aren’t an admin of a Page, you can invite up to 30 of your 1st-degree connections to follow your employer’s Page each month.

Other Pages

If you aren’t the admin or employee of a Page, you can invite up to 50 of your 1st-degree connections each month to follow Pages that have fewer than 5,000 followers.

Here’s a tip

If you’ve exhausted your invitation credits for the month, you won’t be able to invite members to follow your Page. In this situation, you can either wait for the credit limit to be renewed next month, or you can upgrade to Premium Company Page, if eligible, to access a higher number of monthly invitation credits. When someone accepts your invitation, that credit is returned to your balance.

Invite connections to follow your LinkedIn Page

As a super admin or content admin of your LinkedIn Page, you can grow your follower base by inviting your 1st-degree connections and other members to follow your Page. The invitation will include your name, so members know who sent the invite. We recommend that you only send Page invitations to members who are likely to be interested in your Page.

Pages are granted monthly invitation credits which are shared across all admins of the Page. The invitation credit limit renews on the first day of every month. We are changing the available invitation credits for free Pages and Premium Company Pages. This change is gradually being made available and you might not have access to it right now.

If you’ve exhausted your invitation credits for the month, you won’t be able to invite members to follow your Page. In this situation, you can either wait for the credit limit to be renewed next month, or you can upgrade to Premium Company Page, if eligible, to access a higher number of monthly invitation credits.

Before you begin

  1. You should have added details for the following fields for your Page:

    • Overview
    • Industry
    • Company size

    You can add information for these fields by clicking Edit Page from your super admin view, and then clicking the Details option.

  2. If you have added language support for your Page, and if you haven’t already, you must enter information in the Description field for all languages that your Page is available in.

Important to know

This feature isn’t available to Pages that have more than 100,000 followers on LinkedIn.

To send an invitation to your connections:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Click Invite to follow in the left menu.

    You may see Unlock invites if you have not filled out all of the required sections (Industry, Company size, or Overview) for your LinkedIn Page. You must also have a minimum number of connections to send invitations. Once the required sections of your LinkedIn Page are complete, and you have enough LinkedIn profile connections, you will see the Invite to follow feature in the left menu.

  3. Complete one or more of the following:

    • Search for a connection using the Search by name field.
    • Use the filters to focus your search.

Invite followers of similar Pages to follow your LinkedIn Page

With a LinkedIn Premium Company Page subscription, you can grow your followers by inviting members who currently follow Pages similar to yours, including Pages in your industry, near your location, and with a similar number of employees. We recommend that Pages have at least 150 followers to help optimize growth, and invitations to followers of similar Pages can help you reach your follower goals.

Who can use this feature?

We’re gradually making this feature available, and you might not have access to it at this time. Invitations to followers of similar Pages are only available to super admins with a LinkedIn Premium Company Page subscription. Without a subscription, you can only invite 1st-degree connections.

To invite members who follow similar Pages:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Click Invite to followin the left menu.

  3. Click the Connections dropdown and select Followers of similar Pages.

  4. Complete one or more of the following:

    • Select the checkbox next to members from the populated list.
    • Use the filters to focus your search.

Here’s a tip

Click Auto-Invite content engagers to automatically invite people who interacted with your content in the past 30 days. Automatic invitations are only available with a Premium Company Page subscription. 5. Click Invite.

To invite members who follow similar Pages:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Tap Dashboardfrom the upper-left corner and select Share pagefrom the dropdown.

  3. Tap Invite connections.

  4. Tap the Connections dropdown and select Followers of similar Pages.

  5. Complete one or more of the following:

    • Select the checkbox next to members from the populated list.
    • Tap the Filter icon to focus your search.

  6. Tap the Review invites button.

  7. Tap the Invite button.

After you send the invite, your connections will receive a notification. The invite will come from your personal LinkedIn profile.

Sending invites to followers of similar Pages uses your monthly invitation limit credits, which are shared across all admins of the Page. If an error appears, you might have reached your invitation limit.

LinkedIn Page Follow button

Any company, university, or high school with a LinkedIn Page can add a Follow button to their website, making it easier to grow their Page follower base. When members click the Follow button, they automatically follow that company, university, or high school on LinkedIn.

Organizations can engage with members from their LinkedIn Page and through Page posts. Page posts appear on followers’ LinkedIn feed and on your Page.

You can build a LinkedIn Page Follow button for your website using our developer resources, and you can learn how to increase your LinkedIn Page follower base through Page analytics or the Invite Connections tool.

LinkedIn Pages features for admins and followers

LinkedIn Pages are a platform for organizations to post industry updates, job opportunities, information about life at their organization, and much more. Pages can be used by admins and followers when signed in to LinkedIn.com on desktop and mobile devices.

Admins

As an admin of a Page, you can access the features below depending on the type of admin access you have.

  • Admin feature: Admin view (Page admin); Benefit: Manage Page components directly from your Page.
  • Admin feature: Admin view (paid media admin); Benefit: Interact with a Page through leads, analytics, and ads.
  • Admin feature: Post, edit, and sponsor posts; Benefit: Engage with your followers to create community.
  • Admin feature: Edit Page information; Benefit: Maintain an accurate brand presence.
  • Admin feature: View Page analytics; Benefit: Analyze how followers and employees are interacting with your brand and content.
  • Admin feature: Create Showcase and Product Pages; Benefit: Exhibit your organization’s brand, business units, initiatives, and products.
  • Admin feature: Manage Life Pages; Benefit: Maintain an accurate portrayal of company culture and available jobs.
  • Admin feature: Post job opportunities; Benefit: Provide available role insight for your followers.
  • Admin feature: View Landing Pages leads and analytics; Benefit: Keep a pulse on candidates who’ve indicated interest from your Landing Page.
  • Admin feature: Create Sponsored Content ads; Benefit: Boost a post to members’ feeds in your target audience.
  • Admin feature: Receive messages from members; Benefit: Enable the messaging button to allow members to send messages to your Page. Messaging is currently only available for certain Pages, and will gradually be made available to all Pages.

Members

LinkedIn.com members can follow organizations to gain access to the features below.

  • Follower feature: Posts in your homepage feed; Benefit: View and engage with content posted such as product releases and industry news.
  • Follower feature: View employees; Benefit: Engage with current employees to build your network and get an inside look at the organization.
  • Follower feature: Affiliated, Showcase, and Product Pages; Benefit: Discover and explore related organizations, brands, business units, initiatives, and products.
  • Follower feature: Jobs tab; Benefit: Explore available job opportunities.
  • Follower feature: Life tab (optional); Benefit: A look into an organization’s culture.
  • Follower feature: Alumni (Pages for schools); Benefit: Explore information about their alumni such as location, skills, and occupation.
  • Follower feature: Additional insights (Premium members); Benefit: Gain an understanding of headcount growth and allocation, notable alumni, and total job openings.
  • Follower feature: Message a Page; Benefit: If a Page has messaging enabled, send a message to the admins of the Page.
  • Follower feature: Stock Ticker; Benefit: When a company trades on the NYSE and NASDAQ exchange it will show a stock ticker on their Page.

Manage who can follow you settings

While your 1st-degree connections automatically follow your posts and articles, anyone can follow you, even if they’re not in your network. You can limit followers to only your 1st-degree connections from the Settings & Privacy page. You can also opt to make Follow the primary action members see when they view your account.

To update your settings:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.

  3. Select Visibility on the left pane.

  4. Under the Visibility of your LinkedIn activity section, click Followers.

  5. In the Who can follow you section, select one of the following options:

    • Everyone on LinkedIn - All LinkedIn members can follow your updates. This option also enables your posts to be shared off of LinkedIn.
    • Your connections - Only your 1st-degree connections can follow your updates.

  6. Under the Make follow primary section:

    • Turn on the toggle to display Follow as the primary action for members viewing your profile
    • Turn off the toggle to display Connect as the primary action for members viewing your profile

To update your settings:

  1. Tap your profile picture, then tap Settings.

  2. Tap the Visibility tab.

  3. Tap Followers in the Visibility of your LinkedIn activity section.

  4. In the Who can follow you screen, select one of the following options:

    • Everyone on LinkedIn - All LinkedIn members can follow your updates. This option also enables your posts to be shared off of LinkedIn.
    • Your connections - Only your connections can follow your updates.

  5. Under the Make follow primary section:

    • Turn on the toggle to display Follow as the primary action for members viewing your profile
    • Turn off the toggle to display Connect as the primary action for members viewing your profile

Notes:

  • If you limit followers to your connections, followers outside your network will be removed and your follower number will be the same as your total connections.

  • Once you select Your connections, there will no longer be a Follow button next to your posts or articles.

  • Changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

Missing connect button on profile

You won’t see the Connect button on a member’s profile if:

  • You haven’t confirmed your primary email, the email bounced, or new email needs confirmation.
  • You’re already connected to that member.
  • You’ve already sent the member a connection request.
  • You have over 500 connections. By default, the Connect button will be replaced with Follow and it’ll appear in the dropdown when you click the More button in your introduction card.
  • You’ve selected Follow as the default option instead of Connect.
  • You’re out of network.

Note: InMail messages allows you to send a direct message to a member you aren’t connected to within your network. If you have a Basic (free) account, you must upgrade to a Premium account to use InMail credits. If you have a Premium account and want more InMail message credits than the number you’ve been allotted, you can always purchase up to 10 more.

Network size limit

LinkedIn members can have up to 30,000 1st-degree connections. To ensure an optimal experience on LinkedIn, we recommend:

  • Connect with people you know personally and trust professionally
  • Follow anyone whose posts you want to keep up with, so you always stay informed

While there is a limit to the number of 1st-degree connections you can have, the number of people who can follow you (and who you can follow) is unlimited. People who follow you can view, like, or comment on what you share publicly.

If you have reached 30,000 connections, Follow will become the default option on your profile. You will not be able to accept or send new connection invitations unless you remove connections to keep network size under the limit.

Personalize invitations to connect

Adding a short, thoughtful message to your connection request helps you explain who you are and why you’re reaching out. This can help the recipient decide whether to accept your request.

Adding a message helps you:

  • Explain who you areand why you’re reaching out
  • Build trust when connecting with someone you don’t know yet
  • Stand out from generic requests

Invitation limits

  • You can add a personalized message to up to three connection requests per month
  • Each message can be up to 200 characters
  • LinkedIn Premium members can send unlimited personalized invitations to all their connection requests (connection request limits may still apply)

Why personalize a connection invitation

This is especially useful if you’re growing your network, exploring new roles, or reconnecting with people outside your immediate circle.

What to include in your message

Keep your message short and specific. A good personalized invitation usually includes:

  • How you found the person or what you have in common
  • Why you’d like to connect now
  • A clear and polite tone

For example, you might reference a shared role, event, group, or post you found helpful. This helps the recipient quickly understand the context of your request.

Add a personalized message to a connection invitation

To add a message to an invitation:

  1. Navigate to the profile of the member you’d like to connect with.
  2. Select Connect in the introduction section.
  3. Click Add a note.
  4. Add your personalized message in the text field.
  5. Select Send invitation.

To add a message to an invitation:

  1. Navigate to the profile of the member you’d like to connect with.
  2. Tap the More icon in the top section of the member’s profile.
  3. Tap Personalize Invite.
  4. Enter your personalized invitation message.
  5. Tap Send Invitation.
Here’s a tip

If you’re having trouble sending personalized invitations, try updating the LinkedIn mobile app to the most current version.

If the recipient replies to your message or accepts your invitation, the conversation appears in your messages.

Important to know:

  • If the recipient replies to your message, it will appear in your messages.
  • When you select We don’t know each other, you may be prompted to send a message before the invitation is sent.
  • Invitations sent from People You May Know on the LinkedIn mobile app can’t be personalized.
  • A primary email address is mandatory to send invitations.
  • If the recipient responds to your message, they can reply without accepting your invitation.

These limits help ensure outreach remains thoughtful and relevant.

Remove a connection on LinkedIn

You can remove a connection:

  • By visiting their LinkedIn profile.
  • From your Connections page.

Important: Connections you remove will no longer be 1st-degree connections and won’t appear in your Contacts section.

To remove a connection from their profile page:

  1. Navigate to the connection’s profile.
  2. Click More or the ** More** button in the introduction section.
  3. Select Remove Connection.

Note: Once you select Remove Connection, the status will change to Connection Removed.

To remove a connection from your Connections page:

  1. Click the My Network icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Under your profile name, click the link that displays the number of connections you have. For example, click on 465 connections.

  4. Click Remove from the Remove Connection pop-up window.

To remove a connection:

  1. Go to the profile of the member you’d like to remove.
  2. Tap the More button or the ** More** icon.
  3. Tap Remove connection > Remove connection in the pop-up window to confirm.

Notes:

  • When you remove a connection, they won’t be notified.
  • After removing a connection, any recommendations or endorsements between you and that person will be withdrawn. They will not be restored if the connection is reestablished.

Requests to duplicate followers or migrate associated members for your LinkedIn Page

After you rebrand or merge duplicate Pages, you can duplicate your followers or migrate associated members to the new Page.

At LinkedIn, member experience is our top priority, and our policies are designed to protect member trust. We can’t approve requests that would significantly change information provided by a member or modify an action taken by a member in a way that deviates from their original intentions without their expressed acknowledgment or approval.

Approved follower duplication requests include:

  • Creating a new Page for the same organization that represents the same entity and its primary purpose is to reflect the organization’s rebrand.

  • Consolidating duplicate or regional Pages for an organization with a large number of associated members.  

    Pages with a small number of associated members won’t be approved for Page merges, but they might be approved for follower duplication. As an alternative, we recommend deactivating your duplicate or regional Pages.

  • Merging duplicate Pages for a university, including Pages for universities that represent schools, departments, or campuses of the same university and not partners or affiliations.

Unapproved follower duplication and associated member migration requests include:

  • Associated member migration to a new Page due to a rebrand, acquisition, or merger.
  • Follower duplication to a new Page due to a business or subsidiary merger or acquisition.

To request a follower duplication or associated member migration, please contact us with the following information:

  • The name and URL of your original Page.
  • The name and URL of your rebranded or duplicate Page.
  • The URL of the press release or other material verifying that your followers should be duplicated or your associated members should be migrated.

Respond to LinkedIn Events invitations

To attend a LinkedIn Event, you must have received an invitation from the organizer or an attendee. You can only be invited by your 1st-degree connections. You can also visit an Event’s URL (after it has been shared with you) or find an Event to attend via LinkedIn.

An invitee can choose to respond to an invitation by accepting or ignoring the invite. An invitee who accepts an invitation is labeled as an attendee. As an attendee, you can also invite your connections to attend the Event.

To accept or ignore an Event invitation:

  1. Click the My Network icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • Any pending invitations will be displayed at the top of the page.

  2. Navigate to the Event invitation.

  3. Click Accept or Ignore.

To add an additional reminder for the event you want to attend, you can do any of the following:

  • Download the .ics attachment in the confirmation email you receive after accepting an invitation and add it to your preferred calendar.
  • Click on any of your preferred Add to calendar options in the confirmation email.

To accept or ignore an Event invitation:

  1. Tap the My Network tab in the navigation bar.

    • Pending invitations are displayed at the top of the page.

  2. Navigate to the Event invitation.

  3. Click Accept or Ignore.

If you decide to ignore the invitation, you will be declining your attendance and won’t be able to modify your decision. The organizer won’t be notified if you decide to ignore the invitation.

To adjust notifications sent to your network about profile changes:

Important:

Stopping Invitation Emails to Join LinkedIn

You may receive invitations to join LinkedIn . Here’s what to do if you wish not to receive these invitations.

If you’re not a LinkedIn member and want to stop getting invitation emails to join LinkedIn, unsubscribe here or click the Unsubscribe link in the footer of that email.

Some members receive invitations to join LinkedIn although they are already a member. Often times this happens if you have a second email such as a work or personal email. If you are receiving invitations to join LinkedIn sent to an email address not on your LinkedIn account, you have two options.

  • Option 1 (Recommended): You can add that email address as a secondary email to your account. You’ll stop receiving guest invitations to join LinkedIn to that email address, but receive any invitations to join as connection requests.
  • Option 2: You can unsubscribe the other email address. When you unsubscribe from LinkedIn email communications, you will stop receiving invitations from LinkedIn.

Learn more about managing the type and frequency of email you receive from LinkedIn.
