Various ways to connect with people on LinkedIn

Building your LinkedIn network helps you stay in touch with colleagues, alumni, and recruiters, and discover new professional opportunities.

Sending a connection invitation creates a 1st‑degree connection. As 1st‑degree connections, you can message each other and see more information on each other’s profiles. Connecting works best when you have a clear professional reason to reach out, such as having worked or studied together, meeting at an event, or wanting to continue a conversation.

To connect on LinkedIn, you can send or accept invitations from several places:

  • From a member’s profile: Select Connect on their profile page. If you don’t see Connect (for example, if Follow is the primary option), select More and then select Connect.
  • From People you may know: Review suggested connections and select Connect below a member’s name. If you don’t see Connect (for example, if Follow is the primary option), select More and then select Connect.
  • From My Network: Go to My Network and accept pending invitations from people who want to connect with you.

Important to know:

  • You can add up to 30,000 1st-degree connections.
  • You need a primary email address to send connection invitations.
  • Your LinkedIn account may be temporarily restricted from sending invitations if members report your invitations as unwanted or spam.
  • When you send a connection request, you may be asked How do you know [member name]? If you select We don’t know each other, you may be prompted to send a message first to establish a relationship. Depending on the recipient’s messaging settings, this could include sending an InMail message.
  • Messaging access depends on your connection status and the recipient’s messaging settings.

Your Network and Degrees of Connection

Your network on LinkedIn is made up of your 1st-degree, 2nd-degree, and 3rd-degree connections, as well as your followers and fellow members of your LinkedIn groups. You can build your network by sending invitations to connect with other LinkedIn members and your contacts you’ve imported or by accepting invites from others. The degree of connection you have with another member affects how you can interact with them on LinkedIn.

Note: To ensure an optimal site experience, LinkedIn members can have a maximum of 30,000 1st-degree connections. Learn more about LinkedIn’s network size limit.

1st-degree connections - People you’re directly connected to because you’ve accepted their invitation to connect, or they’ve accepted your invitation. You’ll see a 1st degree icon next to their name in search results and on their profile. You can contact them by sending a message on LinkedIn.

2nd-degree connections - People who are connected to your 1st-degree connections. You’ll see a 2nd degree icon next to their name in search results and on their profile. You can send them an invitation by clicking the Connect button on their profile page.

3rd-degree connections - People who are connected to your 2nd-degree connections. You’ll see a 3rd degree icon next to their name in search results and on their profile.

Followers - People who choose to follow your public updates in their LinkedIn feed, subject to your settings.

Fellow members of your LinkedIn Groups - People who are considered part of your network because you’re members of the same group. The Highlights section of a member profile may display the groups you’re both a part of. You can contact them by sending a message on LinkedIn or directly through the group.

LinkedIn Member (Out of Network) - LinkedIn members who fall outside the categories listed above. Some fields of profiles out of your network have limited visibility as described here, but you can build your network with other valuable connections to see more profiles. If the option is available, you can also send them an InMail to introduce yourself.

Add your organization’s email domain to control job posting permissions

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can add email domains that you own (such as yourcompany.com) to your Page to control access to job posting. When you add a domain, people can only post a job with your Page as the associated company if they verify that they have an email address with the domain you added (such as name@yourcompany.com). AI interviews in LinkedIn Hiring Pro

AI interview enables hirers to invite top applicants to complete an audio or video (if available) screening call with an AI interviewer as a first step of the interview process. It is an early-stage LinkedIn Hiring Pro Jobs feature. The interview is generated based on the role’s qualifications and includes AI-recommended questions and ideal answers, which the hirer can review and edit before sending to applicants.

How it works

  • Hirers can select up to 40 applicants to receive an AI screening interview invitation.
  • The draft interview is designed using AI-generated questions and expected ideal responses based on the job description.
  • Hirers should review and edit both the questions and the ideal answers before sending.
  • Hirers choose who to invite and send the interview link via LinkedIn Messaging.
  • Candidates can choose to take a practice interview or to complete the hirer’s voice-based or video-based AI screening interview at their convenience.
  • Candidate answers are evaluated based on alignment with the hirer’s ideal answers.
  • Hirers receive a transcript of the candidates’ AI screening interviews, AI-generated summaries and ratings, along with the audio or video recording.
  • Hirers then decide which candidates to invite to the next stage of their recruitment process.

How hirers access and use the feature

To set up AI screening interviews, select Edit questions from your Hiring Plan. We’ll use your job post and AI to suggest questions and ideal responses, which are used for ratings (see below). Make sure to review and edit the questions and responses.

To invite applicants to take an AI screening interview, navigate to your applicant list and select Interview with AI. We’ll suggest language for an InMail message to send the applicant inviting them to participate. Make sure to review and edit the message, as you may be required by law to include certain information, such as privacy notices or instructions for requesting an accommodation. Note that AI screening interviews are optional for applicants, and they will not be automatically disqualified if they decide not to participate.

How to turn on Hiring Pro-led invites

Hiring Pro can proactively send invitations to selected applicants to complete an AI screening interview, helping you engage strong candidates early.

Top-fit and shortlisted applicants

Hiring Pro can send AI interview invitations to a limited set of applicants based on how they match your job criteria and actions you take. If you turn on Hiring Pro top-fit and shortlist invites during your job set up:

  • Invitations may be sent starting 1 day after your job is posted, via messages from the LinkedIn team. The message will include an invitation from you and will link to your profile.
  • To view the message template, navigate to the AI interview setting page and click “View invite message.”

Hiring Pro will invite up to 20 applicants, prioritized in the following order:

  1. Candidates you have manually shortlisted
  2. Candidates you have marked as Top Fit
  3. Top Fit applicants who meet all of your must-have qualifications

Shortlisted applicants only

Turn on shortlist invites to allow Hiring Pro to send AI interview invitations as soon as you shortlist an applicant. After you click Shortlist on an applicant’s profile, some hirers will see the option to enable Hiring Pro shortlist invites. Once enabled, any applicant you shortlist will receive an AI interview invitation, which is sent from your LinkedIn messages. You can review the sent invitation by navigating to the message thread with the applicant.

Note: Hiring Pro-led invites is available to a limited group of users. You can turn on or turn off Hiring Pro-led invites at any time, within the AI interview settings page. Only one invite type can be selected at a time.

Where to find interview status

Once an interview invite has been sent, the status is included within the applicant list.

“Created AI screening Xm ago” appears when the hirer has sent an AI screening interview to an applicant.

[Image: created AI screening]

“Completed AI screening Xm ago” appears with an AI screening rating, for interviews that have been completed by the applicant and are ready to be reviewed by the hirer.

[Image: completed AI screening]

What hirers receive after screening interview

Once the candidate completes the AI screening interview, you receive the full transcript and the audio or video recording, along with AI-generated summaries and a 5-point rating based on your ideal responses. As the hirer, you are responsible for reviewing and verifying all AI-generated information before making any hiring decisions. Candidates may contact you to request an accommodation, or to access their rating, summaries, transcript, or recording. You retain full control over evaluation and can decide how to proceed with each candidate.

How interview ratings work

Ratings are determined by using AI to analyze the applicant’s interview transcript. The overall rating provided to the hirer is the average rating of the applicant’s responses to each of your questions. Each of the applicant’s responses is rated on the following criteria:

  • Its match to the hirer’s ideal response
  • Whether the applicant supported it with details, such as evidence and examples
  • Whether it was clear, concise, and well structured

Note that as the hirer, you may have legal obligations associated with AI screening interviews and ratings, and are responsible for final hiring decisions. We encourage you to review the candidates’ AI interview transcripts or recordings, in addition to the ratings and summaries, before making any decision on candidate advancement.

If you prefer not to receive candidate ratings, you can turn them off and still receive an interview summary without a numerical rating or agentic recommendation. To update this preference, go to the AI Interview module on the Hiring Plan page and select AI Interview Settings. On the settings page, you’ll find an option to turn off AI-generated applicant ratings.

Important to know

Like other generative AI features, the AI screening interview outputs may be inaccurate. We have taken several steps to reduce inaccuracy, but AI responses and summaries should be reviewed closely.

Hirers should ensure that their interview questions are job-relevant and follow our Professional Community Policies. We recommend avoiding questions that request sensitive information from members.

Can candidates access interview ratings?

No. Candidates don’t automatically receive interview ratings, transcripts, or interview summaries. They can request access by contacting the hirer directly.

How AI screening interviews and practice interviews process candidates’ (members’) data

AI screening interviews need to process candidates’ personal data on behalf of the hirer in order to record candidates that choose to use the feature, and facilitate and analyze the interview conversation. More information about how personal data is collected, generated and shared for AI Interviews follows:

  • Interview Content. Personal data is recorded by LinkedIn on behalf of the hirer during an AI screening interview, including candidate image (if their camera is on) and verbal responses. Candidate verbal responses are processed with AI to facilitate the conversation. Candidates can take steps to limit the personal data by the nature of their responses and by participating in AI interviews in a private environment free of audio or video from others.
  • Interview Insights. Personal data is generated about the AI screening interview, including date, time, length of interview, and interview transcript, which is used to create AI-generated ratings and summaries of the interview (see more above on the rating).

How is data processed by the hirer and LinkedIn under GDPR

  • AI Interviews: Hirers are the data controller of applicant AI Interviews; LinkedIn is a data processor on behalf of the hirer. AI screening interviews are a service that hirers instruct LinkedIn to provide. Under GDPR, hirers are the “controllers” or the responsible party for personal data generated during the AI screening interview. Candidates can contact the hirer or refer to their privacy notices for information about the hirer’s use and processing of personal data, to request an accommodation or to exercise your data protection rights.

    Recordings and transcripts are shared with the hiring manager for applicant evaluation and review. The LinkedIn team may use automated or human review of interview transcripts or recordings for quality assurance and product improvement purposes.

  • Practice Interviews: LinkedIn is the data controller for practice interviews. Personal data generated during practice interview sessions is used by LinkedIn to provide the service and help us improve the AI interview product and experience in line with our Privacy Policy. Note: LinkedIn does not provide hirers any information about practice interviews of candidates. If candidates do not want us to use this information to train GAI models that generate content, they can choose to opt-out through this setting.

AI screening interviews leverage generative AI models to be able to suggest questions and ideal answers, engage with the candidates in the interview and generate the ratings and summaries shared with a hirer. LinkedIn assesses and uses a variety of generative AI models to enable its products so that it can seek to continually improve its products. For this product, LinkedIn may use Microsoft’s Azure OpenAI API service to power the feature. Member inputs are processed by LinkedIn using the Microsoft service, but are not accessed by Microsoft or OpenAI except by Microsoft in circumstances described here.

How is LinkedIn ensuring AI content won’t include any discriminatory, abusive, or biased content?

LinkedIn strives to ensure that its products and services are fair, including by measuring and mitigating algorithmic bias. Our objective is to ensure equally qualified members receive equal treatment by our models. As with all our products, our teams continuously assess our systems, and if harmful biases are identified, we will work to address them.

What are LinkedIn’s Responsible AI Principles?

AI is not new to LinkedIn. LinkedIn has long used AI to enhance our members’ professional experiences. By leveraging the power of AI, we help our members connect, increase productivity, and achieve success in their careers. 

Inspired by, and aligned with, Microsoft’s leadership in Responsible AI, LinkedIn applies Responsible AI Principles that we use to guide our work.

Your LinkedIn job posts will remain active until you manually close them or after 6 months when they’ll be automatically closed. Additionally, the job post will automatically pause if a total budget is set and met. Billing for your post will continue until the job has been closed. You can close your job post by clicking the Close job button on the Job Info page of that job post.

Important to know

You can repost a job as a new post but once a job is closed, it can’t be reopened. When you repost a job that has been closed, this will create a new job post. All applicant information gathered previously will only be associated with the closed job post.

Important to know

Job posts cannot be deleted. They can only be closed.

To close your job post:

  1. Click the Jobs icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click Manage job posts.
  3. Find the job you wish to close and click the More icon to the right of the title.
  4. Click the Close job button.
  5. Confirm you’d like to proceed with closing the job by Close job.

To close your job post:

  1. Tap the Jobs icon.
  2. Tap the More icon next to the search bar.
  3. Tap Manage job posts.
  4. Find the job you wish to close and tap the More icon to the right of the title.
  5. Tap Manage Job.
  6. Tap the Close job button.
  7. Confirm you’d like to proceed with closing the job by tapping Close job.

Once you close a job post:

  • The post will be removed from search results.
  • Applicants will no longer be able to apply to the job post.
  • You will still be able to review the applicant list for the closed job post if you chose to collect the applications on LinkedIn. However, if you chose to route applicants through an external URL or applicant tracking system, the applicant list for the closed job will not be visible on LinkedIn.

Important to know

If the charges for a current job are unable to be processed for any reason, the job will be closed automatically.

Create and share a job post via #Hiring on LinkedIn

Share that you’re #Hiring

You can share that you’re hiring with your network and add the #Hiring frame to your profile photo.

Add or manage the #Hiring frame

You can create and share a new job post or share an existing job post associated with your organization’s LinkedIn Page from your homepage or profile using the #Hiring feature.

Here are some important things to keep in mind:

  • When you create or share a job from your profile, we’ll add the #Hiring photo frame to your profile, feature your profile on the job post’s Meet the team section, and notify your network that you’re hiring so they can also share the job with their own networks.

  5. Edit the auto-populated text, if necessary.

  6. Click Post.

  2. Click View profile.
  3. Click Open to below your profile photo.
  4. In the drop-down that appears, select Hiring.
  5. Click Add to profile to add the job and the #Hiring photo frame to your profile.

To share that you’re hiring:

  1. Tap Post > Share that you’re hiring > Select company.

  2. For existing jobs, select a job from the list.

  3. For new jobs, tap Create new job and enter the Job title, Location, Employment type, and Job description (optional).

    • The job title must be selected from the menu of options that appear once you start typing.
    • The location will be auto-populated to your current location, but can be changed.

  4. Edit the auto-populated text, if necessary.

  5. Tap Next and Post job.

Differences between free and promoted jobs

Ready to post a job now?

You can post your job on LinkedIn and get matched with qualified candidates.

Post a job now

LinkedIn makes it easy to post jobs quickly and reach a wide network of professionals, including those who aren’t actively looking. You can choose between free or promoted posts to target the right candidates and fill roles efficiently.

Here’s a tip

Hirers can now promote their jobs directly from both iOS and Android devices.

Free jobs

  • One free job at a time over 30 days.
  • Appear in search results and are searchable on LinkedIn.
  • Allow you to collect applicants on LinkedIn, and easily filter and manage your applicants.
  • Will be paused after being active for 14 days. You can promote your job to make it active and receive more applicants.
  • Will remain active but will be hidden from search results after reaching the free applicant limit. The free applicant limit typically ranges from 10 to 30, depending on the role. The job can still be accessed via a direct link or on your company’s job tab.
  • 25 recommended candidates based on your criteria.
  • One evaluation of a top fit applicant.
  • A preview of Interview AI.

Promoted jobs

  • Are shown at the top of search results and can include a Promoted tag.
  • Custom audience targeting helps your promoted job reach more qualified candidates
  • Encourage candidates to apply to your job with instant mobile notifications of your job posting.
  • Notify you when a qualified candidate applies to your job.
  • Stay active until you close them or will expire after 6 months of being active.
  • Appear in highly visible placements in job recommendations.
  • Can receive unlimited applicants.
  • Set a daily average or total budget for your job.
  • Up to 350 invites to recommended candidates.
  • 5 InMail messages to sourced candidates per day.
  • Unlimited applicant evaluations.
  • 40 AI video interviews.

Basic jobs (limited listings)

  • Appear only in limited LinkedIn placements, such as the Jobs tab on the employer’s company page and within the Jobs search page.
  • Included in Job Wrapping services and do not require additional budget unless promoted.
  • Not available for search and staffing companies.

Promoted jobs (job slots)

  • Remain active as long as they are tied to a slot or manually closed.
  • Can receive unlimited applications.
  • High visibility by appearing at the top of search results, in candidates’ job recommendations, LinkedIn feeds, and email alerts, all marked with a prominent Promoted tag for easy recognition.
  • Enhanced applicant notifications and tracking, helping employers promptly identify qualified candidates.

Job wrapping

  • Included with Job Slots.
  • Allows jobs to be automated from an employer’s Applicant Tracking System (ATS) or career site and posted directly to LinkedIn.
  • The process of LinkedIn’s system automatically scraping or pulling jobs from external job sources (e.g., career sites, job boards, ATS).
  • Jobs can be posted as free Basic Jobs or wrapped to Job Slots on a Recruiter Dashboard.

Free job posts become less visible in search results over time to give newer job posts the opportunity to be seen by job seekers. When your job post receives a certain number of applications, it’ll be paused and removed from search results. If you have shared a direct URL, through LinkedIn or through other channels, your job post will appear closed until you take action to unpause it. To unpause your job, you must promote it.

To ensure a fair and equitable balance between free and paid jobs and reduce job posting abuse, members can post a maximum of 1 free job at a time and a limited number of free jobs in a 30-day window.

Easy Apply limits

When applying for jobs, the quality of your application often matters more than the number you send. To help members focus on creating thoughtful, genuine applications, LinkedIn has introduced limits on Easy Apply submissions. These measures are designed to foster more intentional job searches, ensure fairness by curbing automation and bots, and give real applications the attention they deserve.

Why are there Easy Apply limits?

Submitting too many applications makes it harder for recruiters to identify genuine applicants amid the noise. To address this, we’ve implemented limits that:

  • Help you stand out: By focusing on quality over quantity, members can improve their chances of being noticed and contacted by recruiters.
  • Maintain platform integrity: These limits serve as a safeguard against automated activity like bots, ensuring a fair process for all users.
  • Improve the quality of applications: Submitting targeted and personalized applications may increase the chance of meaningful matches with employers. Thoughtful applications resonate better with recruiters.

Daily Easy Apply limit 

You can submit a set number of Easy Apply applications each day. If you reach this limit, you’ll need to wait until it resets at the end of the day (UTC). Most members rarely exceed this limit. If you do, it’s an opportunity to reassess your application strategy and focus on roles that align more effectively with your qualifications.

Speed Easy Apply limit 

Rapidly submitting applications in a short time triggers a temporary pause on Easy Apply. This helps prevent automation and bots from flooding job postings with irrelevant applications. Use this time as a chance to revisit job descriptions and tailor your materials for better matches.

Easy Apply limits for inauthentic behavior

To help keep LinkedIn a safe and trusted space, we may lower a member’s daily Easy Apply limit if we notice activity that seems inauthentic.

If you think your account was flagged by mistake, you can verify your account to increase your Easy Apply limit.

How to use Easy Apply effectively

Here are ways to make the most of Easy Apply and these limits:

  • Leverage Job Match insights: Job Match is LinkedIn’s AI-powered feature that helps you quickly evaluate how strongly your skills and qualifications align with a job listing. Every job seeker can access a match summary that highlights required and preferred qualifications, giving you transparency into areas where you excel—and areas for improvement.
  • Personalize your application: Tailor your resume and LinkedIn profile to showcase how your specific skills and experiences meet the job requirements.

Filter and sort job search results

After searching for jobs on LinkedIn, you can filter and sort your job search results to narrow down your results.

Here’s a tip

Any job search performed on LinkedIn will render up to 1,000 results by default.

Important to know

You may see additional suggestions based on your search query and preferences.

Use the following filters on the job search results page to refine your results:

Location - You can specify a location in your search query or by entering a location (postal code, city, state, province, or country) in the location field at the top of your screen.

Date posted - By default, your job search results will show results from any time, but you can also choose to display jobs posted within the last 24 hours, the past week, and the past month.

Easy Apply – You can filter for jobs where you can apply directly on LinkedIn.

Company - You can filter your job search by a specific company or multiple companies.

Experience level - You can filter your job search by specific level(s) of experience.

Employment type - You can filter for full-time, contract, internship, volunteer, or part time job types.

Under 10 applicants - You can filter for jobs that currently have less than 10 applicants.

In your network - You can filter for jobs in your network.

To search for job-related posts, change the search criteria by clicking or tapping the Jobs dropdown at the top of the page and selecting Posts, then choose the Job posts option under the Content type filter.

Before we return results, we consider your search activity on LinkedIn, the set of jobs returned by the query, and other members who have made similar searches in determining the order of results.

Find jobs on LinkedIn – Best Practices

There are a few things you can do to get the most out of your job search on LinkedIn and to ensure that your profile stands out to employers and recruiters. Check out some best practices for how you can make a good impression, build your network, and discover the right opportunities.

Find the Right Job

  • You can easily search for jobs on LinkedIn from the Jobs homepage by describing the job that you want in your own words. For example, you can write “I want to use my marketing skills to help cure cancer” or “senior designer for fintech in California.” You can narrow down results by adding more detail.

  • Consider researching the companies and ways you can recognize and avoid fraudulent tactics before you apply.

    Note: If you have any concerns about a job post, you can report it.

  • Set up job alerts based on your previous job searches, preferences, and specific companies to ensure you’ll regularly receive relevant job notifications.

  • Find remote jobs and set up a job alert to increase your chances of being one of the first applicants.

  • Save jobs while browsing job search results on LinkedIn to come back later to apply for them.

  • Access unique insights about jobs (exclusive to Premium accounts) to help you make informed decisions on whether the job is a good fit for you.

Apply and Prepare for the Job

  • Upload a default resume to use when applying for jobs posted on LinkedIn and save up to four additional resume options for different job descriptions.

  • Keep track of jobs you’ve applied to on a spreadsheet with dates and notes.

    Note: You can view all applications for Easy Apply jobs hosted on LinkedIn. Jobs that require application completion on their company website won’t be available on this list.

Update Your LinkedIn Profile

  • Add a recent profile photo.
  • Update your current location.
  • Update your education information.
  • Add contact information if you’d like to be contacted outside of LinkedIn.

Make Your Profile Stand Out

  • Use the summary to share more information about yourself and what types of opportunities you’re pursuing.
  • Enable the #OpenToWork feature to let recruiters know that you’re open to new opportunities.
  • Ask connections to endorse your skills and provide a recommendation.

Expand Your Professional Network

  • Connect with other LinkedIn members who share a professional relationship with you.
  • Explore topics and conversations of interest in LinkedIn Groups.
  • Contact the job poster via InMail (when available) to tell them why you want the job.
  • Follow the company’s LinkedIn Page for their most recent news and updates.
  • Engage with content posted by the companies you’re interested in.

Hiring Pro features FAQ

What is Hiring Pro?

Hiring Pro leverages AI to find, connect, screen and shortlist qualified candidates for your role, reducing the time spent on manual tasks and increasing your reach to qualified candidates. Here’s how it works:

  • AI-assisted job descriptions: When you post a job on LinkedIn, Hiring Pro can help draft a job description based on the role. To use this feature, click on the Continue button when posting a job.
  • AI-assisted applicant sorting: If you promote your job, Hiring Pro can sort through all your applications and help identify top-fit applicants that best match the qualifications you define.
  • AI-assisted sourcing and inviting job seekers to apply: If you promote your job, Hiring Pro can continuously search for qualified candidates and invite them to apply on your behalf, based on criteria you set.
  • AI‑powered outreach messaging: With Hiring Pro’s InMail, invite qualified members to apply by generating personalized InMail messages based on the job you’re hiring for and each candidate’s profile.

Hiring Pro will assist you in identifying potential candidates and reviewing applicants based on the qualifications you select for your role, but the final hiring decisions and responsibility lie with you and your organization.

To opt out of Hiring Pro features, either post your job for free or go to the Job Details page, click the  icon, and select Switch to classic experience. Note: If you have already invited applicants to an AI interview, you will not be able to switch to the classic experience.

Check out some frequently asked questions below.

Using Hiring Pro

Go to Post a job and start by entering the role you’re hiring for. If you click Continue, Hiring Pro will help you draft a job post. To use other features like finding and inviting qualified candidates daily or AI-assisted applicant sorting, you’ll need to promote your job.

This feature is gradually being rolled out and may not be available to you at this time. Hiring Pro is currently available only to a subset of English-speaking members who promote their jobs.

No, you don’t have to use Hiring Pro. To opt out of Hiring Pro features, either post your job for free or go to the Job Details page, click the  icon, and select Switch to classic experience.

Hiring Pro makes recommendations based on your inputs and runs all AI-created content through our content filters. While we take safety precautions, the feature may produce surprises or mistakes. You should review all recommendations and make necessary edits. As the job poster, you and your organization are responsible for the final job post and hiring decisions, and you may need to add additional information or follow specific processes as required by law.

No, Hiring Pro will not make hiring decisions for you. It will make recommendations and assist with tasks like drafting job descriptions, sorting applicants according to your settings, and finding and inviting candidates to apply. However, the final hiring decisions, including whom to hire, remain with you. You, the job poster, are responsible for reviewing and verifying information surfaced by Hiring Pro before making any hiring decisions.

AI-assisted job descriptions

When you are posting a job and click Continue, the AI-assistant will use the job title you provide, information from your company’s LinkedIn page, and your LinkedIn profile to draft a job description for your job post. See the Learn more section below for related FAQs.

Finding and inviting job seekers to apply with AI

Qualifications are the must-have and preferred experiences or skills that you set when posting your job. Hiring Pro suggests qualifications from your job description as a starting point, and it is recommended that you always review and edit your job’s qualifications. These qualifications are different from the qualifications you may include in your job description and are not seen by job seekers. You’ll be able to review and refine the qualifications and can edit them throughout your hiring process.

Note that if you edit your qualifications, that will not change your job post. Applicants that have already been advanced or rejected may not have the new qualifications. You may be legally obligated to create a new job post and start a new applicant pool.

When you promote your job, Hiring Pro helps you find qualified candidates faster. It uses your feedback to understand your ideal candidate using the qualifications you set.

Hiring Pro will then suggest up to 25 candidates daily who match most of your qualifications. You can review each suggested candidate and invite them to apply, or let Hiring Pro invite all 25 daily for you. Hiring Pro will continue to invite its suggested candidates until you reach 10 top-fit applicants based on your qualifications. You can turn off this setting at any point.

LinkedIn uses your job description and the ideal qualifications you chose for the role to identify job seekers who may be open to new opportunities. These candidates typically have the experiences, skills, and qualifications you’re looking for, as listed on their resumes and LinkedIn profiles. However, matches may not always meet your set qualifications, for example due to market conditions or possible AI inaccuracies.

LinkedIn uses your feedback and your qualifications to refine its search for potential candidates. If a job seeker matches most of your qualifications, LinkedIn will continue to find similar candidates. If a job seeker doesn’t meet your criteria, you can provide feedback on why or adjust your qualifications. This helps improve the quality of future matches shown to you by Hiring Pro. Note that adjusting your qualifications does not change your job post.

Evaluating and sorting applicants

Hiring Pro sorts applicants based on your must-have qualifications and the number of preferred qualifications the applicants meet. You can adjust the number of preferred qualifications that “top fit” applicants need to meet at any time by updating the top applicant threshold in your qualification settings.

  • Top fit: Applicants who meet all the must-have qualifications and a set number of your  preferred qualifications. You can adjust this threshold at any time.
  • Not a fit: Applicants who meet most but not all of your must-have qualifications.
  • Maybe: Applicants who do not meet most of your must-have qualifications, are from a different country than your hiring location, or fail one or more essential screening questions.

If your job has less than 10 applicants who meet all your must-have qualifications, Hiring Pro will expand the pool to surface the best of those who have applied to your job in the top fit list. You can choose to turn off this feature by adjusting your qualification settings. If turned off, your top fits will only be those who meet 100% of must have quals.

You can also move applicants between lists or change how applicants are ordered within a list (by qualification match, date applied, or alphabetical order) or filter within a list (by location or years of experience) through the dropdowns at the top of the list. It’s important to review and edit your settings for sorting applicants. In the case Hiring Pro is unsure whether a candidate meets a qualification, this will be indicated by a grey question mark (?).

Hiring Pro will show whether an applicant meets each qualification based on the applicant’s profile and resume. How the applicant matches each qualification is indicated with the following four icons:

  • Match (green checkmark icon) - the applicant meets the qualification
  • Partial Match (half green checkmark icon) - the applicant shows some evidence or matches part of the qualification
  • Not a match (X icon) - the applicant does not meet the qualification
  • Cannot evaluate (question mark icon) - the information was not specific enough to draw a conclusion or cannot be evaluated

Hiring Pro will review information from each applicant’s resume, screening question answers, and LinkedIn profile and compare it against the must have and preferred qualifications you set for the role. Based on this information, Hiring Pro provides an AI‑generated evaluation and places applicants into lists such as Top fit, Maybe, or Not a fit. These evaluations are meant to help you review applicants more efficiently, but you’re always in control of final hiring decisions and can move applicants into different lists at any time.

To see the source of the qualification details, click Show more details while reviewing each applicant’s qualifications. This will display whether the information comes from the candidate’s LinkedIn profile, resume (either submitted with application, or stored on LinkedIn), or screening questions (if applicable).

You can modify the top applicant threshold within your qualifications. Adjusting your qualifications or top applicant threshold will change the sorting of your applicants. You can also manually move applicants into a different list using Move to dropdown, and change the sorting of applicants within a list to be based on qualification match, date applied, or alphabetical order under Sort dropdown.

Yes, updating your qualifications will result in a re-evaluation of all applicants based on your latest qualifications, and applicants will be re-sorted. Hiring Pro will not move any applicants that you’ve already moved to different lists, but it will update to show how the applicant meets your updated qualifications. This process can take several seconds. Note that if you edit your qualifications, that will not change your job post. Applicants that have already been advanced or rejected may not have the new qualifications.

Note that if you change your qualifications, you may be legally obligated to create a new job post and start a new applicant pool.

LinkedIn strives to ensure that its products and services are fair, including by measuring and mitigating algorithmic bias. Our objective is to ensure equally qualified members receive equal treatment by our models. As with all our products, our teams continuously assess our systems, and if harmful biases are identified, we will work to address them.

Shortlisting applicants

Shortlisting is a way to help you organize and manage applicants you want to move forward with or review again later. Shortlisting doesn’t change how Hiring Pro evaluates applicants and Hiring Pro will never shortlist applicants for you.

You can find your shortlist from the Applicants tab within Hiring Pro. Within Applicants, use the drop‑down to switch between different applicant lists (Shortlist, Top Fit, Maybe, Not a Fit).

You can move applicants between lists directly from each applicant’s profile. Once you’ve selected an applicant, select the Move to drop‑down on an applicant’s profile and choose where you want them to go. You can move applicants between Top fit, Maybe, Not a fit, and your shortlist.

All applicants who apply to your job can be found in the Applicants tab. Hiring Pro automatically organizes applicants into lists — Top fit, Maybe, or Not a fit — based on how they match your job qualifications. To view all applicants, use the drop‑down in the Applicants tab to switch between each list and review those who have applied.

Hiring Plan tab

The Hiring Plan tab provides an overview of your hiring process, including applicant statistics, job details, budget, and helpful links. It allows you to:

  • Review all applicants
  • Track how many candidates have been invited to apply
  • Monitor your spending or close your job
  • Contact LinkedIn support

Additionally, you can keep track of Hiring Pro work here. You can:

  • Turn on/off the setting that allows Hiring Pro to invite candidates to apply
  • Edit your role’s qualifications
  • See the status of tasks (completed and in progress)

How do I use the Top Applicant feature?

As a Premium member you can use the Top Applicant feature to further help you to identify and apply for jobs where you’re considered a top candidate based on the information listed on your profile.

From the Jobs page, navigate to the Jobs where you’re a top applicant section to view a list of job posts where you may be considered a top applicant.

How LinkedIn uses your job application information

How LinkedIn uses your data when you apply to Jobs

When you apply to jobs, in addition to information that you include with your application (such as resumes, cover letters, answers to screening questions, or contact information), we will include the primary email address associated with your LinkedIn account and your full LinkedIn profile. 

Saving job application information

You can save certain information you enter when you apply for a job on LinkedIn, and use it as default information for future job applications from the Job application settings page. This will allow you to apply for jobs more quickly. Your saved answers and resumes are not automatically shared with employers – you are able to edit before you submit your application. 

You can save the following information:

  • Answers to screening questions: We will pre-fill answers to screening questions that you have previously answered. For example, do you have a particular level of education or are you willing to work remote.
  • Resumes: We’ll pre-select your most recently used resume. You can save up to 4 resumes.

You can opt-out of saving job application data in your settings. We may use your answers to screening questions (with identifying information removed) and resumes for product improvement, including the training and improvement of generative AI models. Learn more about how we use resumes. 

Saving voluntary self-identification demographic information from job applications in the United States

When you apply to a job on LinkedIn, the hiring company may ask that you voluntarily submit self-identification demographic information to fulfill certain government requirements in the United States (ex. EEOC and OFCCP requirements). After you submit an application that includes this information, we give you the option to save it. If you choose to have LinkedIn save this information, this data may be used:

  • For future job applications: You can complete your applications faster by pre-filling these fields in future applications.
  • For aggregated insights and product improvements: LinkedIn will combine your data with other members’ information to generate aggregate insights, such as workforce and hiring trends. We may use these aggregate insights to improve our products, including by understanding bias in our products.

Your saved self-identification demographic data won’t be shown on your profile or disclosed to others on LinkedIn (except when you choose to include it with a job application). It won’t be used for advertising, personalizing your LinkedIn experience, or recommending jobs or other content. Outside of job application self-identification demographic data, we separately collect similar information as personal demographic information, which may be collected and used in different ways. Learn more about our collection and use of personal demographic data.

Image specifications for your LinkedIn Pages and Career Pages

When updating your LinkedIn Page images, we recommend the following specifications. All images must be PNG or JPEG files and have a maximum size of 3MB.

  • Tab: Page; Module: Logo image; Minimum image size: 268 (w) x 268 (h) pixels; Recommended image size: 400 (w) x 400 (h) pixels
  • Tab: Page; Module: Cover image; Minimum image size: 4200 (w) x 700 (h) pixels; Recommended image size: 4200 (w) x 700 (h) pixels
  • Tab: Life; Module: Main image; Minimum image size: 1128 (w) x 376 (h) pixels; Recommended image size: 1128 (w) x 376 (h) pixels
  • Tab: Life; Module: Custom modules; Minimum image size: 502 (w) x 282 (h) pixels; Recommended image size: 502 (w) x 282 (h) pixels
  • Tab: Life; Module: Company photos; Minimum image size: 264 (w) x 176 (h) pixels; Recommended image size: 900 (w) x 600 (h) pixels

Important to know

The Life tab modules are only available if you’ve enhanced your LinkedIn Pages with Career Pages. The dynamic cover image slideshow is available with a Premium Company Page subscription.

Since members view LinkedIn Pages on different devices and screen sizes, consider the following tips when adding images to your LinkedIn Page or Career Page.

  • To achieve the best image resolution, use the recommended dimensions and choose a high-resolution JPEG instead of a PNG file.

  • Your cover image might be adjusted to fit the screen, which might trim the image horizontally or vertically. We recommend uploading a high-quality image with limited text to ensure an optimal display on all devices and screen sizes.

  • You should place key details away from the edges of your cover photo, especially in the lower-right corner. Since images may get cropped on different screen sizes, placing important information in the center ensures that it is always visible.

  • Your logo image will be displayed on both light and dark backgrounds. If your logo is transparent, it will be shown on a white background. We recommend testing your logo to ensure it displays correctly on both light and dark backgrounds.

  • If your dynamic cover image appears blurry or pixelated, please choose an image with a larger file size. We recommend using photos, which look clearer than images with logos. If your image is still blurry or pixelated, you could use a compression tool such as Trimage for Windows or ImageOptim for Mac before uploading it to LinkedIn.

You can also use Vimeo or YouTube URLs for the main image or video and custom module sections of your Life tab. The static image for the video is taken from the thumbnail image on Vimeo or YouTube. To change the static image, update the thumbnail for that video on Vimeo or YouTube.

Here’s a tip

Members can click an image from the Company photos section of the Life tab to view a larger version of the photo. If you follow the minimum image size guidelines, rather than the recommended guidelines, the image will likely appear small when a member click it.

Custom image specifications

When adding custom images to a Page post with a URL, consider the following image display guidelines:

  • Use a 1.91:1 ratio (1200 x 627 pixels).

  • Image must be more than 200 pixels wide.

    • If your image width is less than 200 pixels, it will appear as a thumbnail on the left side of the post.
    • This doesn’t apply if you’re posting an image only or an image and text. The image will be enlarged to fit the feed.

  • Images on mobile won’t be cropped. Images of other ratios will appear in full size with subtle white padding.

Job posts in countries sanctioned by OFAC

LinkedIn complies with all sanctions imposed by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of Treasury. Because of this, you’re unable to post jobs on LinkedIn to any trade-sanctioned countries under U.S. laws and regulations. Please refer to the Sanctions Programs and Country Information for an updated list on trade-sanctioned countries.

Job recommendations based on your preferences and profile

The Jobs tab shows job recommendations based on different types of information, helping you understand why a job is shown to you and how it relates to your interests and experience.

You may see recommendations from one or more of the following categories:

  • Jobs based on preferences that you add
  • Jobs that match your profile (members with basic (free) accounts)
  • Jobs where you’d be a top applicant (Premium subscribers)

Jobs based on your preferences

Jobs based on your preferences reflect information you share with LinkedIn in Open to Work, such as:

  • Job titles
  • Locations
  • Location types (remote, hybrid, or on‑site)
  • Employment types

You can add or update these preferences at any time from the Jobs tab. If you haven’t added preferences yet, you may be prompted to do so. You can also update your preferences by clicking Preferences > Open to work. When you make changes, recommendations in this section refresh immediately.

Your job preferences are visible only to you by default and are used to personalize the jobs you see. If you choose to share that you’re Open to Work with recruiters or the LinkedIn community, your location and location type (remote, hybrid, or on-site) preferences will be visible to others. All other preferences remain private.

Jobs that match your profile or where you’d be a top applicant

Jobs that match your profile are recommendations based on information from your LinkedIn profile, such as your headline, about section, experience and education, as well as your location preferences. LinkedIn identifies job opportunities where the qualifications needed may match these details. If you are a LinkedIn Premium subscriber, you will instead have access to jobs where you’d be a top applicant. These recommendations go a step further by not only factoring in your profile information and the job posting criteria, but also the likelihood that a recruiter will respond based on previous recruiter feedback for similar jobs. To optimize your job recommendations, make sure to keep your profile up to date, including your headline, about, experience, and education sections.

In addition to the Jobs tab, you may also receive these job recommendations by email or through in-app notifications. You can create job alerts for specific searches to get notified when new matching jobs are posted.

Let recruiters know you’re Open to Work

Let recruiters know you’re Open to Work

You can let recruiters and your network on LinkedIn know you’re open to new job opportunities with the #OpenToWork feature.

Enable or Manage #OpenToWork

[Embedded video omitted]

If you’re looking for a job, you can let recruiters and your network on LinkedIn know you’re open to new job opportunities. If you specify the types of job opportunities that you’re interested in and your preferred location, we’ll help your profile show up in search results when recruiters look for suitable job candidates.

With #OpenToWork you have control of who is able to see that you are ready to take on a new opportunity. You can choose who sees you’re open:

  • All LinkedIn Members: This also includes recruiters and people at your current company. It also adds the #OpenToWork photo frame.
  • Recruiters only: People using LinkedIn Recruiter only. To protect your privacy, we take steps to prevent LinkedIn Recruiter users who work at your current company from seeing your shared career interests, but we can’t guarantee complete privacy.
  • Visible only to you: Your job preferences are used for LinkedIn to tailor your job recommendation.

If you’re Open to Work in India:

You can specify notice period or availability to join and expected annual salary. This information is visible to recruiters only, regardless of your Open To Work visibility setting.

Adding your notice period or availability to join helps recruiters understand when you can start. Indicating your expected annual salary helps recruiters to assess alignment with their roles, and connect you to the right job opportunities faster.

Important to know

To protect your privacy, we take steps to prevent LinkedIn Recruiter users who work at your company from seeing your shared career interests. We take the current company on your LinkedIn profile marked as I am currently working here to know who to hide your Open to Work status from, however, we can’t guarantee complete privacy.

To enable the #OpenToWork feature:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View profile.

  3. Click the Open to button.

  4. Click Finding a new job.

  5. Provide the requested information in the pop-up window that appears.

    • You can choose whether all LinkedIn members or only recruiters can see that you’re open to job opportunities. If you choose to share with all LinkedIn members, we’ll add an #OpenToWork photo frame to your profile photo.
    • If you are Open to Work in India, you can specify notice period or availability to join and expected annual salary. This information is visible to recruiters only, regardless of your Open To Work visibility setting.

  6. Click Save.

Here’s a tip

Some members may see Choose what you need in your next job instead of Open to Opportunities.

You can edit or remove the #OpenToWork feature from your LinkedIn profile at any time:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click View profile.
  3. Click the Edit icon from the Open to Work box (at the top of your profile).
  4. Edit the information you previously provided.
  5. Click Save.

Click Delete to disable the feature. You can re-enable it at any time, but your previous preferences won’t be saved.

  1. Click on the Jobs tab.

  2. In the left-hand rail, click Preferences.

  3. In the Preferences window, click the arrow next to Open to work.

  4. Update the following settings to show what kind of work you’re open to:

    • Job titles
    • Location types
    • Locations
    • Start date
    • Employment types
    • Visibility (who can view you’re open to work)
    • For Open to Work in India, notice period or availability to join and expected annual salary (visible to recruiters only)

  5. Click Save.

To enable #OpenToWork from your LinkedIn profile:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap on your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap the Open to button in your introduction card (at the top of your profile).

  4. Tap Finding a new job.

  5. Provide the requested information in the screen that appears.

    • You can choose whether all LinkedIn members or only recruiters can see that you’re open to job opportunities. If you choose to share with all LinkedIn members, we’ll add an #OpenToWork photo frame to your profile photo.
    • If you are Open to Work in India, you can specify notice period or availability to join and expected annual salary. This information is visible to recruiters only, regardless of your Open To Work visibility setting.

  6. Tap Save.

You can edit or remove this information at any time:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap on your profile photo again to access your profile.
  3. Tap the  Edit icon from the Open to work box (at the top of your profile).
  4. Edit the information you previously provided, and tap Save.

Tap Delete to disable the feature. You can re-enable it at any time, but your previous preferences won’t be saved.

Important to know

If we notice that you stop responding to InMails from recruiters, we’ll email you to confirm that you’re still open to work. If we don’t receive confirmation, we’ll automatically remove the #OpenToWork feature from your profile until you manually enable it again.

Post a free job on LinkedIn

You can post a job on LinkedIn to advertise open roles at your company. Job seekers can discover your job through LinkedIn search and recommendations. You can post one job for free or choose to promote a job to increase its visibility and reach more qualified candidates.

A free job post remains active for up to 14 days. After 14 days, the job is paused and you can choose to promote it or close it. If the job isn’t promoted, it will automatically close after 30 days. Members can have up to one free job post active at a time and a limited number of free job posts within a 30‑day period.

Free job posts also include an application limit, which typically ranges from 10 to 30 applications depending on the role.

Free job posts must be associated with your company’s LinkedIn Page. If you don’t already have a LinkedIn Page, see Create a LinkedIn Page in the Related tasks section below.

Important to know

Free job posts become less visible in search results over time to give newer job posts the opportunity to be seen by job seekers. When your job post receives a certain number of applications, it’ll be paused and removed from search results. If you have shared a direct URL, through LinkedIn or through other channels, your job post will appear closed until you take action to unpause it. To unpause your job, you must promote it.

Note: If you’ve purchased job slots through a corporate contract, please learn more about posting jobs in LinkedIn Recruiter in the links below.

  3. Enter the job title and click Start hiring with AI or Start with my job description.

    • When you click Start hiring with AI, Hiring Pro will help draft a job post. If you choose to promote your job, it will also help find potential candidates and review applicants.

  4. Update the job description drafted by Hiring Pro or enter your own in the text box.

Important to know

At LinkedIn, we are continuously testing our features to improve the customer experience. You may or may not see an option to add skills to your job post. If you do not see this option, it will not negatively impact your job. 5. Click Continue. 6. On the Job settings page, enable or complete the following fields:

  • Screening questions: Add questions to help identify qualified applicants.
  • Rejection settings: Filter out and send rejections to applicants who don’t provide ideal answers to must-have screening questions.
  • Manage applicants: Send email updates through LinkedIn or an external website. Add email address for applicant updates.
  • #Hiring frame: Let your network know you’re hiring by adding the #Hiring frame to your profile.
  1. You can promote your job or post your job without promoting.
  2. Click Promote job or Post without promoting.

Post a job with Hiring Pro

We’re always making routine improvements to LinkedIn Job Posts to help our customers find and hire qualified candidates faster. One of the ways we’re doing this now is by introducing LinkedIn Hiring Pro, which helps streamline tasks and save you time throughout the hiring process.

What is Hiring Pro?

Hiring Pro leverages AI to streamline parts of the hiring process and reduce the time spent on manual tasks. Here’s how it works:

  • AI-assisted job descriptions: When you post a job on LinkedIn, Hiring Pro can help draft a job description based on the role. To use this feature, click on the Start hiring with AI button when posting a job.
  • AI-assisted applicant sorting: If you promote your job, Hiring Pro can sort through all your applications and help identify top-fit applicants that best match the qualifications you define.
  • Finds and can invite job seekers to apply with AI: If you promote your job, Hiring Pro can continuously search for qualified candidates and invite them to apply on your behalf, based on criteria you set.
  • AI‑powered outreach messaging: With Hiring Pro’s InMail, invite qualified members to apply by generating personalized InMail messages based on the job you’re hiring for and each candidate’s profile.
  • Collaborate with coworkers: Invite teammates to review applicants, share feedback, and track candidate activity in one place.

Hiring Pro will assist you in identifying potential candidates and reviewing applicants based on the qualifications you select for your role, but the final hiring decisions and responsibility lie with you and your organization. If you do not want access to the Hiring Pro, you can post your job for free or opt out of AI-assisted features.

Who can use this feature?

At this time, Hiring Pro is currently available only to a subset of English-speaking members who promote their jobs. Please note that Hiring Pro can only be selected when you first post your job on linkedin.com. It is not available when posting a job via the mobile app.

Post jobs on LinkedIn – Best practices

LinkedIn helps you find the best candidates for open jobs with features such as listing specific skills, job functions, and industries when posting a job.

There are a few things you can do to get the most out of your hiring experience on LinkedIn. We recommend the following best practices when posting a job.

(Optional) Establish your company’s brand

  • Create and maintain your LinkedIn Page. Your LinkedIn Page reflects your company’s standards, visions, and values.

    • Include a company description and website.

  • Post company updates regularly.

  • Encourage employees to follow your LinkedIn Page.

  • If you’re linking your profile to the job post, make sure you update your LinkedIn profile.

Post the job

  • Write an effective and detailed job description that includes the required skills to target job seekers who match your criteria. If you want applicants to include a cover letter or resume, include that in the job description. You can also use our Hiring Pro feature to help write your job description.
  • Associate the job post with your LinkedIn Page so the job will be displayed on the LinkedIn Page.
  • When it is a volunteer, internship, or otherwise unpaid opportunity, the job post must clearly state those details and the relevant expectations.

Set a job post budget

  • Post a free job on LinkedIn or promote your job to reach more relevant candidates.
  • Set your daily average or total budget for promoted job posts based on your billing preferences.
  • Edit the budget, or close your job post to stop spending, at any time.

Review and share your job post

  • View your published job post by clicking Manage job posts from the Jobs homepage.
  • (Optional) Edit the job post.
  • Share the job post with your LinkedIn network.
  • Share that you’re hiring.

Review job applicants

  • Review job applicants. View their profile, resume, and cover letter (if provided) directly from the application.
  • Rate applicants as Top fit (for promoted jobs), Good fit, Maybe, or Not a Fit.
  • Set up automatic ratings and rejection messages to automate your hiring workflow.
  • Contact applicants directly from the Applicants tab of your job post.

Once you’ve found a good fit for your role, close the job post. You can repost the job at any time.

Quality job post guidelines

All jobs posted on LinkedIn must meet certain quality standards to comply with our policies and remain on the site. All job posts must contain truthful, accurate, and complete information about the jobs they promote and comply with LinkedIn’s User Agreement, Professional Community Policies and Jobs Policies.

Ready to post a job now?

You can post your job on LinkedIn and get matched with qualified candidates.

Post a job now

Here are some guidelines to follow when posting a job on LinkedIn:

Job posts can’t discriminate

  • LinkedIn prohibits discrimination in job postings based on protected characteristics, including age, gender, gender identity, religion, ethnicity, race, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, and any other basis protected under law; however, in a jurisdiction where it is legally permissible to do so, LinkedIn may permit language in posts expressing preference for members of certain groups historically disadvantaged in hiring in that location. Learn more about discriminatory jobs.

Job posts must be clear and should communicate all relevant and factual details.

  • Include title, responsibilities, qualifications, and if available, job type (e.g., full-time, part-time, contract, etc.), as well as information about the employer, such as the company’s physical address or contact details, valid website, and a valid email associated with the company domain (if applicable).
  • The job post must clearly state the role and avoid ambiguous job responsibilities and/or qualifications. Be concise but detailed so job seekers can understand exactly what the job entails.
  • When it is a volunteer, internship, or otherwise unpaid opportunity, the job post must clearly state whether it is paid or unpaid, along with any relevant details and expectations.
  • The primary location for the role must be plainly visible within the job description. The requirement and/or conditions of relocation and travel should be indicated in the post. Note: The user posting the job doesn’t need to be in the same location as the primary location of the role.

Posts must communicate all relevant and factual details.

  • Only create postings for bona fide job opportunities with a reasonable and legitimate intent to hire for the specific position listed. Jobs cannot advertise for general resume drops or applications.

Job titles and descriptions should match.

  • While titles and levels vary across companies and industries, a job shouldn’t advertise a position that the job description doesn’t support or contradicts.

Job posts should reflect a high degree of professionalism.

  • Different roles, locations, and company cultures can call for a wide range of writing styles and terminology to attract the right talent. However, posts containing egregious typos, grammatical errors, symbols, unprofessional or inappropriate language, or incomplete sentences don’t inspire trust and confidence in applicants. We recommend avoiding phrases that may seem spam-like to job seekers, such as “plz” or “ez jobs.”
  • Avoid excessive use of internal jargon, offensive slang, capitalization, or emojis.

Other helpful tips

  • Add key skills needed for the position in the Add skills field after you’ve posted your job.

  • You may hire multiple candidates for the same role, but cannot use one job post for multiple roles. For example, you may say you’re “Hiring for 5 Data Scientists,” but cannot say “Hiring for a Data Scientist and Marketing Manager.”

  • Link to your company’s LinkedIn Page by choosing your company name from the dropdown list. Describe your company if it’s not well known.

  • List any benefits or special perks, like 401k, flex time, or stock options in the Job Description field.

  • Make sure your coworkers are using LinkedIn so they can share job posts with people in their networks.

  • Use a job description template to get started and stand out to a potential hire.

  • Post your job using the company’s email domain to gain more trust with applicants.

  • Avoid asking for personal information (such as photos or ID information) upfront in the application, as applicants should not be asked to give out such information before they even apply.

  • Use between 500-600 words in your job description to create a high-performing job post.

Repost a closed or expired job

You can repost a closed, expired, or modified version of a job at any time from the Manage job posts page on LinkedIn.

To repost a job:

  1. Click the Jobs icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click Manage job posts.

  3. Find the job you wish to access by clicking the Closed tab and click the More icon to the right of the title.

  4. Click the Repost job icon from the menu that appears.

  5. Click Continue with my job.

  6. Update the job description and click Continue.

  7. On the Job settings page, complete the fields below and click Continue:

    • Screening questions: Add questions to help identify qualified applicants.
    • Rejection settings: Filter out and send rejections to applicants who don’t provide ideal answers to must-have screening questions.
    • Manage applicants: Send email updates through LinkedIn or an external website. Add email address for applicant updates.
    • #Hiring frame: Let your network know you’re hiring by adding the #Hiring frame to your profile.

  8. On the Ideal qualifications page, add must-have and preferred qualifications and click Continue.

  9. Select either Free or Promoted. Set your daily average or total budget for your post or you can choose to post for free.

    • You’ll see an estimated number of applicants populated on the page.
    • If you’d like to adjust the budget for your job, click the Edit icon.
    • You can set your budget for your post from this page. Your job post will be paused once your budget is met.

  10. Fill in your credit card details.

    • If you already have a payment method on file, your default payment method will appear. Select + Add a new payment method if you’d like to add a new payment method for this purchase.
    • If this is your first promoted job and you are using a free trial or promotional credit, this will be reflected in checkout.

  11. Review the order details before posting your job.

  12. Click Post without promoting or Promote job.

The posting will be treated as a new job. Any prior applicants from the closed job won’t be included in your new posting, but will still be available by viewing the closed posting.

Search for jobs confidently and safely

Looking for your next role can feel exciting – and sometimes overwhelming. LinkedIn is here to help you find opportunities with confidence and keep your job search safe every step of the way.

We continuously work to protect our members by removing fake accounts and fraudulent job postings, offering verification tools, and more. This guide provides best practices on how to search for jobs safely and stay alert for suspicious activity.

How to use verifications in your job search

When you see a verification badge, it means LinkedIn or a trusted partner has confirmed certain details. This helps you feel confident about who you connect with and the opportunities you explore.

Look for these indicators that help build trust:

  • Profile Verification Badge: The member has verified their identity or workplace on LinkedIn by fulfilling certain identity requirements.
  • Company Page Verification Badge: LinkedIn has verified details about the company through trusted verification methods.
  • Job Post Verification Badge: Information about the company or the job poster is verified through LinkedIn or our trusted third-party partners.

When you see a verification badge (pictured below), you can feel more confident about who you connect and interact with.

[Image: Verified badge]

How to evaluate recruiters and job opportunities

When evaluating a recruiter’s profile, look for:

  • A professional profile photo (not stock imagery)
  • A verification badge
  • Detailed work history
  • A link to their Company Page with active employees
  • An email address with their company domain (e.g. @company.com), not a generic email address (e.g. @hotmail.com)
  • Conversations that stay on LinkedIn (avoid pressure to move off-platform immediately)
  • Respect for your timeline and privacy

To validate job postings, look for:

  • A verification badge on the job post or the company page. Learn more
  • Activity, updates, and multiple employees on the company’s LinkedIn page
  • Cross-checking the role on the company’s official career page
  • Trusted job application methods (LinkedIn jobs or company’s official career page)
  • Indicators of legitimacy, such as (Learn more):
    • Promoted by hirer - The employer paid to promote the job, signaling priority
    • Actively Reviewing Applicants - The company is responsive and reviewing candidates
    • Hiring Responsive Insights - Shows how quickly a company responds to questions and job applications
  • No third-party links in messages or emails

What’s safe to share (and what’s not)

You should expect to share some basic information early in the job application process. Information that is safe to share early in the process:

  • Resume / CV
  • LinkedIn profile link
  • General location (city, state)
  • Salary expectations
  • Interview availability

Never share before receiving a legitimate job offer:

  • Social Security Number or National ID
  • Bank account or credit card information
  • Passport or driver’s license copies
  • Any form of payment

Warning signs to watch for

Be cautious if you notice:

  • Requests for payment (background checks, training, resume services or equipment)
  • Checks sent for deposit followed by refund requests. These checks will bounce, leaving you responsible for large amounts of money
  • Early requests for sensitive information like your social security number (SSN), banking details, ID pictures, or before formal hiring
  • Password requests. You should never share passwords.
  • Too-good-to-be-true offers. Exceptionally high salaries for minimal experience, immediate job offers without interviews, or guaranteed positions
  • Pressure to move communications off-platform immediately (e.g. Whatsapp/Telegram/external forms)
  • Vague or poorly written postings
  • Quick hiring processes (most legitimate processes take 2-6 weeks)
  • Links or emails that don’t match the company’s official domain

How to report suspicious jobs, recruiters or companies:

If you notice suspicious activity, stop communicating with the member and do not share additional information, personal or financial. Submit a report to help protect the Linkedin community.

  • Report a fake account
  • Report a job as spam or a scam
  • Report a company page

Once you’ve submitted the report, consider blocking the member. Our team reviews every report carefully.

Search for jobs on LinkedIn

LinkedIn helps you find relevant jobs that suit your skills and qualifications. You can either search for a job using the search field on top of the LinkedIn homepage or you can directly access the Jobs page where you can search and apply for jobs.

Note: If you’re new to LinkedIn, we suggest you read about how you can use LinkedIn and its features to easily get started with your job search. Also, make sure that you’ve created a good LinkedIn profile that stands out and showcases your skills and expertise.

There are two types of job postings on LinkedIn:

  • Easy Apply: This allows you to apply for the job on LinkedIn.
  • Apply: You’ll be redirected to the company or third-party website where you can apply for the job externally.

To search for jobs:

  1. Click the Jobs icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click into the Search bar on the top of the page and describe the job you’re looking for in your own words. For example, you can write “I want to use my marketing skills to help cure cancer” or “senior product designer for fintech in California.” Add more details to fine-tune your search.

    • You can also select from the job roles suggested by LinkedIn based on your preferences and qualifications. Please make sure that your LinkedIn profile and job preferences are up to date. You can update your job preferences by navigating to Jobs > Preferences > Open to work.
    • You’ll be directed to the search results page where you’ll see a list of job postings that suit your search query and location.

  3. Use the filters or suggestions at the top of the search results to refine your search query and the results.

    • Once you’ve applied all the filters, you can get job alerts for the search by turning on the alerts toggle.

  4. Click the job posting to view the job description and apply for the job if the job suits your requirement.

Note: Click the Save button on the job details page to save the job.

To search for jobs:

  1. Tap the Jobs icon.

  2. Tap into the Search bar on the top of the page and describe the job you’re looking for in your own words. For example, you can write “I want to use my marketing skills to help cure cancer” or “senior product designer for fintech in California.” Add more details to fine-tune your search.

    • You can also select from the job roles suggested by LinkedIn based on your preferences and qualifications. Make sure that your LinkedIn profile and job preferences are up to date. You can update your job preferences by navigating to Jobs > Preferences.
    • You’ll be directed to the search results page where you’ll see a list of job postings that suit your search query and location.

  3. Use the filters or suggestions at the top of the search results to refine your search query and results.

    • Once you’ve applied all the filters, you can get job alerts for the search by turning on the alerts toggle.

  4. Tap the job posting to view the job description and apply if the job suits your requirement.

  5. To apply for a job through your mobile device, tap Easy Apply or Apply at the top of the job post and follow the prompts.

To view your saved jobs and manage your job search most effectively, we recommend downloading the LinkedIn mobile app or accessing it via desktop. You may find it easier to complete your application on your computer.

Note: Tap Save to save the job post.

Here’s a tip

To search for job related posts, change the search criteria by clicking or tapping the Jobs dropdown at the top of the page and selecting Posts, then choose the Job posts option under the Content type filter.

Share a job you’ve posted on LinkedIn

You can share a job post from LinkedIn to various external social media networks, in addition to sharing with LinkedIn members through posts and messages.

To share a job you’ve posted:

  1. Click the Jobs icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click Manage job posts.

  3. Find the job you wish to share and click the More icon to the right of the title.

  4. Click the Share in a post icon or the Share in a message icon.

    • Share in a message – Opens a new message box with the link to the job post, where you can enter the names of 1st-degree connections who you’d like to share the job post with. You can customize the message before sending.

  5. Tap and select from the following options:

    • Share in a message to share the profile in a private message on LinkedIn.
    • Share via… to choose another messaging application to share the profile from on your device.
