Share and manage your resumes with recruiters

Discover more opportunities and increase your chances of getting hired with LinkedIn’s resume sharing feature. Once enabled, your profile will appear in search results when recruiters search for skills, experiences, education, and accomplishments that match data found in resumes that you’ve saved over the past 2 years. You must have at least one saved resume to enable this feature. Recruiters will not have access to your full resume unless you provide it to them directly, including by applying for a job. See the article linked below for more information on visibility and usage of your uploaded resume.

Important to know

To protect your privacy, we take steps to prevent LinkedIn Recruiter users who work at your company and related companies from seeing that you have shared a resume. We take the current company on your LinkedIn profile marked as “I am currently working here” to know who to hide your resume information from, however, we can’t guarantee complete privacy. For more information, check out the links below.

After applying for a job on LinkedIn, you’ll be presented with a prompt to share your resume data with all recruiters, and the Share resume data with recruiters toggle will be turned on. You can either turn it off from the prompt, the Job application settings page, or the Resumes and application data page.

To opt-in/out of resume sharing from your Preferences settings, take the following steps:

  1. Navigate to the Jobs tab.
  2. Click on Preferences.
  3. In the pop-up modal, click on Resumes and application data.
  4. Toggle on Share resume data with recruiters to access the resume sharing feature.
  5. Toggle off Share resume data with recruiters to stop sharing.

To manage your resumes through your Preferences settings:

  1. Navigate to the Jobs tab.
  2. Click on Preferences.
  3. In the pop-up modal, click on Resumes and application data.
  4. Upload a new resume by clicking Upload resume.
  5. Delete a resume by clicking on the  icon and clicking Delete.

Who can use this feature?

This feature is available only in English.

Share applicants with coworkers

Share applicants with coworkers so you can review candidates together, gather input faster, and make more confident hiring decisions.

You can invite up to five coworkers to a job and share all applicants or specific candidates with them. Coworkers can then view, rate, and shortlist applicants, while you stay aligned by tracking their most recent actions.

  1. Navigate to your job.

  2. Click + Add a coworker at the top right of your page.

  3. Select your suggested coworker(s) or search their name.

  4. Click Next.

  5. Choose how to notify them:

    • Click Send message to invite them
    • Select Copy URL to share the link another way

When you send an applicant to a coworker, they’ll receive an invite message with a link to review the applicant. Coworkers will land directly on the Applicants tab for quick access and you’ll see updates on candidate activity (like who shortlisted someone). You can remove a coworker from a job by clicking Manage coworkers on the Hiring plan page.

Troubleshoot job alerts

You can create job alerts on LinkedIn to stay updated with new job postings that match your preferences. You can choose whether you want to receive these alerts on a daily or weekly basis through email, app notifications, or both.

If you’re receiving an error message when trying to create a job alert, it may be because:

  • Your settings won’t allow any LinkedIn emails to be sent to your email address.

  • We’re not able to create an email alert due to the use of offensive words or phrases.

  • You may have reached your maximum number of active email alerts.

Upload your resume to LinkedIn

LinkedIn offers multiple methods to upload your resume to LinkedIn, including uploading it to job applications as well as displaying it on your profile.

If you don’t already have a resume, you can create one with your LinkedIn profile one of two ways:

  • You can download your entire profile as a PDF in a resume format.

  • You can use LinkedIn Resume Builder to create and download a custom resume. #### Important to know

    Resume Builder feature is not currently available to all LinkedIn members.

You can upload your resume from the Job Application Settings page by clicking Upload under the Resume section. You can also upload your resume navigating to the Jobs tab and clicking Preferences and then Resumes and application data. We’ll store your four most recently uploaded resumes on LinkedIn, allowing you to reuse them for future job applications.

To upload a new resume from your computer or mobile device:

  1. Search for a job.

  2. Click or tap on a job title to view details.

  3. Click or tap the Easy Apply button.

    • Note: If you see the Apply button instead of the Easy Apply button, you’ll be routed to that company’s website or job board to continue the application process.

  4. Complete the required fields.

  5. Under Resume (optional), select Upload resume to upload your resume.

    • Note: If you aren’t logged in to LinkedIn, then uploading a resume is mandatory.
    • We recommend a file size less than 2MB and the file format must be either Microsoft Word or PDF.

  6. Click or tap Submit application when finished.

Here are some things to remember:

  • If you have trouble attaching your resume, try a different browser.
  • If you’ve submitted your application without a resume attached, you can’t reopen your application to attach your resume or reapply for the same job post.
  • If you need to send your resume after submitting your application, you can directly contact the job poster with an InMail message if they’ve provided contact information in the job posting.

If you want to showcase your resume on your profile, you can upload the document, which will allow you to share it with your network. Viewers will have the option to download it directly from your profile page.

Note: You won’t be able to use the resume uploaded to your profile for job applications. Please use one of the previously described upload methods for job applications.

To delete a resume from your profile:

  1. Go to the Job Application Settings page or the Resumes and application data page.
  2. Click the ellipsis (…) to the right of the resume.
  3. Select Delete.

Important to know

Previously submitted applications will not be affected.

Use the Top Applicant feature to apply for jobs

LinkedIn Premium feature

LinkedIn Premium members can use the Top Applicant feature to enhance their job search. This feature helps job searchers identify and apply for jobs where they’re considered a top candidate based on their profile information, the job posting criteria, and recruiter feedback on previous applicants to similar jobs.

The feature only displays if you’re in the top 50% of applicants for at least one role. This will be determined by the current members who’ve applied for the role and requires at least 10 applicants.

Video specifications for your LinkedIn Pages and Career Pages

When updating your LinkedIn Page or Career Page videos, consider the following file type guidelines.

File types

We support the following video file types:

  • AAC
  • ASF
  • FLV
  • MP3
  • MP4
  • MPEG-1
  • MPEG-4
  • MKV
  • WebM
  • H264/AVC
  • Vorbis
  • VP8
  • VP9
  • WMV2
  • WMV3

We no longer support AVI, QuickTime, or MOV files.

Guidelines

Videos must follow these guidelines:

  • Max file size - 5 GB
  • Minimum file size - 75 KB
  • Max video duration - 10 minutes
  • Minimum video duration - 3 seconds
  • Resolution range - 256x144 – 4096x2304
  • Aspect ratio - 1:2.4 – 2.4:1
  • Frame rates - 10 FPS – 60 FPS
  • Bit rates - 192 KBPS – 30 MBPS

What to expect after you apply for a job

After you apply for a job on LinkedIn, the job poster will have the option to review your application. If you applied via Easy Apply for a job hosted on LinkedIn, you’ll receive application updates that’ll inform you when the job poster views your application or downloads your resume.

Here are some things to keep in mind:

  • A notification for an application view means that the job poster opened and viewed your application on LinkedIn. This can include views to your screening questions.
  • A notification for a resume download means that the job poster downloaded the resume you attached to your job application. This occurs commonly when the job poster wants to view the details of your attached resume or forward the attachment to someone else in the company.

Important to know

An application view or a resume download doesn’t guarantee that you’ll receive a message, interview, or job offer from the job poster.

You can send an InMail to the job poster if you want to thank them for reviewing your application.

Write an effective job description

An effective job description is the first chance your candidate will learn about your role. Make sure that it is appealing, accurate, and detailed enough to interest the most qualified candidates. Additionally, you can use relevant keywords, which include your job functions and industries, to help the right candidates find your job post.

Here are some other suggestions to ensure you write a good job description:

  • Use a standard title for the position to help qualified candidates find your posting during their job searches.

  • Include job functions and industry details that are relevant to your job to help potential candidates easily search for your posting.

  • Provide as many details as possible within all other fields so that our matching technology can find the best candidates for your posting.

  • Be specific when describing roles and responsibilities.

  • Outline any specific requirements (sometimes the best candidates may not match every single one).

  • Link to your company’s LinkedIn Page by choosing your company name from the dropdown list. Describe your company if it’s not well known.

  • List any benefits or special perks like 401k, flex time, or stock options in the Description field.

  • Make sure your coworkers are using LinkedIn so they can share job posts with people in their networks.

  • Use a job description template (linked below) to get started and stand out to a potential hire.

Messaging and InMail

Add or remove participants in a group chat

Your ability to add or remove participants depends on the type of group chat:

  • In member-created group chats, any participant can add or remove others.
  • In Community chats, participants can’t add or remove others. These chats are invite-only, and managed by LinkedIn.

To add a participant:

  1. Click the  Messagingicon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • You can also click on the messaging conversation window at the lower-right corner of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Open the group chat.

  3. Click the ** More** icon in the upper-right corner of the group chat.

  4. Click Add / Remove people.

InMail message credits and renewal process

You’ll receive a new allotment of InMail message credits every month, on the first day of your billing cycle. The InMail messages credit auto-renewal date is based on the date of your initial sign-up. You can find this date on your My Premium page.

Important to know

We currently don’t offer a subscription plan with unlimited InMail message credits; however, you can receive InMail message credits back if a recipient accepts your InMail message.

Note: For Sales Navigator Core, InMail message credits renew on the last day of every month, regardless of your billing cycle.

Note: If you’re using Hiring Pro, you may see an AI‑powered InMail experience for inviting qualified candidates to apply. This experience is available only when contacting candidates recommended by Hiring Pro.

Here’s a tip

InMail messages is a Premium account feature. Any InMail messages balance will become zero when a Premium subscription is canceled. InMail message credits are not transferrable when upgrading your account. Premium InMail message credits can’t be used to send InMail messages on Sales Navigator or LinkedIn Recruiter.

Understanding credits for InMail messages with and without responses

You can’t send another InMail message to a member until they respond to the first message you sent. An automatic reminder is sent to the recipient within three days of the InMail message being sent.

Every InMail message that is accepted/declined or responded to directly within 90 days of it being sent is credited back. A pending InMail message isn’t counted as either accepted or declined. As part of the LinkedIn messaging experience, Quick Replies to InMail messages also count as a response.

Monthly InMail messages allotment per account type

This is the number of InMail message credits you receive on a monthly basis:

  • Premium Career: 5
  • Premium Business: 15
  • Sales Navigator Core: 50
  • Recruiter Lite: 30

Maximum InMail message credits accumulation per account type

This is the maximum number of InMail message credits you can accumulate in total:

  • Premium Career: 15
  • Premium Business: 45
  • Sales Navigator: 150
  • Recruiter Lite: 120
  • Hiring Pro: 5 per job
Important to know

The InMail messages compose window will display the number of InMail message credits left on your account, so you can easily view your current allotment.

LinkedIn Messaging - Overview

LinkedIn Messaging allows you to communicate with other LinkedIn members that you’re connected to. On LinkedIn, you can only message your 1st-degree connections (and, within group pages, fellow group members) for free. If you aren’t connected, you always have the option to send an InMail to another LinkedIn member.

Conversations with your connections can be initiated directly from your Messaging page or from your connection’s profile. You can send a message to a single, 1st-degree connection or, start a message thread with two or more connections by sending a message to multiple recipients.

You can also forward a message to share a conversation with another connection. Once you send a message, it will be sent to the recipient’s messaging list and possibly to their email address.

In addition, you can continue a dialogue with your connections by searching for sent and received messages using filters or keywords in order to reply to a message.

LinkedIn messaging gives you the option to leave a conversation or you can mute a conversation to stop receiving notifications for new messages on the thread. If you’ve started a conversation, you can also terminate the thread by deleting the conversation.

If a message you’ve received is inappropriate or offensive, you can report the message as spam.

Manage group chat notification settings in LinkedIn Messaging

You can manage how you want to be notified about activity in a group chat. You can choose from all activity, only mentions, or mute notifications completely. By default, notifications are set to all activity.

Important to know

This feature is only available on the LinkedIn mobile app.

To manage notifications for a group chat:

  1. Tap the  ** Messaging** icon in the upper right.

  2. Open the group chat.

  3. Tap the More icon in the upper right.

  4. Tap Notification settings.

  5. From the overlay menu, choose one of the following:

    • All activity: Get notified for every message in the group chat.
    • Only mentions: Get notified only when someone mentions you.
    • Mute notifications: Turn off all notifications for the group chat.
  • Mute or unmute a conversation in LinkedIn Messaging

Manage messages sent to your LinkedIn Page

As a super admin or content admin, you can manage messages sent to your LinkedIn Page, organizing them by topic, and filtering archived or spam messages.

To view and reply to your Page’s messages:

  1. Go to your Page super admin or content admin view.

  2. Click Inbox in the left menu.

  3. Click a conversation to view or reply to a message.

    • To edit the topic of a conversation, click the More menu in the upper-right corner of the message, click Edit conversation topic, and select a new topic.

    • Admins can see the name of the admin who sent each message, but members can’t see admin names.

  4. Click Inbox drop-down at the top of your messages, and choose Archived or Spam to quickly filter your conversations.

To view and reply to your Page’s messages:

  1. Go to your Page super admin or content admin view.

  2. Tap the Message icon in the upper-right corner to open your member inbox.

  3. Tap the banner at the top of the inbox.

    • If you manage one Page, tap your Page name.
    • If you manage multiple Pages or you have a Sales Navigator or Recruiter account, tap More inboxes.

  4. Tap a conversation to view or reply to a message.

    • To edit the topic of a conversation, tap the More menu in the upper-right corner of the message, tap Edit conversation topic, and select a new topic.

    • Admins can see the name of the admin who sent each message, but members can’t see admin names.

  5. Tap the Inboxdrop-down at the top of your messages, and choose Archivedor Spam to quickly filter your conversations.

If a message is spam, inappropriate, or abusive, you can restrict the member from your Page to stop them from sending more messages, or you can mark the message as spam which will move to a Spam folder. You can also mute the conversation or report the message.

Messages for LinkedIn Pages

When messaging for your Page is enabled, members can click the Message button to directly communicate with your Page. If you turn on Page messaging notifications, you’ll receive a notification when someone messages your Page. Messages appear in your Page inbox, where you can view and respond to the messages as your Page. You can also see the number of unread messages on the left navigation panel of your Page. Admins can see the name of the admin who sent each message but members can’t see admin names.

When you use messaging for Pages as an admin, your activity is on behalf of your Page. Admins can only send a message to a member if they message the Page first.

Who can use this feature?

You must be a super or content admin to view and reply to messages for your Page.

We recommend the following best practices:

  • Ensure that the right people in your company are assigned a super or content admin role so they can reply to messages. For example, if you have “Careers” enabled as a conversation topic, make sure the right subject matter expert at your company has the right correct access to manage and reply to messages.
  • Enable messaging so that visitors can message you directly from search results.
  • Reply to messages as quickly as possible.
  • When you set up messaging, choose conversation topics that reflect subjects you’d like members to ask you about.
  • Edit the conversation topic of a message to make sure it accurately describes the message. From your inbox, you can filter by topic.
  • Try managing your messages through one of our API partner platforms (Bird CRM, Brandwatch, Hootsuite, Oktopost, Sprinklr, and Zoho).

You can disable the messaging feature from your inbox settings to remove the Message button from your Page and stop receiving new messages from members.

Receive quick reply InMail messages from candidates

We’ve recently updated the candidate InMail experience to provide quicker and clearer responses to InMail messages with one-click reply buttons. Candidates can now accept or decline your InMail message with a quick reply before responding to your message with additional details. Because of this, when a candidate responds with only the No thanks or Yes quick reply and no text, the InMail message notification you receive won’t show any additional information.

After you receive a quick reply InMail message in LinkedIn Recruiter, we recommend replying to the candidate to prompt next steps.

If the candidate responds with both a quick reply and an additional message, you’ll receive two separate InMail messages.

This change doesn’t impact your InMail response rate.

Send a message to a LinkedIn Page

You can send a message to a LinkedIn Page to communicate directly with the admins of that Page. Use messages to ask Page admins about subjects like their business, services, products, or the jobs posted on their Page. We recommend making your message as specific and as detailed as possible and sending messages about one of the conversation topics that the Page has selected. For example, you might ask to schedule a product demo or request information about a job from their company.

To send a message to a LinkedIn Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Page.

  2. Click the Message button. If you don’t see the Message button, the Page might not have messaging turned on.

    [Image: message page]

  3. Select a topic from the Conversation topic dropdown menu.

    If you select the Services topic, your message will open a request for services. Learn more about considerations before you request for services from a provider.

  4. Click Write a message… and enter your message.

  5. Click the Send message button.

To send a message to a LinkedIn Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Page.

  2. Tap the Message button. If you don’t see the Message button, the Page might not have messaging turned on.

    [Image: message page]

  3. Select a topic from the Conversation topic dropdown menu.

    If you select the Services topic, your message will open a request for services. Learn more about considerations before you request for services from a provider.

  4. Tap Write a message… and enter your message.

  5. Tap the Send message button.

Here’s a tip

You can also send a message to a Page from search results.

Responses to your message will appear in your LinkedIn inbox. To stop receiving notifications for messages from a Page, you can mute the conversation.

Once you send a message to a Page admin, they may retain a copy for their own purposes. Keep in mind that the Page admin may use various third-party service providers to manage member messages, such as messaging applications that categorize messages and customer service applications. As part of these integrations, copies of your messages and related profile information may be made available to these service providers. Please do not include sensitive or confidential data in your messages. If you have any questions, or for more information, you can reach out to the Page admin directly.

Troubleshoot message sending issues on LinkedIn

If you can’t send messages on LinkedIn, try these troubleshooting steps. After each step, try sending the message again to see if the issue is resolved. This can also help to identify the cause.

Important to know

You can’t message a member if they’ve chosen not to receive InMail messages in their message preferences settings.

  • If you’re sending a message to a non-connection, check if you have adequate InMail message credits.
  • Try sending a message on a different browser or in incognito/private mode.
  • Disable any browser extensions.
  • Clear cache and cookies from your current browser.
  • If you’re using a VPN, turn it off.
  • If you’re using a workplace issued device, try logging in from a different device. If the issue persists only on a workplace issued device or work VPN, contact your workplace IT department.

If these steps don’t resolve the issue, please contact us with the following details:

  • HAR file of the issue
  • Screenshot of the error message
  • Profile URL of message recipient
  • Message content which can be sent to recipient
  • Permission to replicate issue by sending message to intended recipient.

Troubleshoot messaging a LinkedIn Page

Learn about some common issues with messaging a Page.

Before reviewing these common issues, make sure you enable messages for your LinkedIn Page.

Page admins

  • Issue: I can’t access messages sent to my Page.; Explanation: To view messages sent to your Page, you must be a super or content admin. If you previously enabled messaging for your Page, you can still see existing conversations.

Members

  • Issue: I want to message a Page but I don’t see the message button.; Explanation: The Page may not have messages enabled or it has restricted you from sending them a message.
  • Issue: I can’t send a message to a Page.; Explanation: To protect our overall Page admin and member experience, and to help ensure Pages receive only relevant messages, we limit the number of Pages that you can message every month. If you can’t send a message to a Page, you might have reached the message limit.
  • Issue: I can’t send additional messages to an existing conversation with a Page.; Explanation: If you can’t send messages in an existing conversation, it’s possible that the Page has restricted you from sending additional messages.

Writing InMail Messages - Best Practices

LinkedIn doesn’t provide templates for InMail messages. However, you can customize your InMail messages and follow some best practices which could increase your response rates.

If you’re looking to network with someone about a new job or business opportunity

  1. Be brief and to the point.

  2. Share your goal and any common associations

    • Mention the profile content that prompted you to write.
    • Share any mutual experiences, interests or connections.
    • Explain what you’re hoping to achieve from the conversation.

  3. Adopt a conversational, enthusiastic tone.

    • Choose words that reflect your personal voice.
    • Express interest in helping them in their goals too.

  4. Don’t cut and paste the job description or URL to the job post.

  5. Give them a reason to reply by asking for advice, opinions, or referrals.

Learn more about some of the frequently asked questions about InMails.

To take a screenshot on iOS:

  1. Go to the screen where you see the error or issue.

  2. Do one of the following:

    • On an iPhone with Face ID: Press and release the Power and the Volume up buttons at the same time.

  4. Tap the preview to open it or swipe left to close it.

To take a screenshot on your Android device:

  2. Depending on your phone:

    • Press the Power and Volume down buttons at the same time.
    • If that doesn’t work, press and hold the Power button for a few seconds. Then tap Screenshot.
    • If neither of these work, go to your phone manufacturer’s support site for help.

  3. At the lower-left corner, you’ll find a preview of your screenshot. On some phones, at the top of the screen, you’ll find screenshot preview.

LinkedIn for Android mobile app permissions explained

Nearly all apps require your permission to use features from your Android. These permissions are written by Google, but don’t necessarily reflect how the LinkedIn app will use them on your device.

When you install or upgrade the LinkedIn Android application, we may ask you for consent to access permissions on your mobile device. Consent to these permissions is optional and you can use the app regardless of whether you provide consent. If you refuse to provide consent within the app for optional access permissions, certain app features may not work properly.

Below are some of the permissions the LinkedIn app requires and examples of how we use them. You can see a full list of permissions the app uses by visiting the Play Store.

Optional Permissions

  • Phone, Contacts/Calendar (read your contacts, modify your contacts, read/write call log, read calendar events plus confidential information): This lets you invite contacts from your address book to connect on LinkedIn and sync your LinkedIn contacts with your phone book. This also lets you sync your calendar with LinkedIn so you can see when you most recently met with your connections.
  • Photos/Media/Files: This lets you upload photos, videos, or audio files from your device and save them to your LinkedIn profile.
  • Microphone: This lets you record sound, such as to record voice messages and video content.
  • Camera: This lets you record videos to post on LinkedIn, take profile pictures, and scan QR codes.
  • Identity(find accounts on the device, add or remove accounts, read your own contact card, create accounts and set passwords): This lets LinkedIn provide personalized recommendations using your Google contact card. For instance, this allows you to easily use your Google contact card photo for your LinkedIn profile if you don’t have a photo on LinkedIn yet. This also lets you quickly access your LinkedIn account from the Accounts section on your phone. If you’re signing up for a new LinkedIn account with a verified Google account, this lets us verify your email address with Google.
  • Location(GPS and network-based): This lets us help you add a location to your profile. When you add a location to your profile, you’ll find jobs in your area and you’ll show up in recruiter searches for candidates in your area. Your GPS data is temporarily collected to determine the postal code and then deleted.
  • Device ID & call information (read phone status and identity): We may use this permission to provide features such as showing a profile photo when you receive a call from a LinkedIn connection.
  • Systems tools (send sticky broadcast, test access to protected storage): We use sticky broadcast mechanism to communicate between different modules inside the LinkedIn App. For example, it allows us to sync recommended and saved jobs for you to return to at any time.
  • Other (control vibration, prevent phone from sleeping, read sync settings, read sync statistics, toggle sync on and off, send sticky broadcasts, view network connections): This allows us to send you push notifications. This also gives you the option to download your LinkedIn connections to your phone book if you’d like.

Troubleshoot common LinkedIn mobile app issues

If you’re experiencing issues with the LinkedIn mobile app, such as app getting stuck or crashing, update to the latest version of the LinkedIn mobile app.

If the issue persists, try these troubleshooting steps to resolve the issue.

Uninstalling and reinstalling the LinkedIn mobile app from the App Store can often resolve common issues.

To uninstall and reinstall the LinkedIn mobile app:

  1. Press and hold the LinkedIn mobile app icon on your home screen
  2. Tap Remove App.
  3. Tap Delete App to uninstall.
  4. Download the LinkedIn mobile app from the App Store and log in

Clearing the LinkedIn mobile app data can resolve most common issues.

To clear LinkedIn mobile app data:

  1. Open the Settings app on your mobile device.
  2. Tap Apps.
  3. Find LinkedIn and tap it.

Here’s a tip

If your device has a different menu layout, you can search for LinkedIn in the Settings app to access it. 4. Tap Storage. 5. Tap Clear data and confirm when prompted. 6. Open the LinkedIn mobile app and log in.

If these steps don’t resolve the issue, please contact us with the following details:

  • An explanation of the issue, including the steps to reproduce it.
  • The link or button you clicked before the issue occurred.
  • A screenshot of the issue for better understanding.
  • The version of your LinkedIn mobile app.
  • The OS version of your mobile device.
  • The make and model of your mobile device.
  • Whether the issue occurs only on the LinkedIn mobile app or also on the desktop site.

Manage your LinkedIn notification updates

You can directly manage notifications about yourself, your activity, and your connections from the Notifications tab to determine which types of notifications you’d like to receive.

  • Delete - Removes the notification.
  • ** Turn off** - Stop receiving updates on a specific post, person, or a particular thread on your feed or a certain type of notification, such as likes, job changes, or work anniversaries from the people you’re following.

Note: You may not see all these options depending on the type of notification you’re managing.

To manage notification updates:

  1. Click the Notifications icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click the ** More** icon to the right of a specific notification and select Delete or ** Turn off** from the dropdown.

To turn on a notification update and improve your notifications:

  1. Click the Notifications icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Under Manage your Notifications on the left pane of the page, click View Settings.

  3. Under Notifications you receive, click a category to see the types of notification settings you can manage.

To turn on a notification update and improve your notifications:

To manage notification updates:

To turn on a notification update and improve your notifications:

    • You can also turn on or off other notification updates from this page.

Notes:

  • If you turn back on a notification update, you’ll receive these alerts again. All previous notifications of this type will reappear in the Notifications tab.

  • If you turn off a notification update, all existing notifications for that type will be removed from the Notifications tab, and you’ll no longer receive the alerts.

  • You won’t receive any push notifications on the LinkedIn mobile app for notification updates that are turned off from the Notifications tab.

  • You’ll still receive notification updates on the Notifications tab when push notifications are turned off from the LinkedIn mobile app Settings page.

  • Turning off notifications will only affect the notifications you receive, it will not change the content that appears on your feed.

Manage your notification settings

Notifications are a way to get updates about activity on LinkedIn. These include, but are not limited to, notifications about reactions to your posts, updates from your network or from groups that you are a part of or manage, pages you follow or manage, or events that you attend or organize.

We’ve recently made updates to simplify your notification settings experience by reorganizing them into logical topics. We haven’t changed any of your previous settings choices.

Control the notifications you receive from LinkedIn

You can enable or disable the types of notifications you want to receive and how often you wish to receive them.

Update notification settings

How does LinkedIn notify you?

You can choose to receive notifications for updates on your job search, posting and commenting or attending events, and more. There are three ways you can receive notifications:

  • In-app notifications: These notifications are delivered silently to you by prompting a badge on the LinkedIn app icon. They are found in the Notifications tab inside the app or by signing into linkedin.com.
  • Push notifications: These notifications pop up on your device immediately. Think of these as important notifications you want to receive as they happen. Push notifications can only be turned on when you allow In-app notifications.
  • Email notifications: These are delivered to the primary email address you’ve given to LinkedIn.

How to manage your notification settings?

  1. Navigate to the Settings screen by clicking here.
  2. Tap on Notifications.
  3. Select any topic that you wish to enable or disable notifications.
  4. Switch the toggle on or off for that topic to turn on or off notifications.
  5. If the toggle is ON, you can manage the type of notifications you want to receive.
  6. For each type of notification, you can choose to receive notifications in-app, via a push notification, or email.
  7. For certain email settings, you also select the frequency of your emails.

Notifications on LinkedIn

On LinkedIn, you can receive notifications about yourself, your activity, and your connections. These include alerts for your posts or shares, career opportunities, and updates about people in your network.

There are three ways you can receive LinkedIn notifications. They can appear at the top of your LinkedIn homepage on the My Network, Jobs, Messaging or Notifications tabs, they can be sent to your primary email address, or you may receive push notifications on your mobile device.

You can manage notification settings for several categories:

  • Invitations and messages
  • Jobs and opportunities
  • Activity in your network
  • Activity that involves you
  • News and articles
  • Offers and tips from LinkedIn
  • Updates from events

Note: The below notification represents a post that is in the top one percentile of all posts on LinkedIn, ranked by the number of reactions and comments.

Troubleshoot LinkedIn emails not received

If you’re not receiving emails from LinkedIn to your email account be sure to check your email’s spam folder, junk folder, social tab, and promotional tab. Email providers sometimes route emails from new sources to these folders.

You can also follow these steps to troubleshoot:

To verify your email settings in your LinkedIn account:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click Notifications on the left rail.
  4. Review the categories.
  5. To individually select items from within a category, click on a category name or arrow to the right of the category name and make sure the email setting is set to On.

To ensure that your primary email address is confirmed:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.

  3. Click Sign in & security on the left rail.

  4. In Account access, click Email addresses.

  5. Click Make primary next to your email address if you’d like to change your primary email address on your account.

    • You may be required to provide your password for security purposes.

To ensure that you receive emails when members invite you to connect:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click Notifications on the left rail.
  4. Select Connecting with others, and then click Email addresses.
  5. Select Invitations to connect and then set the toggle next to Allow connections related notifications to On.
  6. Select Invitations to Connect and set the toggle next to Email to On. You can also select the frequency of email delivery and other notification options.

Here are a few other troubleshooting steps you can try:

  • Add LinkedIn as a trusted email domain in your email’s address book.

  • Check with your email provider to ensure emails from LinkedIn aren’t blocked.

  • Make sure the email associated with the account is the email address of an individual and not a distribution list nor a role-based email address.

    • A role account/alias is an account that isn’t associated with a particular person, but with an office, position, or task (ex: webmaster@, postmaster@, admin@, etc.). To ensure you’re getting the most of LinkedIn, we recommend using a personal email address.

  • In some cases, like password resets or security verification, you’ll need to request the email again after making any of the above changes.

If you’re not receiving emails from LinkedIn:

  1. Tap your profile picture.

  2. Tap Settings.

  3. Tap Notifications.

  4. Next to Allow messaging notifications, set the toggle to On.

  5. To individually select items from within a particular category, tap on that category.

  6. Select the frequency email delivery: Individually, Weekly, or LinkedIn recommended.

    Note: Your changes will be saved automatically.

Note: If your email settings are set to LinkedIn recommended, you may receive related messages grouped together so you get fewer emails. Also, in some instances, if you’ve already interacted with a feature or notification on LinkedIn.com or on your app, you won’t receive an email for it. Adjust your email settings if you would like to change your email frequency.

Troubleshoot notification issues

If you’re experiencing notification issues, follow this troubleshooting procedure to reset your notification settings.

Here are some common notification issues that you might experience:

  • You’re not receiving notifications even though your notification settings are turned on.
  • You’re not getting notified when someone comments on your posts or reacts to them.

Important to know

To resolve notification issues, you must reset notification settings related to Updates from your network and Comments and reactions and any sub-settings associated with these notification categories and notification delivery method. Push notifications won’t work correctly unless the In-app notifications are also turned On.

To reset your notification settings:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click Settings & Privacy.

  3. Click ** Notifications** on the left pane.

  4. Under Notifications you receive:

    Click Connecting with others, then click on Updates from your network, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

    Click Posting and commenting, then click on Comments and reactions, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

To reset your notification settings:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap ** Settings**.

  3. Tap ** Notifications**.

  4. Under Notifications you receive:

    Tap Connecting with others, then tap on Updates from your network, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

    Tap Posting and commenting, then tap on Comments and reactions, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

Here’s a tip

If the above reset is unsuccessful, then go to Troubleshoot common LinkedIn mobile app issues for instructions on how to uninstall and reinstall the LinkedIn app.

To reset your notification settings:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap the  Settings icon in the upper-right corner.

  3. Tap  Notifications.

  4. Under Notifications you receive:

    Tap Connecting with others, then tap on Updates from your network, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

    Tap Posting and commenting, then tap on Comments and reactions, and do the following:

    • If the notification is currently On: Switch the toggle to Off, and then switch it back to On.
    • If the notification is currently Off: Switch the toggle to On, and then switch it back to Off.

Once you update the settings, new notifications should start to appear within 48-72 hours.

Access LinkedIn Pages admin view

LinkedIn Page admins can access the Pages they manage through an admin view respective to their assigned admin role. Admins don’t need a separate LinkedIn account login to access a Page.

Important to know

To access the admin view for a Page, you’ll need to request admin access to the Page first, or be granted access by an existing admin.

To access your Page admin view:

  1. Sign in to your LinkedIn profile that has admin access to the LinkedIn Page.

  2. From the My pages pane on the left side of your LinkedIn homepage, click the desired Page name. If you don’t see the Page, try clicking See all or request admin access to the Page.

    [Image: Access Page admin view on LinkedIn]

To access your Page admin view:

  1. Sign in to your LinkedIn profile that has admin access to the LinkedIn Page.
  2. Tap your profile picture in the upper-left corner.
  3. From the Manage pages section, tap the desired Page. If you don’t see the Page name, try tapping See all or request admin access to the Page.

Important to know

Paid media admins don’t have an admin view on the mobile app.

You’ll be routed to your super admin view, content admin view, or analyst view, respectively.

Here’s a tip

Paid media admins, including Lead Gen Forms managers, Landing Pages admins, and Sponsored Content poster admins, aren’t able to access the Page admin view on LinkedIn. Instead, they can take specified actions through Campaign Manager.

Acquired LinkedIn Pages

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can manage your organization’s brand through an acquired Page.

While we won’t delete the LinkedIn Page of an acquired organization, a super admin of Pages (parent and acquired) can request to add a notification to the Page of an acquired organization. The parent Page will automatically be listed as an affiliated Page on the acquired (child) Page.

Review the following information prior to submitting your request for an acquired banner and Page affiliation. The actions are irreversible.

  • The acquired banner Page will state (acquired organization) was acquired by (acquiring organization). To see what’s new, visit (link to acquiring organization Page).

    • Members can still follow the acquired Page by navigating to the parent Page and click Follow from the Affiliated Pages pane on the right.

  • Jobs associated with the acquired Page can be made visible on the parent Page.

  • Employees associated with the acquired Page can be added to the employee total of the parent Page. The associated employee’s profile won’t be changed.

Here’s a tip

It’s not possible to migrate followers from the Page of an acquired organization to the acquiring organization’s Page.

By requesting an acquired banner and Page affiliation, you’re:

  • Verifying that you’re authorized to act on behalf of both Pages.
  • Authorizing LinkedIn to list the acquired Page as an affiliated Page of the parent Page.
  • Verifying that admins of both Pages are aware of the request.
  • Acknowledging that no changes to admins, followers, or analytics will be applied to either Page as result of the process.
  • Acknowledging that admins and followers will continue to be distinct between both Pages.
  • Acknowledging that an Affiliated pages module will appear on the acquired Page.

To request a Page acquisition and an acquired banner, please contact us with the following information:

  • Both Page URLs.
  • The date the company was acquired.
  • State if you want the acquired Page jobs visible on the parent Page.
  • State if you want the employees associated with the acquired Page to be added to the employee total of the parent Page.

Add admins on your LinkedIn Page

LinkedIn Page super admins can add Page admins and paid media admins through the super admin view. Super admins receive admin requests via email and can view pending requests through their admin tools.

Before you begin

  • You must be a super admin of the Page to add another admin to the Page.
  • You can only add someone as an admin if:
    • They’re a 1st-degree, 2nd-degree, or 3rd-degree connection
    • They follow the Page that you’re adding them to
    • The Page hasn’t blocked the member and the member hasn’t blocked the Page. Learn more about blocking and unblocking a member.
    • The member’s account has not been flagged for any violations.

To add an admin:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.

  2. Click Settings in the left menu and select Manage admins.

  3. Click the Page admins or Paid media admins tab.

  4. Click the Add admin button. If you don’t see this button, you might need to request a higher level of admin access from a super admin of your Page.

  5. Enter the name of the member, associated employee, or advertiser you’d like to add in the Search for a member field.

  6. Select the admin’s name from the list that appears.

  7. Select the required admin role.

    Only one page admin role can be assigned per person, but more than one paid media admin role can be assigned. Paid media admin roles can be granted without an associated Campaign Manager ads account.

  8. Click Save.

If you run into issues with adding an admin to Page, you could try:

  • Verifying your own account
  • Asking the requesting member to verify their own account.

Important to know

You may reach a limit on how many admins can be added to your LinkedIn Page. Learn more about limits on adding admins to a LinkedIn Page.

Showcase Pages

Super admins of a parent Page aren’t automatically granted admin access to affiliated Showcase Pages. Showcase Pages become inactive if there have been no posts on the Page for six months. If you require admin access to an inactive Showcase Page, please contact us.

Add dynamic cover images to your LinkedIn Page

If you’re a LinkedIn Page admin and subscribe to Premium Company Page, you can use the dynamic cover image feature to set your brand apart by engaging your audience with Page customizations.

You can upload a single dynamic cover image as your Page’s background photo, or you can select up to five background images and create a slideshow. If you create a slideshow, you can choose the order of the images, and members will see them rotate at the top of your Page.

Here’s a tip

Admin dashboard for your LinkedIn Page

If you’re a super admin or content Page admin, you can use the dashboard as the main landing page to help you gain insights across your LinkedIn Page. When you access the dashboard from the super admin or content admin view, you can review insights from different modules.

Today’s actions

The Today’s actions module suggests actions you can take to improve your Page and grow and engage with your audience. The actions refresh daily and appear at the top of your dashboard.

Manage recent posts

Recent posts appear in the Manage recent posts module. You can interact with your recent posts directly on the dashboard with comments, mentions, reposts and reactions. You can also take actions like editing or featuring posts. If you select Show all page posts at the bottom of the module, you’ll be redirected to the Page posts tab.

Track performance

The Track performance module includes metrics from the Analytics tab of the Page’s admin view. This module includes the following metrics:

  • Search appearance - Review the number of searches your page appeared in.
  • Page Visitors - After you select Visitors, you’ll be directed to the Visitor analytics page, and you’ll see the number of visitors to your Page within a certain time frame.
  • Followers - After you select Followers, you’ll be redirected to the Followers analytics page, and you’ll see the number of new followers on your Page within a certain time frame.
  • Post impressions - After you select Post impressions, you’ll be directed to the Content analytics page. You can view information about your posts’ impressions in the Metrics and Content engagement sections.

Join conversations

In the Join conversations module, you can see trending posts from your employees or from Pages that you follow. After you select a post from this module, you’ll be redirected to the Feed tab where you can interact with comments, mentions, reposts and reactions.

Affiliated LinkedIn Pages

An affiliated LinkedIn Page is linked to another LinkedIn Page by the LinkedIn Support team and represents a parent or subsidiary organization. The Affiliated pages section on a LinkedIn Page shows all affiliations, including acquired Pages. A Page can have multiple affiliated Pages, but only one parent Page.

Affiliating two Pages might be necessary when an organization:

  • Wants their affiliations or initiatives to be more visible to their followers.
  • Is acquired but remains a separate working entity.
  • Is acquired and its products continue to function under the acquired brand.

Before submitting your affiliation request, please review the following irreversible actions:

  • Jobs associated with the affiliated Page can be made visible on the parent Page.
  • Employees associated with the affiliated Page can be added to the employee total of the parent Page. The associated employee’s profile won’t be changed.

You must be an admin of both Pages to request affiliation. By requesting a Page affiliation as an admin, you’re also:

  • Verifying that you’re authorized to act on behalf of both organizations’ Pages.
  • Authorizing LinkedIn to list the indicated Page as an affiliated Page of the parent Page.
  • Verifying that admins of both Pages are aware of the request.
  • Acknowledging that no changes to admins, followers, or analytics will be applied to both Pages as result of the affiliation process.
  • Acknowledging that parent Page admins don’t gain admin access to the child Page.
  • Acknowledging that an Affiliated pages module will appear on the parent Page.

To request a Page affiliation, please contact us with the following information:

  • Both Page URLs.
  • State if you want the affiliated Page jobs visible on the parent Page.
  • State if you want the employees associated with the affiliated Page to be added to the employee total of the parent Page.

Here’s a tip

Another option to consider for building brand and initiative awareness is Showcase Pages. Learn more about LinkedIn Showcase Pages and other types of LinkedIn Pages.

Before and after you deactivate a LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page

Your LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page can only be deactivated by a super admin of the Page. While it isn’t possible to completely delete a Page, deactivating the Page hides it from members and removes it from search results on LinkedIn.

If your organization is no longer in operation or has been rebranded, we suggest keeping your Page active so current and former employees can maintain their work experience association on their LinkedIn profile. If the organization is active but you’re no longer affiliated with them, you can remove yourself as an admin from the Page.

Before you deactivate your Page, you’ll need to meet the below criteria:

  • The Page is active.
  • You’re a super admin of the Page and currently signed in to LinkedIn.
  • If the page you want to deactivate was auto-created by LinkedIn (a listing Page), you may be able to claim and deactivate it if you meet the eligibility criteria.
  • The Page doesn’t have any active Showcase Pages. If you have active Showcase Pages, a super admin of the Showcase Pages must deactivate them before you can deactivate your Page.
  • The Page doesn’t have a Career Page. Please contact us if your page has a Career Page.
  • The Page doesn’t have affiliated Pages. Please contact us to remove affiliations with other Pages.
  • The Page has fewer than 100 associated members.
  • The Page doesn’t have any active or paused ad campaigns. Delete or archive any active or paused ad campaigns associated with your Page.
  • The company hasn’t been acquired.
  • The Page doesn’t have any published Product Pages. If you have published Product Pages, a super or content admin of the Page must unpublish the Product Pages to deactivate your Page.
  • Your Page does not have any apps integrated with it that are still required.

After confirming that you meet this criteria, learn how to deactivate a LinkedIn Page or a Showcase Page.

Here’s a tip

If you’d like to use your current Page URL for a new Page, please contact us for assistance before deactivating your Page.

After you deactivate your Page:

  • Your Page URL can be repurposed for another Page upon request by other Page admins.
  • If a member previously added the company to the Experience section of their profile, the deactivated Page name will still appear on their profile. However, the logo will be replaced by a placeholder image, and the link to your Page will be removed.
  • After a Page is deactivated, super admins will receive an email confirmation along with a link to reactivate the Page.

Important to know

LinkedIn may remove Pages that go against our Professional Community Policies. If you believe your Page was incorrectly removed, please contact us to request reactivation.

Claim a LinkedIn Listing Page

Listing Pages are Pages created by LinkedIn to help members and companies build their presence on LinkedIn. All Listing Pages have a banner indicating that it was created by LinkedIn.

Who can use this feature?

If you’re eligible, you will see the Claim this page option at the top of the Listing Page to claim it. If you’re not eligible to claim, we recommend you check to see whether your colleagues are eligible.

If you’re a current employee, you can claim the Listing Page to continue building your organization’s presence on LinkedIn.

If another eligible member has claimed the Listing Page, you can request admin access. If you notice an organization has a Listing Page, an admin who meets the eligibility criteria can claim and manage the Listing Page. Until the Listing Page is claimed, they are not being actively managed by Page admins.

To share the Listing Page with the admin, you would select Share this page in the top banner.

To claim a Listing Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Listing Page.
  2. Click the Claim this page button in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select the checkbox to verify that you’re an authorized representative of your organization to claim the Page.
  4. Click Confirm. You’ll be routed to your Page admin view.

To claim a Listing Page:

  1. Find the organization’s Listing Page.
  2. Tap Claim this page.
  3. Tap the checkbox to verify that you’re an authorized representative.
  4. Tap Confirm. You’ll be routed to your Page admin view.

Once you claim a Listing Page, the banner is removed, and it becomes a LinkedIn Page.

Convert your LinkedIn Page type

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can change your Page type to accurately represent your organization. When a Page is converted, the original Page no longer exists and it can’t be reverted to the original Page type. Followers, content, and the Page’s custom URL will remain the same.

Important to know

Please review the available Page conversion types and their effects before requesting a conversion. Page conversions are irreversible.

Convert a Company Page to a Showcase Page

  • The only change in the URL will be the replacement of “company” to “showcase”. For example: Xyz (linkedin.com) will change to Xyz (linkedin.com).
  • The Showcase Page will appear as an affiliated Page of the designated parent Page.
  • Member work experience will link to the new parent Page within 24 hours of the conversion.
  • The existing cover image of the converted Page might need to be updated.
  • The description field will be lessened to 200 characters.
  • Admins of the converted LinkedIn Page will be admins of the new Showcase Page.
  • Followers will be migrated to the new Showcase Page.
  • All shared posts or sponsored posts will be migrated to the new Showcase Page.
  • Jobs associated with the converted LinkedIn Page will be automatically associated with the new parent LinkedIn Page or will need to be manually re-associated to a different LinkedIn Page by the job poster.
  • Any affiliated Page and Showcase Page associated with the converted LinkedIn Page will automatically migrate to the parent LinkedIn Page.
Here’s a tip

A Company Page can’t be converted to a Showcase Page if the request is due to an acquisition or if the desired Showcase Page is a subsidiary.

Convert a Showcase Page to a Company Page

  • The only change in the URL will be the replacement of “showcase” to “company.” For example: Xyz (linkedin.com) will change to Xyz (linkedin.com).
  • The newly converted Company Page will no longer appear as an affiliated Page of the designated parent Page unless otherwise requested.
  • The existing cover image of the converted Page might need to be updated.
  • Admins of the converted Showcase Page will have the same admin permissions on the new Company Page.
  • Followers will be migrated to the new Company Page.
  • All shared posts and sponsored posts will be migrated to the new Company Page.

Convert a Company Page to a University Page

  • The only change in the URL will be the replacement of “company” to “school”. For example: Xyz (0) will change to Xyz (linkedin.com).
  • All followers will remain on the newly converted University Page.
  • The Alumni section won’t be visible on your Page until members list your University Page in the Education section of their profile.

By requesting a Page conversion as an Admin, you’re:

  • The rightful super admin of the LinkedIn Page to be converted.
    • For Company to Showcase conversions, you will have to be the admin of the desired parent page
  • Verifying that you’re authorized to act on behalf of the organization in relation to converting a LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page.
  • Acknowledging that this conversion is irreversible. LinkedIn can’t retrieve data once the conversion occurs. The converted Page can’t be reverted.

To convert your Page, please contact us with the following information:

  • The Page name exactly as it appears.
  • The Page URL.
  • The conversion type.
  • The reason the Page should be converted.
  • Company Page to a Showcase Page - Clearly identify the Page name and URL that you’d like to designate as the new parent Page.
  • Showcase Page to a Company Page - State if you’d like the Pages to remain affiliated.

Create a LinkedIn Page

Connect with clients, employees, and the LinkedIn community.

Create

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free, helping you represent and build your organization’s brand on LinkedIn. Pages can help LinkedIn members learn about your business, brand, products and services, and job opportunities.

You must have a LinkedIn account to create a Page. Before you create one, we recommend reviewing our best practices.

Important to know

You can create a LinkedIn Page either using the desktop version or using the LinkedIn mobile app on an iOS device. Creating a LinkedIn Page is not supported on Android mobile devices.

To create a Page:

  1. Click the ** For Business** icon in the upper-right corner of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Scroll down and click Create a Company Page .

  3. Select the Page type:

    • Company
    • Showcase page
    • Educational institution

  4. Enter your Page identity, Company or Institution details, and Profile details information.

  5. Select the verification box to confirm that you have the right to act on behalf of the company or school.

  6. Click the Create page button.

    • If you receive an error message, try our troubleshooting tips for creating your Page.

  7. Click Start building your page! to complete your LinkedIn Page.

To create a Page:

  1. Go to any LinkedIn Page.

  2. Tap the More icon on the right and select Create a LinkedIn Page.

  3. Select the Page type:

    • Company
    • Educational institution

  4. Enter your Company name, LinkedIn public URL, Website, Industry, Company size, Company type, and Tagline (optional).

  5. Tap the verification box to confirm that you have the right to act on behalf of the company or school.

  6. Tap Create in the upper-right corner.

Here’s a tip

As an admin, you can also convert your Page. Learn more about the different types of LinkedIn Pages.

Results

Once you’ve created a Page, you become the super admin of the Page and can assign others to be admins of your Page.

Create a LinkedIn Page best practices

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free, helping you represent and build your organization’s brand on LinkedIn.

LinkedIn Pages provide a platform for companies, universities, and high schools to share information about their brand with visitors and followers. All Page super admins should consider the best practices for Page creation.

Important to know

Your use of LinkedIn Pages is subject to our Professional Community Policies and the LinkedIn Pages Terms. Violations of our policies or terms can result in action against your account or content.

[Embedded video omitted]

Best practices before creating a Page

  • Create a LinkedIn profile with your real first and last name. Confirm the email address associated with your personal LinkedIn account.
  • Ensure a Page doesn’t currently exist for your organization. If one already exists, you can request admin access.
  • If the Page exists on LinkedIn as a Listing Page, you can claim it. If you aren’t eligible to claim the Listing Page, you can share it with someone else from the organization to claim it. Once they have claimed the Page, they can add you as an admin on the Page.
  • Build your professional network to ensure you have enough connections to create a Page.

Best practices when creating a Page

  • Members can search for your Page based on keywords or attributes.
  • All Page URLs will be structured as linkedin.com/company/[your company name]. LinkedIn members and search engines will use this unique URL to find your Page. If your desired URL has already been taken by another organization, you can still create a Page for your organization by using a different URL for your Page.
  • Any improper characters are automatically replaced with a hyphen. Your Page URL must be formatted accordingly:
    • Must contain at least one non-numeric character.
    • Can’t contain uppercase alphabet letters. Can contain lowercase alphabet, numeric, hyphen, or Chinese, Japanese, or Korean (CJK) Unicode characters.
    • Can’t include more than one consecutive hyphen, for example, company–name, and can’t have a hyphen at the beginning or end. For example, -company-name or company-name-.
  • Complete all of the sections for your Page. Complete Pages see a 30 percent increase in weekly Page views.

Best practices after your Page is complete

  • Add other super admins to your Page in case a super admin loses access to the Page or leaves the organization. LinkedIn can’t provide Page admin information to members or replace or remove admins.
  • Review how you can protect your Page by turning on two-factor authentication, verification, and managing messages to your Page. Learn more about ways to protect your LinkedIn Page.
  • Share your Page information with other employees in your organization, such as your Human Resources department.
  • Share your Page on LinkedIn and other platforms by clicking the  Share Page button in your admin view.
  • If you don’t see your Page in search results, keep in mind that the search experience uses a variety of factors to provide relevant results. To help boost the Page’s ranking, try building your Page’s following.
  • If you add your Page as your employer to your LinkedIn profile, it might take between 14 and 30 days for you to show up as an associated employee on that Page.
  • Review analytics for each type of post by clicking on Page posts in the left panel of your admin view.
  • Consider subscribing to a Premium Company Page to help you make your Page stand out and convert more LinkedIn members into clients for your business.

Create a LinkedIn Showcase Page

Showcase Pages are extensions of your LinkedIn Page designed to spotlight a brand, business unit, or initiative. You can create Showcase Pages for aspects of your business with their own messages and audience segments.

Important to know

You must be a super admin of the parent LinkedIn Page to create a Showcase Page. You can create up to 25 Showcase Pages. A Showcase Page can only be associated with one parent LinkedIn Page.

To create a Showcase Page:

  1. Access your Page super admin view of the parent Page.
  2. Click Create in the upper-left corner of the Page.
  3. Select Create a Showcase Page from the dropdown.
  4. Enter the desired parent Page in the Associated organization page box.
  5. Enter the required information as indicated by an asterisk.
  6. Click Create page.

From your admin view, you can edit or complete your new Showcase Page.

Here’s a tip

To help prevent spam, there are limits on how many Showcase Pages you can create in a day. If you receive this error message, wait at least 24 hours before you create another Showcase Page.

Create and publish a LinkedIn Product Page

As a LinkedIn Page super or content admin, you can create Product Pages that showcase your organization’s products on your LinkedIn Page’s Product tab. When you create a new Product Page, our team must review it before it can be published.

Who can use this feature?

Product Pages are currently only available to Pages in the following types of industries: business-to-business (B2B) software, computer hardware, financial services, insurance, education, healthcare, and pharmaceutical. While creating a Product Page, you will need to specifically mention an industry name within these industry groups.

To create a Product Page:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.

  2. Select + Create below the Page name in the upper-left corner, then select +Add a product. If you don’t see the +Add a product option, your Page industry might not be eligible.

  3. Select whether your product and organization have the same name.

  4. If your product and organization have the same name, you’ll create a flagship Product Page.

    • Select Yes, my product and organization have the same name and click the Next button.
    • On the confirmation page, select the checkbox next to I understand, then click Create.

  5. If your product and organization have different names:

    • SelectNo, my product has a different name and click the Next button.
    • Enter your product name and click the Get started button.

  6. You’ll be routed to your new Product Page.

  7. Enter all required information by clicking the Edit icon next to each field. Required fields are highlighted and include an asterisk.

Important to know

Click and type in the Add category field to see category options. Adding a category is mandatory, and your Product Page won’t be approved if you leave the field blank.

  • Your default #Hashtag is your #productname. For example, ABC Tools would be #abctools. Custom hashtags aren’t currently available.

  1. Click the Save button for each item edited.

  2. Click the Submit for review button.

    You’ll receive a notification in the Activity tab once the approval process is complete.

To publish your Product Page once it’s approved:

  1. Go to your Page super or content admin view.
  2. Click Activity in the left menu.
  3. Click the View product button, then Publish product.

Important to know

After a flagship Product Page has been published, the name and logo can’t be changed.

If your company offers more than one product, you can create up to 35 additional Product Pages. Only the ten mostly recently created Product Pages will be shown to your Page visitors.

Difference between flagship and separate LinkedIn Product Pages

LinkedIn Product Pages allow organizations to highlight their products on LinkedIn. Page super or content admins can create a flagship product or a standard product, which each have different features.

Flagship

Flagship products have the same name as your company. If you have a flagship product, your product information is combined with your Page and appears directly in the Product tab. Flagship products will also feature customers directly in the Page top card.

[Image: combined linkedin product page]

You can have a flagship product as well as separate Product Pages.

Important to know

Your flagship product is integrated into, and a direct reflection of your Company Page. Your name, URL or logo for your flagship product can’t be changed.

Separate

If your Page has more than one product, or a single product with a different name from your Page, you can create separate Pages for each product. Each Product Page is linked in the Products tab.

[Image: separate linkedin product page]

Here’s a tip

If you want to convert your separate Product Page to a flagship Product Page, you’ll need to unpublish the Page and then create a new one using the flagship creation process. If you aren’t able to do this, please contact us.

Differences between LinkedIn Pages and Listing Pages

To represent and build your organization’s presence on LinkedIn, you can create a LinkedIn Page or claim a Listing Page to represent your organization.

LinkedIn Pages

LinkedIn Pages help members learn about the organization’s business, brand, products and services, and job opportunities. To interact with members of an organization, you must have a Page on LinkedIn.

To create a Page, you’ll first need to have a personal LinkedIn profile. You can then designate anyone affiliated with the organization as an admin.

Important to know

Although you must have a LinkedIn profile to create a Page, you don’t need a separate LinkedIn account login to access the Page’s admin view.

LinkedIn Listing Pages

LinkedIn creates Listing Pages to help members and companies build their presence on LinkedIn. If you’re a current employee, you can claim a Listing Page created by LinkedIn to continue building your organization’s presence on LinkedIn.

All Listing Pages have a banner indicating that it was created by LinkedIn. Once claimed, the banner will be automatically removed, and the Listing Page will become like a LinkedIn Page. It’s a violation of LinkedIn’s User Agreement for non-employees to misrepresent themselves as members of an organization.

Use of business information

The information we obtain to create Listing Pages is compiled from a variety of sources, including publicly available information, licensed data from third parties, and data collected via APIs. Information contained in Listing Pages has been collected for business-related purposes only, and any information on Listing Pages which identifies an individual relates to their professional capacity only.

If you believe a local listing is inaccurate or should be removed, please contact us. If you have a question or concern about your personal data associated with a Listing Page or would like further information on how LinkedIn processes your personal data, please visit LinkedIn’s Privacy Policy.

Edit notification settings for your LinkedIn Page

With a LinkedIn Page, you can manage notifications of the Page’s activity. Notification types include push notifications to your mobile device, notifications sent to your email address associated with your LinkedIn profile, and notifications sent within the LinkedIn app. As a Page admin, you can edit your notification settings so that you can stay informed about any insights or trends in your Page analytics.

To edit notifications for your LinkedIn Page:

  1. Click the Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown menu.

  3. Click Notifications and then click Pages.

  4. Switch the Allow page notifications toggle to On and then turn on notifications for:

    • Page invitations -Status of invitations to Pages that you’ve sent or received
    • Page updates - Activity on your employer’s Page or by companies you follow
    • Activity on pages you manage - Summarized activity such as likes, comments, messages, and reminders to post on your Page
    • Page messaging – Notifications of when your Page receives a message
    • Insights on your pages - Insights on new followers and page views for the Pages you manage
    • Service page project updates - Updates on your projects, such as new requests for proposals
    • Reviews for your services - New reviews for your Service Page that have been added
    • Sponsored requests - Notifications about your posts being sponsored by pages

  5. For every Page activity or update, select how you would like to receive notifications. You can choose from:

    • In-app notifications – Delivered inside the app
    • Push notifications – Pushed to your device immediately
    • Email – Sent to your primary email address

  6. Tap the Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  7. Tap Settings from the left side menu.

  8. Tap Notifications, and then Pages.

  9. Switch the Allow page notifications toggle to On and then turn on notifications for:

    • Page invitations – Status of invitations to Pages that you’ve sent or received
    • Page updates – Activity on your employer’s Page or by companies you follow
    • Activity on pages you manage - Summarized activity such as likes, comments, messages, and reminders to post on your Page
    • Insights on your pages – Insights on new followers and page views for the Pages you manage
    • Service page project updates - Updates on your projects, such as new requests for proposals
    • Reviews for your services - New reviews for your Service Page that have been added
    • Sponsored requests - Notifications about your posts being sponsored by pages

  10. For every Page activity or update, select how you would like to receive notifications. You can choose from:

    • In-app notifications – Delivered inside the app
    • Push notifications – Pushed to your device immediately
    • Email – Sent to your primary email address

Optionally, you can turn off all notifications by turning off the Allow page notifications toggle. You can make changes to your notification settings at any time.

Find an organization’s Page on LinkedIn

LinkedIn Pages allow you to explore companies, universities, and high schools you’re interested in by offering culture insights, the latest organization updates and industry news, and information about new job opportunities.

To find a Page:

  1. From the top of your LinkedIn homepage, type the company, university, or high school name into the Search bar.

  2. Click Companies or Schools at the top of the search results page.

    • Click Locations, Industry, or Company size to filter the results for a company (optional).

  3. Click the correct organization name in the results list.

To find a Page:

  1. Tap the Search field.
  2. Enter the organization name.
  3. Tap Search.
  4. Tap Companies or Schools at the top of the page, then tap the correct name in the results list.

Here’s a tip

We can’t guarantee that a Page will be displayed in the results list that appears as you type its name into a search box. The Page names that appear are based on exact, partial, stock, and domain name matches. If you don’t find a match, it’s possible the organization hasn’t added a Page yet.

  • If you’d like to manage a Page you’ll need to request admin access.
  • If you’re not an employee, learn more about how you can interact and use LinkedIn Pages as a member.
