If you want to change your LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page name

As a super admin, you may need to make changes to the name of your LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page to clarify its business structure and entity information or reduce the name’s complexity.

Following are some scenarios in which you might want to consider changing your LinkedIn Page or Showcase Page name:

  • Clarify your company’s structure
  • Correct a typographical error in the Page name
  • Rebrand your Page name because of a merger or acquisition

Depending on the scope of change to the Page name, the change can be categorized as a minimal change or a significant change. This scope of change, and number of employees associated with your Company Page determines the actions you will need to take to change your Page name.

Before you change your LinkedIn Page name, keep in mind that:

  • Followers can’t be migrated when a Page change is due to an acquisition, merger, de-merger, or company split, as we can’t assume followers would want to follow the newly formed company.
  • Changing your Page name doesn’t change work experience on the profiles of current and former employees. We recommend posting a Page post and notifying members so they can update their profiles to reflect the name change.
  • The Page URL isn’t automatically changed when you change your Page name.
  • There is a 100-character limit on the company name.

Important to know

If you are an admin of a verified company Page and would like to change your Company Page name, then irrespective of the type of change you need to make to your Page name, you must contact us.

The table below describes the different types of name changes and the steps that you need to take to make those name changes.

  • Type of Page name change: Minimal name change; Example of change: Correcting typographical errors Changing Ltd. to Inc.; Number of associated employees: Small; Actions needed: Use the Edit Page option from your Page admin view to change the name. After changing the name, notify employees of the name change.
  • Type of Page name change: Large; Example of change: Contact us to change the name.
  • Type of Page name change: Significant name change; Example of change: Does not meet the minimal name change factors; Number of associated employees: Small; Actions needed: Use the Edit Page option from your Page admin view to change the name. After changing the name, notify employees of the name change.
  • Type of Page name change: Large; Example of change: Create a new Page with the new Page name. Affiliate the old Page and the new Page. Migrate followers, if applicable.
  • Type of Page name change: Rebranding; Example of change: Name change because of merger or acquisition; Number of associated employees: Small; Actions needed: Use the Edit Page option from your Page admin view to change the name. After changing the name, notify employees of the name change
  • Type of Page name change: Large; Example of change: Create a press release indicating the name change, and the reasons for the rebrand, and share it publicly. Contact us with the publicly shared press release. We’ll review the press release to determine if the rebrand meets the criteria for a name change and follower migration. We’ll provide the next steps after reviewing the provided material

Limits on number of admins for a LinkedIn Page

As a super admin for a LinkedIn Page, you can add admins with the following roles for your Page:

  • Content admins
  • Analysts

To ensure that LinkedIn remains a trusted platform, we may limit the number of admins who can be added to a LinkedIn Page. Different LinkedIn Pages may have unique limits on the number of admins that can be added. Once the limit has been reached, you will see an error message that prevents you from adding additional admins due to one or more of the following reasons:

  • Your LinkedIn Page has too many admins
  • Your Page has several pending admin requests that need a response
  • Not enough existing admins who are verified

To continue with adding additional admins to your LinkedIn Page, you can:

  • Respond to existing requests for admin access
  • Remove any admins who are no longer needed to manage the Page
  • Verify your member account

LinkedIn Events organized by Pages FAQ

LinkedIn Page super and content admins can use LinkedIn Events to bring their professional community together safely and in real-time.

Creating an Event

Any Page super or content admin can create an Event that will be organized and hosted by the Page.

Only members who are also a Page super or content admin can see this option. If you want to create an Event for a Page, you’ll need to have admin access.

A Page for a company, organization, school, or university can create and organize an Event.

Yes. As a LinkedIn Page admin, you can create a test event to learn how events work and validate your setup before going live.

To test your event, use the built‑in test event option during event creation or live streaming.

  • Don’t create test or temporary Pages to test your event.
  • Test events let you check your setup, including your streaming configuration, without broadcasting to your audience.

Learn how to create a LinkedIn Live Test event from your LinkedIn Page.

Managing an Event

Yes, you can create, modify, and view a list of all past and upcoming Events through the Manage module of your admin view.

You can only invite your connections to the Event. All attendees of the Event can also invite their connections.

You can only invite your 1st-degree connections to attend your event. Page followers can’t be invited to an Event if they aren’t connected to any of the Page’s admins.

Each Page admin can send up to 1000 invitations per week. If you organize multiple events, this limit applies across events and does not increase.

A super or content admin can also share the Event on their Page so it can be seen by the Page’s followers. This can help the Event to reach the target audience by sponsoring the post within the Page.

Any super or content admin of your Page can manage an Event you’ve created. A super or content admin can edit and manage the Event even if they aren’t attending it.

Yes. Once you make the member a super or content admin of your Page, they’ll be able to manage the Event.

While an admin can see all attendees (including other admins attending the Event) from the Manage Attendees view, there is no label that identifies an admin from other attendees.

No, non-admin attendees of the Event can’t see the individual Page admins.

No, the organizer can’t be changed once the Event has been created.

If the Event was organized by a Page, only the Page super and content admins can manage it. If the Event was organized by an individual profile (Page admin or not), only the individual can manage it.

Any Page super or content admin (even if they aren’t attending) can edit, cancel, or delete the Event.

The Organizer, Event type (Online or In person), and the Event format (LinkedIn Live or External event link) cannot be changed after the event has been posted.

Yes, any Page super or content admin can remove an attendee from the Event.

Posts and engagement on the Event page

You can copy the Event URL and post or share it directly on the Page so that the post about the Event is visible to the Page’s followers. You can also promote or target the post.

Event notifications

The notifications that are generated for Events organized by individual profiles are the same for Events organized by Pages.

For attendees of the Event, this includes:

  • A reminder notification about the Event’s start date and time, which is sent to members seven days and three days before the Event, as well as 15 minutes before the scheduled Event.
  • A notification for changes to the Event, such as the day, time, venue, or if the Event has been cancelled.

For further assistance with your Event, please contact us.

LinkedIn Life tab content marked as inappropriate

At LinkedIn, we have Professional Community Policies which outline activities that are acceptable on the platform, and what is unacceptable and may be stopped. To ensure members are served quality and appropriate content, Life tab content undergoes checks by LinkedIn’s filtering system and may be marked as inappropriate and indicated by an in-product message.

Your Life tab content will not be published until inappropriate elements are removed. If your Life tab content has already been published, it may still be marked as inappropriate during a secondary check. In such cases, the Life tab content will remain published, but will not be visible to members. Only super admins of the Page will be able to view the Life tab content that has been marked as inappropriate. The main LinkedIn Page and additional other Life tab content will remain visible to the members.

If you have additional questions as to why your Life tab content has been marked as inappropriate, please contact us.

  • Recognize and report spam, inappropriate, and abusive content

LinkedIn Page admin roles

LinkedIn Pages offer Page admin and paid media admin roles to allow for tiered levels of management for all activities related to your Page. Paid media admins can primarily take specific actions on behalf of the Page through Campaign Manager or LinkedIn Recruiter. A member can have Page admin and paid media admin roles assigned at the same time. Admin roles can be granted to members, associated employees, and advertisers.

Important to know

To become an admin of a Page, you’ll need to request admin access or be granted access by an existing admin.

Page admins

  • Super admin - Gives access to every Page admin permission available, including adding and removing any type of admin, editing Page information, creating job postings, and deactivating the Page. Your main landing page is the super admin view.
  • Content admin – Gives permission to create and manage Page content, including posts (as well as boosting posts), and events. Your main landing page is the content admin view.
  • Analyst – Gives permission to monitor the Page’s performance through analytics to help drive goals. Analysts have limited access to the Page in third-party tools. You’ll only have access to the Analytics tab of a Page, which is also your main landing page.

Super and content admins who create job postings might require additional permissions through email verification.

Paid media admins

  • Sponsored Content poster – Gives permission to create Sponsored Content ads on behalf of an organization or to sponsor organic posts in Campaign Manager. This role doesn’t grant access to boosting organic posts directly on a Page (see content admin information above).
  • Lead Gen Forms manager – Gives permission to download leads received from Lead Gen Forms created in Campaign Manager.
  • Landing Pages manager – Gives permission to create and edit Landing Pages that are associated with your Page. You can create and manage Landing Pages in Campaign Manager.

LinkedIn Page types and their functions

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free to represent your organization and build its presence on LinkedIn. Pages make it easy for members to learn more about your company or school, including brand, products and services, and job opportunities.

Here’s a tip

You need to have a LinkedIn profile before you can create a Page. Once your profile is set up, you can create, access, and manage your organization’s Page directly from your LinkedIn profile.

A LinkedIn Page is your organization’s official presence on LinkedIn, separate from the personal profiles that individuals use. Learn more about the differences between a LinkedIn profile and a LinkedIn Page.

Important to know

Your use of LinkedIn Pages is subject to our Professional Community Policies and the LinkedIn Pages Terms. Violations of our policies or terms can result in action against your account or content.

When you create a Page on LinkedIn, you’re assigned as the admin by default.

Following are the types of Pages that you can create on LinkedIn:

  • Page type: Company Page; Key functions: You can create a free Company Page to represent your organization on LinkedIn, share posts to grow and engage your followers, use analytics to understand your audience, and add a call to action to attract and convert leads. To further enhance your Page and convert more members into clients, you can purchase a Premium Company Page subscription.; Requirements: Personal LinkedIn Profile
  • Page type: Career Page; Key functions: You can create a Career Page to help attract the right talent by showcasing your culture and open roles. After you purchase a Career Page license, you can add a Life tab (for educational institutions and businesses) or a What We Do tab (for search and staffing companies) to create a targeted audience for your Career Page.; Requirements: Company Page or University Page
  • Page type: Showcase Page; Key functions: You can use a Showcase Page to represent a brand, business unit, or organizational initiative, with the goal of developing a long-term relationship with a specific audience.; Requirements: Company Page or University Page
  • Page type: Service Page; Key functions: You can offer services to LinkedIn members, making your offers more discoverable both on LinkedIn and through search engines like Google. Any LinkedIn member can message you for free regarding your services and may also request a proposal for your services.; Requirements: Personal profile + Company page or University Page
  • Page type: Product Page; Key functions: You can showcase your company products to LinkedIn members. You can choose from a variety of categories, including digital products like online courses, e-commerce platforms, and administrative support.; Requirements: Company Page or University Page
  • Page type: University Page; Key functions: You can create a Page for your university or high school to highlight your alumni. They’ll appear on your Page once students add your school in the Education section of their profiles.; Requirements: Personal LinkedIn Profile
  • Page type: Listing Page; Key functions: LinkedIn creates Listing Pages to help universities and companies build their presence on the platform. If you’re a current employee, you can claim a Listing Page, which automatically removes its banner and makes it function like a Company or University Page. Non-employees violate LinkedIn’s User Agreement if they misrepresent themselves as members of an organization.; Requirements: Must be an eligible employee

Important to know

You must have a Company or University Page already created to create a Career, Showcase, or Product Page.You must have a LinkedIn Profile or a Company Page or a University Page already created to create a Service Page.

LinkedIn Pages admin view features

As a LinkedIn Page admin, your admin view is a centralized place to view, edit, engage with, and analyze all aspects of your Page, depending on your admin role. Features available in the admin view depend on your admin role and the type of Page you have.

Important to know

You must be a LinkedIn Page admin to access admin view features. If you do not have access, learn how to request it here. To boost posts, you must also be a Page admin. To learn more about boosting a post, click here.

You can use the Create button in the upper-left corner to create new posts, events, jobs, boosted posts, newsletters, Product Pages, Service Pages, and Showcase Pages.

The left-side navigation allows you to manage all aspects of your Page in one place. The navigation includes the following sections:

  • Tab: Dashboard; Benefits: The dashboard is the main landing page for your admin view to help you gain insights across your LinkedIn Page. Use the Today’s actions module to view suggested actions you can take to improve your Page and engage with your audience. You can also view Recent Posts, track performance and join Trending Conversations.
  • Tab: Page posts; Benefits: Review and interact with top-performing posts with comments, mentions, reposts and reactions. You can boost posts directly from this tab, and you can also take actions like editing or featuring posts.
  • Tab: Analytics; Benefits: Gain insight into the performance of your LinkedIn Page with analytics that gauge trends across metrics and time periods. View your Page’s competitor, content, follower, lead, search, employer brand (Career Pages only), and visitor highlights.
  • Tab: Feed; Benefits: The feed tab includes posts from Pages you’re following and posts from employees.
  • Tab: Activity; Benefits: View interactions with your Page, including comments, mentions, reposts, reactions, and analytics.
  • Tab: Inbox; Benefits: When messaging for your Page is enabled, you can view and reply to messages sent to your Page from your Page inbox. You can also adjust your inbox settings.
  • Tab: Edit Page; Benefits: Edit aspects of your Page such as your Page info, locations, commitments, and languages.
  • Tab: Life or What We Do; Benefits: If you’ve enhanced your LinkedIn Page with Career Pages, you can use the Life or What We Do tab to provide a preview of life at your organization through photos, testimonials, employee-written content, and more.
  • Tab: Products; Benefits: View and edit all published and unpublished LinkedIn Product Pages for your organization. Product Pages allow you to highlight your products on LinkedIn.
  • Tab: Services; Benefits: Offer services to attract new clients through a Service Page managed on your Company Page. Service Pages allow you to highlight your services on LinkedIn, upload work samples, and respond to requests for services.
  • Tab: Jobs; Benefits: Post and edit jobs and manage your automatic job posting settings.
  • Tab: Events; Benefits: Manage LinkedIn Events created by your Page. Organizing Events allows members to join professional Events and engage with your Page.
  • Tab: Newsletters; Benefits: You can create and edit newsletters as your LinkedIn Page to talk about a professional topic you’re passionate about on a regular basis. Newsletters are only available to Pages that meet the newsletter access criteria.
  • Tab: Settings; Benefits: Manage your Page’s settings, such as admin roles, who your Page follows, your messaging settings, employee verification, and Page deactivation.

The admin view of your Page allows you to manage some aspects of your Page, though some features are only available on desktop. The navigation includes the following sections:

  • Feature: Dashboard; Benefits: The dashboard is the main landing page for your admin view to help you gain insights across your LinkedIn Page. Use the Today’s actions module to view suggested actions you can take to improve your Page and engage with your audience. You can also view Recent Posts, Track Performance, and join Trending Conversations.

  • Feature: Analytics; Benefits: View your Page’s competitor, content, follower, lead, and visitor highlights.
  • Feature: Feed; Benefits: The feed tab includes posts from Pages you’re following and posts from employees.
  • Feature: Activity; Benefits: View reactions, likes, shares, comments, mentions, and post highlights generated by your Page’s follower and visitor community.
  • Feature: Inbox; Benefits: When messaging for your Page is enabled, you can view and reply to messages sent to your Page from your Page inbox. You can also adjust your inbox settings. Messaging is currently only available for certain Pages, and will gradually be made available to all Pages.
  • Feature: Edit page; Benefits: Edit aspects of your Page such as your Page info, locations, commitments, and languages.
  • Feature: Start a post; Benefits: You can create posts and include an optional image, manage comment permissions, and include brand partnerships on Page posts. You can also set a specific time to publish posts and use the AI-powered post writing assistance tool.
  • Feature: View as a member; Benefits: View your Page as a non-admin member will see it.
  • Feature: Premium features; Benefits: Explore different features to include on your Page when you have a Premium Company Page subscription.
  • Feature: Share Page; Benefits: Share your Page in a post, message, or externally to LinkedIn, or invite members to follow your Page.

LinkedIn Pages for members

Discover how to explore and engage with LinkedIn Pages to learn about organizations, their employees, and professional opportunities.

LinkedIn Pages are organizational profiles on LinkedIn that serve as a platform to represent and build an organization’s brand. It allows companies, educational institutions, and other entities to interact with LinkedIn members, showcase their business information, promote products and services, share job opportunities, and engage with specific audiences.

As a member of LinkedIn, you can use LinkedIn Pages to search for and follow organizations that you are interested in, explore job opportunities and stay updated with latest developments at that organization.

An organization’s LinkedIn Page is designed to provide you with all the information that you need in specific tabs and sections. The Top section of a LinkedIn Page displays overall information about the organization, such as industry, office locations, number of employees and followers, and the number of your connections that work there. It also includes quick action buttons, such as Follow, or Message. The toolbar includes tabs for you to use to browse detailed information about the organization.

[Image: LinkedIn Page member view]

Important to know

Options and tabs on an organization’s LinkedIn Page are dependent on whether the Page is a Premium Company Page, and if it is a Page for an educational institution or a staffing company.

You can access an organization’s LinkedIn Page from your desktop or from your mobile device. However, the number of features and options available to you on mobile could be fewer than those available from your desktop view.

The table below describes the various options on a LinkedIn Page and how you can use these options to maximize your interaction with an organization.

  • Options: Follow; Desktop: √; Mobile: X; Benefits: You can follow Pages to stay updated on companies that you are interested in.
  • Options: Custom call-to-action button (For Premium Company Page only); Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefits: Makes it easy for you to connect with organizations with actions such as Contact Us, or Learn more.
  • Options: More; Desktop: √; Mobile: X; Benefits: Displays additional options such as Send message, Request admin access, or Report abusive content.
  • Options: Ranking on Top Lists; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefits: Highlights top organizations based on LinkedIn activity which helps you identify attractive opportunities.
  • Options: Connections; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefits: Displays the number of your connections that work at the organization.
  • Options: Employee count; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefits: Displays the number of employees linked with the Page that you can use for networking opportunities
  • Options: View in Sales Navigator (Premium members only); Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefits: Premium members can gain advanced insights into the organization’s performance and business strategy

The table below describes the various tabs available to you on an organization’s LinkedIn Page and how you can use them to suit your purpose.

  • Tab: Home; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays the organization’s posts and engagement with its member community, as well as the companies, schools, or brands it is affiliated with. Services, Page posts, Products, events, recent job openings, and newsletters also appear here.
  • Tab: About; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays information about the organization’s size, industry, locations, and more. You can also privately express interest in working for a company without having to apply for a specific role, even if there are no open roles at the company, using the I’m interested button.
  • Tab: Services; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays services offered by the organization. This tab appears only if the organization offers services through a Company Page.
  • Tab: Products; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays products featured by the organization. This tab will appear if the organization has one or more Product Pages.
  • Tab: Posts; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: View posts on a Page and filter by All, Articles, Documents, Images, or Videos on desktop. Filtering posts and viewing Sponsored Ads as separate categories is not available on mobile. Use the Sort by dropdown to sort the feed by Top or Recent posts. Top posts have high engagement from Page followers while recent posts are based on the post’s timestamp.
  • Tab: Jobs; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Shows available job opportunities with the organization. You can also privately express interest in working with the organization without having to apply for a specific role.
  • Tab: Life (available for companies, universities, colleges and high schools); Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Showcases the organization’s culture through photos, testimonials, employee-written content, and more.
  • Tab: People; Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Offers employee insights on their job title, areas of study, skills, and how you’re connected with them. This tab only appears if the Page has one or more employees associated with it.
  • Tab: Alumni (For university Pages only); Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays information about alumni careers, locations, skills, and degrees earned.
  • Tab: Insights (Premium members only); Desktop: √; Mobile: √; Benefit: Displays additional organization insights such as total employee count, employee distribution, new hires, and notable company alumni and total number of job openings.

LinkedIn Product Pages

LinkedIn Product Pages allow organizations to highlight their products on LinkedIn. Products appear on your Page’s Product or Products tab, which only appears for members after you create a Product Page.

Who can use this feature?

You must be a LinkedIn Page super admin or content admin to create and edit Product Pages.

Product Pages are currently only available to Pages in the following types of industries: business-to-business (B2B) software, computer hardware, financial services, insurance, education, healthcare, and pharmaceuticals. While creating a Product page, you will need to specifically mention an industry name within these industry groups.

Here’s a tip

If your Page has a single flagship product with the same name as your company, your product information may be combined with your Page and appear directly in the Products tab.

A LinkedIn Page is a platform for organizations to share information about their organization. A LinkedIn Product Page is an extension of a LinkedIn Page where organizations can showcase the products they offer.

If your Page has a product with the same name as your company, your product information may be combined with your Page and appears directly in the Product tab as a flagship product. If your Page has more than one product, you can create separate Pages for each product. Each Product Page is linked in the Products tab. Different features are available to Pages with flagship products and separate products. If you would like to convert your separate Product page to a flagship Product Page, please contact us.

LinkedIn Service Pages FAQs

LinkedIn Service Pages are free dedicated landing pages that showcase your services and businesses.

Freelancers and small business owners who offer a service can create a Service Page. Service Pages are available globally, except in China.

You can either offer services on your Company Page or on your personal LinkedIn profile. After you set up your services, you can’t currently change whether the services are managed by your Company Page or your profile. Learn more about the differences between offering services on LinkedIn on your Company Page or on your personal profile.

A Service Page makes your services more discoverable from LinkedIn or using search sites, such as Google. Any LinkedIn member can message you for free about your services.

Any member can create a Service Page, market their brand, and build an audience on LinkedIn for free. If you have a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription, certain additional features are also available for your Service Page.

Without a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription, the Services section of your profile shows a list of services you offer. With a Premium Business subscription, including Sales Navigator and Recruiter Lite, your profile will show Services Showcase to represent your services, including media in a carousel, a Request proposal button, a preview of your service description, your ratings, and your most recent four or five star review. You are also eligible to receive additional project requests from potential clients.

LinkedIn Showcase Pages

A Showcase Page can be used by a Page admin to represent a brand, business unit, or organization initiative. Showcase Pages are intended to develop a long-term relationship with a specific audience. If you have a one-time event, we recommend other advertising products to promote your event on LinkedIn.

You can share posts and Sponsored Content with LinkedIn members who follow your Showcase Pages, separate from the parent LinkedIn Page.

A Showcase Page can only be associated to one LinkedIn Page (known as the parent Page). Below you’ll find the features offered on both Showcase Pages and LinkedIn Pages as well as features that are specific to LinkedIn Pages only.

  • Feature: Page analytics; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Activity notifications; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Sponsor posts; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Featured groups; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Social media content management; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Appear in search results for searches and Ads business accounts on LinkedIn; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Members can follow the Page; LinkedIn Page: ✓; Showcase Page: ✓
  • Feature: Associating a profile with a Page; LinkedIn Page: ✓
  • Feature: Associating a job posting with a Page; LinkedIn Page: ✓
  • Feature: Career Pages; LinkedIn Page: ✓

Showcase Page analytics and notifications are calculated separately from Page analytics and notifications.

Followers and follower counts aren’t shared between Showcase Pages and Pages. Followers from the parent Page also can’t be migrated or carried over to a Showcase Page.

A Showcase Page will only appear in a LinkedIn search for members who also follow the Showcase Page.

Members associated with a LinkedIn Page

When LinkedIn members add work experience to their profile, they can include the organization where they work. If they select a company, university, or high school from the list of organizations, they automatically appear on that organization’s LinkedIn Page.

If a colleague or employee isn’t shown in the list of associated members on your Page, they can add the organization as a position to the Experience section of their profile. Only members who are currently associated will appear on your Page. It can take up to 30 days for the associated member count to update after new members are added or former members are removed. Currently, admins can’t manually add an associated member to a Page.

If someone accidentally selects the wrong company, university, or high school name from the list, their profile may be associated with the wrong Page. Keep in mind that even if someone incorrectly appears on a Page, they can’t edit the Page or manage its admins unless they’re a super admin.

Important to know

Only admins can report inaccurate employment or education details on another member’s profile that appear on their Page.

If you accidentally associated your profile with the wrong company, university, or high school, you can edit your Experience section to remove your association. It can take up to 30 days for changes to take effect. If you can’t add the correct Page when updating your experience, follow the Page, clear your cache and cookies, sign out of LinkedIn and then sign in again.

Here’s a tip

The employee count displayed on an organization’s LinkedIn Page is clickable. You can click it to view a list of employees associated with the organization, including their profiles and job information.

Merge duplicate Pages for a university

A LinkedIn Page super admin may want to merge more than one of their Pages for a university to strengthen and centralize their brand on LinkedIn with one concise Page. You can only merge Pages by contacting our support team.

The following criteria must be met before submitting a merge request:

  • You’re a super admin of the Pages you’d like to merge.
  • The Pages are duplicate Pages for the same university.
  • There must be at least one member associated with the Page that’s being merged.
  • The names on both Pages need to match.
  • Both Pages must be university Pages. We can’t merge a university Page with a Company Page.

Important to know

At LinkedIn, the member experience is our top priority and our policies are designed to protect member trust. The parameters below will be upheld to maintain information provided by a member and not modify an action taken by a member in a way that deviates from their original intentions without their expressed acknowledgment or approval.

Before submitting your merge request, consider the following information:

  • A merge applied to Pages for a university are final; changes can’t be reversed.
  • All merging Pages for universities will be inactive and any parent relationships to other Pages will be removed.
  • Only the main Page for a university will remain active.
  • All subsidiary Pages of the merging universities will be moved under the active Page for a university.
  • Associated members and alumni will be migrated and followers will be duplicated to the active Page. It can take several days for the new associated member count to update. If members edit the Education or Experience sections on their profiles with the correct Page name, the count might update more quickly.
  • Merging your Pages doesn’t automatically change the Page name in the Education or Experience sections of the profiles of associated members. We recommend creating a Page post to notify members so they can update their profiles to reflect the retained Page.
  • The vanity URL of the merged Page will be appended with “Invalidated.” Invalidated vanity URLs are available for other Pages to use.

Important to know

Admins won’t be merged to the active Page. Confirm that all admins are added to the active Page if you want them to retain admin access.

To merge your Pages for a university, please contact us with the following information:

  • The school names exactly as they appear on the Pages for the university.
  • The URLs of the duplicate Pages for the university.
  • Clearly identify the Pages that need to be merged, and the Page that needs to remain active.
  • The reason the Pages should be merged.

Merge your LinkedIn Pages for a company

A LinkedIn Page super admin can merge their Company Pages to strengthen and centralize their brand on LinkedIn with one concise Page. Merging Company Pages can only be done by contacting our support team.

The following criteria must be met before submitting a merge request:

  • You’re a super admin of the Pages you’d like to merge.
  • The Pages are duplicates, regional, or divisional Pages for the same company. Company Pages can’t be merged with University Pages.
  • There must be at least one member associated with the Company Page that’s being merged.
  • The names on both Pages need to match.
  • Both Pages must be for organizations. A Page can’t be merged with a member profile or group.

Important to know

At LinkedIn, the member experience is our top priority, and our policies are designed to protect member trust. The parameters outlined below will be upheld to maintain information provided by a member and not modify an action taken by a member in a way that deviates from their original intentions without their expressed acknowledgment or approval.

Before submitting your merge request consider the following information:

  • Once a Page is merged it can’t be reversed.
  • Data associated with a merged Page, including text and image content, boosted posts, analytics, posts and shared posts, and app integrations can’t be moved to the retained Page and will no longer be accessible once the merge is complete.
  • LinkedIn Ads accounts associated with the merged Page can’t be moved to the retained Page, and ad creatives associated with them can’t be reactivated.
  • Followers are duplicated to the retained Page.
  • All the members associated with the merged Page, including any subsidiary Pages, will be associated with the retained Page. It can take several days for the new associated member count to update. If members edit their work experience on their profiles with the correct Page name, the count might update more quickly.
  • Merging your Pages doesn’t automatically change the Page name in the Experience section of the profiles of current and former associated members. We recommend creating a Page post to notify members so they can update their profiles to reflect the retained Page.
  • Job postings associated with the merged Page will continue to be active but won’t be migrated to the retained Page. You’ll need to manually re-associate the job posting with the retained Page.
  • The merged Page will no longer be active or discoverable through search.
  • Admins of the merged Page won’t automatically become admins of the retained Page. Any specific admin access must be actioned by a super admin on the retained Page.
  • Acquired Company Pages can’t be merged into the parent company’s Page.
  • Showcase Pages can’t be merged as there are no associated members. To request a Showcase Page follower duplication, a super admin must contact our support team.

Additionally, if you see discrepancies in the number of followers on your retained Page, wait 24 hours to check your Page’s follower count as there might be a data latency.

To request a merge for your Pages, please contact us with the following information:

  • The company names exactly as they appear on the Company Page.
  • The URLs for the Pages you want to merge.
  • Clearly identify the Page or multiple Pages that need to be merged and the Page that needs to be retained.
  • The reason the Pages should be merged.

Important to know

If you find another LinkedIn Page representing your organization, you can request to have it removed as a duplicate or merged with your Page. Learn more about the actions you can take as a Page admin to manage your organization’s presence on LinkedIn.

My Company tab and Employee Advocacy tab is no longer available

At LinkedIn, we strive to create a simple and efficient experience for our members. To enhance our offerings, we periodically evaluate our features and may discontinue some to redirect resources toward better products.

As part of this process, the My Company tab, Employee Advocacy tab, and curator admin role will be gradually discontinued beginning in November 2024. If you held a curator admin role, you’ll automatically transition into the analyst role which has the same permissions as the curator role without the Employee Advocacy features.

As a LinkedIn member, you can continue to engage with your employer’s Page posts and reshared employee content.

As a Page admin, you can continue to engage with your employees on LinkedIn by sharing your organization’s content:

  • Reshare your employees’ best @mentions and posts from the Feed tab in your dashboard.
  • Notify employees of your most important posts to boost organic reach.

If you’d like to use an alternative solution to employee engagement, we recommend contacting your preferred external partner, such as a LinkedIn Marketing Partner, for potential solutions.

To retain your Employee Advocacy analytics data stored on LinkedIn, we recommend exporting your analytics. You’ll need to export your analytics before November 2024. You can also access the data from your Page, including the My Company tab, using the Pages Data Portability API.

Request admin access to a LinkedIn Page

Request LinkedIn Page admin access to a LinkedIn Page to manage the Page and be eligible to contact support about the Page. Requesting admin access grants all current super admins of that Page access to your public profile information.

Here’s a tip

To access a Page as an admin, no separate LinkedIn account login is needed. Instead, you’ll sign in to your own LinkedIn account where you have admin access and go to your Page admin view.

Before you begin

  • List your current position with the organization on your profile in the Experience section.
  • Verify your workplace using your current company email address using these steps.
  • Follow the Page that you are requesting admin access to.

To request admin access to a Page:

  1. Go to the Page you’d like admin access to.

  2. Click the More button and select Request admin access from the dropdown.

    [Image: Request admin access]

  3. Click the checkbox to verify that you’re authorized to become an admin of the Page.

  4. Click the Request access button.

    You may be prompted to confirm your company email address.

To request admin access to a Page:

  1. Go to the Page you’d like admin access to.

  2. Tap More, then tap Request admin access.

    [Image: request admin access]

  3. Tap the checkbox to verify that you’re authorized to become a Page admin.

  4. Tap the Request access button. This grants all current super admins access to your public profile information.

    You may be prompted to confirm your company email address.

After you request access

You’ll receive confirmation in your Notifications tab if you’ve been assigned Page admin access.

If the Page is actively managed, current super admins will review and must approve your request. However, if the Page is not actively managed—meaning there are no active admins or the previous admins are no longer with your organization—you may be granted access automatically.

If the current admins don’t respond to your request, you can contact us to request access. Before contacting support, please add the Page as your current employer on your profile, and verify your work email address if your company offers work email verification. In some cases, LinkedIn customer support may need to ask you for more information.

Important to know

If you don’t receive a notification about gaining admin access, it means the existing admins haven’t accepted your request. LinkedIn customer support can’t provide admin information to members or employees of the Page.

Additional permissions

Advertisers who want to create new ads or sponsor organic content can request Sponsored Content poster admin permission through Campaign Manager. It can also be assigned by an existing Page super admin.

Request Landing Pages admin and Lead Gen Form manager access by contacting your Page super admin.

Targeted audience pages on your Life or What We Do tab

LinkedIn Pages enhanced with Career Pages have a Life page that can be configured to display different versions to targeted audiences, based on information in the viewer’s LinkedIn profile such as language, geography, job function, company size, industry, and seniority level.

Targeted audience pages allow you to customize what viewers see based on what most likely applies to them. For example, if you want to create a Life page showcasing the company culture for your engineering department in Germany, you can target audiences that have the German language setting and engineering as their job function on their LinkedIn profile.

When a viewer matches the criteria for multiple targeted audience pages, they’ll see pages based on the following attributes of their profile in comparison to the page criteria, in order of priority: language, geography, job function, industry, title/seniority, and company size. The order in which targeted audience pages are displayed depends on how many criteria the viewer meets for a particular page.

Here’s a tip

Members can see a specific targeted audience page and can navigate to other versions by clicking Next at the top of the Life page. This can be enabled through the targeted audience settings.

Troubleshoot creating a LinkedIn Page

With LinkedIn Pages, you can help members learn more about your business or school, brand, products and services, and job opportunities.

Important to know

LinkedIn Pages should represent your business or school, not a LinkedIn member profile. For the safety and trust of our members, personal profiles that represent businesses or groups rather than authentic member names might be flagged as spam or abuse. Learn more about the differences between a LinkedIn profile and a LinkedIn Page.

If you see one of the error messages below when creating a Page, review the following tips to solve these common issues:

Page with the same name already exists

A Page representing your organization might already exist on LinkedIn. Check to see if the existing Page represents your organization. If your organization already has a Page, you can request admin access to it instead of creating a new Page.

If the existing Page represents a different organization, you can create a new Page for your organization, but you’ll need to select a LinkedIn URL that hasn’t already been taken.

Not enough LinkedIn connections

To create a Page, your LinkedIn account must have more than one connection with another member. Send invitations to connect with people you know on LinkedIn before you try creating a Page.

More than 25 Showcase Pages

Each LinkedIn Page can only have 25 or fewer associated Showcase Pages. To create an additional Showcase Page for your LinkedIn Page, you can deactivate inactive Showcase Pages.

Created too many Pages in one day

To help prevent spam, there are limits on the number of Pages you can create in a short period of time. If you see an error message, please wait for a few days before trying again.

New LinkedIn account

If you recently created your LinkedIn account, you’ll need to wait at least one day before creating a Page.

LinkedIn URL already in use

Each Page needs to have a unique public URL. If your desired URL is taken, you’ll need to select a different URL. For example, if linkedin.com/company/abc is already in use, you can try linkedin.com/company/abcinc.

Unverified workplace

You might need to verify the work experience listed on your profile before creating a Page. To continue with creating a Page, verify your workplace through work email verification or Microsoft Entra Verified ID.

Browser issues

If the above issues don’t apply, try clearing your browser’s cache and cookies or using a different browser.

Ways to protect your LinkedIn Page

At LinkedIn, we know that authenticity is key to creating meaningful interactions.

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free, helping you represent and build your organization’s brand on LinkedIn. Pages help members learn more about your business or school, brand, products and services, and job opportunities.

Important to know

Your use of LinkedIn Pages is subject to our Professional Community Policies and the LinkedIn Pages Terms. Violations of our policies or terms can result in action against your account or content.

Once you create a Page, we recommend you review the following ways to help protect your Page and brand on LinkedIn.

Two-factor authentication can greatly reduce unauthorized access to most accounts by identifying new or unknown computers or devices. To further protect your Page, each admin who has access to your Page can set up two-factor authentication to protect their own profiles and all Pages that they have admin access to.

You can set up two-factor authentication using an authenticator app, your phone number, and through a sign-in security prompt. If you believe someone has hacked your account, learn more about how to report a compromised account.

If you believe a member is sending your Page spam, inappropriate, or abusive messages, you can:

  • Restrict the member from your Page to stop them from sending more messages.
  • Mark the message as spam which will move to a spam folder.
  • Mute the conversation or report the message.

As an admin, you can disable messaging from all members, either temporarily or permanently, from your inbox settings. This will remove the Message button from your Page. Learn more about how to disable messages for your LinkedIn Page.

As an admin, we recommend you periodically review and update permission settings for admins of your Page.

As a super admin, you’ll have the most access to a Page, including the ability to view public profile information for other admins of the Page. You can assign specific types of admin roles based on the level of access that each person requires on the Page. For example, if an intern needs access to export monthly analytics, you may want to assign them Analyst permissions, rather than Super Admin permissions.

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can add email domains that you own (such as yourcompany.com) to your Page to control access to job posting.

When you add a domain, people can only post a job with your Page as the associated company if they verify that they have an email address with the domain you added (such as name@yourcompany.com). If no email domains are added, any member can post a job with your Page as the associated company.

Learn more on how to add your organization’s email domain to control job posting permissions.

As a member, you can add a verification badge to your profile by confirming specific information about your account, including your identity, workplace, and educational institution.

Who can use this feature?

  • Identity verification is currently available to select geographies.
  • Workplace verification is only available to members working at select companies as LinkedIn continues to expand support for this feature.

If you don’t see the option to verify your workplace with work email, it might be because your current company doesn’t have workplace verification enabled.

Learn more about verifications on your LinkedIn profile.

The verification badge on a LinkedIn Page helps signal that the Page is an official Page of the organization. Verification helps organizations build credibility with potential customers, and helps members find the actual organizations they intended to engage with.

Page verification isn’t currently available for all Pages. We’re gradually making Page verification available to more organizations.

Learn more about LinkedIn Page verification.

To ensure your organization’s Page remains actively managed, it’s a best practice to make consistent Page posts. Pages that haven’t had much activity may appear as if they’re not an official Page of an organization or that they’re not active on LinkedIn. Maintaining some activity on the Page will keep members interested in learning more about the company, and for employees to associate the Page with their organization.

If you find any Pages that represent your organization, which is already represented by an established LinkedIn Page, you can request to have it removed as a duplicate. To report duplicate Pages, you can contact our support team. If you find any Pages that do not belong on LinkedIn, you can report the Page.

Add a workplace policy to your LinkedIn Page

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can add a workplace policy to the About section of your Page. Workplace policies help job seekers understand your company’s guidelines for remote, hybrid, or on-site work, Covid-19 vaccinations, and location-based pay adjustments. You can also include information about the workplace benefits you offer.

To add a workplace policy to your Page:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.

  2. Click the Edit Page in the left menu.

  3. Click the Workplace tab.

  4. Turn on the Workplace module toggle.

  5. Select a policy from the Primary workplace policy dropdown menu.

    • If you select Hybrid, specify the amount of time employees typically spend on-site.

  6. Enter any additional details about your policy.

  7. Optional: Add a link to your company’s work policy.

  8. Click Add a benefit to add up to three benefits your company offers.

  9. Select an option from the Location-based pay adjustment dropdown menu.

  10. Select an option from the Vaccine policy dropdown menu. You can also add a link to your company’s vaccine policy.

  11. Click the Save button in the upper-right corner.

Commercial use limit

If you reach the commercial use limit for searching, your activity on LinkedIn indicates that you’re likely using LinkedIn for commercial use, like hiring or prospecting.

You’ll see a warning as you approach the limit. Your free monthly usage resets at midnight PST on the 1st of each calendar month. We are not able to display the exact number of searches or views you have left and we also cannot lift the limit upon request. Also note that the warning that you are approaching the limit may not display if you run through the full amount of searches or views too quickly.

Specific activities that contribute to the limit include:

  • Searching for LinkedIn profiles on LinkedIn.com and mobile
  • Browsing LinkedIn profiles using the People Also Viewed section located on the right pane of a profile
  • Viewing member profiles on the People tab of LinkedIn Pages

These activities do not count toward the limit:

  • Searching profiles by name using the search box located at the top of every page on LinkedIn.com
  • Browsing your 1st-degree connections from the Connections page
  • Searching for jobs on the Jobs page

You can always upgrade to any one of the below mentioned LinkedIn’s Premium account plans to increase the number of profile searches and views.

  • Premium Business
  • Recruiter Lite
  • Sales Navigator

Here’s a tip

Our Premium DACH Essentials plans still include the commercial use limit.

If you choose to cancel your Premium subscription, you will be given the basic limit of search and profile browsing. In addition, your limit will not be reset upon cancellation.

Designated Countries

We use the term “Designated Countries” to refer to countries in the European Union (EU), European Economic Area (EEA), and Switzerland. Members and Visitors located in the Designated Countries or the UK can review additional information in our European Regional Privacy Notice.

Learn more about the LinkedIn Professional Community Policies

We periodically update our Professional Community Policies to ensure that the millions of conversations taking place each day on our services help our members be more productive, successful, and free of inappropriate and unwanted content or behavior.

We encourage you to take a look and familiarize yourself with our Professional Community Policies, which we continue to develop and provide guidance for the use of our services.

LinkedIn Pages Data Portability API application review and developer support

LinkedIn provides an API program to enable Page owners, including Page admins and their authorized third-party developers, to access their LinkedIn Pages data programmatically. The API is available to third parties and Page admins, such that they can build applications that integrate with LinkedIn, and upon the Page admin’s consent, the application can programmatically access the Page’s data.

Below you’ll find information on the application review process for the Pages Data Portability API.

Pages Data Portability API Request Form review process

  1. Create a LinkedIn Page.
  2. Create a developer application in the Developer Portal.
  3. Apply to Pages Data Portability API below your app’s Products tab.
  4. Complete the access form.

After completing the Access Request Form, we’ll review and notify you of the status and outcome.

Check the status of your application

To check the status of your application:

  1. Sign in to the Developer portal using your LinkedIn account.
  2. Click My Apps and select the app you’re interested in.
  3. Once in the app, select the Products tab.
  4. The status of your application will be reflected under the Products tab. If denied, the reason for denial will be displayed.

Access Request Form denial

There are a variety of reasons your application to Pages Data Portability API may be rejected; including, but not limited to:

  • Your application was missing required information such as your name, company name, or website.

Re-apply for the Pages Data Portability API

If your application is missing information (Insufficient Details, Incomplete Access Request Form), you’ll see a re-apply button in the Products Tab and you can re-apply on your app.

For any other reasons, you can re-apply for the Pages Data Portability API. However, you’ll need to create a new app through our Developer Portal.

Application approved

You’ll receive an email notifying you of your acceptance to the Pages Data Portability API and additional information on how to get started. You’ll also receive details on how to seek technical support.

For email support, contact our developer support team.

Important to know

The Page owners exporting your data setting gives members control over whether to share some of their profile data and individual interactions with Pages via the Pages Data Portability API. When a member’s privacy setting is turned off, relevant fields will be removed from the API response.

LinkedIn refund policy

Refund Request

Submit a refund request if you believe you are eligible for a refund.

Request a Refund

Premium subscriptions

LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, such as Premium Career, Premium Business, Premium All-in-One, Premium Company Page, LinkedIn Learning, Recruiter Lite, and Sales Navigator may be refundable within 7 days from the date the subscription is charged without Premium usage. A previous refund may affect your eligibility. If you cancel your Premium subscription, all your Premium features, including InMail messages, will expire at the end of your billing cycle.

Note: If your subscription was purchased via the LinkedIn iOS app, please Contact Apple to inquire about cancellations and refunds. All iOS refunds must be issued by Apple. You’ll need to click the No Thanks, Continue button to connect with an Apple support rep via email or chat.

Pay-per-action products

Pay-per-action products charge per click, impression, applicant, etc. These products include, for example, LinkedIn Ads, Sponsored Jobs, and any other product where you’re charged per action. Any actions delivered and charged are non-refundable.

Keep in mind:

Under the laws applicable in your jurisdiction, you may qualify for a refund. For example, if you’re using our services for yourself (instead of on behalf of a business):

  • If you live in Denmark or the Netherlands, we’ll cancel your subscription with a one-month notice and refund any part of your subscription period remaining.

  • Citizens of the European Union are entitled to a full refund during the 14 days after the subscription begins.

    Note: This 14-day period begins when the subscription service starts. For example, if you signed up for a free trial, the period begins on the first day of your free trial, so there will be no fees paid as a refund.

  • If you live in Germany, we’ll cancel your subscription with a one-month notice and refund any part of your subscription period remaining (excluding the first year of an annual subscription).

  • If you live in India and your subscription includes a withholding tax, refund requests must be submitted to LinkedIn within 180 days from the start of your subscription.

  • If you made a purchase using Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) direct debit, you’re entitled to a refund from your bank under the terms and conditions of your agreement with your bank. A SEPA direct debit refund must be claimed within eight weeks starting from the date on which your account was debited.

LinkedIn’s Copyright Policy

Pursuant to the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (17 U.S.C. § 512), LinkedIn has implemented procedures for receiving written notification of claimed infringements.

If you believe in good faith that your copyright has been infringed, you may complete the Notice of Copyright Infringement form.

You can also find a link to our Copyright and Content Policies at the bottom of your homepage which details LinkedIn’s policies for handling these claims.

If you believe this claim was submitted in error, you can submit a Counter-Notice form.

Member portability APIs

LinkedIn provides an API program to enable members located in the EU/EEA and Switzerland to access their LinkedIn data programmatically. The API is available to third parties and members, such that they can build applications that integrate with LinkedIn, and upon member consent, the application can programmatically access the consenting-member’s LinkedIn data.  

At this time, only members located in the EU/EEA or Switzerland (as determined by the location provided by the member in their LinkedIn profile) can utilize this functionality. Members not located in the EU/EEA or Switzerland will receive error messages if they try to apply for access to this API or try to consent to a third party’s request for access to their LinkedIn data. 

All members (including those outside of the EU/EEA and Switzerland) are able to request access to their member data through their settings. Please refer to this article: Download your account data.

Premium and Subscriptions

Adding website link to profile available through Premium Business plan

At LinkedIn, we are constantly evaluating our features and thinking about how we can best add value for our members and customers.

We have removed the option to add a hyperlink to your profile, which was previously supported through Creator Mode and is no longer available today.

Looking forward, we will continue to support website links with the custom button feature through the Premium Business plan. With a custom button, users can link to a website of their choice which will appear on profile, posts, messages and search results - and is available to Premium Business subscribers, and Sales Navigator and Recruiter customers.

Auto-renewals for Premium subscriptions after free trial

When you sign up for a Premium subscription on LinkedIn’s desktop site, you’ll receive an email reminder sent to the primary email address on your LinkedIn account before your free trial ends and before your credit card is charged for the auto-renewal.

The card you used to sign up for a free trial for any LinkedIn Premium subscription will automatically be charged one month from the date you signed up.

You must cancel the trial at least one day prior to the auto-renewal billing date to avoid being charged after your free trial. You can see your Premium free trial auto-renewal date on your LinkedIn Admin Center page.

  • To avoid being automatically downgraded to a Basic (free) account, make sure to update outdated billing information within five days after your renewal date.
  • LinkedIn offers a free trial that allows members to explore Premium features at no cost. Trial eligibility and duration may vary based on regional availability or promotional terms. At the end of the trial period, unless canceled beforehand, the subscription will automatically convert to a paid plan and your card will be charged.
  • Billing, cancellation, or renewal dates for free trials and billing charges are based on the date and time that the subscription was activated, in local US time zones for US-based English-speaking members only. For all other countries or languages, this is in Universal Time Coordinated (UTC).

Note: If you purchased a subscription on your mobile device, you won’t receive an email reminder prior to the auto-renewal of your subscription. If you purchased using iOS, you’ll receive a notification on your device prior to auto-renewal.

  • Update your payment information

Bank authorization for premium services from LinkedIn

When you add your credit card for a free trial or any other Premium service, LinkedIn contacts the issuing bank to make sure the payment method is valid. Your bank may reserve the funds until the transaction processes or the authorization expires, this isn’t an actual charge and you will not have to pay it.

The authorization will be removed from your account according to the policies of your bank.

In some cases, the authorization status may appear as Failed or Cancelled because LinkedIn voids it after completing card verification. This does not mean the payment method is unusable. It can still be charged later for recurring payments.

To remove an authorization, please contact your bank for clarification on how long they will hold the authorizations.

Cancel LinkedIn Premium Company Page

LinkedIn Premium Company Page is a subscription to help you make your Page stand out and convert more LinkedIn members into clients for your business. If you cancel your subscription, your Page won’t have access to the features available to premium subscribers unless another Page admin subscribes.

Who can use this feature?

Only the admin who subscribed to Premium Company Page can cancel the subscription.

As a LinkedIn Page super admin, you can buy a Premium Company Page subscription and an individual Premium subscription together in a single purchase and get a 20% discount on the purchase. With this combined purchase, you get simpler access to enhanced company visibility and Premium tools to meet your business objectives. While you can purchase a Premium Company Page subscription and an individual Premium subscription as a bundle, you cannot cancel these subscriptions together. In LinkedIn Admin Center, you must cancel either one of these subscriptions separately.

To cancel your Premium Company Page subscription:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.
  2. Click Premium features in the left menu.
  3. Click the Subscription details dropdown menu near the upper-right corner of the page.
  4. Click the Manage subscription button.
  5. Click Cancel subscription.
  6. Follow the prompts to complete cancellation.

To cancel your Premium Company Page subscription:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.
  2. Tap Dashboard from the upper-left corner and select Premium features from the dropdown.
  3. Tap the Subscription details dropdown menu.
  4. Tap Manage subscription.
  5. Tap Cancel subscription.
  6. Follow the prompts to complete cancellation.

Important to know

If you’ve been removed as an admin from the Page with your Premium Company Page subscription, you can cancel your subscription from your LinkedIn Admin Center.

To cancel your Premium Company Page subscription from LinkedIn Admin Center:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Scroll down to the Subscriptions & payments section and click Manage Premium account.
  4. Click Cancel subscription.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel.

To cancel your Premium Company Page subscription from LinkedIn Admin Center:

  1. Tap your profile picture in the upper-left corner of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap Account preferences.
  4. Scroll down to the Subscriptions & payments section and tap Manage Premium account.
  5. Tap Cancel subscription.
  6. Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel.

Please contact us if you need help canceling a Premium Company Page subscription.

Cancel LinkedIn Premium subscription

Important to know

You can request to cancel a LinkedIn Premium subscription, promotion, or trial at any time.

  • If you cancel a paid Premium subscription, your plan will remain active until the end of your current billing cycle. You’ll continue to have access to Premium features until the plan expires.
  • If you cancel a Premium free trial, the trial will end immediately, and Premium access will stop right away.
  • To avoid getting charged for another billing cycle, you need to cancel your plan at least one day before your next scheduled billing date.

You can cancel your LinkedIn Premium subscription at any time. After cancellation, your account returns to a Basic (free) plan, and you’ll lose access to the Premium features such as InMail credits, profile insights, LinkedIn Learning, the Premium badge, advanced search filters, and competitive insights at the end of your current billing cycle. These features support faster outreach, continuous learning, and better visibility.

Before you begin

  • Cancel at least one day before your billing date to avoid being charged for the next cycle.
  • If you missed cancelling your Premium trial, review the LinkedIn refund policy.

Cancel Premium

    • You’ll be redirected to LinkedIn Admin Center.

  4. Click Purchases on the left pane.

  5. Select your Active subscription.

  6. Click ** Cancel subscription** under Actions.

  7. Click Confirm cancel to cancel your subscription.

Important to know

If you purchased Premium on iOS through the mobile web, LinkedIn processes your payment. Cancellation must be done on desktop and not on the iOS app.

To cancel your Premium subscription:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap Premium features.

  3. Tap Manage your subscription.

    • You’ll be redirected to Manage Premium account settings page.

Change the billing cycle for your Premium Company Page subscription

LinkedIn Premium Company Page is a subscription to help you make your Page stand out and convert more LinkedIn members into clients for your business. Premium Company Page gives you access to certain features that are only available to premium subscribers. You can choose one of the following billing cycle options for your subscription:

  • Annual
  • Monthly

Who can use this feature?

Only the admin who subscribed to Premium Company Page can change the billing cycle for the subscription.

Your subscription is renewed at the end of each billing cycle. All billing, cancellation, or renewal dates are shown in local US time zones for US-based English-speaking members only. For all other countries or languages, this is in UTC.

Keep in mind:

  • Your billing cycle will be updated at the end of the current billing period. The price you pay will be based on the new billing cycle, not the original one.
  • You can upgrade to annual from the switcher page, which will take effect immediately, however, this option isn’t available for subscriptions purchased through Google Play or iOS App Store.
  • If you’re a paying member on a monthly subscription and decide to upgrade to an annual plan in the middle of the month, the cost for the remaining days of your monthly cycle will be adjusted in your new annual billing, which begins right away.
  • If you’re on a free trial and choose to upgrade to an annual subscription, you’ll be charged immediately, and your annual plan will start right away, meaning you’ll forfeit any remaining days of the free trial.

To change your billing cycle:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.
  2. Click Premium features in the left menu.
  3. Click the Subscription details dropdown near the upper-right corner of the page.
  4. Click the Manage subscription button. You’ll be redirected to the LinkedIn Admin Center, where the subscription page appears by default.
  5. In the Billing information section, under Billing frequency, click Edit.
  6. In the Edit billing cycle pop-up, choose Monthly or Annual.
  7. Click Update to confirm your changes.

To change your billing cycle:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.
  2. Tap Dashboard from the upper-left corner and select Premium features from the dropdown.
  3. Tap the Subscription details dropdown menu.
  4. Tap Manage subscription. You’ll be redirected to the LinkedIn Admin Center, where the subscription page appears by default.
  5. In the Billing information section, under Billing frequency, tap Edit.
  6. In the Edit billing cycle pop-up, choose Monthly or Annual.
  7. Tap Update to confirm your changes.

Difference between free LinkedIn and LinkedIn Premium accounts

Important to know

Get ahead with LinkedIn Premium

LinkedIn Premium helps you get hired, grow your business, or learn new skills.

Eligible users can try Premium for free.

With a basic account, you can:

  • Find and reconnect with colleagues and classmates
  • Request and provide recommendations
  • Search for and view profiles of other LinkedIn members
  • Receive unlimited InMail Messages
  • Save up to three searches and get weekly alerts on those searches

We also offer various paid or Premium subscriptions which members can opt for based on their need.

The various Premium subscriptions we offer and their features are:

  • Premium Company Page helps make your Page stand out and effectively convert more visitors to paying customers.

These subscriptions can be directly purchased only by the account owner. Access to Premium services is available to Premium Business, Sales Navigator, and Recruiter Lite users. For business solutions available for your team, please visit: business.linkedin.com.

Differences between Recruiter Corporate, Recruiter Professional Services Plus (RPS+), Recruiter Professional Services, and Recruiter Lite

Discover the different LinkedIn Recruiter solutions available for various business needs, including Recruiter, Recruiter Professional Services (RPS), and Recruiter Lite.

To meet your hiring needs, LinkedIn Talent Solutions offers several LinkedIn Recruiter products from which you can choose to best suit your business demands.

LinkedIn Recruiter

LinkedIn Recruiter (Recruiter Corporate) is LinkedIn’s most powerful recruiting solution for teams and is best suited for mid-market to enterprise companies.

To learn more about the Recruiter Corporate solution, contact our Sales team.

Recruiter Corporate key features include:

  • Full LinkedIn network access (unlimited profiles)
  • 40+ advanced search filters
  • 150 InMail credits per month, per seat
  • Collaboration features (shared projects, tagging, centralized workflows, and more)
  • Additional filters and insights such as Open to contract work filter, Search insights, and more
  • ATS integration for 28+ partners
  • Advanced reporting
  • Advanced AI-assisted features
  • Hiring Assistant (AI-powered partner, add-on)

LinkedIn Recruiter Professional Services Plus (RPS+)

LinkedIn Recruiter Professional Services Plus (RPS plus) is a premium solution with advanced AI and Business Development tools specifically built for staffing agencies and large recruiting teams that are looking to boost efficiency and growth.

To learn more about the RPS+ solution, contact our Sales team.

RPS+ key features include:

  • Limited LinkedIn network access (Up to your 3rd-degree connections, with 50 unlocks per month for out-of-network profiles)
  • 40+ advanced search filters
  • 140 InMails credits per month, per seat
  • Collaboration features (shared projects, tagging, centralized workflows, and more)
  • Additional filters and insights such as Open to contract work filter, Search insights, and more
  • ATS integration for 28+ partners
  • Advanced reporting
  • Advanced AI-assisted features
  • Talent Insights
  • Business Development features (business development mode for AI-Assisted messaging, business development mode for search, and more)
  • Hiring Assistant (AI-powered partner) (add-on)

For more detail on how to use RPS+, visit our RPS+ Community page.

LinkedIn Recruiter Professional Services (RPS)

LinkedIn Recruiter Professional Services (RPS) is a solution best suited for staffing agencies and large recruiting teams managing multiple clients and job openings at scale.

To learn more about the Recruiter Professional Services solution, contact our Sales team.

RPS key features include:

  • Limited LinkedIn network access (Up to your 3rd-degree connections, with 30 unlocks per month for out-of-network profiles)
  • 40+ advanced search filters
  • 100 InMail credits per month, per seat
  • Collaboration features (shared projects, tagging, centralized workflows, and more)
  • Additional filters and insights such as Open to contract work filter, Search insights, and more
  • ATS integration for 28+ partners
  • Advanced reporting
  • Base level AI-assisted features
  • Talent Insights

LinkedIn Recruiter Lite

LinkedIn Recruiter Lite is the entry-level recruiting solution that is best suited for individuals, self-employed recruiters and small businesses with light hiring needs.

Recruiter Lite can be purchased online as a monthly or yearly subscription, and you can cancel at any time. If it’s your first time signing up, you may be eligible for a free trial. Recruiter Lite is not currently available to members in China.

Recruiter Lite key features include:

  • Limited LinkedIn network access (Up to your 3rd-degree connections)
  • 20+ advanced search filters
  • 30 InMail messages per month

Downgrade your Premium Subscription plan

You can downgrade your Premium subscription to a lower-tier plan on LinkedIn. Keep in mind that downgrading removes access to features included in your current plan.

Before you start

  • Where to downgrade: You can only downgrade through the LinkedIn desktop site.
  • Eligible plans: Downgrading is available for:
  • Premium Business
  • Sales Navigator Core
  • Sales Navigator Advanced (single active seat)
  • Not eligible: You cannot downgrade if you have a Premium Career subscription.
  • Billing impact: Your billing cycle resets immediately when you switch plans. You’ll pay the price for the new plan starting that day.

To downgrade your Premium subscription:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Premium features from the dropdown.

  3. You’ll be redirected to the Manage Premium account settings page.

  4. Click Subscription details on the left pane under Resources.

    • You’ll be redirected to LinkedIn Admin Center.

  5. Click Purchases on the left pane.

  6. Select your Active subscription.

  7. Click Switch plans Under Actions.

  8. Click Explore other plans on the upper left or select from the subscription plans displayed on the page.

  9. Select a plan (that is lower than the existing plan) from the Explore other plans pop-up window and click Apply.

  10. Click Downgrade plan on the Premium subscription you’d like to downgrade to.

  11. Follow the prompts to complete the downgrade.

Expected result

Your subscription will switch to the new plan immediately, and your billing cycle will restart based on the downgraded plan’s price.

Troubleshooting

  • Can’t find downgrade option? Ensure you’re on the LinkedIn desktop site and have an eligible plan.

  • Downgrade unavailable? You may have a Premium Career subscription, which cannot be downgraded.

  • Difference between free LinkedIn and Premium LinkedIn accounts
