Running a small business can feel overwhelming, especially when you’re balancing responsibilities like finding new clients, marketing your services, and hiring the right people. Premium All‑in‑One (formerly LinkedIn Premium Business Suite) is designed to simplify this work. It brings essential features together in one place so small business owners can save time, work more efficiently, and stay focused on growing their business.

Here’s a tip

If you’d like to learn more about LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, please join us and attend a free live webinar.

Key features

The Premium All-in-One subscription is a comprehensive product to help you find new business with easy-to-use sales, marketing, and hiring tools all in one place. With step-by-step guidance and intelligent AI capabilities, this subscription removes complexity and streamlines your tasks, so you can focus on what matters most: growing your business.

  • Category: Getting started; Feature: Premium dashboard: Simplify your day-to-day with sales, marketing, and hiring tools, plus recommended actions to grow your business all in one place.
  • Category: Sales; Feature: Daily prospect suggestions: Find new business with 15 daily suggestions for prospective clients based on your target criteria. Unlimited search with advanced filters: Quickly find prospective clients with search filters for job function, seniority, location, headcount, and years of experience. Prospect insights: Get exclusive insights like recent company changes, mutual connections, and more signals to help you connect with new clients. AI message drafts: Easily draft and send personalized messages to prospective clients. See Who’s Viewed Your Profile from the last 365 days: See if prospective clients are viewing you. Access trends and insights for the past 365 days. Note: These features are available on the My Premium page. The Premium All‑in‑One subscription does not include access to the Sales Navigator interface.
  • Category: Marketing; Feature: $50 monthly credit to boost your posts: Amplify your reach when you boost your post as an ad to your target client audience. Top Prospect Posts: Join the right conversations by seeing relevant trending posts among your target client audience. Auto-invite to follow: Grow your following faster by automatically inviting people who engage with your content to follow your profile. AI profile writing assistant: Get personalized suggestions using best practices for how to enhance your profile with AI. Company spotlight: Showcase your business to attract more prospective clients within the Featured content section of your profile.
  • Category: Hiring; Feature: Attract the right applicants US$100 hiring credit during free trial, followed by US$50 monthly hiring credit (or US600peryearwithanannualplan) * * * * : * * Find, screen, andshortlisttherightcandidateswithLinkedInHiringPro : yourbuilt‑inhiringpartner.Useyourhiringcreditstoattracttherightpeoplebypromotingyouropenroleswhenit’stimetohire. * *Note * * : CreditamountsareshowninUS for the US market. LinkedIn localizes pricing and credits by country, check your plan selection page to see your local currency. AI message drafts for hiring:** Easily draft and send personalized messages to qualified applicants based on profile insights, your company details, and your open roles.

Here’s a tip

The credit is shown in USD for the US market. LinkedIn localizes both Premium All-in-One pricing and promotional credits by country, so the amount you see is adjusted to your location.

Explore other Premium features

The Premium All-in-One subscription also includes additional features like services showcase, LinkedIn Learning and more to enhance your experience.

How it works

The Premium All-in-One  helps you create a customized plan to achieve your business objectives. During the signup process, the AI-powered tool reviews your profile, company page, and website to help you select your target client criteria, identify products/services your company sells and enhance your profile. You can also manually edit each of these as needed. This enables it to offer specific recommendations for finding new clients, marketing, and hiring.

Important to know

Premium Career, Business, or Sales Navigator Core subscribers can switch or upgrade to Premium All-in-One. You also cannot be the primary subscriber (or administrator) of a Sales Navigator Advanced or Recruiter Lite subscription. You can add a Premium Company Page subscription to your Premium All-in-One subscription.

Sign up: Navigate to the Premium subscription plan page on LinkedIn and select the Premium All-in-One plan.

Hiring credits with Premium All-in-One

Important to know

We are currently in the process of rolling out Premium All-in-One to all our members. During this time, you may not yet see it in your Premium subscription plans page. If this is the case for you, please check back in the coming months.

With the Premium All-in-One subscription, you can find, screen, and shortlist the right candidates with LinkedIn Hiring Pro: your built‑in hiring partner. Your hiring credits help increase the visibility of your job posts, making it easier to attract and hire the right people.

During the free trial, you are given US$100 worth of hiring credits across all the active job posts you promote. After the free trial ends, subscribers on a monthly plan will receive US$50 hiring credits each month at the beginning of their billing cycle. Subscribers on an annual plan will receive one upfront grant of US$600 for the year at the beginning of their billing cycle.

Note: The credit amount shown above is in US$ for the US market. LinkedIn localizes both Premium All-in-One pricing and promotional credits by country. To see the credit amounts for your local currency, refer to your plan selection page.

Important to know

  • Credits expire 12 months after being issued.
  • If you’ve already promoted a job, the credit balance might take up to 24 hours to reflect the promotion.

Hiring options with Premium All-in-One

When posting your job, you have three options to find the right candidates:

  1. Post your job for free: Post one job for free with access to basic Hiring Pro features for up to 21 days or 50 applicants.
  2. Promote with hiring credits: Promote your job using credits to unlock advanced Hiring Pro features to find, attract, and shortlist top talent.
  3. Promote with a custom budget: You can set a custom daily or total budget to further increase visibility beyond your included hiring credits.

Using hiring credits

Your hiring credits will be applied first when you find and hire candidates with Hiring Pro. If there is any remaining balance after the credit is used, it will be charged to your card. Hiring credit balance is shared across all promoted jobs. Any unused credit will expire if you cancel your Premium All-in-One subscription.

AI messagedrafts for hiring

With AI message drafts, you can send personalized outreach messages to potential hires and qualified applicants directly through LinkedIn messaging. Messages are automatically tailored to the candidate’s profile, your company, and the role you’re hiring for.

LinkedIn Customer Learning Centers and Marketing Academy

The LinkedIn Customer Learning Centers and Marketing Academy are sites that offer free online courses about LinkedIn Talent, Sales, and Advertising solutions to help you discover customer learning content.

To access these sites, you must create an account. Your account allows you to access your course progress, review your transcript, and receive platform communications (for example, live training reminders, certificates, and recommended courses).

When creating an account, keep in mind:

  • You must sign into LinkedIn to create an account. You can’t access these sites without a LinkedIn profile.
  • LinkedIn Customer Learning Centers and Marketing Academy are hosted by eLearning software Skilljar.
  • When you create an account, you’ll be asked to grant permission for Skilljar to use certain information. Skilljar may use this information to service the eLearning experience that LinkedIn creates, and as described in its privacy policy.
  • LinkedIn may use your LinkedIn profile, transcript information, and your Skilljar activity to inform enhancements to the platforms and contact you with information related to LinkedIn’s products and services.

LinkedIn may also share information about your use of the Customer Learning Centers with your employer. If you’d like to remove your account on these sites, please contact our support team.

More information about how LinkedIn uses data can be found in our Privacy Policy.

LinkedIn free Premium trial eligibility

Understand the eligibility criteria and conditions for LinkedIn’s free Premium trial.

To be eligible for LinkedIn’s free Premium trial, consider the following conditions:

  • If you are already using, or have already used, a free Premium trial, you may not be eligible for any further free Premium subscriptions.
  • You cannot switch between different Premium plans for free during the trial period.

Important to Know:

  • Trial eligibility and duration may vary based on regional availability or promotional terms. At the end of the trial period, unless canceled beforehand, the subscription will automatically convert to a paid plan.
  • Billing, cancellation, or renewal dates for free trials and billing charges are based on the date and time that the subscription was activated, in local US time zones for US-based English-speaking members only. For all other countries or languages, this is in Universal Time Coordinated (UTC).
  • If you switch to a different Premium Subscription plan during a free trial, you’ll lose the free trial benefits of the original plan. Your billing cycle will begin immediately on the day you switch plans, and the price you pay will be based on the new Premium Subscription plan, not the original one. You cannot switch back to the original Premium Subscription plan or any other plan and regain the free trial benefits.
  • If you cancel a free Premium trial, you won’t be eligible to sign up for another free trial for at least 12 months. You have free access to Premium features as long as you have an active free trial. If you choose to end your free trial early, you will immediately lose access to Premium features.

LinkedIn Premium Company Page is a subscription to help you make your Page stand out and convert more LinkedIn members into clients for your business. Premium Company Page gives you access to certain features that are only available to premium subscribers. All admins of the Page with a Premium Company Page subscription can use the premium features. For an overview of how to make the most use of your Premium Company Page subscription, use this guide to help get you started.

Who can use this feature?

We’re gradually making this product available, and you might not have access to it at this time. You must be a super admin of the Page to subscribe to Premium Company Page.

Premium Company Page features

  • Feature: Who’s visited my Page; Description: See eligible members who visited your Page each week to view their profile details or invite them to follow your Page.
  • Feature: Auto-invite engaged members and invite followers of similar Pages to follow your Page; Description: Without Premium Company Page, you can only invite 1st-degree connections to follow your Page. Save time with two exclusive invite-to-follow options that allow you invite followers of similar Pages and automatically invite people who have engaged with your content to follow your Page, regardless of their connection degree. You can see how many followers came from auto-invites in your follower analytics.
  • Feature: Custom call-to-action (CTA) button; Description: Drive your prospects to take a desired action by adding a custom CTA button like Visit website, Contact us, and more. The button appears at the top of your Page, next to your Page posts in the LinkedIn feed, and in search results.
  • Feature: Custom testimonial; Description: Build a credible presence and earn trust from prospects by showcasing a client testimonial. Add a quote from your client and an image at the top of your Page.
  • Feature: Credibility highlights; Description: Highlight unique strengths like awards, certifications, rankings, news features, or other notable highlights from the company to stand out across LinkedIn. Credibility highlights appear in the About section, search results, and top of the Page.
  • Feature: AI-powered post writing assistance; Description: Optimize your content with AI-powered post writing assistance to save time and engage more clients with your posts. Enhance your notes and ideas to create a first draft of posts.
  • Feature: Dynamic cover images; Description: Make a stronger first impression with your Page visitors by adding dynamic cover images to your Page. You can add a single dynamic cover image to appear as a Page’s background photo, or you can set your brand apart with a slideshow of up to five images to appear at the top of your Page.
  • Feature: Get more service requests; Description: Receive requests that match the services you offer (enabled by default).   Also, add a prominent Request services button on your Page, profile, posts, and messages to get additional projects that match the services you offer.
  • Feature: LinkedIn Premium logo; Description: A gold LinkedIn IN logo will appear at the top right of your Page header to show that you have a Premium Company Page subscription and to help your Page stand out.

To learn more about how you can grow your business with Premium Company Page, please register here for a free, recorded webinar.

Important to know

Premium Company Page is separate from other LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, such as LinkedIn Premium Business.

LinkedIn Premium Company Page and individual Premium subscription bundle FAQ

Premium Company Page bundle allows eligible LinkedIn Page super admins to purchase both a Premium Company Page subscription and an individual Premium subscription (Business, Career, Sales Navigator Core, or Premium All-in-One) in a single, streamlined transaction and get a 20% discount on the purchase.

Check out some of these frequently asked questions about Premium Company Page and individual Premium subscription bundle.

Purchasing a Premium Company Page bundle offers a 20% discount on the first purchase of a Premium Company Page subscription combined with an eligible individual Premium (Business, Career, Sales Navigator Core, or Premium All-in-One). This bundle simplifies subscription management, reduces overall cost, and highlights the added value of using business Page features alongside individual Premium tools.

Only the super admin of a LinkedIn Page can purchase a LinkedIn Premium Company Page and individual Premium subscription bundle.

Admins cannot buy multiple bundles, the offer applies only to the most recently accessed eligible Page without an active Premium Company Page subscription. If that Page isn’t eligible, they must switch to an eligible Page before purchasing.

Free trials depend on eligibility rules:

  • If eligible for both Premium Company Page and the individual subscription, free trials for both will be offered.
  • If eligible for only one subscription, both subscriptions will be billed when purchased in the bundle.
  • Once the bundle is purchased, free-trial eligibility is consumed for both subscriptions.

At the time of purchase, the bundle appears as one unified charge. However, during renewal, charges will be split by subscription—one for Premium Company Page and another for the individual Premium subscription.

Yes, refunds for individual cancellations are available within seven days of purchase or renewal. Members can request refunds throughsupport. For more details about eligibility and conditions, review the LinkedIn refund policy.

No, upgrading or switching personal Premium subscription is not available while it is part of a bundle.

Tax rates may differ for each product in the bundle, depending on regional tax laws. This is especially relevant for U.S. customers, where different tax jurisdictions apply.

Yes, both subscriptions must be either monthly or annual. Members can choose their preferred billing frequency during purchase.

LinkedIn Premium Duo subscription

Directly access the Premium subscription page

View details of the available Premium subscription plans.

Access the Premium subscription plan page

Premium Duo allows you to subscribe to LinkedIn Premium Career or Business and share the subscription with another person via email, whether they are within or outside your network. The secondary subscriber will have access to Premium features for the remainder of the billing cycle once added. Only the primary subscriber can manage additions and removals of the secondary subscriber. This role cannot be transferred to the secondary subscriber.

With Premium Duo, each account remains fully private and independent, even though both subscribers share the same subscription. The primary (paying) subscriber does not have access to any of the invited member’s personal information, activities, or account information beyond whether the Duo invitation has been accept.

Premium Duo is available for both monthly and annual billing cycles. The membership will continue as long as the primary subscriber renews their subscription. Only the primary subscriber has the ability to cancel a Premium Duo subscription. If the primary subscriber cancels, it will cancel Premium for both accounts.

Important:

  • At this time, you can only subscribe to Premium Duo via the LinkedIn desktop website. This feature is not currently available on the LinkedIn mobile app. Existing subscribers will not be able to use the “Switch plans” option in their Admin Center to change their existing subscription to Premium Duo
  • To be eligible as a primary or secondary member on a Duo subscription, you cannot have an active Career, Business, or Sales Navigator Core subscription. You also cannot be the primary subscriber (or administrator) of a Sales Navigator Advanced or Recruiter Lite subscription (Note: As this feature is still being rolled out, you may not yet have access to subscribe to Premium Duo even if you do not have an active subscription).
  • If you currently have an active subscription to one of the above and receive an invitation to join Premium Duo, you can cancel your current Premium subscription and allow it to end before accepting the invitation.

To subscribe to Premium Duo as a primary subscriber:

  1. Navigate to the Premium subscription plans page to view the details of the available subscriptions.

  2. Select Premium Career or Premium Business.

  3. Select the Duo subscription type and click Confirm to navigate to the order summary.

    • Note: You can try the subscription for free based on your eligibility.

  4. Choose your preferred billing cycle and click Place Order.

  5. After signing up, you will be prompted in the next screen to invite another LinkedIn member to your Duo plan by entering their email address.

    Note: To verify whether your secondary subscriber is eligible for a Duo subscription, check to see if they have an active Career, Business, or Sales Navigator Core subscription, or are the primary subscriber (or administrator) of a Sales Navigator Advanced or Recruiter Lite subscription.

  6. Your secondary subscriber will have access to Premium once they receive the invitation email and follow the instructions.

To join Premium Duo as a secondary subscriber:

  1. Click Accept invitation or Accept Premium Invitation from the Duo invite email.

    • If you’re not receiving emails from LinkedIn to your email account, be sure to check your email’s spam folder or junk folder. Email providers sometimes route emails from new sources to these folders. Additionally, you can also directly reach out to the Primary member to request an activation link that’s available in their Admin Center.

  2. Follow prompts to complete setting up your Premium Duo subscription.

Notes

For primary subscribers:

  • You will lose access to your free trial after subscribing to or being added onto a Premium Duo subscription.
  • As a primary subscriber, you will receive a single bill every billing cycle for the Premium Duo plan, even if you have not invited a secondary member or the secondary member hasn’t accepted the invitation to join the plan.
  • Primary subscribers will receive all InMail credits for the month immediately after subscribing to Premium Duo, with credits refreshing every 30 days at the start of their billing cycle.

For secondary subscribers:

  • If the invitation link isn’t working, try opening it in an incognito or private browser window.
  • If the invite link is expired, request a new invite link from the primary subscriber.
  • Secondary subscribers will receive all InMail credits for the month immediately after accepting the invitation. Credits will refresh every 30 days from the start of the primary subscriber’s billing cycle (not from when the secondary subscriber accepted the invitation).

LinkedIn Premium free trial

LinkedIn offers a free trial so you can explore Premium features at no cost. This trial helps you experience tools that can boost your networking, job search, and learning opportunities.

Before you start

  • Eligibility: Not all members qualify for a free trial. Eligibility depends on several factors, including whether you’ve used a Premium trial before.
  • Duration: Trial length may vary based on region or promotional terms.
  • Payment info: You must enter a valid credit card to start the trial.
  • Plan changes: You cannot switch between Premium plans for free during the trial period.

Key points

  • If you’ve already used a free Premium trial, you may not be eligible for another.
  • At the end of the trial, your subscription will automatically convert to a paid plan unless you cancel before the trial ends.

Expected result

You’ll have access to Premium features for the duration of your trial. If you don’t cancel before the trial ends, you’ll be charged for the next billing cycle.

Troubleshooting

  • Not eligible? You may have already used a free trial or not meet current eligibility criteria.
  • Payment declined? Check your card details or use a different payment method.

Benefits of Premium

  • Job seekers: See who viewed your profile, access InMail, and get insights on job postings.
  • Business growth: Reach more prospects and build stronger connections.
  • Skill development: Access LinkedIn Learning courses.

Note: If you cancel a free Premium trial, you won’t be eligible to sign up for another free trial for at least 12 months. You have free access to Premium features as long as you have an active free trial. If you choose to end your free trial early, you will immediately lose access to Premium features.

LinkedIn Premium subscription FAQ

Find answers to frequently asked questions about LinkedIn Premium subscriptions and accounts, including subscription plans, billing cycles, payment updates, and more.

The Premium subscriptions include:

  • Premium Career helps you get hired and get ahead in your professional life.
  • Premium Business helps you get detailed business insights and further expand your business.
  • Premium All-in-One helps you find new clients, showcase your small business, and hire when you need to.
  • Sales Navigator helps you generate leads and build your clientele.
  • Recruiter Lite helps you find and hire talent.
  • Premium Company Page helps make your Page stand out and convert visitors more efficiently.
  • LinkedIn Learning: Helps you improve your skills and learn new ones.

You can choose between a monthly or annual billing cycle for your Premium account.

Your membership will be renewed at the end of each billing cycle. Billing due date information is available on the Manage Premium account page.

If you’ve purchased Premium subscriptions, Job Postings, and InMail credits, you can add, edit, or delete payment information from the Manage Payment Methods section of the Premium Subscriptions Setting page.

You can access the My Premium page on the LinkedIn desktop site or mobile app to view all Premium features and manage your LinkedIn Premium subscription. On the My Premium page, you can view the status of your subscription, InMail Message credits, see Premium insights, and other Premium profile settings.

If you signed up directly through LinkedIn (desktop or mobile web), you can cancel your LinkedIn Premium subscription from the LinkedIn desktop website or through the LinkedIn mobile app on an Android device. Members can schedule cancellation for the next billing date or contact LinkedIn customer support for immediate cancellation.

Apple users: LinkedIn Premium subscriptions purchased via Apple Store can be cancelled using the LinkedIn mobile app on an Apple device.

Android users: LinkedIn Premium subscriptions purchased via Google Play Store can be cancelled using the LinkedIn desktop site, LinkedIn mobile app, Google Play desktop, or the Google Play mobile app.

LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, such as Premium Career, Premium Business, Premium All-in-One, LinkedIn Learning, Recruiter Lite, and Sales Navigator may be refundable within seven days from the date the subscription is charged without Premium usage. If you cancel your Premium subscription, all your Premium features, including InMail messages, will expire at the end of your billing cycle.

You can downgrade your Premium subscription from your existing plan and choose a plan that better suits your needs. This feature is available on the LinkedIn desktop website only. You can only downgrade your Premium subscription through the LinkedIn desktop site (online) if you’ve subscribed to Premium Business, Sales Navigator Core, or the Sales Navigator Advanced (with single active seat) subscription.

We will send an email reminder to the primary email address on your LinkedIn account prior to the end of your free trial for any subscriptions purchased via LinkedIn desktop site.

Manage your Open Profile settings as a Premium subscriber

Quickly adjust your Premium Open Profile settings

As a Premium subscriber, you can adjust who sends you messages on LinkedIn. To allow messages from members without using an InMail, simply adjust your profile’s Open Profile settings.

Allow messages

Open Profile feature allows other LinkedIn members to message you for free, without using InMail messages.

Important to know

Members with basic or free accounts can only send a limited number of open profile messages each month.

To change your Open Profile setting from your profile:

  1. Click the ** Me** icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click the ** Edit** icon in the introduction section.

  4. Click the Dropdown icon next to the gold Linkedin Premium profile badge on the upper left in the Edit intro pop-up window,

  5. From the dropdown switch the toggle right under Open Profile to allow anyone on LinkedIn to contact you directly for free, even if they aren’t connected with you.

    • Switch the toggle to the left to disable Open Profile.

  6. Click Save on the lower right.

To change your Open Profile setting from your profile:

  1. Tap your profile picture.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap the Edit icon in your introduction section.

  4. Tap the Dropdown icon next to the gold Linkedin Premium profile badge.

  5. Switch the toggle to the right under Open Profile to allow anyone on LinkedIn to contact you directly for free, even if they aren’t connected with you.

    • Switch the toggle to the left to disable Open Profile.

  6. Tap Save.

Note: You can still show your Premium membership without accepting Open Profile messages. The settings for each are controlled separately.

Opt in or out of Premium Insights on LinkedIn Pages

As a Premium subscriber, you’re able to opt in and out of featuring your profile information in the Premium Insights on LinkedIn Pages.

To opt in or out of having your profile information included in Premium Insights:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Under the Visibility of your profile & network section, click Change next to Representing your organization and interests.
  4. Switch the toggle on the right of Profile information on content to show or hide your information from appearing on your employer’s Pages.

To opt in or out of having your profile information included in Premium Insights:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap the Visibility tab.
  4. Tap Representing your organization and interests.
  5. Switch the toggle on the right ofProfile information on contentto show or hide your information from appearing on your employer’s Pages.

Premium Business and Premium Company Page features for LinkedIn Service Pages

With LinkedIn Service Pages, service providers can offer professional services to LinkedIn members. Certain Service Page features are only available to users with a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription.

Who can use this feature?

We’re gradually making Premium Business features for Service Pages available, and you might not have access to them at this time.

The following table provides details on the features that are only available with a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription.

  • Feature: Get matched with potential clients; Description: When clients send a request for services to a specific provider, they can choose to also send their request to similar providers. With Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription, you can choose to automatically receive these additional requests to help you get more potential clients.
  • Feature: Request services button; Description: Add a Request services custom button to your profile to help clients discover your services. This button also appears in your LinkedIn feed posts, messages, and search results.
  • Feature: Additional details about your services on your profile; Description: Your services appear in the Services section on your profile. With a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription, your Services section, known as a Services Showcase, is enhanced with a preview of your services description, your ratings, and your most recent four or five star review. You can also add images, videos, and URLs to highlight projects you’ve worked on to give visitors an idea of what you do. Without a Premium Business, Sales Navigator, or Recruiter Lite subscription, the Services section of your profile only shows a preview of your services description.

The following table provides details on the features that are available for Service Pages with a Premium Company Page subscription.

  • Feature: Get matched with potential clients; Description: When clients send a request for services, page admins are notified after which they can submit a proposal. Page admins can also report a request as spam.
  • Feature: Greater visibility for Services module on the Page; Description: The Services module on the Company Page is larger allowing it to stand out more effectively.
  • Feature: Additional details to your services offered on the Company Page; Description: The services you offer appear in the Services section of your Company Page. With a Premium Company page subscription, the Services section includes an overview of the services provided. You can add images and videos to the service offering.
  • Feature: Custom call-to-action button to request services; Description: Add a Request services custom button to your profile to help clients discover your services. This button also appears in your LinkedIn feed posts, messages, and search results.
  • Feature: Request services and opt to get more service requests; Description: Page admins can opt-in to receive additional service requests. From the Edit Services page, toggle the Receive additional projects option to On.

Premium free trial expiration notification

Learn how LinkedIn notifies you before your Premium free trial ends and what to do to avoid being charged.

Important to know

You can request to cancel a LinkedIn Premium subscription, promotion, or trial at any time.

  • If you cancel a paid Premium subscription, your plan will remain active until the end of your current billing cycle. You’ll continue to have access to Premium features until the plan expires.
  • If you cancel a Premium free trial, the trial will end immediately, and Premium access will stop right away.
  • To avoid getting charged for another billing cycle, you need to cancel your plan at least one day before your next scheduled billing date.

LinkedIn sends an email reminder before your Premium free trial ends if you purchased your subscription through the LinkedIn desktop site. This helps you decide whether to continue with Premium or cancel before billing begins.

How we notify you

We send an email reminder to the primary email address on your LinkedIn account before your free trial ends.

  • The subject line may include, but is not limited to, one of the following:
    • Important information about your LinkedIn Premium account
    • Important notice about your LinkedIn Premium Free Trial
    • Important notice regarding your Recruiter Lite account
    • Important notice regarding your Sales Navigator account
    • Enjoy uninterrupted access to your LinkedIn Premium benefits
    • Maximize your Premium benefits

Platform-specific notifications

  • Google Play Store (Android): You’ll receive a similar notification from Google.
  • Apple App Store (iOS): Apple does not send a reminder email for subscriptions purchased via iTunes or the App Store.

Important to know

  • If your email address is bounced or unconfirmed, you will not receive the reminder email.
  • If you believe you weren’t notified before being billed, search your inbox for the subject lines listed above. We send this email before your free trial ends and before your first charge, but not for subsequent billing cycles.

Notes

  • Didn’t get the email? Check your spam folder and confirm your email address in LinkedIn settings.

  • Charged unexpectedly? Verify if your trial was canceled before the billing date.

  • If you cancel a free Premium trial, you won’t be eligible to sign up for another free trial for at least 12 months. You have free access to Premium features as long as you have an active free trial. If you choose to end your free trial early, you will immediately lose access to Premium features.

Premium insights about job applicants, hiring companies, and company strategic priorities and competitive landscapes

LinkedIn Premium feature

Who can use this feature?

Premium subscribers can view insights about job applicants and hiring companies to help make informed career decisions.

This feature is available only to LinkedIn Premium subscribers. It provides competitive intelligence about applicants on job postings and an inside look at hiring companies. These insights can help job seekers understand their position among applicants and learn more about potential employers.

[Embedded video omitted]

Insights appear after a job posting has at least three applicants. For jobs you’re interested in, you can view:

  • Number of applicants for the job.
  • Your ranking compared to other applicants, shown as a percentage if you’re within the top 50%.
  • Top skills among applicants, including skills you share.
  • Experience and education levels of applicants.

Note: Applicant ranking is based on LinkedIn data and is not endorsed by the hiring company. If applications are accepted on an external site, data reflects people who clicked to apply, not completed applications.

Company insights are based on LinkedIn profile data and appear only if the company has enough employees with complete profiles. You can view:

  • Number of employees and hiring trends over the past 24 months.
  • Company growth rate over the past 24 months.
  • Average employee tenure and top job titles (if available).
  • Other companies and schools the hiring company hires from.
  • Hires who worked at the same company or attended the same school listed on your profile.

Additional Premium features

On the Jobs homepage, Premium subscribers can also see:

  • Jobs where you’re a top applicant, based on your profile’s role, experience, and skills.
  • Fastest-growing companies in your field, based on hiring trends for similar industries and job titles.

LinkedIn uses AI and trusted third-party sources to provide additional company insights, including:

  • Headcount and total job openings.

  • Strategic priorities and competitive landscape.

  • These insights are powered by Bing and sourced from reliable information across the web.

  • Difference between free LinkedIn and Premium LinkedIn accounts

  • Using the top applicant feature to apply for jobs

  • LinkedIn content and ad marketplace guidelines

Premium insights on LinkedIn Pages

LinkedIn Premium Feature

Premium Business, Sales Navigator, and some Recruiter subscribers have access to unique company insights to aid them in research and analysis. These insights are accessible via the Insights tab located near the top of each LinkedIn Page and typically include:

  • Total employee count: The total number of LinkedIn members employed at the company over time.
  • Employee distribution and headcount growth by function: The distribution and growth of company employees by function trending over time.
  • Notable company alumni: Former employees with past titles of Vice President or higher who have a past position with the company that ended within the last 24 months.
  • Total job openings: The company’s total job posts available on LinkedIn, segmented by seniority and function, trending over time.

For the job openings insight, all functions not listed in the table are included in the Other function. Because companies differ in function composition, peer growth for Other may include different functions across peers.

We collect, organize, and develop insights on companies based on profile information of LinkedIn members. At times, actual employee counts may differ from what we have computed. This can be due to a variety of reasons, including but not limited to, a company’s industry, the frequency with which the company updates its self-reported numbers on LinkedIn, as well as differences between what a company counts as an employee and how an employee represents themself on LinkedIn. Any Page with less than 30 employee profiles on LinkedIn will not have Premium Insights displayed.

Note: We cannot add members to any modules upon request. We also cannot remove any modules upon request.

  • Feature: Filter Data; Description: Filter viewer data by date range (up to 365 days for Premium Business and Premium Career), company, industry, and more.

Purchase a LinkedIn Premium Company Page and individual Premium subscription bundle

Premium Company Page bundle allows eligible LinkedIn Page super admins to purchase both a Premium Company Page subscription and an individual Premium subscription (Business, Career, Sales Navigator Core, or Premium All-in-One) in a single, streamlined transaction and get a 20% discount on the purchase. This bundle offer helps admins to enhance their company’s visibility while accessing Premium tools for business, career, or sales growth.

Important to know

Bundle purchases are currently supported on desktop only.

Prerequisite

  • You must be a super admin of your Company Page with less than 500 employees and no active Premium Company Page subscription.
  • You must not have an active individual Premium subscription, or manage a LinkedIn Page with an active Premium Company Page subscription

Notes

  • You cannot purchase multi-seat subscriptions, such as Sales Navigator Advanced as part of this bundle.
  • While you can purchase a Premium Company Page subscription and an individual Premium subscription as a bundle, you cannot cancel these subscriptions together. In LinkedIn Admin Center, you must cancel either one of these subscriptions separately.
  • Refunds for individual cancellations are available within seven days of purchase or renewal. Members can request refunds through LinkedIn customer support. For more details about eligibility and conditions, review the LinkedIn refund policy.
  • Analytics information for Premium Company Page subscriptions and your individual Premium subscriptions remain separate. You will continue to access this information separately.

To purchase a LinkedIn Premium Company Page and individual Premium subscription bundle:

  1. Navigate to the Premium subscription chooser page on LinkedIn and select the individual Premium subscription you want to bundle with your Premium Company Page subscription.
  2. Click Start my free month.
  3. In the Bundle Premium for you and your company pop-up, click Try bundle for [amount].
  4. On the payment page, select either monthly or annual billing cycle based on your preference.
  5. View the list of available payment methods in the Select your payment method dropdown.
  6. Select your preferred payment method, and click Start free trial. A confirmation page appears stating that your order was successful.

Understand InMail credits in Sales Navigator

As a Sales Navigator user, you’re allocated 50 InMail credits per month to send InMail messages. InMail messages are private messages that enable you to connect with any LinkedIn user without requiring an introduction or contact details, so you can engage with potential leads and facilitate conversations to enhance your sales efforts.

How InMail credits are allocated

You’ll receive a new allocation of InMail credits on the first day of each month (in UTC time). The grant date for InMail credits is separate from the date you received a Sales Navigator license or the date of your initial account sign-up, if you made the purchase online. If your InMail credits have not been renewed by the second day of the month, please contact support.

Important to know

At this time, you can’t purchase additional InMail credits. All Sales Navigator subscription types provide the same number of credits.

You can accumulate up to 150 total InMail credits; unused credits will transfer to the following month and must be used within 90 days.

  • Account types: Sales Navigator Core, Advanced, and Advanced Plus; Monthly allocation of InMail credits: 50; Maximum accumulation of InMail credits: 150

How InMail credits work

In addition to the monthly allocated credits, you will also receive an InMail credit for every InMail message that receives a response within 90 days of the date sent. InMail messages that don’t receive a response won’t get credited back.

If you send a second InMail to the same person before receiving a response, another InMail credit will be used. An automatic reminder is sent to the recipient within three days of the InMail being sent.

Keep in mind, if you cancel your subscription or change your subscription type, your InMail credits won’t be transferred.

How auto replies work towards InMail credits

Auto replies to InMail messages count as a response. “Interested” and “Maybe later” are considered accepted messages, while “Not interested” is recorded as declined. All three responses are eligible for a credit back, which you’ll receive immediately upon the recipient’s response.

Important to know

You can only edit or delete a message within 60 minutes of sending the message. If your sent message receives a response (including auto replies), your InMail credit will be refunded. However, if you delete an InMail that hasn’t received a response, no InMail credit will be credited back to you.

View your InMail credits

You can check your remaining InMail credits on the Sales Navigator Settings page.

Privacy and Data

Adjust your birthday privacy settings

You can control who sees your birthday information, as well as who receives notifications about your birthday on LinkedIn from the Contact info section of your introduction section on your profile.

To adjust your birthday privacy settings:

  1. Click the Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click Contact info in your introduction section.

  4. Click the Edit icon in the Contact Info pop-up window.

  5. In the Edit contact info pop-up window, fill out the Birthday date.

  6. Click the Visibility icon and select one of the following options:

    • Only you - Visible to you
    • Your connections - Visible to members directly connected to you
    • Your network - Visible to LinkedIn members connected up to three degrees away from you
    • All LinkedIn members - Visible to all members signed into LinkedIn

  7. Click Save.

To adjust your birthday privacy settings:

  1. Tap your profile picture.

  2. Tap View Profile.

  3. Tap the More icon (next to Add section) in your introduction section and select Contact info.

  4. (iOS)Tap Edit to the right of Contact.

  5. In the Edit contact info page, fill out the Birthday date.

  6. Tap Done/Set.

  7. Tap the Visibility icon and select one of the following:

    • Only you - Visible to you
    • Your connections - Visible to members directly connected to you
    • Your network - Visible to LinkedIn members connected up to three degrees away from you
    • All LinkedIn members - Visible to all members signed into LinkedIn

  8. Tap Save.

Note: We currently don’t offer privacy controls for your work anniversary.

Delete your data on LinkedIn

You’re able to delete all or some of your account data (e.g., if it’s no longer necessary to provide LinkedIn services to you). If you would like to delete all your account data, you will need to close your LinkedIn account. You can also hibernate your account as an alternative to closing it.

Select a link below to learn how to delete the following:

  • Data Type: Articles; Description of Deletion: Articles you’ve drafted and published.
  • Data Type: Close account; Description of Deletion: All of your LinkedIn data and close your account.
  • Data Type: Certifications; Description of Deletion: Remove certifications from your profile.
  • Data Type: Contributions; Description of Deletion: Remove Contributions you’ve made to collaborative articles.
  • Data Type: Conversation data; Description of Deletion: Conversation transcript from AI-powered profile setup.
  • Data Type: Email Address; Description of Deletion: Remove an Email Address from Your LinkedIn Account.
  • Data Type: Feed; Description of Deletion: Comments made in posts, articles, or replies to other comments.
  • Data Type: Groups; Description of Deletion: Comments you’ve posted in a group.
  • Data Type: Group Posts; Description of Deletion: Posts and comments posted in a group.
  • Data Type: Messages; Description of Deletion: Delete individual or group message threads and conversation history.
  • Data Type: Positions; Description of Deletion: Add, change, or remove positions from the Experience section of your profile.
  • Data Type: Profile activity; Description of Deletion: Posts of changes and activity you’ve made to your profile.
  • Data Type: Public Profile Visibility; Description of Deletion: Delete individual or group message threads and conversation history.
  • Data Type: Recommendations; Description of Deletion: Revise or delete a recommendation you’ve given to another member.
  • Data Type: Resume/CV; Description of Deletion: Delete your resume/CV saved for job applications.
  • Data Type: Resume data; Description of Deletion: Resume data on profile from job apply.
  • Data Type: Search history; Description of Deletion: Past searches from the search bar.
  • Data Type: Shared content; Description of Deletion: Content you’ve recently shared, such as updates or posts.

You can control the visibility of your profile and posts and easily view and modify your account information, privacy preferences, ads settings, and communication notifications from the Settings & Privacy page.

If you’d like to request assistance to delete your data or delete data that isn’t listed above, please complete the LinkedIn Data Deletion Form.

Download your account data

The easiest and fastest way to obtain a copy of your LinkedIn data is to initiate a data download from your Settings & Privacy page:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click the Data Privacy on the left rail.
  4. Under the How LinkedIn uses your data section, click Get a copy of your data.
  5. Select the data that you’re looking for and Request archive.

You can select specific categories of data or a larger download. If you select a specific type of data, we’ll email you within minutes. If you select the larger download, you’ll receive an email within 24 hours. Use the link provided in the email to download the information you requested. The data will be available for download for 72 hours.

Additionally, LinkedIn provides an API program to enable EU/EEA/Switzerland members to access their LinkedIn data programmatically. You can find more details in the Member Portability APIs help center article.

Important:

  • You should only download your data from a personal computer and not a public computer.
  • This feature is currently not available on mobile.
  • You’ll only receive the categories of data that are applicable to your account and activities on LinkedIn. For example, if you don’t have certifications listed on your profile, you won’t receive a Certifications file.
  • LinkedIn will only provide your own personal data and not that of other members. LinkedIn does not provide People You May Know or Who’s Viewed Your Profile data.
  • If you close your account, you’ll no longer have access to your LinkedIn account data. For more information, you can check out what happens after you close your account.
  • You may notice in your connection data that some of your connections’ email addresses are missing. That’s because members choose in their privacy settings whether to allow others to download their email address.

Below is a list of data categories, and their description, that you can request and when to expect receipt:

  • Data Category: Ad Targeting; Description of Data Category: Contains information we use to figure out what ads to show you. Some of the targeting data may be derived from other information you’ve given us. For example, we might use your title as a clue to your seniority level.

  • Data Category: Articles; Description of Data Category: Contains URLs of a member’s published articles.

  • Data Category: Causes You Care About; Description of Data Category: Contains a list of available causes a member has selected to include on their profile.

  • Data Category: Certifications; Description of Data Category: Contains licenses or certifications a member has obtained, including the issuing authority name or company, start date, finish date, and license number.

  • Data Category: Company Follows; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to companies followed. This includes the company name and date followed. A list of the entities (e.g., companies) you follow on LinkedIn.

  • Data Category: Courses; Description of Data Category: Contains information about courses the member has taken and how they are associated with their experience or education.

  • Data Category: EasyApply Blocking; Description of Data Category: Contains user account records for job applications on third-party application tracking systems.

  • Data Category: Education; Description of Data Category: Contains the school’s name, start and end date, degree title, activities, and other notes the member chose to include relating to their education.

  • Data Category: Endorsements; Description of Data Category: Contains details of given and received endorsements.

  • Data Category: Events; Description of Data Category: The names of all the events (including the ones you’ve attended, been invited to but declined, or have requested to attend), the date and time, your status as an attendee, and any external URL for the event shared by the event organizer.

  • Data Category: Honors; Description of Data Category: Contains the title of honors and awards the member has received, including details such as the description, who issued it, the date, and attached media files.

  • Data Category: Invitations; Description of Data Category: Contains the invitations sent and received. This includes the invitee and inviter’s first and last name, URL, date sent, and message.

  • Data Category: Job Application Saved Answers; Description of Data Category: Contains the member’s answer to basic job application questions. This includes first and last name, mobile number, location, address, and more.

  • Data Category: Job Applicant Saved Screening Question Responses; Description of Data Category: Contains the member’s answers to job application questions provided by the job poster.

  • Data Category: Job Applications; Description of Data Category: Contains jobs the member has applied for, application date, company name, job title, and LinkedIn’s job posting URL.

  • Data Category: Job Seeker Preferences; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to a member’s chosen job preferences. Some categories include location, industries, company size, dream company, job titles, and activity level.

  • Data Category: Languages; Description of Data Category: Contains languages understood or spoken and the member’s level of proficiency.

  • Data Category: Learning; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to LinkedIn Learning courses, including the course name, description, date last watched, and completion date.

  • Data Category: Marketplace Engagements; Description of Data Category: Contains the event name, date and time, status, and external URL if the event organizer shared one. Under status, a member can choose to approve, decline, or ignore an event.

  • Data Category: Marketplace Opportunities; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to services a member is looking for on Services Marketplace. Information includes the creation date and the member’s answers to a provider’s potential services.

  • Data Category: Marketplace Providers; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to services a member provides on Services Marketplace.

  • Data Category: Online Job Postings; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to jobs the member has posted on LinkedIn. This includes the posted date, expiration date, company name, job title, and employment status.

  • Data Category: Organizations; Description of Data Category: Organizations the member has listed on the profile. Contains the organization’s name, description, and the member’s position.

  • Data Category: Patents; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to patents the member lists on the profile. Patents include the title, number, status (issued or pending), URL, and description.

  • Data Category: Phone Numbers; Description of Data Category: Contains phone numbers the member has added to their account.

  • Data Category: Positions; Description of Data Category: Contains job positions the member has included in the Experience section on their profile. This includes the company name, title, job description, location, and employment dates.

  • Data Category: Profile; Description of Data Category: Contains basic biographical information the member has added to their profile. This includes first and last name, address, date of birth, and zip code.

  • Data Category: Projects; Description of Data Category: Contains the names of projects listed on a member’s profile, description, contributors, date started and finished, and attached media URLs.

  • Data Category: Publications; Description of Data Category: Contains the publication title, description, publishing company, date, contributors, and publication URL of publications listed on the member profile.

  • Data Category: Receipts; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to the member’s purchases of LinkedIn services (e.g., job postings). Receipts include the payment date, method, amount, and description of the purchase.

  • Data Category: Recommendations Given; Description of Data Category: Contains the recommendations a member has given to 1st degree connections.  This includes the first and last name, associated company, description, and published date.

  • Data Category: Recommendations Received; Description of Data Category: Contains the recommendations a member has received by 1st degree connections. This includes the first and last name, associated company, description, and published date.

  • Data Category: Registration; Description of Data Category: Contains the member’s registered date, IP address, and current subscription type.

  • Data Category: Rich Media; Description of Data Category: Includes URL links to any photos, videos, or documents shared on LinkedIn.

  • Data Category: Saved Jobs; Description of Data Category: Contains information related to a job a member has saved. This includes the date saved, job title, company name, and the LinkedIn job posting URL.

  • Data Category: Saved Job Alerts; Description of Data Category: Contains the word or phrase and the date of a saved search within the “Job” search function.

  • Data Category: Skills; Description of Data Category: Contains the skills a member has added to their profile.

  • Data Category: Verifications; Description of Data Category: Contains confirmed verification information related to identity, workplace, and educational institutions. This may include a workplace email or valid government-issued ID. LinkedIn partners with CLEAR, a third-party verification partner.

  • Data Type: Account Status History; Description of Data Type: Contains the date and time the member’s account status changed within the last year.

  • Data Type: Ads Clicked; Description of Data Type: Contains the date and LinkedIn’s advertising identifier a member has clicked on.

  • Data Type: Ads LAN; Description of Data Type: Contains LAN ads engagement information. This includes the date, LinkedIn’s advertising identifier, corresponding web page or mobile application, and the action type.

  • Data Type: AI-powered conversations; Description of Data Type: Contains information relating to your conversations with some of LinkedIn’s AI-powered chat and voice experiences, including AI-powered onboarding conversations, insights on jobs, and writing assistant.

  • Data Type: Calendar; Description of Data Type: Contains the calendar source, owner, and last sync date of the member’s calendar.

  • Data Type: Comments; Description of Data Type: Contains comments a member has made to posts, articles, shares, and collaborative articles. This includes the date and URL.

  • Data Type: Connections; Description of Data Type: Contains the first and last name, public profile URL, email address, company, position, and connection date for all 1st degree connections. An email address for the connection will be included only when authorized by the connection in their privacy settings.

  • Data Type: Contacts; Description of Data Type: Contacts imported on LinkedIn, including name, phone numbers, and email addresses.

  • Data Type: Email Addresses; Description of Data Type: History of email addresses associated with the member’s account, past or present.

  • Data Type: Groups; Description of Data Type: LinkedIn groups that the member is a part of.

  • Data Type: Inferences; Description of Data Type: Inferences LinkedIn has made based on data the member provided, content created, activity, and other factors.

  • Data Type: Instant Reposts; Description of Data Type: Contains the reposts date, time, and link.

  • Data Type: Learning Coach AI Takeout; Description of Data Type: Stores past conversations with LinkedIn Learning’s chatbot, Learning Coach.

  • Data Type: Learning Coach Inbox; Description of Data Type: Stores past conversations with LinkedIn Learning’s chatbot, Learning Coach.

  • Data Type: Learning Coach Roleplay Inbox; Description of Data Type: Provides insights and feedback from interactive learning and real-world practice scenarios.

  • Data Type: Logins; Description of Data Type: Contains IP login details, including the date and time, IP address, user agent string, and login type.

  • Data Type: Member Follows; Description of Data Type: Contains information related to who a member follows. This includes the followed member’s first and last name and following or unfollowing date.

  • Data Type: Messages; Description of Data Type: Contains information related to messages sent, received, and archived. Messages include the date it was sent or received, subject line, content, and the member’s public profile URL.

  • Data Type: Other; Description of Data Type: If you would like access to data that’s not included in the data files described above, you may complete LinkedIn’s Data Access Request Form. Completed forms will automatically be sent to us for review, but note that it may take several days to receive a response.

  • Data Type: Profile Summary; Description of Data Type: AI generated summaries of your profile that may be shared with other members when you are recommended as a connection for them.

  • Data Type: Reactions; Description of Data Type: Contains the reaction type a member has made to a post. The reaction type includes like, celebrate, support, love, insightful, or funny, the date, and URL of the post reacted to.

  • Data Type: Resume data; Description of Data Type: Resume data from job applications.

  • Data Type: Reviews; Description of Data Type: Contains information related to ratings and reviews a member has provided, and received, for services within the Services Marketplace and LinkedIn Learning.

  • Data Type: Saved Items; Description of Data Type: Contains the saved date and URL of a post, article, or other content.

  • Data Type: Search Queries; Description of Data Type: Contains the word or phrase and date of a search using LinkedIn’s search bar.

  • Data Type: Security Challenges; Description of Data Type: Contains challenge event information when a member signs in from an unfamiliar device or has enabled two-factor authentication. This includes the date, IP address, user agent string, country, and challenge type.

  • Data Type: Shares; Description of Data Type: Contains all shared or re-shared posts. This includes the date, URL, shared comments, and visibility status.

  • Data Type: Test Scores; Description of Data Type: Contains test scores related to workplace and educational institutions a member added to the profile. This includes the test score, test date, and a description.

  • Data Type: Volunteering; Description of Data Type: Contains volunteering experience. This includes an organization’s name, role, cause, start and end date, and description.

  • Data Type: Votes; Description of Data Type: Contains information related to polls members have created and voted on. Information includes the member’s voting date, URL of the poll voted on, and voting selection.

Additional Information:

  • For information about how we collect and use your personal data and about how long we retain it, please see our Privacy Policy. Our Privacy Policy also details how and with whom we share your personal data when providing our Services. Information about your rights with respect to your personal data and how you can exercise them is also contained in our Privacy Policy. Further, it outlines how LinkedIn transfers your data when providing our Services and the mechanisms we rely on to lawfully transfer your personal data across borders.
  • In addition to downloading your data, under the California Consumer Privacy Act, you also can request that we disclose how we’ve collected, used, and shared your personal information since January 1, 2022.
  • To see information about your Microsoft personal account, please visit the Microsoft Privacy Dashboard.

Edit or Rectify Your Data on LinkedIn

You can edit some of your personal data through your LinkedIn account. Upon your request, we can change, update or fix your data in certain cases; particularly if it’s inaccurate.

  • Edit Type: Add or Change Email Address; Description: Add or change your email address for your LinkedIn account.
  • Edit Type: Background Photo; Description: Add or change your background photo on your profile.
  • Edit Type: Certifications; Description: Add, edit, or remove certifications on your account.
  • Edit Type: Custom URL; Description: Edit your public profile URL.
  • Edit Type: Headline; Description: Edit your profile headline.
  • Edit Type: Name Change; Description: Change how your name appears on your profile.
  • Edit Type: Positions; Description: Update your previous and current positions.
  • Edit Type: Posts; Description: Edit any posts you share with your connections.
  • Edit Type: Profile; Description: You’re able to edit what appears on your profile and who can see it.
  • Edit Type: Profile Photo; Description: Upload, edit, or remove your profile photo.

You can control the visibility of your profile and posts and easily view and modify your account information, privacy preferences, ads settings, and communication notifications from the Settings & Privacy page.

For additional information on how to navigate and edit sections of your profile, please utilize our Help Center search options.

If you’d like to edit data not listed above, please complete a Data Rectification form.

Find your LinkedIn public profile URL

If your LinkedIn profile is set to public, it’ll have a link (URL) you can use to share your profile with others.

To find your public profile URL:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Your public profile URL is displayed under Public profile & URL on the right pane.

    • It’ll be an address that starts with www.linkedin.com/in.

  4. Copy and paste this link to share it with others.

Here’s a tip

You can also click on Resources and select Send profile in a message to share your profile URL via LinkedIn messages.

To find your public profile URL:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap on the More icon next to Add section button.

  4. Tap Contact info.

  5. Under the Your Profile section, locate your public profile URL.

    • It’ll be an address that starts with www.linkedin.com/in.

  6. Copy and paste this link to share it with others.

Here’s a tip

You can also tap on the More icon next to Add section button and select Send profile in a message to share your profile URL via LinkedIn messages.

To find your public profile URL:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Scroll down to the Contact section.

  3. Under LinkedIn, locate your public profile URL.

    • It’ll be an address that starts with **In.** (linkedin.com)

  4. Copy and paste this link to share it with others.

Notes:

  • This URL won’t appear if you don’t have a public profile.
  • Members who live in certain countries have a public profile URL that begins with a 2-letter code based on the country listed on their profile. For example, if you live in Canada, your public profile URL could be **Linkedinyourname** (ca.linkedin.com).
  • If you change the country listed on your profile, your public profile URL automatically changes. The old URLs will still work.

LinkedIn Page visit visibility

Admins of LinkedIn Pages can review a list of recent visitors to their Page, subject to those visitors’ privacy settings.

As a member, you can control whether organizations can see that you’ve visited their Page by updating your Page visit visibility settings. When the toggle is turned on, organizations can see that you’ve visited their Page. You may also appear in Sales Navigator (LinkedIn’s platform for sellers) search results for LinkedIn members who have viewed the LinkedIn Page associated with that Sales Navigator account. You can turn the setting on or off at any time.

Keep in mind that admins of a Page with a Premium Company Page subscription might only see a limited number of Page visitors. When you visit a Premium Company Page and if your Page visit visibility setting is turned on, here’s what admins can see:

  • Job title
  • Industry
  • Full name
  • Photo
  • Location
  • Company

Page admins who don’t subscribe to a Premium Company Page might see the job title and company of some Page visitors.

You can change your Page visit visibilitysetting at any time, but if you previously visited a Page while this setting was turned on, those visits might still appear to Page admins for up to 365 days.

Important to know

LinkedIn Page visit visibility settings are separate from Who’s viewed your profile visibility settings.

LinkedIn public profile visibility

Manage your public profile information

Control what sections of your profile are eligible for display to people who are not signed in to LinkedIn, or can be viewed on search tools such as Google or Bing.

Edit public profile sections

Important to know

After you make changes to your public profile, it can take several weeks or months at times for search tools like Google, Yahoo, or Bing to detect changes and refresh. LinkedIn doesn’t control that refresh process. If you’re incorrectly appearing in search results on those sites, you can contact them directly to resolve incorrect search results.

Your public profile is a simplified version of your LinkedIn profile. Not all sections of your profile can be displayed publicly. On the Public profile settings page, you’ll be able to see and adjust the sections of your profile that are eligible to be displayed publicly. Keep in mind that in some contexts we may show a more limited profile preview that includes some but not all of the profile fields you’ve allowed.

If you’d like to edit a specific section of your public profile, first edit your profile and then enable that section’s public visibility. Simply turn on or off the profile sections according to whether you want allow visibility on public search tools.

Your public profile may be visible to people who aren’t members, viewers who aren’t signed in to LinkedIn, or those who haven’t linked their LinkedIn account to their account on other approved services, subject to your off-LinkedIn visibility settings. You can access off-LinkedIn visibility preferences, on the Off LinkedIn Visibility settings page.

Your public profile appears:

  • When people search for you using search tools like Google, Yahoo!, Bing, DuckDuckGo, etc.
  • On public profile badges.
  • On affiliate and approved other services like Outlook.

Notes:

  • The default photo setting is Public.
    • If you edit the settings of your profile photo from your profile page, then your public profile page will be updated with the new setting. For example, if you change your profile photo visibility setting from Public to 1st-degree connections only, that change will only appear for your 1st-degree connections.
    • You can update your photo visibility settings while you’re editing your public profile page (or by disabling your public profile).
  • In order to see your full profile, visitors may need to log in to their LinkedIn accounts.
  • The Articles & Activity setting toggle will not be present if you haven’t made any post.
  • Disabling your public profile hides your public profile from non-LinkedIn members or search tools results. It could also prevent you from recovering your account if you lose access to your primary email address as we may require your public profile URL.
  • LinkedIn does not share your personal data with any other external platform without your consent. LinkedIn values your privacy and maintains strict policies to protect your information.

Manage who can see Members you Follow

When a member becomes one of your 1st degree connections, you automatically follow them and their activity. You can always unfollow them, and they won’t be notified you’ve unfollowed them.

You can also Follow a member on LinkedIn without being connected to them. Following a member on LinkedIn allows you to see the person’s posts and articles on your homepage without being connected to them. Members are able to see if you follow them and will receive a notification whenever a non-connection follows them. However, you control how others can see your follow activity via your Settings page.

To change who can see members you follow:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click Visibility on the left side and select Visibility of your profile & network.
  4. Click Change next to Who can see members you follow.
  5. Select Only visible to me or Anyone on LinkedIn to choose who can see members you follow.

To change who can see members you follow:

  1. Tap your profile picture, then tap Settings.
  2. Tap Visibility, then tap Who can see members you follow.
  3. Select Only visible to me or Anyone on LinkedIn to choose who can see members you follow.

Notes:

  • If you follow a member, that member can always see that you follow them.
  • This setting only applies to members you follow and not Groups or LinkedIn Pages.
  • Unless you make your connections only visible to you, your 1st degree connections can see who you’re connected to on LinkedIn. Also, all members who have connections in common with you can see those shared connections. Learn more about controlling who can see your connections.

Manage your account and privacy settings

Change your account and privacy settings

The Settings page allows you to manage your account settings, update your privacy and security settings, and set your preferences for how frequently you’re contacted by and through LinkedIn.

View and change your settings

The Settings page allows you to manage your account settings, update your privacy and security settings, and set your preferences for how frequently you’re contacted by and through LinkedIn. At the top of the page, you’ll also see an overview of your account details, including your profile headline, number of connections, and what Premium subscriptions you currently have, if any.

The Settings page is organized into six sections to help you easily view and modify your account information, data privacy, ads settings, and communication notifications.

  • Account preferences: Manage your basic profile information for your LinkedIn experience, networking, subscriptions, and more.
  • Sign in & security: Manage the settings that keep your account secure.
  • Visibility: Control who can see your profile, network, and LinkedIn activity.
  • Data Privacy: Configure privacy settings related to how LinkedIn uses your data, who can reach you, your messaging experience, job seeking preferences, and other applications.
  • Advertising data: Control the information that LinkedIn uses to show you relevant ads by adjusting your account’s ads settings.
  • Notifications: Enable or disable the types of notifications you want to receive and how often you wish to receive them.

To access this page:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.

Note: You can also type **** (linkedin.com) into your browser’s address bar.

To access this page:

  1. Click Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Tap ** Settings** at the bottom of the left pane.
  3. Tap the required category to manage your privacy settings.

To access this page:

  1. Tap the Profile icon in the navigation bar.
  2. Tap the Settings icon in the upper right corner.

Note: You can also type Psettings (linkedin.com) into your browser’s address bar.

Check out the following information to learn more about key settings you can manage through the Settings & Privacy page:
