Manage your Personal Data

We want to make it easy for you to understand your choices, as well as the control you have over your data and content, on LinkedIn.

You have various options about how your data is collected, used, and shared. We offer you the ability to control some of your personal data through your LinkedIn account.

You can erase or delete all or some of your personal data.

  • If you would like to delete all of your data from LinkedIn, you can do so by closing your account. We generally delete data within 30 days of account closure, except as noted in Section 4.3 of our Privacy Policy.
  • You can also delete certain types of data such as editing your profile, comments made in posts, or past searches. Learn more about the personal data that you have the ability to delete through your LinkedIn account.

You can download a copy of your personal data.

  • You can initiate a download of your LinkedIn data from your Settings & Privacy page.
  • You can learn more about the data provided in that download.

You can change, update, or correct your personal data in certain cases.

  • You can edit some of your data,such as certifications, positions, and posts. View a list of what you have the ability to change through your LinkedIn account.
  • You can control the visibility of your profile and posts and easily view and modify your account information, privacy preferences, ads settings, and communication notifications from the Settings & Privacy page.
  • If you’d like further assistance with editing your profile, please contact our support team.

You can ask us to stop using all or some of your personal data.

  • You can control and manage how we use your personal data by adjusting your privacy settings or your ads settings.
  • You can control and manage how you are notified through email and notifications.
  • You can object to our use of your data for direct marketing by clicking the unsubscribe link in such marketing communications. Learn more about managing the types and frequencies of emails you receive.
  • You can manage apps and services of others you have allowed to access some of your data and you can choose to stop access at any time.
  • For any other objections to or requests for the restriction of use of personal data, please submit LinkedIn’s Data Processing Objection/Restriction form.

Manage your profile’s visibility on and off LinkedIn

LinkedIn enables members to find their contacts and discover new people to connect with in many different ways. Your profile may appear in LinkedIn search results and on search tools or other services off LinkedIn.

Members can search for your profile from the LinkedIn search bar the top of every page. They can search by first name, last name, company, or other search fields to find the people they know and discover new people to connect with.

We don’t allow members to search for an email address directly on LinkedIn to discover a member’s profile.

Some sections of your profile may appear off LinkedIn when people search for you using search tools, like Google or Bing. Additionally, some sections of your profile may appear in approved services—for example, to display information from member profiles to users with whom they exchange emails. Learn more about how to control your profile visibility off LinkedIn below:

  • Search tools- You can opt out of appearing on search tools or you can determine what sections of your profile are eligible to appear through your public profile. Users of search tools can enter search terms such as your name and company to discover you.
  • Other services off LinkedIn - We enable certain affiliates, partners, customers, and other permitted developers to display member profile information. This helps users learn more about people they’re interacting with by showing elements of members’ profiles. You can control if other users are able to look up your profile from your email address or phone number using your discover by email setting and your discover by phone setting. To control if your profile is visible at all off LinkedIn, you can edit your Profile discovery and visibility setting.

Note: Changing the Profile discovery and visibility setting doesn’t limit visibility of your public profile (for example, on search tools), which can be controlled by the public profile setting. It also doesn’t limit the ability for Page owners to export your profile data and individual interactions with their Page, if you permit such access via the Page owners exporting your data setting.

To control if you’re able to be discovered based on your email address or phone number within your settings:

To control if you’re able to be discovered based on your email address or phone number within your settings:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click Visibility on the left rail.
  4. Under Visibility of your profile & network section, click Change next to Profile discovery using email address or Profile discovery using phone number.
  5. Select from Anyone, 1st-degree connections, 2nd-degree connections, 1st and 2nd-degree connections, or Nobody (Options may vary).
  6. Your changes will be saved automatically.

To control if you’re able to be discovered based on your email address or phone number within your settings:

  1. Tap your  profile photo.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap Visibility.
  4. Under Visibility of your profile & network section, tap Profile discovery using email address or Profile discovery using phone number.
  5. Select from Anyone, 1st-degree connections, 2nd-degree connections, 1st and 2nd-degree connections, or Nobody (Options may vary).
  6. Your changes will be saved automatically.

Note: If you disable discover by email or discover by phone number lookup, others using permitted services off LinkedIn can still discover your profile based on your name and your organization. If you don’t wish your profile to be discovered in off-LinkedIn services, edit your off-LinkedIn visibility setting instead.

Manage your public profile URL

Edit your public profile URL

Promote your public profile and allow others to easily identify you in search results by changing or customizing your public profile URL.

Customize your URL

You can create your public profile URL on LinkedIn. Having a custom public profile URL will help other members and recruiters identify your profile easily and connect with you. Custom public profile URLs are available on a first come, first serve basis. You can only have one custom public profile URL at a time.

To create or edit your custom public profile URL:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click View Profile.
  3. On your profile page, click the   Edit icon next to Public profile & URL on the right pane.
  4. Under Edit your custom URL on the right pane, click the Edit icon next to your public profile URL.
  5. Type or edit the last part of your new custom public profile URL in the text box.
  6. Click Save.

To view assigned URL and unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. On your profile page, click the   Edit icon next to Public profile & URL on the right pane.

  4. Under Edit your custom URL on the right pane, you can:

    • See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Click See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you. You’ll see a list of custom public profile URLs that might have been previously linked to your profile (if any).
    • Unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Click unlink next to the custom public profile URL you want to unlink.
    • View your assigned URL: Your assigned public profile URL will be displayed under Assigned URL cannot be changed.

To create or edit your custom public profile URL:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap on the  More icon next to Add section button.

  4. Tap Contact info.

  5. Tap on the Edit icon on the upper right.

  6. On the Edit contact info page, tap on your Profile URL.

    • You’ll be redirected to the Public profile settings page.

  7. Under Edit your custom URL, tap the Edit icon next to your public profile URL.

  8. Type or edit the last part of your new custom public profile URL in the text box.

  9. Tap Save.

To view assigned URL and unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap View profile.

  3. Tap on the  More icon next to Add section button.

  4. Tap Contact info.

  5. Tap on the Edit icon on the upper right.

  6. On the Edit contact info page, tap on your Profile URL.

    • You’ll be redirected to the Public profile settings page.

  7. Under Edit your custom URL, you can:

    • See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Tap See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you. You’ll see a list of custom public profile URLs that might have been previously linked to your profile (if any).
    • Unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Tap unlink next to the custom public profile URL you want to unlink.
    • View your assigned URL: Your assigned public profile URL will be displayed under Assigned URL cannot be changed.

To change or edit your public profile URL:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Scroll to the Contact section and tap the Edit icon.

  3. On the Edit contact info page, tap on your Profile URL.

    • You’ll be redirected to the Public profile settings page.

  4. Under Edit your custom URL, tap the Edit icon next to your public profile URL.

  5. Type or edit the last part of your new custom URL in the text box.

  6. Tap Save.

To view assigned URL and unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Scroll to the Contact section and tap the Edit icon.

  3. On the Edit contact info page, tap on your Profile URL.

    • You’ll be redirected to the Public profile settings page.

  4. Under Edit your custom URL, you can:

    • See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Tap See prior custom URLs that might be linked to you. You’ll see a list of custom public profile URLs that might have been previously linked to your profile (if any).
    • Unlink prior custom URLs that might be linked to you: Tap unlink next to the custom public profile URL you want to unlink.
    • View your assigned URL: Your assigned public profile URL will be displayed under Assigned URL cannot be changed.

Notes:

  • Your custom URL can be 3-100 characters long and should not contain spaces, symbols, special characters, or the word LinkedIn.

  • We recommend using a variation of your name and/or your professional brand since you’ll share this public profile URL with people, so they can find your LinkedIn profile. Some job applications may also ask you for your LinkedIn public profile URL.

  • The customizable part of the URL is case insensitive, which means using JohnSmith, johnsmith, or johnSmith will all point to the same profile.

  • If the custom public profile URL you want isn’t available, please select a different one. We can’t make custom public profile URLs available to members upon request.

  • You can change your custom public profile URL up to five times within six months. Once you have changed your custom public profile URL for the fifth time, you won’t be able to change it for another six months. Changing your custom public profile URL several times may make it hard for people to find you.

  • You should be able to revert to your old URL immediately after changing. If you’re unable to, please contact us.

  • If you change your custom public profile URL, the previous URL is still linked to you for six months unless you unlink it. Other members won’t be able to claim during this period.

  • If you unlink a custom public profile URL, it won’t be visible to other members for seven days, after which they can claim it.

  • If you navigate to a previously claimed custom public profile URL, you may see a page that reads Profile Not Found.

  • Additional language profiles have the same public profile URL, but LinkedIn will add a language field at the end. For example, “fr” would be added at the end of the URL for a member’s French profile.

  • Once an account is closed, the custom public profile URL will be available after 180 days from the date of the close.

  • A public profile URL is automatically assigned when you create your LinkedIn profile. This URL can be changed only if you update your name.

  • Promote your public profile

Off-LinkedIn visibility

LinkedIn aims to help members get discovered for professional opportunities both on and off the platform. For example, public profiles may appear in search tool results. Additionally, users of certain email or other communication or networking services may see “mini” profiles of members they interact with.

If you prefer to limit the visibility of your profile information outside of LinkedIn, there are two settings that enable you to do that.

This setting controls which sections of your LinkedIn public profile are eligible for display to people who are not signed in to LinkedIn, or who can view your public profile via search tools such as Google or Bing. Learn how to hide or show your public profile.

Through our partnerships and developer program, we enable certain affiliates, partners, customers, and other permitted developers to display to their users information from the profiles of members they meet, write to or about, manage or consider for talent or other opportunities, take social actions (e.g. follow their company), etc. Some examples include email integrations, social media aggregators (e.g. tools for company brand administrators to consolidate interactions with followers across social media), talent and lead managers.

You can opt out using this setting (formerly known as “sharing data with third parties”).

To manage your Profile discovery and visibility off LinkedIn setting:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy.
  3. In the Visibility section, click Profile discovery and visibility off LinkedIn.
  4. Switch the toggle to On to show information from your profile to users of permitted services. Switch the toggle to Off to opt out of this setting.

Note: Changing the Profile discovery and visibility setting doesn’t limit visibility of your public profile (for example, on search tools), which can be controlled by the public profile setting. It also doesn’t limit the ability for Page owners to export your profile data and individual interactions with their Page, if you permit such access via the Page owners exporting your data setting.

Many of the users of these third-party services are LinkedIn members who opt in to link their LinkedIn account with their account on the other service. Depending on the nature of the specific integration, these users could see up to the same profile information (including connections data) seen while logged in to LinkedIn. This may be more than the public profile of members who haven’t disabled profile visibility and discovery off LinkedIn in their settings.

It is possible that users of external services who are not LinkedIn members or who haven’t linked their accounts can still view public profiles of LinkedIn members who have not opted out through the settings listed above.

  • LinkedIn public profile visibility
  • Private mode viewers of profiles
  • Browsing profiles in private and semi-private mode

Privacy for shared career interests

Once you have indicated that you’re open to job opportunities, users of LinkedIn’s Recruiter product will be able to find you based on your shared career interests when they’re searching for profiles.

Only recruiters who use LinkedIn’s Recruiter product will have access to your preferences and career interest information. It won’t be added to your LinkedIn.com profile unless you’ve opted to share that you’re open to job opportunities with all members.

We’ll share the following information with recruiters if you’ve provided it:

  • Flag you as open to hearing about new opportunities
  • Job titles or roles you’re interested in
  • If you’re open to full-time or contract opportunities
  • Date you flagged yourself as open to new opportunities

In order to protect your privacy, we take steps to keep Recruiter users who work at your company, as well as related companies, from seeing the career interests that you share.

We do this by comparing a unique number (Company ID) assigned to the current employer listed on your profile with the Company ID for recruiters on our network. If a recruiter’s Company ID is the same as the current employer listed on your profile, or the same as a company affiliated with that current employer based on our platform mapping, then we won’t show your career interest preferences.

We can’t guarantee, however, that every company is accurately identified, or that affiliated companies are accurately mapped on our platform. We also can’t guarantee that every recruiter has an up-to-date and correct Company ID, so there’s a small chance that your career interest preferences will be visible to a recruiter at your current employer or an affiliated company.

Settings for profile photo visibility

You can control the visibility of your profile photo. Posting a profile photo is optional, but it helps your connections and others to recognize you. In fact, members with a profile photo receive up to 2X more profile views and 3X more connection requests.

To change the visibility of your profile photo:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click on your profile photo.

  4. Click the ** Visibility** icon on the left of the Profile photo pop-up window, and select the visibility from the following options:

    • 1st-degree connections only
    • Your network
    • All LinkedIn members
    • Anyone

  5. Click Save.

To change the visibility of your profile photo in your public profile (as it appears in web browser searches):

  1. Click the Me icon at top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Click Edit public profile & URL on the right pane.

  4. In the right pane of the Public profile settings page, you can change the details of your profile that are publicly visible under Edit Visibility.

  5. Select one of the following options below the Profile Photo section to change the visibility to:

    • Only 1st-degree connections
    • Your network
    • All LinkedIn Members
    • Public

Your changes will be saved automatically.

Important: These settings must be updated on our desktop site and can’t be changed on the LinkedIn mobile app.

Note: On the public profile settings page, you’ll be able to see and adjust all the sections of your profile that can be displayed to users who aren’t logged in to LinkedIn and find you through a web browser or other permitted services.

To change the visibility of your profile photo:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.

  3. Tap your profile photo near the top of the page.

  4. Tap ** View or edit profile photo**.

  5. Tap the ** Visibility** icon and select the visibility from the following options:

    • 1st-degree connections only
    • Your network
    • All LinkedIn members
    • Anyone

  6. The change is saved automatically.

To change the visibility of your profile photo:

  1. Tap the Profile photo.

  2. Tap the Profile photo on your profile page.

    • You can also tap the Camera icon on your profile photo to access the Edit photo page.

  3. Tap Edit.

  4. Select one of the following options from the Visible To dropdown:

    • Everyone
    • Connections
    • Network
    • All LinkedIn members

  5. Tap Save on the upper-right corner to save the photo.

Notes:

  • The default photo setting is Anyone/Everyone.

  • If you edit your profile photo visibility settings from your profile page, it automatically updates the settings on your public profile page too. For example, if you change your profile photo visibility setting from Public to 1st-degree connections Only, that change will also be applied to your public profile.

  • You can set different visibility for your public profile and the profile view your LinkedIn connections see. For example, you can opt to exclude your Posts and Activities, or other parts of your profile, from your public profile.

  • If your public profile is disabled (visible to no one), your profile photo visibility setting cannot be set as Public.

Understand your privacy settings

The Privacy tab covers all privacy and security settings related to what can be seen about you, how information can be used, and downloading your data.

To access your LinkedIn privacy settings:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.
  3. Click the Data Privacy on the left rail.

You’ll find the following sub-sections in the Data privacy section:

  • How LinkedIn uses your data: Manage the ways your data is used on LinkedIn.
  • Who can reach you: Manage invitations and messages.
  • Messaging experience: Choose how you would like LinkedIn to customize your experience. This includes read receipts, typing indicators, and reply suggestions.
  • Job seeking preferences: Set your preferences regarding job seeking, including letting recruiters know you’re open to opportunities.
  • Other applications: Control how associated accounts can use your data.

Learn more about managing your account and privacy settings.

Visibility and impact of your social activity on the LinkedIn feed

Your LinkedIn feed contains professional content from your network, your shares, likes, and posts, companies you follow, and other content that we believe you may be interested in.

LinkedIn’s systems track and analyze social actions such as writing a post or article, liking content, or commenting on another member’s posts or articles. We use this data in our algorithms to provide content relevant to you in your LinkedIn feed.

You may see recommended content with labels such as Trending, Recommended for you, or Popular. Your social actions also influence the ads we show you.

Notes:

  • Your posts, comments, and likes on LinkedIn Groups also impact the content in your feed.
  • If you are accessing LinkedIn from one of the Designated Countries, LinkedIn’s ability to track and analyze your social actions may depend on your cookie preferences.

You can customize your feed to manage what content appears. Also, you can control the content you see by following new people or companies to improve your feed.

  • Manage cookie preferences
  • Best practices to customize what you see on your LinkedIn feed

Visibility and usage of your uploaded resume

There are several ways to upload resumes on LinkedIn. If you upload your resume while applying for a job on LinkedIn, it’ll be shared with that hirer. You can also upload your resume from the Job Application Settingspage. When you upload your resume we’ll save a copy and retain your four most recently uploaded resumes, enabling you to reuse them for future job applications. We’ll use your saved resumes to personalize and improve LinkedIn consistent with our Privacy Policy and as described below. You can manage which resumes are saved and can opt-out of saving resumes in your resume settings.

Examples of how we may use your saved resumes include recommending and ranking jobs you might be interested in and personalizing other content recommendations (such as LinkedIn Learning courses, suggesting updates to your profile, feed posts, connections, or companies to follow). To do this, we may infer data about you, such as your skills, interests and experiences from your saved resumes. We may also use data from your saved resumes when you use generative AI features (for example, when you are searching for jobs, we may use your saved resume data in AI-powered features that show you how well you match the qualifications of a particular role).

Your saved resume data may also contribute to improvements in our AI models. This includes training content-generating AI models consistent with practices outlined in our FAQ on LinkedIn’s use of Generative AI and subject to your settings, where you can opt out of information you share being used to improve content-generating AI models.

Finally, in addition to sharing your resume with hirers when you apply to a job on LinkedIn, you have additional options to share your resumes with others including:

  • If you have not turned off the Share resume data with hirers setting, we will also use your shared resume data as inputs into features that allow hirers to see how you match their job qualifications, as well as including certain resume data on your profile in our hiring products.
  • If you post a resume as a media attachment to your LinkedIn profile or in a LinkedIn post, it will be visible to anyone viewing your profile or that post and may be visible off LinkedIn.

For more information on these features, see linked articles below.

Visibility of shared posts

The visibility of posts and engagement activity that appear in the main feed and profile may vary depending on the visibility option that the author has selected for the post. You can’t change the visibility option after you’ve shared your post.

The visibility options are:

  • Anyone – visible to anyone on or off LinkedIn, including your extended network.
  • Connections only – visible to only 1st-degree connections of the post author.
  • ** Group** – visible only to members of the group where the post was shared.

Once you select a visibility option, it is saved as your default visibility option. But you can change this before posting content the next time.

Note: For schedule posts, the post will be published with the visibility setting you choose at the time the post is created.

If your post visibility is set to Anyone, the post may appear on:

  • The homepage of your 1st-degree connections.

  • The homepage of your 2nd or 3rd-degree connections if re-shared, commented on, or liked by your 1st-degree connections.

  • Content search results for topics you’ve posted.

  • Your Activity page.

  • Your public profile, which is also visible to people who aren’t signed in to LinkedIn. This may not show if you’ve turned off public profile visibility from Public profile settings page.

  • Other sites off LinkedIn. This means that even people who aren’t signed in to LinkedIn can see your post.

  • Your followers’ feeds, who may not be connected to you.

  • Post and share content on LinkedIn

  • Your network and degrees of connection

  • Share public posts on and off LinkedIn

  • Your recent activity on LinkedIn

By default, your 1st-degree connections can see and browse your list of connections. However, you can manage who can see your connections from your Settings page.

To adjust who can see your list of connections:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap Visibility.

To adjust who can see your list of connections:

  1. Tap your profile photo.
  2. Tap the Settings icon in the upper-right corner.
  3. Tap Visibility.
  4. Under Visibility of your profile & network section, tap Connections.

Notes:

  • Your 1st-degree connections may sync their LinkedIn account to their account on a partner service and see your connections on that service unless you opt out of profile visibility on partner services.

  • By default, advertisers can serve ads specifically to the connections of a company’s employees, but advertisers can’t see these connections (except to the extent they may be personally connected to you, as described above). You can stop advertisers from serving such ads to your connections (to the extent they are not also the connections of other employees at your company), by selecting No/Off under Connections.

Who’s viewed your profile visibility settings

There are three ways we show information on Who’s Viewed Your Profile. Based on the profile viewer’s privacy settings, you’ll see one of these:

  • Your name and headline - The viewer’s name, headline, location, and industry.
  • Private profile characteristics -The viewer’s semi-private profile characteristics such as job title, company, school, and industry. We might vary the information we show to protect members’ privacy (for example, VP of Marketing in Internet Industry, Student at University of North Carolina, Someone at Accenture).
  • Private mode - LinkedIn Member. These are members who have viewed your profile and chose to use complete private mode in their privacy settings.

You can control who can see if you’ve viewed their profile by updating your profile viewing options from the Settings & Privacy page.

Here’s a tip

To stop receiving emails from LinkedIn about Who’s Viewed Your Profile, click Unsubscribe in the email footer.

To access the profile visibility setting:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.

  3. Click Visibility on the left pane and under Visibility of your profile & network, click Profile viewing options.

  4. Select one of the following options:

    • Your name and headline
    • Private profile characteristics
    • Private mode

Your changes will be saved automatically.

To access the profile visibility setting:

  1. Tap your profile photo, then tap Settings.

  2. Tap the Visibility tab.

  3. Tap Profile viewing options.

  4. Select one of the following options:

    • Your name and headline
    • Private profile characteristics
    • Private mode

Your changes will be saved automatically.

Notes:

  • If a member viewed your profile prior to any blocking, they’ll still appear in your profile viewer count, but their details won’t be reflected in the viewer details. Once a member is blocked, they won’t be able to view your profile.

  • You can’t view the names of members who’ve chosen to view your profile in private mode, even if you have a Premium account.

  • If you have a Basic (free) account, you must choose Your name and headline if you want to see the viewer history on your own Who’s Viewed Your Profile page.

  • If you select a specific member’s name in search suggestions with their description and profile picture (by clicking on the search suggestion or pressing enter when it is highlighted), you view their mini profile in the search results page. This is treated as a profile view that may result in a notification being sent to the member whose profile you viewed, depending on your settings.

Accept or dismiss recommendations

A recommendation is a commendation written by a LinkedIn member to recognize your work. You can request recommendations from your 1st-degree connections you work with or have worked with.

When someone writes you a recommendation, you’ll be notified via a message from the sender on LinkedIn. You can accept, dismiss, or ask for a revision of the recommendation.

Note: Recommendations appear in a chronological order and currently can’t be reordered.

To accept the recommendation from your email:

  1. Log in to the email account you’ve associated with LinkedIn.
  2. Locate the recommendation email and open it.
  3. Click the link provided in the message to Review Recommendation.
  4. From the Pending recommendations pop-up window, click Add to profile to accept and display the recommendation on your profile. You can click Ignore if you don’t want to accept the recommendation.

To accept the recommendation from the message in your LinkedIn account:

  1. Click the Messaging icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

    • Alternatively, you can select the Review Recommendation message from the LinkedIn Messaging Conversation Windows on the lower-right of any LinkedIn page and click on the link.

  2. Select the recommendation message from the left rail of the Messaging page.

  3. Click the link provided in the message to Review Recommendation.

  4. From the Recommendations page, you can:

    • Click Add to profile to accept and display the recommendation on your profile.
    • Click ** More** to the right of the recommendation and select Ask for revision or Dismiss recommendation.

To accept, dismiss, or ask for revision of recommendations:

  1. Tap your profile photo.

  2. Tap your profile photo again to view profile.

  3. Scroll down to the Recommendations section, then tap Show all pending.

  4. From the Recommendations page, you can:

    • Tap Add to profile to accept and display the recommendation on your profile.
    • Tap the ** More** icon to the right of the recommendation and select Ask for revision or ** Dismiss recommendation**.

  5. Tap Add to profile to accept and display the recommendation on your profile. You can also tap:

    • Dismiss
    • Ask for revision

Once you’ve accepted the recommendation, it will appear in the Recommendations section of your profile and an update will go out to your network.

Note: Once you’ve dismissed a recommendation you received, it can’t retrieved again. The member who recommended you must delete the recommendation before you can request for a new recommendation.

Account age on LinkedIn profiles

LinkedIn is a trusted platform both for people both hiring and looking for jobs. As an online marketplace, we want to ensure every job posted on LinkedIn is authentic and provide job seekers with additional context and transparency around the jobs they may consider applying for.

When you post a job on LinkedIn, the date you created your LinkedIn profile will appear on your job post to seekers. For example, if you created your account in June 2018, your job post will include “Joined LinkedIn in June 2018.”

At this time, you won’t be able to opt out of sharing this information.

No. Information around when you joined LinkedIn will only show up on the jobs you create and post on LinkedIn.

Yes. Even if you decide not to attach your LinkedIn profile to your job post, information around when you joined LinkedIn will still appear, though your identity will remain private and secure.

Add and remove skills on your profile

You can add and remove skills from the Skills section on your profile. Maintaining a relevant list of skills on your profile will help others understand your strengths and match you with the right opportunities. You can add up to 100 skills to your profile.

If you don’t have any skills listed on your profile, the Skills section won’t appear.

To add the Skills section and skills:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage, then View Profile.

  2. Click Add profile section button in your introduction section.

  3. Click Core and select Add skills from the dropdown.

  4. In the Add skill pop-up window, you can:

    • Type the name of a skill and select it from the dropdown list that appears or select a skill from Suggested based on your profile. Once selected, it is automatically added to your list of skills.
    • Select the checkboxes that show where you put this skill to use.
    • Select the checkbox to follow this skill’s collaborative articles page.

  5. Click Save.

Repeat the above steps to add more skills to your profile.

To remove skills:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage, then View Profile.
  2. Scroll to the Skills section and click the Edit icon.
  3. In the Skills page, click the Edit icon to the right of the skill that you want to delete.
  4. Click Delete skill on the lower left, and then confirm Delete.

If you don’t have any skills listed on your profile, the Skills section won’t appear.

To add the Skills section to your profile and add skills:

  1. Tap your profile picture, then tap View profile.

  2. Tap Add section in your introduction section.

  3. Tap Core and select Add skills.

  4. From the Skill page, you can:

    • Type the name of a skill and select it from the dropdown list that appears or select a skill from Suggested based on your profile. Once selected, it is automatically added to your list of skills.
    • Select the checkboxes that show where you put this skill to use.
    • Select the checkbox to follow this skill’s collaborative articles page.

  5. Tap Save.

Repeat the above steps to add more skills to your profile.

To remove skills from your profile:

  1. Tap your profile picture, then tap View profile.
  2. Scroll to the Skills section and tap the Edit icon.
  3. In the Skills page, click the Edit icon to the right of the skill that you want to delete.
  4. Tap Delete skill at the bottom of the page and confirm Delete.

Live Video stream on the cover image

When a LinkedIn Live Video broadcaster begins a live stream, the cover image will automatically change to display the live stream. This cover image change is temporary and the image will revert after the stream has ended.

Note: Currently there is no option to opt out of this feature.

Cover image specifications:

  • JPG or PNG file
  • Lesser than 8MB
  • 1584 (w) x 396 (h) pixels (recommended)

If your cover image appears blurry or pixelated, please choose an image with a larger file size. Photos will also look better than images with logos. If your image is still blurry or pixelated, you could use a compression tool such as Trimage for Windows or ImageOptim for Mac before uploading it to LinkedIn.

Notes:

  • LinkedIn doesn’t provide support for any third-party tools that you use
  • How your image appears may change based on the size of your web browser window and screen resolution
  • Cover image that you upload must comply with our User Agreement

Boost a post from your LinkedIn profile

As a LinkedIn member, you can boost your posts on the LinkedIn feed from both desktop and mobile devices to increase your visibility, grow your followers, and get more website clicks. You can select your budget and target audience to boost key posts, increase visibility to target audiences by selecting from facets including location, language, job title, job function, company industries, and job seniorities.

Important to know

  • Boosting a post will turn the post into an ad. See the LinkedIn Ads Agreement for more information.
  • Mobile boosting is currently in testing and is gradually being released. You might not have access to it at this time, and some functionality might change over time.
  • Boost credits included with Premium All-in-One can only be used to boost posts from your personal profile. You can’t use these credits to boost posts from a LinkedIn Page.

Boost on desktop and mobile

To boost a post on desktop:

  1. Click the   Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Scroll down to the Activitysection and click on Posts (Selected by default).

  4. Click Show all posts on the bottom of the Activity section.

  5. Click Boost on the upper right of a post.

  6. From the Boost page, you can:

    • Select your goal
    • Select your budget
    • Select target audience
    • Add payment details

  7. Click Boost on the lower right to boost your posts.

To boost on mobile, you must have ad credits for your budget. When you boost a post on mobile, you’ll set your audience, duration, and budget, then review your boost. Ad credits are purchased in the final step of checkout, right before you complete your order. If you don’t have enough in ad credits for your budget, you will need to purchase additional ad credits. Learn more about prepaid ad credits.

To boost a post on mobile:

  1. Tap the   Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Tap your profile picture and scroll down to the Activity section.

  3. Tap Show all at the bottom of the Activitysection.

  4. Tap Boostin the upper right of a post.

  5. From the Boost page, you can:

    • Select your goal
    • Select your budget
    • Select your target audience
    • Add payment details

  6. Select your payment method and complete the checkout process.

  7. Tap either Boostor Pay and Boostto boost the post.

After you boost your post as an ad, it will be reviewed before it can be displayed to member accounts in your target audience. We strive to review ads as soon as possible and usually within 24 hours.

You can manage your post after it’s been boosted to:

  • Edit the post, audience, or credit card used as the payment method
  • View performance metrics

You can also delete the ad if needed.

Browsing Profiles in Private and Semi-Private Mode

When you view a profile in private mode, you’ll appear in that person’s Who’s Viewed Your Profile section as LinkedIn Member - This person is viewing profiles in private mode. No other information about you will be shared with the member whose profile you viewed.

When you browse in semi-private mode, your profile characteristics such as job title, company, school, and industry will be shown to the member you are viewing (for example, Consultant at State Farm, Someone at Accenture, or Student at Cornell University).

To change your browsing mode:

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown.

  3. Click Visibility on the left rail.

  4. In the Visibility of your profile & network section, click Change next to Profile viewing options.

  5. Select the mode you’d like to browse in. You have three options:

    • Your name and headline
    • Private profile characteristics (i.e. job title and industry)
    • Private mode

Your changes will be saved automatically.

Note: With a Premium account, you can browse in private mode and still see the list of people who viewed your profile in the last 90 days. This isn’t possible with a Basic (free) account. However, we always respect a member’s privacy settings, so even with a Premium account, you can’t view the names of private mode viewers of your own profile.

Learn more if your list of viewers is missing.

Create a good LinkedIn profile

[Embedded video omitted]

Your LinkedIn profile is a professional landing page for you to manage your personal brand. A LinkedIn profile is a great way for you to let people know who you are, what you stand for, and what you’re interested in. Your profile will be your personal storyboard where people can find you and stay updated on your activity, so make sure your profile is complete and representative of you.

Your profile is fully visible to all LinkedIn members who’ve signed in to LinkedIn.com or our apps. However, you can control what appears on your profile, notifications to your network, and your profile privacy preferences.

Having a profile on LinkedIn helps:

  • Manage your professional brand – You can define and develop how other members view your professional experience and qualifications. Since you will have complete control over your profile and its visibility, you can customize it to fit your needs. Your customized profile will help recruiters and other members understand your professional personality.
  • Create opportunities for you – Since people and organizations globally use LinkedIn, a LinkedIn profile will help you get noticed. An updated profile is a great way to ensure that you can be found by right people at the right time. It’s also an excellent way to find job opportunities and connect with recruiters. Once you’ve completed your profile, you’ll be more equipped to find jobs on LinkedIn.
  • Build your network and track your professional milestones – All of your professional achievements (new job, work anniversary, promotion, etc.) can be recorded and displayed on your LinkedIn profile. It’ll help you showcase your professional experience and achievements to other members who view your profile. An updated profile opens the door to meeting new members and making connections.

You can add various sections to your profile to showcase your skills and expertise. A complete LinkedIn profile will increase your discoverability and profile search appearances.

Tips for creating a great LinkedIn profile:

  • Add a professional profile photo - A good profile photo increases the credibility of your profile and helps you stand out from the crowd. Members with a profile photo on LinkedIn receive up to 2X more profile views. You can also add a background image to personalize your profile. Check out some more tips for picking the right LinkedIn profile photo.
  • Make your headline stand out – Your headline is created when you add your positions to your profile. However, you can re-write it to either promote an area of expertise or to let your personality shine through.
  • Write a summary - The About section of your profile should express your mission, motivation, and skills to people who view your profile. Ideally, you should limit the text to one or two paragraphs while filling this section. You can use bullet points if you’re not comfortable with writing paragraphs. Check out some LinkedIn profile summaries that we love.
  • Add all your relevant work and education experiences – You should keep the profile updated with all your professional experiences that align with your current career goals. You can also add media samples to provide quick access to your work portfolio.
  • Add relevant skills – A list of relevant skills on your profile helps you showcase your abilities to other members, like your colleagues and recruiters. It helps other understand your strengths. Once you add your skills, your connections can endorse them. If someone endorses your skills, it will increase the likelihood of you being discovered for opportunities related to the skills you possess. You can also take assessments for the skills you’ve listed on your profile to showcase your proficiency.
  • Request recommendations from your connections - A recommendation is written to recognize or commend a connection, such as a colleague, business partner, or student. There’s no limit to the number of recommendations you can request for. Once you accept a recommendation written by a connection, it becomes visible to your network by default. You can also hide recommendations that you think don’t suit your professional goals.
  • Use your profile strength meter to gauge the strength of your profile.

Once you’ve created and updated different sections of your profile, you can begin sharing your public profile with your wider network. Your public profile is a simplified version of your complete LinkedIn profile that shows up in search engines and is visible to everyone. You can promote your profile to show up better in search engine results by creating a personal URL. You can also create a badge for your public profile that you can add to your online resume, blog, or website from the Public profile settings page.

Watch this course on LinkedIn Learning to learn more about how to create a LinkedIn profile.

Once you’ve given a recommendation to a connection, it can be revised or deleted. The recipient can also choose to hide or unhide a recommendation at any time.

Differences between a LinkedIn profile and a LinkedIn Page

LinkedIn Pages represent collective organizations, while LinkedIn profiles represent individuals.

Your LinkedIn profile is a professional landing page for you to manage your own, personal brand. You can find and connect with colleagues and classmates and display a general history of your professional experiences and achievements which a typical resume or CV might not reflect.

Here’s a tip

You can also upgrade your profile with a Premium subscription, which offers more features like Premium Career and LinkedIn Learning.

LinkedIn profiles versus LinkedIn Pages

Review some of the features that exist for both profiles and Pages:

  • LinkedIn profile; Represents: A person; Completion Meter: Profile level meter; Become a follower: Follow or unfollow people, LinkedIn Pages, or topics; Visitor Analytics: Who’s viewed my profile; Verification: Member verification; LinkedIn Premium: Get started with LinkedIn Premium subscription
  • LinkedIn Page; Represents: An organization; Completion Meter: Complete your Page; Become a follower: Follow a Page as a LinkedIn Page; Visitor Analytics: Who’s visited my Page; Verification: Page verification; LinkedIn Premium: Get started with LinkedIn Premium Company Page subscription

You can create a LinkedIn Page for free, helping you represent and build your organization’s brand on LinkedIn. LinkedIn Pages help members learn about the organization’s business, brand, products and services, and job opportunities. You must have a LinkedIn profile to create a Page, and you can’t convert a profile into a Page. You can then designate anyone affiliated with the organization as an admin, including yourself.

All LinkedIn profiles must comply with our User Agreement and Professional Community Policies which require you to:

  • Use your real name
  • Not use or attempt to use another’s account
  • Not create a member account for anyone other than yourself
  • Not associate yourself on LinkedIn with a business or organization that you’re not professionally associated with

Switching from a LinkedIn profile to a LinkedIn Page

Keep in mind that you can’t represent your organization with a LinkedIn profile since LinkedIn profiles must represent real people. If you attempt to represent your organization with a LinkedIn profile instead of a Page, LinkedIn may automatically log you out of your account. Repeat or prolonged violations of our profile policies may lead to your LinkedIn account being restricted.

If you’ve mistakenly created a LinkedIn profile to represent your organization, we recommend that you update the profile name to your real name and create a new LinkedIn Page to represent your organization instead, before your LinkedIn profile becomes restricted. If you believe that your account has been incorrectly restricted, you can contact the support team for assistance.

Here are some ways to make it easier to build out a new LinkedIn Page to represent your organization:

  • Once you’ve created a new LinkedIn Page, you can add your LinkedIn profile as an admin to the Page and invite your profile connections on the LinkedIn profile to follow your new Page. To do this, you can invite your connections from your Page admin view.
  • Review how you can protect your Page by turning on two-factor authentication, verification, and managing messages to your Page. Learn more about ways to protect your LinkedIn Page.
  • You can also download account data from your personal profile to easily include onto your Page. Review the types of data you can download by going to your Data Privacy settings. Different data types will become available within 10 minutes or 48 hours depending on the data you select.
  • Consider subscribing to a Premium Company Page to help you make your Page stand out and convert more LinkedIn members into clients for your business. For example, you can automatically invite people who you aren’t connected with to follow your Page and you can also see eligible members who visited your Page each week.

You can create different types of Pages that represent organizations, products, services, and more. Learn more about the types of LinkedIn Pages available.

Differences between offering services on your Company Page and your personal profile

To help you find more clients for your business, you can offer your services on LinkedIn with a dedicated landing page at no cost to you. Services on LinkedIn operate on a request and proposal model.

You can offer services either on your Company Page or on your personal LinkedIn profile. Keep in mind that you can only manage your Company Page’s services from the page, and the Profile’s services from your profile. The following table compares the differences between Page-managed and profile-managed services.

  • Feature: Recommended use; Services managed by a profile: When you want to associate your personal name and profile with your services, and you’re the only person who needs to manage the service requests; Services managed by a Company Page: When you want to associate your Page’s professional brand with your services, and you want to let other admins of the Page view and manage service requests
  • Feature: Who can manage the services and receive requests for services; Services managed by a profile: Only the member who created the Services Page; Services managed by a Company Page: Any super or content admin of the Company Page that set up the services.
  • Feature: Cost of a Service Page; Services managed by a profile: Free, with optional upgrades with a Premium Business subscription; Services managed by a Company Page: Free, with optional upgrades with a Premium Company Page subscription
  • Feature: Number of services; Services managed by a profile: Offer up to 10 different service types; Services managed by a Company Page: Offer up to 10 service types
  • Feature: Requirements to set up services; Services managed by a profile: No requirements; Services managed by a Company Page: Only companies with 500 employess or less are eligible to offer services on their Company Page. You cannot offer services on a Showcase Page or a University Page. Your Company Page will automatically  enable messages for the Page when setting up services
  • Feature: Reviews; Services managed by a profile: You can invite client to review your services; Services managed by a Company Page: Reviews are currently not available
  • Feature: How to manage your services; Services managed by a profile: Services admin view is available on desktop and mobile; Services managed by a Company Page: Services admin view is currently available only on desktop

Display Order of Skills

Important to know

You can only reorder the Education and Skills sections on your profile.

Including specific skills on your LinkedIn profile is a great way to showcase your abilities to other members, such as your peers, colleagues, managers, and even recruiters. You can add a maximum of 100 skills to your profile. They’re a simple and effective way to build your professional brand and engage your network.

Notes:

  • If you don’t have any skills listed on your profile, the Skills section won’t appear.
  • You must have more than three skills listed in your Skills section for your skills to be categorized.

Your skills are categorized by areas of expertise:

To reorder your skills:

  4. Click the  More icon on the upper right of the Skills page.
  5. Click  Reorder from the dropdown.
  6. In the pop-up window, click and drag the  Sort icon to the right of the corresponding skill you’d like to reorder.

To reorder your skills:

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap your profile photo again to access your profile.
  3. Scroll down to the Skills section.
  4. Tap the Edit icon.

Display your ID name as an additional name on your profile

We can use your ID name to verify your identity on LinkedIn if your name on your profile doesn’t match the name on your government-issued ID (your “legal name” or your “ID name”). We match your ID name because your ID name can be verified.

We understand that your LinkedIn name may not always match your legal name. That’s why we offer flexible identity verification options tailored to your situation. Participating in identity verification is optional.

Display your legal name on your profile

One way to verify your identity is by consenting to display your legal name alongside your LinkedIn name.

  • This will not replace your LinkedIn name but your legal name will appear in parenthesis after it.
  • Your ID name will also appear if you have a secondary profile in another language.
  • However, your ID name will not be visible on public profiles to anyone who is not logged in to LinkedIn.

If your LinkedIn name does not match your legal name, your identity verification is contingent on the legal name being displayed.

[Image: ID name with profile name]

Add your legal name to your profile

If you have not added your legal name to your profile and you receive a message stating that verification couldn’t be added yet, follow these steps:

  1. Select Display your ID name as an additional name on your profile.
  2. Select Display ID name to consent to displaying your ID name as an additional name on your profile.
  3. When completed, you’ll see a confirmation that identity verification has been added.

Find your legal name

  • You can view your additional name when you edit your profile. (To edit your profile click your profile image and then select the edit icon on your profile).
  • Your ID name is view-only and cannot be changed or updated.
  • Deleting your ID name will remove both your legal name and your identity verification.

Who can see your legal name?

If you choose to display your ID name, it will be visible to all logged-in LinkedIn members.

However, it will not appear:

  • On public profiles
  • To visitors who are not logged into LinkedIn
  • In public search engine results

What happens if you delete your verification?

If you delete your identity verification in Settings, your legal name will also be removed from your profile.

Edit Company Photos on the Life or What We Do tab of your LinkedIn Page

If you’ve enhanced your LinkedIn Page with Career Pages, you can leverage the Life or What We Do tab to provide a preview of life at your organization through photos, testimonials, employee-written content, and more.

Customizing the Company Photos on your LinkedIn Page allows you to exemplify your organization and culture. For optimal results, follow our image specifications.

To add or edit Company Photos on your Page:

  1. Go to your Page super admin view.

  2. Click Life or What we do in the left menu.

  3. Click the correct targeted audience page.

    • Note: If you previously saved a draft of the page, go to the Unpublished section and click on the correct draft.

  4. In the Company Photos section, add a minimum of four photos and no more than twenty photos from your computer.

    • To add a new photo: Click Add photo. Select a photo file.
    • To remove an existing photo: Move your cursor over the photo you wish to remove and click the  Delete icon.

  5. After you’ve added photos, you can rearrange them by clicking and dragging them to the left or right. If your photo doesn’t fit the fixed frame, make sure it meets the image specification of 900 pixels x 600 pixels.

  6. Once you’re finished editing the page, click one of the following options in the upper-right corner of the screen:

    • Preview – View a member preview of the page. Click Back to edit mode from the preview page to go back and either save or publish your edits.
    • Save – Creates a draft of the page but won’t publish the edits. Your previously published version of the page will remain the same.
    • Publish – Makes your edits public and replaces the previously published version of the page.

Edit or delete a boosted post from your LinkedIn profile

After you’ve boosted your post as a LinkedIn member, you can edit or delete it if you choose to. When you edit a boosted post, you can edit the post itself, the audience, and the credit card used as the payment method.

Important to know

You can’t change the budget of a boosted post. If you need to change the budget, you must delete the ad and boost the post again with a new budget. Boosting a post will turn the post into an ad. See the LinkedIn Ads Agreement for more information.

To edit or delete a boosted post on desktop:

  1. Click the   Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Click View Profile.

  3. Scroll down to the Activitysection and click on Posts (selected by default).

  4. Click Show all posts on the bottom of the Activity section.

  5. Click Manage on the upper right of a boosted post.

  6. From here, you can:

    • Edit an active ad
    • Change the audience
    • Update the payment details
    • Click Delete ad on the upper right of the Manage ad page

Important to know

Mobile boosting is currently in testing and is gradually being released. You might not have access to it at this time, and some functionality might change over time.

To edit or delete a boosted post on mobile:

  1. Tap the   Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.

  2. Tap View Profile.

  3. Scroll down to the Activitysection and tap Posts(selected by default).

  4. Tap Show all posts at the bottom of the Activitysection.

  5. Tap Manageon the upper right of a boosted post.

  6. From here, you can:

    • Edit an active ad
    • Change the audience
    • Stop boosting the post

If you edited the post itself, it might need to be reviewed again before it can be shown to member accounts in your target audience. We strive to review ads as soon as possible and usually within 24 hours.

Skill endorsements are a great way to recognize your 1st-degree connections’ skills. You can only endorse skills already listed on someone’s profile.

After you endorse someone, your name and picture will appear next to the skill on that person’s profile. They’ll also receive an email, if they’ve opted for it. The most endorsed skills will move to the top of the Skills & endorsements section.

You can choose to hide or unhide a recommendation you’ve given to, or received from another member on your profile.

Notes:

  4. Click the Visibility button below the name of the member and select from All LinkedIn members, 1st-degree connections only and Only you.

Note: Recommendations you’ve written for others can also be displayed on your own profile. Choosing to hide or unhide this recommendation doesn’t impact how it’s displayed on the recipient’s profile page.

LinkedIn Page public URL

When you create a LinkedIn Page as an admin, you’ll create a primary URL.

The primary URL is also called a public URL which members of your Page can see. Your Page will also generate a secondary URL which is a unique identification number that only you, as an admin, can see. Every LinkedIn Page and Showcase Page is assigned with a secondary URL, and both the primary and secondary URL can be used to direct traffic to your Page.

Important to know

The primary URL of your Page can be edited at any time but can’t be changed more than once in a 30-day period. The unique secondary URL can’t be edited.

If you decide to change the primary URL, it may take a few weeks for search engines to direct traffic to the new Page URL. Keep in mind, changing the Page’s name doesn’t change the URL. The original URL you previously used will also become available for another Page to use upon request.

Here are a few things to keep in mind about your Page’s public URL:

  • Page URLs are subject to availability.
  • If eligible, it’s required that you first update your company name, and then match the proposed URL as closely as possible if it’s not already taken. We also suggest avoiding ambiguity by using acronyms that could match another company name. For example, use “/the-dream-company” instead of “/tdc”.
  • Changing your Page name doesn’t automatically change the URL.
  • If you edit your Page URL, both the old and new Page URL will direct to your LinkedIn Page. However, if an admin makes a request for your old Page URL, it can be reassigned to their Page, and the old URL will no longer redirect to your Page. If you’d like to repurpose your LinkedIn Page URL to another one of your LinkedIn Pages, you can contact LinkedIn Support to make this change.

Associations with organizations in the Experience section of your profile must be accurately labeled and must reflect professional experience with the named organization, such as employment, contract work, official internship or volunteer experience, board service, among others. Informal associations or non-professional experience with organizations shouldn’t be included, such as a customer or user of an organization’s products or services.

Missing Who’s viewed your profile history

The Who’s viewed your profile feature leverages your profile visitor data to display trends and additional insights about the people viewing your profile (last 90 days), such as where your viewers work, their job titles, and industries they work in.

Important to know

You won’t see this information if you haven’t had any profile views in the past 90 days. Also, viewing timeframes may vary over time and as people view your profile. When possible, we try to display a minimum of three views over any timeframe. Viewer insights are only available to LinkedIn’s Premium subscribers, and they are subject to the viewer’s privacy settings. A Premium Business and a Premium Career subscriber will be able to see list of viewers, viewer trends, and insights for the past 365 days.

You won’t be able to see Who’s viewed your profile if:

  • You have a Basic (free) account and,
  • You choose not to show your name and headline when viewing other people’s profiles by browsing in semi-private or private mode.

If you have a basic account and have set your profile viewing options to display your name and headline when viewing profiles, you’ll see the three most recent viewers in the last 90 days, as well as a list of suggestions for increasing your profile views.

Note: Even if you have a Premium account, you won’t see the names of viewers who choose to browse in private mode or private profile characteristics. We respect the privacy of members who don’t wish to reveal information about themselves when viewing profiles.

Photo won’t upload to your profile

Adding a photograph to your profile helps your current and potential connections recognize you. You can use an illustration, caricature, or other artistic rendering of yourself, but your profile photo must reflect your likeness.

If you’re unable to upload a photo to your profile, please ensure that the photo file meets these specifications:

  • Maximum file size is 8MB.

  • Profile photo: Pixel size is between 400 (w) x 400 (h) pixels and 7680 (w) x 4320 (h) pixels. We recommend adding a photo that won’t require much cropping. You can adjust the photo after it has been uploaded.

  • Background photo: Recommended pixel dimensions are 1584 (w) x 396 (h) pixels.

  • File type must be PNG or JPG.

    Note: We don’t support GIFs.

If it still won’t upload, try again using a different browser. If that doesn’t work, you can try compressing a photo, on your system and then upload it to your profile.

Also please ensure that the photo complies with the profile photo guidelines and conditions.

  • Profile photo guidelines and conditions

Position grouping in your profile’s experience section

Positions in your Experience section are automatically grouped if they’re held at the same company. Grouping highlights your career progression within the company and makes it easier for your connections and recruiters to understand your experience.

Positions are grouped when the start date of a new position is within one month of the previous position’s end date at the same company.

Here’s a tip

To show your career progression within a company, make sure to specify the employment type for each position.

[Image: Example of grouped and ungrouped position on your profile]

When positions are grouped:

  • They appear under a single company section, showing the company name and logo.
  • Each position within the company is listed in chronological order.
  • The total tenure at that company is shown under the company name.
  • Each position within the group shows its start and end dates and tenure.

Notes

  • Positions won’t group if the start date of the new position is more than one month after the previous position’s end date.

  • If a position is grouped incorrectly, check and update the company name to separate them.

  • Manage your profile Experience section

  • Reorder your current positions in the Experience section of your profile

  • Access country specific employment types

Private mode viewers of profiles

When a member browses LinkedIn in private mode, their name and other profile information isn’t shared with the owners of the profiles they view. Some LinkedIn members, like recruiters and business professionals, choose to browse profiles in private mode to find candidates, sales leads, potential clients, or business partners.

This setting is affected by the type of account you have:

  • If you have a Basic (free) account, and choose to browse in private mode, you won’t be able to see who’s viewed your profile either.
  • If you have a Premium account, you can browse in private mode and still see the list of people who viewed your profile in the last 90 days.

Notes:

  • You can’t block private mode viewers or make them reveal their names when viewing your profile.
  • We always respect a member’s privacy settings, so even if you have a Premium account, you can’t view the names of private mode viewers of your own profile.

Learn more about who’s viewed your profile and how to browse in private mode.

Profile displays incorrectly in search tool results

After you make changes to your profile, it may take several weeks or even months for search tools like Google, Yahoo, or Bing to detect and reflect those changes. LinkedIn does not control how or when these search tools refresh their results. If your profile appears incorrectly in search results, you’ll need to contact the search tool directly to request a correction.

You may find the below information helpful:

  • If you recently created a LinkedIn account and do not see your profile in search tool results, we encourage you to complete your profile and connect with other LinkedIn members to increase activity and raise visibility to search tools.
  • Verify if your public profile is searchable and displaying correctly on Bing or Yahoo! If other search tools are showing your public profile incorrectly, you can reach out to the support center for the search tool in question directly.
  • If your updated public profile is significantly different from the previous version, you can make a direct request to:
    • Google via their Refresh Outdated Content tool available at: Remove outdated content (search.google.com). You can also Visit the Google Help center for more info. LinkedIn does not control this process.
    • Bing via the Content Removal tool at: Bing’s Content Removal tool LinkedIn does not control this process.
    • Yahoo! via the Yahoo! help center at: Homepage (help.yahoo.com)

Note: If you close your LinkedIn account, it is closed immediately. However, it may take up to 72 hours for your public profile to be removed from LinkedIn.

  • Not all sections of your profile can be displayed publicly. On the Public profile settings page, you’ll be able to see and adjust the sections of your profile that are eligible to be displayed publicly. Viewers who are not signed in to LinkedIn may see all or some portions of the profile eligible to be displayed publicly. Keep in mind that in some contexts we may show a more limited profile preview that includes some but not all of the profile fields you’ve allowed

  • In order to see your full profile, visitors may need to log in to their LinkedIn accounts.

  • Control whether your profile appears in public search engine results

  • Control your LinkedIn profile

Profile does or doesn’t appear after name search on web

When you create a profile on LinkedIn, a public version of your profile is published to our member directory. Search engines like Google and Yahoo periodically review our member directory for new and updated public profile information to show in their search results. This indexes your profile and makes it searchable on the web.

Important to know

We can’t control how quickly search engines make updates after you make changes to your public profile. Some search engines can take several weeks to remove old profiles or show new information. You must display your full last name to have a public profile.

If you want to be indexed by search engines:

  • Turn on Your profile’s public visibility in your public profile settings.
  • Invite and connect with at least one connection.
  • Add additional sections and information to your profile.
  • Edit your profile regularly to keep it current.

Important to know

If you don’t want to be indexed by search engines, toggle Your profile’s public visibilityto Off in your public profile settings.

Notes:

  • You can edit your public profile settings to show only the information you want or to not show at all.

  • Your public profile settings work independently from the LinkedIn profile seen by members who are signed in.

Profile photo guidelines and conditions

Profile photo

Adding a photograph to your profile helps your current and potential connections recognize you. You can use an illustration, caricature, or other artistic rendering of yourself, but your profile photo must reflect your likeness. We may remove profile photos that don’t comply with our User Agreement and Professional Community Policies, including images that consist solely of the following:

  • Company logos
  • Emojis
  • Landscapes
  • Animals
  • Words or phrases
  • Flags
  • Childhood or baby photos
  • Others’ likenesses, including stock imagery, photos of celebrities, and depictions of fictional characters

Background photo

Adding a background photo to your profile can make your professional story more visually appealing. The background photo appears behind your profile photo in the introduction section on your profile. Just like your profile photo, the background photo you select may be removed by LinkedIn if it doesn’t comply with our User Agreement and Professional Community Policies.

If we remove your photo, you can upload a different photo to replace it. If you have questions about why your photo was removed, please contact us.

  • See or edit your current photo
  • See step-by-step instructions for adding your profile photo
  • Learn how to add or change a background photo
  • Learn more if you’re having trouble uploading your photo
  • Personalize your background with a photo - best practices

Questions about your experience and skills on LinkedIn

After you apply for a job on LinkedIn, we may prompt you to answer a few questions about your experience and skills. These answers are private to you only and are used to enhance your job-seeking experience on LinkedIn.

We’ll store and pre-fill these answers for future job applications, so you save time and effort in your future applications. You can always review and update or delete these answers in your future applications before they are submitted.

We may use this information to recommend jobs that are relevant to your qualifications. This ensures more jobs that match your qualifications are delivered to you in your job search.

You can opt out of saving answers through the Job applications settings.

  • Job application settings

Recommendations on LinkedIn

A recommendation is a commendation written by a LinkedIn member to recognize your work.

You can request recommendations from your 1st-degree connections you work with or have worked with.

If a connection writes you a recommendation, you’ll be notified via a message from the sender on LinkedIn. You can accept, dismiss or ask for revision of the recommendation.

Once you’ve accepted a recommendation from your connection, it’ll be visible to your network by default. You can hide a recommendation you’ve accepted.

You can also recognize your connections’ work by writing them a recommendation. If you receive a recommendation request, you can decline the request and aren’t required to respond. However, if you do write a recommendation and change your mind later, you have the option to revise a recommendation you’ve given or delete a recommendation. There’s no limit to the number of recommendations you can request or give. You can request or give only one recommendation per position, per member.

Important to know

If you remove a connection, any recommendations between you and that person will be withdrawn. These recommendations will not be restored if the connection is re-established.
